# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer ## OAuth Authentication

In order to interact with the DigitalOcean API, you or your application must
authenticate.

The DigitalOcean API handles this through OAuth, an open standard for
authorization. OAuth allows you to delegate access to your account.
Scopes can be used to grant full access, read-only access, or access to
a specific set of endpoints.

You can generate an OAuth token by visiting the [Apps & API](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/api/tokens)
section of the DigitalOcean control panel for your account.

An OAuth token functions as a complete authentication request. In effect, it
acts as a substitute for a username and password pair.

Because of this, it is absolutely **essential** that you keep your OAuth
tokens secure. In fact, upon generation, the web interface will only display
each token a single time in order to prevent the token from being compromised.

DigitalOcean access tokens begin with an identifiable prefix in order to
distinguish them from other similar tokens.

- `dop_v1_` for personal access tokens generated in the control panel
- `doo_v1_` for tokens generated by applications using [the OAuth flow](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/oauth-api/)
- `dor_v1_` for OAuth refresh tokens

### Scopes

Scopes act like permissions assigned to an API token. These permissions
determine what actions the token can perform. You can create API
tokens that grant read-only access, full access, or limited access to
specific endpoints by using custom scopes.

Generally, scopes are designed to match HTTP verbs and common CRUD
operations (Create, Read, Update, Delete).

| HTTP Verb | CRUD Operation | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| GET | Read | `<resource>:read` |
| POST | Create | `<resource>:create` |
| PUT/PATCH | Update | `<resource>:update` |
| DELETE | Delete | `<resource>:delete` |

For example, creating a new Droplet by making a `POST` request to the
`/v2/droplets` endpoint requires the `droplet:create` scope while
listing Droplets by making a `GET` request to the `/v2/droplets`
endpoint requires the `droplet:read` scope.

Each endpoint below specifies which scope is required to access it when
using custom scopes.

### How to Authenticate with OAuth

In order to make an authenticated request, include a bearer-type
`Authorization` header containing your OAuth token. All requests must be
made over HTTPS.

### Authenticate with a Bearer Authorization Header

```
curl -X $HTTP_METHOD -H "Authorization: Bearer $DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN" "https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/$OBJECT"
```

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer ## OAuth Authentication

In order to interact with the DigitalOcean API, you or your application must
authenticate.

The DigitalOcean API handles this through OAuth, an open standard for
authorization. OAuth allows you to delegate access to your account.
Scopes can be used to grant full access, read-only access, or access to
a specific set of endpoints.

You can generate an OAuth token by visiting the [Apps & API](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/api/tokens)
section of the DigitalOcean control panel for your account.

An OAuth token functions as a complete authentication request. In effect, it
acts as a substitute for a username and password pair.

Because of this, it is absolutely **essential** that you keep your OAuth
tokens secure. In fact, upon generation, the web interface will only display
each token a single time in order to prevent the token from being compromised.

DigitalOcean access tokens begin with an identifiable prefix in order to
distinguish them from other similar tokens.

- `dop_v1_` for personal access tokens generated in the control panel
- `doo_v1_` for tokens generated by applications using [the OAuth flow](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/oauth-api/)
- `dor_v1_` for OAuth refresh tokens

### Authenticate with a Bearer Authorization Header

**Serverless Inference:**

```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN" "https://inference.do-ai.run/v1/chat/completions"
```

**Agent Inference:**

```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENT_ACCESS_KEY" "https://{your-agent-url}.agents.do-ai.run/v1/chat/completions?agent=true"
```

**Note:** Agent Inference APIs use an `agent_access_key` (endpoint access
key) instead of a DigitalOcean OAuth token. The `agent_access_key` is
provided when you provision an agent endpoint and is scoped to that
specific agent. It is not interchangeable with DigitalOcean OAuth tokens
(`dop_v1_*`, `doo_v1_*`, `dor_v1_*`), which are used with Serverless
Inference and the control-plane API at `https://api.digitalocean.com`.

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-1-click-applications">1-Click Applications</h1>

1-Click applications are pre-built Droplet images or Kubernetes apps with software,
features, and configuration details already set up for you. They can be found in the
[DigitalOcean Marketplace](https://marketplace.digitalocean.com/).

## List 1-Click Applications

<a id="opIdoneClicks_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/1-clicks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/1-clicks`

To list all available 1-Click applications, send a GET request to `/v2/1-clicks`. The `type` may
be provided as query paramater in order to restrict results to a certain type of 1-Click, for
example: `/v2/1-clicks?type=droplet`. Current supported types are `kubernetes` and `droplet`.

The response will be a JSON object with a key called `1_clicks`. This will be set to an array of
1-Click application data, each of which will contain the the slug and type for the 1-Click.


<h3 id="list-1-click-applications-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|query|string|false|Restrict results to a certain type of 1-Click.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|droplet|
|type|kubernetes|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "1_clicks": [
    {
      "slug": "monitoring",
      "type": "kubernetes"
    },
    {
      "slug": "wordpress-18-04",
      "type": "droplet"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Install Kubernetes 1-Click Applications

<a id="opIdoneClicks_install_kubernetes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/1-clicks/kubernetes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "addon_slugs": [
      "kube-state-metrics",
      "loki"
    ],
    "cluster_uuid": "50a994b6-c303-438f-9495-7e896cfe6b08"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/1-clicks/kubernetes`

To install a Kubernetes 1-Click application on a cluster, send a POST request to
`/v2/1-clicks/kubernetes`. The `addon_slugs` and `cluster_uuid` must be provided as body
parameter in order to specify which 1-Click application(s) to install. To list all available
1-Click Kubernetes applications, send a request to `/v2/1-clicks?type=kubernetes`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "addon_slugs": [
    "kube-state-metrics",
    "loki"
  ],
  "cluster_uuid": "50a994b6-c303-438f-9495-7e896cfe6b08"
}
```

<h3 id="install-kubernetes-1-click-applications-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[oneClicks_create](#schemaoneclicks_create)|true|none|
|» addon_slugs|body|[string]|true|An array of 1-Click Application slugs to be installed to the Kubernetes cluster.|
|» cluster_uuid|body|string|true|A unique ID for the Kubernetes cluster to which the 1-Click Applications will be installed.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Successfully kicked off addon job."
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-account">Account</h1>

Provides information about your current account.

## Get User Information

<a id="opIdaccount_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/account \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/account`

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-actions">Actions</h1>

Actions are records of events that have occurred on the resources in your account.
These can be things like rebooting a Droplet, or transferring an image to a new region.

An action object is created every time one of these actions is initiated. The action
object contains information about the current status of the action, start and complete
timestamps, and the associated resource type and ID.

Every action that creates an action object is available through this endpoint. Completed
actions are not removed from this list and are always available for querying.

**Note:** You can pass the following HTTP header with the request to have the API return
the `reserved_ips` stanza instead of the `floating_ips` stanza:

- `Accept: application/vnd.digitalocean.reserveip+json`

## List All Actions

<a id="opIdactions_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/actions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/actions`

This will be the entire list of actions taken on your account, so it will be quite large. As with any large collection returned by the API, the results will be paginated with only 20 on each page by default.

<h3 id="list-all-actions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

> Example responses

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-add-ons">Add-Ons</h1>

Add-ons are third-party applications that can be added to your DigitalOcean account.
They are available through the [DigitalOcean Marketplace](https://marketplace.digitalocean.com/).
Add-ons can be used to enhance the functionality of your existing resources or to provide
additional services.

The Add-Ons API allows you to manage these resources, including creating, listing, and retrieving
details about specific add-on resources.

## List Available Add-On Applications

<a id="opIdaddons_get_app"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/add-ons/apps \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/add-ons/apps`

To fetch details of all available Add-On Applications, send a GET request to `/v2/add-ons/apps`.

## Get Metadata for an Add-On Application

<a id="opIdaddons_get_app_metadata"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/add-ons/apps/example_app/metadata \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/add-ons/apps/{app_slug}/metadata`

To find out what metadata is required for a specific add-on, send a GET request to `/v2/add-ons/apps/{app_slug}/metadata`.
Metadata varies by application.


<h3 id="get-metadata-for-an-add-on-application-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|app_slug|path|string|true|The slug identifier for the application whose metadata is being requested.|

```json
    {
      "id": 1,
      "name": "country_of_origin",
      "display_name": "Country of Origin",
      "description": "Country for localization",
      "type": "string",
      "options": [
        "US",
        "UK",
        "CA"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Create/Provision a New Add-on Resource

<a id="opIdaddons_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/add-ons/saas \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "app_slug": "example-app",
    "plan_slug": "basic_plan",
    "name": "my-resource-01",
    "metadata": [
      {
        "name": "property_name",
        "value": "example_value"
      }
    ],
    "linked_droplet_id": 12345678,
    "fleet_uuid": "f1234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef01"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/add-ons/saas`

To create an add-on resource, send a POST request to `/v2/add-ons/saas` with required parameters.
Some add-ons require additional metadata to be provided in the request body. To find out
what metadata is required for a specific add-on, send a GET request to `/v2/add-ons/apps/{app_slug}/metadata`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "app_slug": "example-app",
  "plan_slug": "basic_plan",
  "name": "my-resource-01",
  "metadata": [
    {
      "name": "property_name",
      "value": "example_value"
    }
  ],
  "linked_droplet_id": 12345678,
  "fleet_uuid": "f1234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef01"
}
```

<h3 id="createprovision-a-new-add-on-resource-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» app_slug|body|string|true|The slug identifier for the application associated with the resource.|
|» plan_slug|body|string|true|The slug identifier for the plan associated with the resource.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the addon resource.|
|» metadata|body|[[addons_resource_metadata](#schemaaddons_resource_metadata)]|true|Metadata associated with the resource, set by the user. Metadata expected varies per app, and can be verified with a GET request to "/v2/add-ons/apps/{app_slug}/metadata"|
|» linked_droplet_id|body|integer|false|ID of the droplet to be linked to this resource, if applicable.|
|» fleet_uuid|body|string|false|UUID of the fleet/project to which this resource will belong.|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-action-gateway">Action Gateway</h1>

Action Gateway gives AI agents governed access to tools over the Model
Context Protocol (MCP). The `/v2/action-gateway` endpoints manage the
tool catalog and the resources that control how agents use it:

- **Tools** browse and search the catalog, its providers, and global
  provider and tool health.
- **Toolbelts** are versioned, team-owned sets of tools that sessions
  and policies reference as `toolbelt:<name>@<version>`.
- **Output views** reshape a tool's output before it reaches the agent.
- **MCP servers** register your own remote MCP servers and choose which
  of their tools to enable.
- **Connections** authorize one of your end users to use a provider's
  tools, for example through OAuth.
- **Sessions** bind a tool selection and permission policy to an MCP URL
  that an agent connects to.
- **Users** and **end user limits** show and limit activity per end
  user, identified by a session's `actorId`.

To find and call tools in a session, use the
[Action Gateway Data Plane](#tag/Action-Gateway-Data-Plane) endpoints or
connect an MCP client to the session's `mcpUrl`.

## Get an Actor's Limits

<a id="opIdactorLimits_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/actors/alice/limits \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/action-gateway/actors/{actor_id}/limits`

Returns the per-minute limits set for the actor and the limits in effect, each the lower of your team's limit and the actor's override. Returns 404 when the actor has no sessions, connections, or limit overrides.

<h3 id="get-an-actors-limits-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actor_id|path|string|true|Actor ID: a session `actor_id` or a connection `user_id`, 1 to 64 characters from `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "configured_limits": [
    {
      "category": "LIMIT_CATEGORY_WEB_SEARCH_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE",
      "requests_per_minute": "10"
    }
  ],
  "effective_limits": {
    "web_search_requests_per_minute": "10",
    "web_fetch_requests_per_minute": "120",
    "native_tool_calls_requests_per_minute": "600",
```

## Clear an Actor's Limits

<a id="opIdactorLimits_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/actors/alice/limits:clear \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "categories": [
      "LIMIT_CATEGORY_WEB_SEARCH_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/action-gateway/actors/{actor_id}/limits:clear`

Removes the actor's overrides for the listed categories, which then follow your team's limits again. Clearing a category without an override succeeds.

```json
{
  "categories": [
```

|body|body|[clear_actor_limits](#schemaclear_actor_limits)|true|none|

## Set an Actor's Limits

<a id="opIdactorLimits_update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/actors/alice/limits:set \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "overrides": [
      {
        "category": "LIMIT_CATEGORY_WEB_SEARCH_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE",
        "requests_per_minute": "10"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/action-gateway/actors/{actor_id}/limits:set`

Sets per-minute limits for the listed categories and leaves the others unchanged. A limit may not exceed your team's current limit for the category (400 otherwise), and 0 blocks every call in the category. The actor does not need to exist yet.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "overrides": [
    {
      "category": "LIMIT_CATEGORY_WEB_SEARCH_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE",
      "requests_per_minute": "10"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="set-an-actors-limits-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actor_id|path|string|true|Actor ID: a session `actor_id` or a connection `user_id`, 1 to 64 characters from `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`.|
|body|body|[set_actor_limits](#schemaset_actor_limits)|true|none|
|» overrides|body|[[limit_override](#schemalimit_override)]|true|Required. Limits to set, at most one per category.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> 400 Response

```json

  "id": "bad_request",
  "message": "error parsing request body",
  "request_id": "4851a473-1621-42ea-b2f9-5071c0ea8414"
```

## List Connections

<a id="opIdconnections_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/connections \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/action-gateway/connections`

Returns the connections you can see, excluding revoked ones. Offset-paged with page and `per_page`; filter by provider, `user_id`, and status.

<h3 id="list-connections-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|provider|query|string|false|Optional provider slug, matched exactly.|
|user_id|query|string|false|Optional substring of `user_id`. It must use the `user_id` alphabet, `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`.|
|status|query|string|false|pending\|active\|revoked\|expired. List results always omit revoked connections, including when this filter is revoked.|
|sort|query|string|false|`created_at`, provider, `user_id`, or status. Defaults to provider, then `user_id`.|
|sort_direction|query|string|false|asc (the default) or desc.|
|page|query|integer|false|1-based page number. Values below 1 are treated as 1.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Page size. Defaults to 20; values above 100 are capped at 100.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|pending|
|status|active|
|status|expired|
|sort|created_at|
|sort|provider|
|sort|user_id|
|sort|status|
|sort_direction|asc|
|sort_direction|desc|

## Create a Connection

<a id="opIdconnections_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/connections \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "provider": "jira",
    "user_id": "alice",
    "scopes": [
      "write:jira-work"
    ],
    "connection_parameters": {
      "site_url": "https://example.atlassian.net"
    },
    "credential": {
      "digitalocean_oauth": {}
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v2/action-gateway/connections`

Connects one of your users, identified by `user_id`, to a provider so tools can act on their
account. An OAuth connection starts pending, and authorization carries the URL to send the user to;
read the connection until it is active or expired. A connection through a team API-key credential is
active immediately.

There is one connection per provider and `user_id` for each DigitalOcean user who creates
connections. Repeating the request returns the existing connection when its scopes cover the
request, reusing a pending connection's link, and restarts an expired or revoked connection under
the same ID. Requesting scopes beyond an existing connection's, or a different credential, returns
400 until that connection is deleted.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "provider": "jira",
  "user_id": "alice",
  "scopes": [
    "write:jira-work"
  ],
  "connection_parameters": {
    "site_url": "https://example.atlassian.net"
  },
  "credential": {
    "digitalocean_oauth": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-connection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[connection_create](#schemaconnection_create)|true|none|
|» provider|body|string|true|Required provider slug, from the provider list.|
|» user_id|body|string|true|Required. Your identifier for the user the connection acts for: 1 to 64 characters from `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`. A session whose `actor_id` equals it uses this connection.|
|» scopes|body|[string]|false|Optional OAuth scopes to request. Defaults to every scope the provider offers; scopes outside that set are rejected. Ignored for API-key credentials.|
|» connection_parameters|body|object|false|Values for the provider's `connection_parameters`, validated against their specifications.|
|» credential|body|object|false|Optional credential to connect through. Omitted uses DigitalOcean's shared OAuth application.|
|» » digitalocean_oauth|body|object|false|Use DigitalOcean's shared OAuth application.|
|» » team_credential|body|object|false|Use one of your team's provider credentials.|
|» » » credential_id|body|string|false|Required. ID of an active provider credential for the same provider that you can use.|
|» network|body|object|false|Optional private network for the connection's calls. Requires VPC networking to be enabled for your account (403 otherwise).|
|» » vpc|body|object|false|Route through a VPC.|
|» » » vpc_uuid|body|string(uuid)|false|UUID of a VPC owned by your team.|
|» » » destinations|body|[object]|false|Private hosts the connection's calls may reach through the VPC. At least one is required.|
|» » » » host|body|string|false|Host name or IP address. It must resolve only to private addresses.|
|» » » » port|body|integer(uint32)|false|Port, 1 to 65535.|
|» » » » allowed_ip_cidrs|body|[string]|false|Optional CIDR ranges; when set, every address the host resolves to must fall within one of them.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "connection": {
    "id": "39f9f768-a7f9-4c91-9557-3328c53dd054",
    "provider": "jira",
    "provider_display_name": "Jira",
    "user_id": "alice",
    "status": "pending",
    "created_at": "2026-07-14T00:50:00Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-07-14T00:50:00Z",
    "revoked_at": null,
    "connection_parameters": {
      "site_url": "https://example.atlassian.net"
    },
    "credential_kind": "digitalocean_oauth",
    "credential_id": "",
    "network": null,
    "scopes": [
      "write:jira-work"
    ],
    "granted_at": null,
    "oauth": {
      "scopes": [
        "write:jira-work"
      ],
      "granted_at": null
    }
  },
  "authorization": {
    "status": "requires_authorization",
    "connect_url": "https://cloud.digitalocean.com/security/connectlinks/confirm?token=eyJhbGciOi",
    "verification_code": "97rwxzcy",
    "expires_at": "2026-07-14T01:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

## Get a Connection

<a id="opIdconnections_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/connections/39f9f768-a7f9-4c91-9557-3328c53dd054 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/action-gateway/connections/{id}`

Returns the connection and, while it is pending, the authorization the user still has to complete. Reading a pending connection picks up a completed authorization, and marks the connection expired once its link has lapsed. Returns 404 for an unknown connection or one you cannot see.

<h3 id="get-a-connection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|

## Delete a Connection

<a id="opIdconnections_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/connections/39f9f768-a7f9-4c91-9557-3328c53dd054 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/action-gateway/connections/{id}`

Marks the connection revoked and returns it; for an OAuth connection, its stored tokens are deleted first. Creating a connection for the same provider and `user_id` later reuses the same ID. Only the user who created the connection can delete it; for anyone else it is 404.

<h3 id="delete-a-connection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|Connection ID.|

## Register an MCP Server

<a id="opIdmcpServers_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/mcp-servers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "serverRef": "docs",
    "endpoint": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
    "credentialRefSource": "secret",
    "api_key": "sk_live_example",
    "description": "Internal documentation search."
  }'
```

`POST /v2/action-gateway/mcp-servers`

Registers a remote MCP server for your team, using the streamable HTTP transport. The server starts with `syncStatus` pending and no tools: discover its tools with `POST .../mcp-servers/{server_ref}/resync`, then choose which to enable with `PUT .../mcp-servers/{server_ref}/tools`. The endpoint must be HTTPS and resolve only to public IP addresses. The number of servers per team is limited (10 by default); registering beyond it returns 429. Returns 409 when `serverRef` is already in use.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "serverRef": "docs",
  "endpoint": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
  "credentialRefSource": "secret",
  "api_key": "sk_live_example",
  "description": "Internal documentation search."
}
```

<h3 id="register-an-mcp-server-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[mcp_server_create](#schemamcp_server_create)|true|none|
|» serverRef|body|string|true|Identifier for the server, unique within your team. Must match `^`[a-z]``[a-z0-9-]`{0,63}$`.|
|» endpoint|body|string|true|HTTPS URL of the server's MCP endpoint. Its host must resolve only to public IP addresses. Required.|
|» transport|body|string|false|Optional. `streamable_http`, the default and only accepted value.|
|» credentialRefSource|body|string|false|How requests to the server authenticate: none (the default), secret, or connection. With secret, the value from `credentialRef` or `api_key` is sent in the Authorization header, prefixed with "Bearer " unless it already contains a space.|
|» description|body|string|false|Optional description shown on the server's catalog card. At most 1024 characters.|
|» credentialRef|body|string|false|For `credentialRefSource` secret: a reference to a secret your team stores with DigitalOcean. Must match `^`[A-Za-z0-9]``[A-Za-z0-9:/_.-]`{0,254}$`. Set exactly one of `credentialRef` and `api_key`.|
|» api_key|body|string|false|For `credentialRefSource` secret: the key or token itself. DigitalOcean stores it; it is write-only and no response returns it. Set exactly one of `credentialRef` and `api_key`.|
|» oauth_client_id|body|string|false|Required for `credentialRefSource` connection: the client ID of your team's OAuth client for the server. Each user of the server then authorizes individually.|
|» oauth_client_secret|body|string|false|Required for `credentialRefSource` connection. Write-only; no response returns it.|
|» oauth_authorize_url|body|string|false|Required for `credentialRefSource` connection: the OAuth authorization endpoint. It must use the endpoint's scheme and port, on the endpoint's host or another host under the same registrable domain.|
|» oauth_token_url|body|string|false|Required for `credentialRefSource` connection: the OAuth token endpoint, under the same rules as `oauth_authorize_url`.|
|» oauth_scopes|body|[string]|false|Required for `credentialRefSource` connection: the scopes to request from each user, 1 to 64 of them.|
|» oauth_authorization_ttl_seconds|body|string(uint64)|false|How long, in seconds, a user's authorization may be reused before they must consent again. Optional;<br>0 means 30 days, and the maximum is 100 years.<br><br>Authorizations are not refreshed automatically, so this window, not the provider's token lifetime,<br>decides how often a user is sent back through consent. Set it no longer than the provider's own<br>token lifetime, so the prompt arrives before a tool call fails against an expired token.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» transport|streamable_http|
|» credentialRefSource|none|
|» credentialRefSource|secret|
|» credentialRefSource|connection|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "mcpServer": {
    "serverRef": "docs",
    "endpoint": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
    "transport": "streamable_http",
    "credentialRefSource": "secret",
    "credentialRef": "action-infra/tool-credentials/mcp/docs/3f5b2c1e-9a7d-4e8b-b6c4-2d1f0e9a8b7c",
    "syncStatus": "pending",
    "syncError": "",
    "lastSyncedAt": "",
    "protocolVersion": "",
    "toolCount": 0,
    "createdAt": "2026-09-20T15:00:00Z",
    "updatedAt": "2026-09-20T15:00:00Z",
    "description": "Internal documentation search.",
    "oauth_authorize_url": "",
    "oauth_scopes": [],
    "oauth_authorization_ttl_seconds": "0"
  }
}
```


```json
}
```

## Get an MCP Server

<a id="opIdmcpServers_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/mcp-servers/docs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/action-gateway/mcp-servers/{server_ref}`

Returns one of your team's MCP servers, or 404 when your team has none with this `serverRef`.

<h3 id="get-an-mcp-server-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|server_ref|path|string|true|Server identifier (`serverRef`) of one of your team's MCP servers.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
```

## Delete an MCP Server

<a id="opIdmcpServers_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/mcp-servers/docs \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/action-gateway/mcp-servers/{server_ref}`

Disables all of the server's tools, removes them from your team's catalog, and deletes the server. An `api_key` supplied at registration is deleted; a `credentialRef` you supplied is left untouched. For a server registered with `credentialRefSource` connection, every user connection made through its OAuth client is revoked. Returns the deleted server, or 404 when it does not exist.

<h3 id="delete-an-mcp-server-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|server_ref|path|string|true|Server identifier (`serverRef`) of one of your team's MCP servers.|

## Update an MCP Server

<a id="opIdmcpServers_patch"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/mcp-servers/docs \
```

`PATCH /v2/action-gateway/mcp-servers/{server_ref}`

```json
}
```

## Discover an MCP Server's Tools

<a id="opIdmcpServers_run_resync"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/mcp-servers/docs/resync \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{}'
```

`POST /v2/action-gateway/mcp-servers/{server_ref}/resync`

Connects to the server, lists its tools, and records them. Discovered tools are not callable until
you enable them.

When discovery finishes in time, returns 200 with the server and its tools; a discovery failure is
reported in `syncStatus` and `syncError` rather than as an error. Otherwise returns 202 with pending
set while discovery continues: poll `GET .../mcp-servers/{server_ref}` until `lastSyncedAt` or
`syncError` changes (`syncStatus` is not reset while discovery runs).

For a server registered with `credentialRefSource` connection, `user_id` is required; if that user
has not authorized the server yet, the response carries authorization with the URL to send them to.
Resyncs are rate limited per team, and a team can run only a few discoveries at once; either limit
returns 429.

> Body parameter

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="discover-an-mcp-servers-tools-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|server_ref|path|string|true|Server identifier (`serverRef`) of one of your team's MCP servers.|
|body|body|[mcp_server_resync](#schemamcp_server_resync)|true|none|
|» user_id|body|string|false|Required for a server registered with `credentialRefSource` connection: discovery reaches the server as this user, through their connection, because such a server has no team-wide credential. Ignored otherwise.|

> Example responses

```json
    "transport": "streamable_http",
```

## List an MCP Server's Tools

<a id="opIdmcpServers_list_tools"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/mcp-servers/docs/tools \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/action-gateway/mcp-servers/{server_ref}/tools`

Returns every tool discovered on the server, sorted by name, with whether each is enabled. Tools that have since disappeared from the server stay listed.

<h3 id="list-an-mcp-servers-tools-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|

```json
      "toolSlug": "docs_search",
      "description": "Search the documentation index.",

}
```

## Set Which of an MCP Server's Tools Are Enabled

<a id="opIdmcpServers_update_tools"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/mcp-servers/docs/tools \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "enabledToolSlugs": [
      "docs_get_page"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/action-gateway/mcp-servers/{server_ref}/tools`

`enabledToolSlugs` is the complete set to enable; every other tool of the server is disabled. An
enabled tool is added to your team's catalog at its latest discovered version, and a disabled one is
removed from it. Repeating the same set changes nothing.

Before changing anything, each tool being enabled, re-enabled, or moved to a newer discovered
version is verified against the live server: it must still be listed there, with the same input
schema as when it was discovered. If any check fails or the server cannot be reached, the request
fails with 400 and nothing changes; resync and try again. An unknown tool slug is also rejected with
400. A request that needs verification counts against the resync rate limit (429). Returns the
server's full tool list.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enabledToolSlugs": [
    "docs_get_page"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="set-which-of-an-mcp-servers-tools-are-enabled-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|server_ref|path|string|true|Server identifier (`serverRef`) of one of your team's MCP servers.|
|body|body|[mcp_server_tools_update](#schemamcp_server_tools_update)|true|none|
|» enabledToolSlugs|body|[string]|true|The complete set of tool slugs (`<server_ref>_<name>`) to enable; every other tool of the server is disabled. Empty disables every tool.|
|» user_id|body|string|false|Required for a server registered with `credentialRefSource` connection when a tool needs verification against the live server, which can only be reached as a user who has authorized it. Ignored otherwise.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "tools": [
    {
      "name": "get_page",
      "toolSlug": "docs_get_page",
      "description": "Fetch one documentation page.",
      "enabled": true,
      "quarantined": false,
      "quarantineReason": ""
    },
    {
      "name": "search",
      "toolSlug": "docs_search",
      "description": "Search the documentation index.",
      "enabled": false,
      "quarantined": false,
      "quarantineReason": ""
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json

  "id": "bad_request",
  "message": "error parsing request body",
  "request_id": "4851a473-1621-42ea-b2f9-5071c0ea8414"
}
```

```json
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

```json
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

## List Output Views

<a id="opIdoutputViews_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/output-views \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/action-gateway/output-views`

Returns the output views your team can use: views DigitalOcean publishes to every team, plus your team's own. Cursor-paged with `page_size` and `page_token`; no total is reported.

<h3 id="list-output-views-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tool|query|string|false|At most one of tool or `tool_id`, as on create. With one set, the list is the published views plus your team's own on that tool version. With neither, it is every live view your team owns plus every published view on a tool version your catalog exposes, across tools.|
|tool_id|query|string|false|Opaque ID of the tool version; see tool.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Page size, 1 to 100. Defaults to 20 when omitted or 0; other values are rejected with 400.|
|page_token|query|string|false|`next_page_token` from the previous response. Valid only with the same tool selection; otherwise the request is rejected with 400.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "views": [
    {
      "view_id": "ov_4f0c2a9d8e1b47c6a3d5f7e9b1c3a5d7",
      "tool_id": "tul_exa_web_search",
      "tool": "exa_web_search",
      "version": "v1",
      "team_id": "123456",
      "name": "titles-and-urls",
      "description": "Keep only result titles and URLs.",
      "kind": "OUTPUT_VIEW_KIND_PROJECTION",
      "fields": [
        "results.title",
        "results.url"
      ],
      "output_schema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "results": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
              "type": "object",
              "properties": {
                "title": {
                  "type": "string"
                },
                "url": {
                  "type": "string"
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      },
      "audit": {
        "createdAt": "2026-09-01T16:00:00Z",
        "updatedAt": "2026-09-01T16:00:00Z",
        "deletedAt": null
      }
    }
  ],
  "tool_id": "tul_exa_web_search",
  "tool": "exa_web_search",
  "version": "v1",
  "next_page_token": ""
}
```

## Create an Output View

<a id="opIdoutputViews_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/output-views \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "tool": "exa_web_search",
    "name": "titles-and-urls",
    "description": "Keep only result titles and URLs.",
    "fields": [
      "results.title",
      "results.url"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/action-gateway/output-views`

An output view is a named projection of one tool version's output: tool calls that use it return only the listed fields, and its `output_schema` describes the result. The view is bound to the tool version your catalog currently releases. Returns 409 when your team already has a view with this name on the tool version, and 429 when your team already has the maximum of 20 views on it.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "tool": "exa_web_search",
  "name": "titles-and-urls",
  "description": "Keep only result titles and URLs.",
  "fields": [
    "results.title",
    "results.url"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-output-view-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[output_view_create](#schemaoutput_view_create)|true|none|
|» tool|body|string|false|Exactly one of tool or `tool_id` selects the tool version. tool is a provider-qualified slug, optionally pinned as `<tool>@<version>`. You can bind only the released version your catalog exposes: an unpinned slug resolves it and the response echoes it as version; a pin must equal it, and a `tool_id` (the opaque identity from tool search) must be that version. Any other version returns 404.|
|» tool_id|body|string|false|Opaque ID of the tool version; see tool.|
|» name|body|string|true|View name. Must match `^`[a-z]``[a-z0-9_-]`{0,63}$` and be unique per tool version within your team.|
|» description|body|string|false|Optional description. At most 512 bytes.|
|» fields|body|[string]|true|Output paths to keep, 1 to 64 of them. Each is a dotted path of up to 8 segments made of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, and must be declared by the tool's output schema; arrays are traversed element-wise. Paths may not repeat or be a prefix of one another. The tool version must declare an object output schema.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "view": {
    "view_id": "ov_4f0c2a9d8e1b47c6a3d5f7e9b1c3a5d7",
    "tool_id": "tul_exa_web_search",
    "tool": "exa_web_search",
    "version": "v1",
    "team_id": "123456",
    "name": "titles-and-urls",
    "description": "Keep only result titles and URLs.",
    "kind": "OUTPUT_VIEW_KIND_PROJECTION",
    "fields": [
      "results.title",
      "results.url"
    ],
    "output_schema": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "results": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
              "title": {
                "type": "string"
              },
              "url": {
                "type": "string"
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "audit": {
      "createdAt": "2026-09-01T16:00:00Z",
      "updatedAt": "2026-09-01T16:00:00Z",
      "deletedAt": null
    }
  }
}
```

`POST /v2/action-gateway/output-views/preview`

Validates a projection exactly as create does and returns the view it would produce, including `output_schema`, without storing anything. name and description are optional here; name uniqueness and the per-tool-version limit are not checked.

> Body parameter

```json
  "fields": [

    "results.url"
  ]
}
```

|body|body|[output_view_preview](#schemaoutput_view_preview)|true|none|
|» tool|body|string|false|Tool slug, optionally pinned; as on create.|
|» tool_id|body|string|false|Opaque ID of the tool version; as on create.|
|» name|body|string|false|Optional view name, validated as on create when present.|
|» description|body|string|false|Optional description, validated as on create when present.|
|» fields|body|[string]|true|Output paths to keep; as on create.|

## Delete an Output View

<a id="opIdoutputViews_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/output-views/ov_4f0c2a9d8e1b47c6a3d5f7e9b1c3a5d7 \
  -X DELETE \
```

`DELETE /v2/action-gateway/output-views/{view_id}`

Deletes one of your team's views and returns it with audit.deleted_at set; it can no longer be used. Published views cannot be deleted. Returns 404 when the view does not exist, is already deleted, or is not your team's.

## List Sessions

<a id="opIdsessions_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/sessions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/action-gateway/sessions`

Returns the sessions you can see, newest first. Offset-paged with page and `per_page`; `end_user_id` filters to one actor.

<h3 id="list-sessions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|end_user_id|query|string|false|Optional `actor_id`, matched exactly.|
|page|query|integer|false|1-based page number. Values below 1 are treated as 1.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Page size. Defaults to 20; values above 100 are capped at 100.|

## Create a Session

<a id="opIdsessions_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/sessions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "support-bot-alice",
    "actorId": "alice",
    "tools": [
      "toolbelt:search-toolbelt@1",
      "jira_create_issue"
    ],
    "policy": {
      "defaultAction": "ask",
      "rules": [
        {
          "tool": "toolbelt:search-toolbelt@1",
          "match": {},
          "action": "allow"
        },
        {
          "tool": "jira_create_issue",
          "match": {},
          "action": "ask"
        }
      ]
    },
    "config": {
      "preloadTools": [
        "exa_web_search"
      ],
      "outputViews": {
        "exa_web_search": "titles-and-urls"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v2/action-gateway/sessions`

Creates a session owned by your team, with a new session URN, and returns the MCP URL an agent connects to. tools selects the tools and toolbelts the session exposes, and policy decides which calls run, need approval, or are refused.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "support-bot-alice",
  "actorId": "alice",
  "tools": [
    "toolbelt:search-toolbelt@1",
    "jira_create_issue"
  ],
  "policy": {
    "defaultAction": "ask",
    "rules": [
      {
        "tool": "toolbelt:search-toolbelt@1",
        "match": {},
        "action": "allow"
      },
      {
        "tool": "jira_create_issue",
        "match": {},
        "action": "ask"
      }
    ]
  },
  "config": {
    "preloadTools": [
      "exa_web_search"
    ],
    "outputViews": {
      "exa_web_search": "titles-and-urls"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[session_create](#schemasession_create)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Required human-readable session name.|
|» actorId|body|string|false|Optional actor binding: the user whose connections the session's tool calls use, matched against connection `user_id`. When set it must use the same alphabet as a connection's `user_id`, `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, at most 64 characters; anything else is rejected with 400.|
|» policy|body|object|false|Optional tool-permission policy. Omitted asks before every call.|
|» » defaultAction|body|string|false|Action for calls no rule matches. Empty means ask; otherwise this must be allow, ask, or deny.|
|» » rules|body|[object]|false|Rules for specific tools or toolbelts.|
|» » » tool|body|string|false|Required. A tool slug, optionally `<tool_slug>@<version>`, or a toolbelt as `toolbelt:<name>@<version>`. When the session selects tools, the rule must name one of them.|
|» » » match|body|object|false|Optional argument conditions, keyed by argument name; the rule applies only to calls whose arguments match.|
|» » » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » » action|body|string|false|Required: allow, ask, or deny.|
|» tools|body|[string]|false|Omitted enables every tool. An explicit empty array enables no tools. Direct tools may be `<tool>` or `<tool>@<version>`, using provider-qualified tool slugs, and a pinned version must be the released one; toolbelt references must be version-pinned as `toolbelt:<belt-name>@<version>`.|
|» config|body|object|false|Optional session options. config.preloadTools may contain concrete tool names (optionally version-pinned) and version-pinned toolbelt references. config.customInstructions is a string of at most 1000 characters. config.outputViews maps up to 100 tool slugs to the name of an output view to apply to that tool's results.|
|» network|body|object|false|Product-level session network binding. When set, `vpc_uuid` must identify a VPC owned by the session's team.|
|» » vpcUuid|body|string(uuid)|false|UUID of a VPC owned by your team, in a region that supports sessions.|
|» insights|body|object|false|Omitted when the request omitted insights or explicitly sent null.|
|» » metrics|body|boolean \| null|false|Accepted and stored for parity with the Insights schema.|
|» » logs|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether the session's customer logs are sent to Insights.|
|» » traces|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether the session's customer traces are sent to Insights.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » defaultAction|allow|
|» » defaultAction|ask|
|» » defaultAction|deny|
|» » » action|allow|
|» » » action|ask|
|» » » action|deny|

> Example responses

```json
  "session": {
    "sessionUrn": "do:managed_agent_session:2b3c9f0e-1a4d-4e5f-8a7b-6c5d4e3f2a1b",
```

## Search Sessions

<a id="opIdsessions_list_search"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/sessions/search \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/action-gateway/sessions/search`

Returns the sessions you can see whose name, `actor_id`, `session_urn`, or `agentName` contains query, case-insensitively, ranked across the whole result set. Cursor-paged with `page_size` and `page_token`; no total is reported.

<h3 id="search-sessions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|false|Matched case-insensitively as a substring of name, `actor_id`, `session_urn`, or `agentName`. Empty matches every session you can see. Results are ordered by match quality (an exact name, `session_urn`, or `actor_id` match, then a prefix, then a substring), then by name, across the whole result set, so a client must not re-sort a page to rank it.|
|end_user_id|query|string|false|`end_user_id`, when set, is an exact filter on `actor_id` (the same filter as on the session list) and combines with query as AND.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Page size, 1 to 100. Defaults to 20 when omitted or 0; other values are rejected with 400.|
|page_token|query|string|false|`next_page_token` from the previous response. Valid only with the same query and `end_user_id`; otherwise the request is rejected with 400.|

## Delete a Session

<a id="opIdsessions_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/sessions/do%3Amanaged_agent_session%3A2b3c9f0e-1a4d-4e5f-8a7b-6c5d4e3f2a1b \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/action-gateway/sessions/{session_urn}`

Deletes the session and its policy. Succeeds without deleting anything when the session does not exist or you cannot delete it, so repeating a delete also succeeds. A malformed `session_urn` is rejected with 400.

|session_urn|path|string|true|URN of the session, for example `do:managed_agent_session:<uuid>`.|

## List Toolbelts


`GET /v2/action-gateway/toolbelts`

Returns your team's toolbelts, one entry per name describing its latest version, sorted by name. Offset-paged with page and `per_page`; pagination reports the total.

<h3 id="list-toolbelts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|status|query|string|false|active (default), deprecated, or all. Case-insensitive.|
|page|query|integer|false|1-based page number. Values below 1 are treated as 1.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Page size. Defaults to 20; values above 100 are capped at 100.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|deprecated|
|status|all|

## Create a Toolbelt

<a id="opIdtoolbelts_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/toolbelts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "search-toolbelt",
    "display_name": "Search Tools",
    "description": "Tools for searching and fetching public web pages.",
    "tools": [
      "exa_web_search",
      "exa_web_fetch"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/action-gateway/toolbelts`

A toolbelt is a named set of tools, each pinned to a version, that your team can attach to sessions as `toolbelt:<name>@<version>`. The first version is 1 unless version is set. Returns 409 if an active toolbelt with the same name exists. The name of a deleted toolbelt can be reused; its versions start again from the initial version.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "search-toolbelt",
  "display_name": "Search Tools",
  "description": "Tools for searching and fetching public web pages.",
  "tools": [
    "exa_web_search",
    "exa_web_fetch"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-toolbelt-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[toolbelt_create](#schematoolbelt_create)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Toolbelt name, unique among your team's active toolbelts. Must match `^`[a-z]``[a-z0-9_-]`{0,63}$`; `search` is reserved.|
|» version|body|string|false|Optional initial version number, a positive integer such as `1`. Defaults to 1.|
|» display_name|body|string|false|Optional human-readable label, separate from name. At most 128 bytes.|
|» description|body|string|false|Optional description. At most 255 bytes.|
|» tools|body|[string]|false|Optional initial members, as catalog tool slugs (`<provider>_<name>`). Each may be pinned as `<tool_slug>@<version>`; a pin must equal the tool's current released version, and an unpinned tool is pinned to that version. Every tool must be an active catalog tool. Duplicates are merged; at most 500 tools. Empty creates a toolbelt with no tools.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "toolbelt": {
    "name": "search-toolbelt",
    "version": "1",
    "display_name": "Search Tools",
    "description": "Tools for searching and fetching public web pages.",
    "tools": [
      "exa_web_fetch@1",
      "exa_web_search@1"
    ],
    "status": "active",
    "reference": "search-toolbelt@1",
    "reference_latest": "search-toolbelt",
    "tool_count": 2,
    "created_at": "2026-06-11T12:00:00Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-06-11T12:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "id": "bad_request",
  "message": "error parsing request body",
  "request_id": "4851a473-1621-42ea-b2f9-5071c0ea8414"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "id": "conflict",
  "message": "The request could not be completed due to a conflict."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Search Toolbelts

<a id="opIdtoolbelts_list_search"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/toolbelts/search \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/action-gateway/toolbelts/search`

Returns your team's toolbelts whose name, display name, or description contains query, case-insensitively, sorted by name. Cursor-paged with `page_size` and `page_token`; no total is reported.

<h3 id="search-toolbelts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|false|Matched case-insensitively as a substring of name, `display_name`, or description. Empty matches every toolbelt of your team.|
|status|query|string|false|active (default), deprecated, or all. Case-insensitive.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Page size, 1 to 100. Defaults to 20 when omitted or 0; other values are rejected with 400.|

## Get a Toolbelt

<a id="opIdtoolbelts_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/toolbelts/search-toolbelt \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/action-gateway/toolbelts/{name}`

Returns the latest version of the named toolbelt, or the version requested, with catalog metadata for one page of its members in `tool_details`. A deleted toolbelt returns 404 unless a version is requested.

<h3 id="get-a-toolbelt-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Toolbelt name.|
|version|query|string|false|Version number to read. Empty returns the latest version.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Page size for `tool_details` only; toolbelt.tools always lists every member. Defaults to 20; values above 100 are capped at 100.|
|page_token|query|string|false|`next_page_token` from the previous response, to continue `tool_details`. Treat it as opaque, and send it only with the same toolbelt, version, and search.|
|search|query|string|false|Restricts `tool_details` to members whose tool slug, name, title, description, provider, or category contains this value, case-insensitively. It does not filter toolbelt.tools. This is a substring match, not a filter expression.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "toolbelt": {
    "name": "search-toolbelt",
    "version": "1",
    "display_name": "Search Tools",
    "description": "Tools for searching and fetching public web pages.",
    "tools": [
      "exa_web_fetch@1",
      "exa_web_search@1"
    ],
    "status": "active",
    "reference": "search-toolbelt@1",
    "reference_latest": "search-toolbelt",
    "tool_count": 2,
    "created_at": "2026-06-11T12:00:00Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-06-11T12:00:00Z"
  },
  "tool_details": [
    {
      "tool_slug": "exa_web_fetch",
      "name": "web_fetch",
      "title": "Web Fetch",
      "description": "Fetch the contents of a public web page with Exa.",
      "provider": "exa",
      "category": "web-fetch",
      "version": 1
    },
    {
      "tool_slug": "exa_web_search",
      "name": "web_search",
      "title": "Web Search",
      "description": "Search the public web with Exa and return relevant results with normalized text snippets.",
      "provider": "exa",
      "category": "web-search",
      "version": 1
    }
  ],
  "next_page_token": ""
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "id": "bad_request",
  "message": "error parsing request body",
  "request_id": "4851a473-1621-42ea-b2f9-5071c0ea8414"
}
```

## Delete a Toolbelt

<a id="opIdtoolbelts_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/toolbelts/search-toolbelt \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/action-gateway/toolbelts/{name}`

Marks the toolbelt deleted and returns its latest version with status deprecated. Its versions stay readable by explicit version until the name is reused. The name is free to reuse immediately; a new toolbelt with it starts a fresh version history. Returns 404 when the toolbelt does not exist or is already deleted.

<h3 id="delete-a-toolbelt-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Toolbelt name.|

> Example responses

```json
    "tools": [
      "exa_web_fetch@1",
      "exa_web_search@1"
    ],
    "status": "deprecated",
    "reference": "search-toolbelt@1",
    "reference_latest": "search-toolbelt",
    "tool_count": 2,

  }
}
```

## List the Providers in a Toolbelt

<a id="opIdtoolbelts_list_providers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/toolbelts/search-toolbelt/providers \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/action-gateway/toolbelts/{name}/providers`

Returns the distinct providers of the toolbelt's members, each with its member count, sorted by provider ID. List one provider's members with `GET .../toolbelts/{name}/providers/{provider}/tools`.

<h3 id="list-the-providers-in-a-toolbelt-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Toolbelt name.|
|version|query|string|false|Version number to read. Empty reads the latest version.|
|page|query|integer|false|1-based page number. Values below 1 are treated as 1.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Page size. Defaults to 20; values above 100 are capped at 100.|
|search|query|string|false|Restricts providers whose ID, name, or description contains this value, case-insensitively.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "toolbelt": {
    "name": "search-toolbelt",
    "version": "1",
    "display_name": "Search Tools",
    "description": "Tools for searching and fetching public web pages.",
    "tools": [
      "exa_web_fetch@1",
      "exa_web_search@1"
    ],
    "status": "active",
    "reference": "search-toolbelt@1",
    "reference_latest": "search-toolbelt",
    "tool_count": 2,
    "created_at": "2026-06-11T12:00:00Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-06-11T12:00:00Z"

    {
      "provider": "exa",
      "tool_count": 2,
      "id": "exa",
      "name": "Exa",
      "description": "Web search tools backed by Exa.",
      "categories": [
        "web-fetch",
        "web-search"
      ],
      "created_at": "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 20,
    "total": 1
  }
}
```

## List a Toolbelt's Tools from One Provider

<a id="opIdtoolbelts_list_provider_tools"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/toolbelts/search-toolbelt/providers/exa/tools \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/action-gateway/toolbelts/{name}/providers/{provider}/tools`

Returns a page of catalog metadata for the toolbelt's members from the named provider, sorted by tool slug. An unknown provider returns an empty page.

<h3 id="list-a-toolbelts-tools-from-one-provider-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Toolbelt name.|
|provider|path|string|true|A provider ID from the toolbelt's provider list, or `_legacy` for members recorded without a provider. Matched exactly.|
|version|query|string|false|Version number to read. Empty reads the latest version.|
|page|query|integer|false|1-based page number. Values below 1 are treated as 1.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Page size. Defaults to 20; values above 100 are capped at 100.|
|search|query|string|false|Restricts tools whose slug, name, title, description, provider, or category contains this value, case-insensitively, within the provider only.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "tools": [
    {
      "tool_slug": "exa_web_fetch",
      "name": "web_fetch",
      "title": "Web Fetch",
      "description": "Fetch the contents of a public web page with Exa.",
      "provider": "exa",
      "category": "web-fetch",
      "version": 1
    },
    {
      "tool_slug": "exa_web_search",
      "name": "web_search",
      "title": "Web Search",
      "description": "Search the public web with Exa and return relevant results with normalized text snippets.",
      "provider": "exa",
      "category": "web-search",
      "version": 1
    }
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 20,
    "total": 2
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "id": "bad_request",
  "message": "error parsing request body",
  "request_id": "4851a473-1621-42ea-b2f9-5071c0ea8414"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Add Tools to a Toolbelt

<a id="opIdtoolbelts_add_tools"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/toolbelts/search-toolbelt/tools/add \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "tools": [
      "jira_create_issue"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/action-gateway/toolbelts/{name}/tools/add`

Adds the listed tools and returns the toolbelt. When membership changes, this creates a new version that keeps the display name and description. Tools already in the toolbelt are left as they are, so a request that adds nothing new returns the current version unchanged. Returns 400 when a tool is not an active catalog tool, when a pin differs from the tool's current released version or from the version the toolbelt already holds, or when the toolbelt would exceed 500 tools. Returns 404 for an unknown or deleted toolbelt.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "tools": [
    "jira_create_issue"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-tools-to-a-toolbelt-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Toolbelt name, from the path.|
|body|body|[toolbelt_tools](#schematoolbelt_tools)|true|none|
|» tools|body|[string]|true|Tool slugs (`<provider>_<name>`) to add or remove, each optionally pinned as `<tool_slug>@<version>`. At least one is required. When adding, a pin must equal the tool's current released version.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "toolbelt": {
    "name": "search-toolbelt",
    "version": "2",
    "display_name": "Search Tools",
    "description": "Tools for searching and fetching public web pages.",
    "tools": [
      "exa_web_fetch@1",
      "exa_web_search@1",
      "jira_create_issue@1"
    ],
    "status": "active",
    "reference": "search-toolbelt@2",
    "reference_latest": "search-toolbelt",
    "tool_count": 3,
    "created_at": "2026-06-11T12:00:00Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-06-12T09:30:00Z"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "id": "bad_request",
  "message": "error parsing request body",
  "request_id": "4851a473-1621-42ea-b2f9-5071c0ea8414"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Remove Tools from a Toolbelt

<a id="opIdtoolbelts_delete_tools"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/toolbelts/search-toolbelt/tools/remove \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "tools": [
      "exa_web_fetch"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/action-gateway/toolbelts/{name}/tools/remove`

Removes the listed tools and returns the toolbelt. When membership changes, this creates a new version that keeps the display name and description. Tools that are not members are ignored, and removing every tool is allowed; deleting the toolbelt itself is a separate DELETE. Returns 400 when a pin differs from the version the toolbelt holds, and 404 for an unknown or deleted toolbelt.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "tools": [
    "exa_web_fetch"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="remove-tools-from-a-toolbelt-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|path|string|true|Toolbelt name, from the path.|
|body|body|[toolbelt_tools](#schematoolbelt_tools)|true|none|
|» tools|body|[string]|true|Tool slugs (`<provider>_<name>`) to add or remove, each optionally pinned as `<tool_slug>@<version>`. At least one is required. When adding, a pin must equal the tool's current released version.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "toolbelt": {
    "name": "search-toolbelt",
    "version": "2",
    "display_name": "Search Tools",
    "description": "Tools for searching and fetching public web pages.",
    "tools": [
      "exa_web_search@1"
    ],
    "status": "active",
    "reference": "search-toolbelt@2",
    "reference_latest": "search-toolbelt",
    "tool_count": 1,
    "created_at": "2026-06-11T12:00:00Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-06-12T09:30:00Z"

}
```

## List Tools

<a id="opIdtools_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/tools \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/action-gateway/tools`

Returns one page of the tools your team can use: released catalog tools plus the enabled tools of your team's MCP servers. definitions[i] describes tools[i]. Offset-paged with page and `per_page`; an unknown `toolkitId` returns an empty page.

<h3 id="list-tools-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|toolkit_id|query|string|false|Restricts the page to one provider. It accepts the provider ID the catalog returns, including the `serverRef` of one of your team's MCP servers.|
|page|query|integer|false|1-based page index; values below 1 are treated as 1. A page past the end returns an empty tools list with the real total.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Page size. Defaults to 100 when omitted or 0; values above 100 are capped at 100.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "version": "v1",
  "tools": [
    {
      "name": "web_search",
      "toolkitId": "exa",
      "title": "Web Search",
      "description": "Search the public web with Exa and return relevant results with normalized text snippets.",
      "inputSchema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "query": {
            "type": "string",
            "description": "Search query string."
          },
          "max_results": {
            "type": "integer",
            "description": "Maximum number of search results to return."
          }
        },
        "required": [
          "query"
        ]
      },
      "annotations": {
        "title": "Web Search",
        "readOnlyHint": true,
        "idempotentHint": true,
```

## List Tool Health

<a id="opIdtools_list_health"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/tools/health \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/action-gateway/tools/health`

Returns availability and latency for each catalog tool over the requested window, sorted by provider and then tool slug. A tool with no calls in the window is listed with `data_status` `HEALTH_DATA_STATUS_NO_DATA`. Metrics are aggregated across all customers; request volumes are not reported. Tools of your team's MCP servers are not included. Offset-paged with page and `per_page`.

<h3 id="list-tool-health-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|provider|query|string|false|Optional provider ID, matched exactly, to return only that provider's tools.|
|window|query|string|false|Window to aggregate over. Defaults to twenty-four hours.<br><br>- `HEALTH_WINDOW_UNSPECIFIED`: Twenty-four hours.<br>- `HEALTH_WINDOW_ONE_HOUR`: One hour; history points are 10 minutes.<br>- `HEALTH_WINDOW_TWENTY_FOUR_HOURS`: Twenty-four hours; history points are 1 hour.<br>- `HEALTH_WINDOW_SEVEN_DAYS`: Seven days; history points are 6 hours.<br>- `HEALTH_WINDOW_THIRTY_DAYS`: Thirty days; history points are 24 hours.|
|page|query|integer|false|1-based page number. Values below 1 are treated as 1.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Page size. Defaults to 20; values above 100 are capped at 100.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|window|HEALTH_WINDOW_ONE_HOUR|
|window|HEALTH_WINDOW_TWENTY_FOUR_HOURS|
|window|HEALTH_WINDOW_SEVEN_DAYS|
|window|HEALTH_WINDOW_THIRTY_DAYS|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "snapshot": {
    "measured_at": "2026-09-24T12:00:00Z",
    "window": "86400s",
    "stale": false
  },
  "tools": [
    {
      "tool_slug": "exa_web_search",
      "provider": "exa",
      "health": {
        "data_status": "HEALTH_DATA_STATUS_AVAILABLE",
        "uptime_percentage": 99.82,
        "latency_p50_ms": 412.5,
        "latency_p95_ms": 1180
      }
    }
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 20,
    "total": 1
  }
}
```

## Get Tool Health

<a id="opIdtools_get_health"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/tools/health/tools/exa_web_search \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/action-gateway/tools/health/tools/{tool_slug}`

Returns availability and latency for one catalog tool over the requested window, optionally with a history series. Metrics are aggregated across all customers; request volumes are not reported. Returns 404 when `tool_slug` is not a catalog tool.

<h3 id="get-tool-health-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tool_slug|path|string|true|Catalog tool slug, for example `exa_search`. Required.|
|window|query|string|false|Window to aggregate over. Defaults to twenty-four hours.<br><br>- `HEALTH_WINDOW_UNSPECIFIED`: Twenty-four hours.<br>- `HEALTH_WINDOW_ONE_HOUR`: One hour; history points are 10 minutes.<br>- `HEALTH_WINDOW_TWENTY_FOUR_HOURS`: Twenty-four hours; history points are 1 hour.<br>- `HEALTH_WINDOW_SEVEN_DAYS`: Seven days; history points are 6 hours.<br>- `HEALTH_WINDOW_THIRTY_DAYS`: Thirty days; history points are 24 hours.|
|include_history|query|boolean|false|Additionally returns the window split into resolution-aligned points (the history field below).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|window|HEALTH_WINDOW_ONE_HOUR|
|window|HEALTH_WINDOW_TWENTY_FOUR_HOURS|
|window|HEALTH_WINDOW_SEVEN_DAYS|
|window|HEALTH_WINDOW_THIRTY_DAYS|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
  "snapshot": {
    "measured_at": "2026-09-24T12:00:00Z",
    "window": "3600s",
    "stale": false
  },
  "tool": {
    "tool_slug": "exa_web_search",
    "provider": "exa",
    "health": {
      "data_status": "HEALTH_DATA_STATUS_AVAILABLE",
      "uptime_percentage": 99.82,
      "latency_p50_ms": 412.5,
      "latency_p95_ms": 1180
    }
  },
  "history": {
    "resolution": "600s",
    "stale": false,
    "points": [
      {
        "bucket_start": "2026-09-24T11:10:00Z",
        "health": {
          "data_status": "HEALTH_DATA_STATUS_AVAILABLE",
          "uptime_percentage": 99.82,
          "latency_p50_ms": 412.5,
          "latency_p95_ms": 1180
        }
      },
      {
        "bucket_start": "2026-09-24T11:20:00Z",
        "health": {
          "data_status": "HEALTH_DATA_STATUS_NO_DATA",
          "uptime_percentage": null,
          "latency_p50_ms": null,
          "latency_p95_ms": null
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Search Providers

<a id="opIdtools_list_search_providers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/action-gateway/tools/providers/search \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/action-gateway/tools/providers/search`

Returns the providers of `GET /v2/action-gateway/tools/providers` whose name, display name, or description contains query, case-insensitively, sorted by name. Cursor-paged with `page_size` and `page_token`; no total is reported.

<h3 id="search-providers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|false|Matched case-insensitively as a substring of name, `display_name`, or description. It does not match the titles of the tools a provider owns: "providers owning a tool that matches" is a tool search grouped by the provider field of each result.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|Page size, 1 to 100. Defaults to 20 when omitted or 0; other values are rejected with 400.|
|page_token|query|string|false|`next_page_token` from the previous response. Valid only with the same query; otherwise the request is rejected with 400.|

```json
  ],

}
```
