## List Scenarios

<a id="opIdgenai_list_scenarios"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/gen-ai/scenario_sets/%22123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000%22/scenarios \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/gen-ai/scenario_sets/{scenario_set_uuid}/scenarios`

To list the scenarios in a scenario set, send a GET request to `/v2/gen-ai/scenario_sets/{scenario_set_uuid}/scenarios`.

<h3 id="list-scenarios-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|scenario_set_uuid|path|string|true|UUID of the scenario set to read.|
|page|query|integer|false|Page number.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Items per page.|
|search|query|string|false|Free-text search across name, description, and user_persona<br>(case-insensitive substring match). Empty means no search.|
|sort_by|query|string|false|Field to sort by. Defaults to original file order when unspecified.<br><br> - SCENARIO_SORT_FIELD_FILE_ORDER: Preserve original file order. Default.<br> - SCENARIO_SORT_FIELD_NAME: Sort by scenario name (case-insensitive). Empty names sort last.<br> - SCENARIO_SORT_FIELD_DESCRIPTION: Sort by scenario description (case-insensitive).|
|sort_direction|query|string|false|Sort direction. Defaults to ascending when unspecified.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort_by|SCENARIO_SORT_FIELD_UNSPECIFIED|
|sort_by|SCENARIO_SORT_FIELD_FILE_ORDER|
|sort_by|SCENARIO_SORT_FIELD_NAME|
|sort_by|SCENARIO_SORT_FIELD_DESCRIPTION|
|sort_direction|SORT_DIRECTION_UNSPECIFIED|
|sort_direction|SORT_DIRECTION_ASC|
|sort_direction|SORT_DIRECTION_DESC|

```json
      ],

}
```

## List Simulation Runs

<a id="opIdgenai_list_simulation_runs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/gen-ai/simulation_runs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/gen-ai/simulation_runs`

To list simulation runs, send a GET request to `/v2/gen-ai/simulation_runs`.

<h3 id="list-simulation-runs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|scenario_set_uuid|query|string|false|Optional filter by scenario set.|
|page|query|integer|false|Page number.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Items per page.|
|statuses|query|[string]|false|Filter by one or more statuses. Empty means no status filter.<br><br> - SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_PENDING: Accepted and queued, not yet executing.<br> - SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_RUNNING: Episodes are executing.<br> - SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_SUCCEEDED: All episodes finished successfully.<br> - SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_FAILED: The run failed, for example because of a timeout or workflow error.<br> - SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_CANCELLED: The run was cancelled.<br> - SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_EVALUATING: Episodes finished and an attached evaluation is running. Only reachable<br>when the create request included evaluation_config. When the evaluation<br>reaches a terminal status, its outcome is reflected in the simulation run<br>status.<br> - SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_PARTIALLY_SUCCESSFUL: The simulation or its attached evaluation completed with a mixture of<br>successful and failed results.|
|search|query|string|false|Free-text search across the run name and scenario set name<br>(case-insensitive substring match). Empty means no search.|
|sort_by|query|string|false|Field to sort by. Defaults to creation date when unspecified.<br><br> - SIMULATION_RUN_SORT_FIELD_CREATED_AT: Sort by creation date. Default.<br> - SIMULATION_RUN_SORT_FIELD_NAME: Sort by customer-supplied run name (case-insensitive).<br> - SIMULATION_RUN_SORT_FIELD_STATUS: Sort by status using lifecycle order (pending → running → terminal).<br> - SIMULATION_RUN_SORT_FIELD_UPDATED_AT: Sort by last update date.|
|sort_direction|query|string|false|Sort direction. Defaults to descending when unspecified.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|statuses|SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED|
|statuses|SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_PENDING|
|statuses|SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_RUNNING|
|statuses|SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_SUCCEEDED|
|statuses|SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_FAILED|
|statuses|SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_CANCELLED|
|statuses|SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_EVALUATING|
|statuses|SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_PARTIALLY_SUCCESSFUL|
|sort_by|SIMULATION_RUN_SORT_FIELD_UNSPECIFIED|
|sort_by|SIMULATION_RUN_SORT_FIELD_CREATED_AT|
|sort_by|SIMULATION_RUN_SORT_FIELD_NAME|
|sort_by|SIMULATION_RUN_SORT_FIELD_STATUS|
|sort_by|SIMULATION_RUN_SORT_FIELD_UPDATED_AT|
|sort_direction|SORT_DIRECTION_UNSPECIFIED|
|sort_direction|SORT_DIRECTION_ASC|
|sort_direction|SORT_DIRECTION_DESC|

`POST /v2/gen-ai/simulation_runs`

To create a simulation run, send a POST request to `/v2/gen-ai/simulation_runs`. The scenario set must be ready. Judge and user simulator models are optional and use platform defaults when omitted. The run is returned in the pending state.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "agent_config": {
    "agent_deployment_uuid": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
    "agent_uuid": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
    "name": "example name"
  },
  "evaluation_config": {
    "metric_uuids": [
      "example string"
    ],
    "star_metric": {
      "metric_uuid": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
      "name": "example name",
      "success_threshold": 123,
      "success_threshold_pct": 123
    }
  },
  "exploration_budget": 123,
  "judge_model_uuid": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
  "max_turns": 123,
  "name": "example name",
  "scenario_set_uuid": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
  "user_simulator_config": {},
  "user_simulator_model_uuid": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"
}
```

<h3 id="create-simulation-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[apiCreateSimulationRunInputPublic](#schemaapicreatesimulationruninputpublic)|false|none|
|» agent_config|body|[apiCandidateAgentConfig](#schemaapicandidateagentconfig)|false|Configuration of the candidate agent under test for a simulation run.|
|» evaluation_config|body|[apiSimulationEvaluationConfig](#schemaapisimulationevaluationconfig)|false|Optional configuration that opts a simulation run into an evaluation. When<br>included on the create-run request, the platform reserves a<br>model_evaluation_run linked to this simulation run and dispatches the<br>evaluation automatically after the simulation finishes. The evaluation<br>reuses the simulation run's judge_model_uuid.|
|» exploration_budget|body|integer(int64)|false|Optional run-level episodes-per-scenario override. When set, overrides each scenario's exploration_budget.|
|» judge_model_uuid|body|string|false|Optional model override for the judge. Platform default when unset.|
|» max_turns|body|integer(int64)|false|Optional run-level turn budget. When set, overrides each scenario's max_turns.|
|» name|body|string|false|Optional run name.|
|» scenario_set_uuid|body|string|false|UUID of the existing scenario set to execute. The set must be ready.|
|» user_simulator_config|body|object|false|Optional user simulator model settings such as temperature and max_tokens.|
|» user_simulator_model_uuid|body|string|false|Optional model override for the user simulator. Platform default when unset.|

## Update Simulation Run

<a id="opIdgenai_update_simulation_run"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/gen-ai/simulation_runs/%22123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000%22 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  -d '{
    "name": "example name",
    "run_uuid": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/gen-ai/simulation_runs/{run_uuid}`

To update a simulation run's display name, send a PUT request to `/v2/gen-ai/simulation_runs/{run_uuid}`. Only the name is mutable; run configuration and results are immutable.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "example name",
  "run_uuid": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|run_uuid|path|string|true|UUID of the simulation run to update. Returned by `CreateSimulationRun`<br>and listed via `ListSimulationRuns`.|
|body|body|[apiUpdateSimulationRunInputPublic](#schemaapiupdatesimulationruninputpublic)|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The new name of the run.|
|» run_uuid|body|string|false|UUID of the run to update.|

## Delete Simulation Run

<a id="opIdgenai_delete_simulation_run"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/gen-ai/simulation_runs/%22123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000%22 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/gen-ai/simulation_runs/{run_uuid}`

To delete a simulation run, send a DELETE request to `/v2/gen-ai/simulation_runs/{run_uuid}`. The run must be in a terminal status (`SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_SUCCEEDED`, `SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_PARTIALLY_SUCCESSFUL`, `SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_FAILED`, or `SIMULATION_RUN_STATUS_CANCELLED`). For runs still in progress, cancel the run first, then retry the delete.

<h3 id="delete-simulation-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|run_uuid|path|string|true|UUID of the simulation run to delete. The run must be in a terminal<br>status. For runs still in progress, cancel the run first, then retry<br>the delete.|

## List Simulation Episodes

<a id="opIdgenai_list_simulation_episodes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/gen-ai/simulation_runs/%22123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000%22/episodes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/gen-ai/simulation_runs/{run_uuid}/episodes`

To list the episodes within a simulation run, send a GET request to `/v2/gen-ai/simulation_runs/{run_uuid}/episodes`.

<h3 id="list-simulation-episodes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|run_uuid|path|string|true|UUID of the run whose episodes to list.|
|scenario_uuid|query|string|false|Optional filter by scenario.|
|page|query|integer|false|Page number.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Items per page.|
|statuses|query|[string]|false|Filter by one or more statuses. Empty means no status filter.<br><br> - SIMULATION_EPISODE_STATUS_RUNNING: The episode is executing and a trajectory is available to retrieve.<br> - SIMULATION_EPISODE_STATUS_FINISHED: The episode reached a stop condition and produced a verdict.<br> - SIMULATION_EPISODE_STATUS_FAILED: The episode failed because of a cancel, timeout, or error.<br> - SIMULATION_EPISODE_STATUS_PREPARING: The episode is allocated but its trajectory is not available yet.|
|verdicts|query|[string]|false|Filter by one or more verdicts. Empty means no verdict filter.<br><br> - SIMULATION_EPISODE_VERDICT_SUCCESS: The candidate agent satisfied the scenario's stopping criteria.<br> - SIMULATION_EPISODE_VERDICT_FAILURE: The candidate agent did not satisfy the stopping criteria.<br> - SIMULATION_EPISODE_VERDICT_INCONCLUSIVE: No conclusive verdict (e.g. max_turns reached without the judge finishing).|
|search|query|string|false|Free-text search across scenario_uuid and session_id<br>(case-insensitive substring match). Empty means no search.|
|sort_by|query|string|false|Field to sort by. Defaults to scenario ordering when unspecified.<br><br> - SIMULATION_EPISODE_SORT_FIELD_SCENARIO: Sort by scenario_uuid then episode_index. Default.<br> - SIMULATION_EPISODE_SORT_FIELD_CREATED_AT: Sort by creation date.<br> - SIMULATION_EPISODE_SORT_FIELD_STATUS: Sort by episode status using lifecycle order.<br> - SIMULATION_EPISODE_SORT_FIELD_VERDICT: Sort by verdict (nulls last).|
|sort_direction|query|string|false|Sort direction. Defaults to ascending when unspecified.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|statuses|SIMULATION_EPISODE_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED|
|statuses|SIMULATION_EPISODE_STATUS_RUNNING|
|statuses|SIMULATION_EPISODE_STATUS_FINISHED|
|statuses|SIMULATION_EPISODE_STATUS_FAILED|
|statuses|SIMULATION_EPISODE_STATUS_PREPARING|
|verdicts|SIMULATION_EPISODE_VERDICT_UNSPECIFIED|
|verdicts|SIMULATION_EPISODE_VERDICT_SUCCESS|
|verdicts|SIMULATION_EPISODE_VERDICT_FAILURE|
|verdicts|SIMULATION_EPISODE_VERDICT_INCONCLUSIVE|
|sort_by|SIMULATION_EPISODE_SORT_FIELD_UNSPECIFIED|
|sort_by|SIMULATION_EPISODE_SORT_FIELD_SCENARIO|
|sort_by|SIMULATION_EPISODE_SORT_FIELD_CREATED_AT|
|sort_by|SIMULATION_EPISODE_SORT_FIELD_STATUS|
|sort_by|SIMULATION_EPISODE_SORT_FIELD_VERDICT|
|sort_direction|SORT_DIRECTION_UNSPECIFIED|
|sort_direction|SORT_DIRECTION_ASC|
|sort_direction|SORT_DIRECTION_DESC|

## Create a Workspace

<a id="opIdgenai_create_workspace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/gen-ai/workspaces \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "agent_uuids": [
      "example string"
    ],
    "description": "example string",
    "name": "example name"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/gen-ai/workspaces`

To create a new workspace, send a POST request to `/v2/gen-ai/workspaces`. The response body contains a JSON object with the newly created workspace object.

> Body parameter

```json
{

    "example string"
  ],
  "description": "example string",
  "name": "example name"
}
```

## Move Agents to a Workspace

<a id="opIdgenai_update_agents_workspace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/gen-ai/workspaces/%22123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000%22/agents \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "agent_uuids": [
      "example string"
    ],
    "workspace_uuid": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/gen-ai/workspaces/{workspace_uuid}/agents`

To move all listed agents a given workspace, send a PUT request to `/v2/gen-ai/workspaces/{workspace_uuid}/agents`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "agent_uuids": [
    "example string"
  ],
  "workspace_uuid": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"
}
```

<h3 id="move-agents-to-a-workspace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workspace_uuid|path|string|true|Workspace uuid to move agents to|
|body|body|[apiMoveAgentsToWorkspaceInputPublic](#schemaapimoveagentstoworkspaceinputpublic)|false|none|
|» agent_uuids|body|[string]|false|Agent uuids|
|» workspace_uuid|body|string|false|Workspace uuid to move agents to|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-harness-runtime">Harness Runtime</h1>

DigitalOcean Harness Runtime API under `/v2/agents`. An environment is a
reusable configuration that defines what an agent needs to do work; starting
a session from an environment provisions an isolated sandbox. Define an
environment with a YAML environment spec, or save it as an Environment Config
and create sessions from `{name, config_id}`.

Environment Configs (`/v2/agents/configs`) are immutable team-scoped
configurations. Soft-delete releases the active name while keeping
`config_id` resolvable for existing sessions; clone copies a sanitized
environment under a new name (credentials are never copied).

Checkpoints capture live sandbox machine state for fork and in-place
rollback. Templates (`/v2/agents/templates`) manage team custom sandbox
templates and their build history.

Triggers (`/v2/agents/triggers`) fire an agent run on a webhook delivery or
cron schedule, each firing recorded as an execution. The session event feed
(`GET /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/events`) is a Server-Sent Events
stream, and port-forward (`GET /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/port-forward/{port}`)
opens a WebSocket tunnel to a guest port.

## List active Environment Configs for the caller's team.

<a id="opIdharness_list_configs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/configs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/agents/configs`

Returns lightweight team-scoped config metadata without loading or returning environment-spec JSON. Soft-deleted configs are excluded.

|page_token|query|string|false|Opaque keyset cursor returned by the previous page.|
|search|query|string|false|Optional case-insensitive substring filter on config name (contains). Empty or omitted returns the unfiltered page. At most 64 characters.|

## Create an Environment Config (environment spec + optional Insights opt-in).

<a id="opIdharness_create_config"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/configs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "support-agent",
    "manifest_yaml": "apiVersion: agents.digitalocean.com/v1alpha1\nkind: Agent\nspec:\n  runtime:\n    adapter: opencode\n",
    "insights": {
      "metrics": true,
      "logs": true,
      "traces": true
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v2/agents/configs`

Accepts name, environment-spec YAML text, and optional Insights telemetry opt-in. Tenant secrets are declared inside the environment spec (write-only values), not as sibling request fields. Responses never echo secret values; GET/create may include credential slot metadata (name/source/provider only). Configs are immutable after create.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "support-agent",
  "manifest_yaml": "apiVersion: agents.digitalocean.com/v1alpha1\nkind: Agent\nspec:\n  runtime:\n    adapter: opencode\n",
  "insights": {
    "metrics": true,
    "logs": true,
    "traces": true
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-environment-config-environment-spec-optional-insights-opt-in-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[agent_config_create_request](#schemaagent_config_create_request)|true|Environment Config create body. Secret values live in the environment-spec YAML and are never returned.|
|» name|body|string|true|Config name, case-insensitively unique among the team's active configs.|
|» manifest_yaml|body|string|true|Customer environment-spec YAML text. The HTTP JSON body is capped at 1 MiB and this field is capped at 512 KiB.|
|» insights|body|object|false|none|
|» » metrics|body|boolean \| null|false|Accepted and stored for parity with the Insights schema, but metrics are always collected: unregistered metrics are dropped at ingest rather than opted out of here.|
|» » logs|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether the agent's logs are sent to Insights.|
|» » traces|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether the agent's traces are sent to Insights.|

## Get an active Environment Config and its environment spec.

<a id="opIdharness_get_config"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/configs/019fb39c-14d9-7080-933e-b9b90e25acda \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/agents/configs/{config_id}`

Returns one team-scoped Environment Config including the sanitized environment spec and redacted credential slot metadata. Secret values are never returned.

## Soft-delete an Environment Config.

<a id="opIdharness_delete_config"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/configs/019fb39c-14d9-7080-933e-b9b90e25acda \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/agents/configs/{config_id}`

Releases the active team-scoped name; the config row is retained (soft delete), so sessions created from it keep a resolvable config_id.

## Clone an Environment Config under a new name.

<a id="opIdharness_create_config_clone"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/configs/019fb39c-14d9-7080-933e-b9b90e25acda/clone \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "secrets": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "oauth_assignments": {
      "property1": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "property2": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v2/agents/configs/{config_id}/clone`

Copies the source config's sanitized manifest to a new UUID. Source and clone are independent (no lineage). Credential bindings are never copied: if the manifest declares secret slots, supply secrets/oauth_assignments again (write-only). content_hash matches the source when the manifest is unchanged.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "secrets": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "oauth_assignments": {
    "property1": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "property2": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="clone-an-environment-config-under-a-new-name-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|config_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The Environment Config UUID.|
|body|body|[agent_config_clone_request](#schemaagent_config_clone_request)|true|Clone body with required new name plus write-only credentials for any declared slots.|
|» name|body|string|true|New config name, unique among the team's active configs.|
|» secrets|body|object|false|Write-only map from tenantSecret logical slot to plaintext. Required when the source declares those slots; never copied from the source.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» oauth_assignments|body|object|false|Write-only map from oauth logical slot to an OAuth assignment UUID. Required when the source declares those slots; never copied from the source.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string(uuid)|false|none|

## List the sessions created from one Environment Config.

<a id="opIdharness_list_config_sessions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/configs/019fb39c-14d9-7080-933e-b9b90e25acda/sessions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/agents/configs/{config_id}/sessions`

Enumerates the caller's team sessions whose session was created from this durable Environment Config. Keyset-paginated on an opaque cursor, newest first, same shape and status semantics as GET /v2/agents/sessions.

<h3 id="list-the-sessions-created-from-one-environment-config-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|config_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The Environment Config UUID.|
|page_size|query|integer(int32)|false|Page size. Defaults to 50 when omitted or non-positive; values above 200 are clamped to 200.|
|page_token|query|string|false|Opaque keyset cursor returned by the previous page. Empty starts from the beginning.|
|status|query|string|false|Optional filter on session status. Empty / SESSION_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED still hides destroyed and failed sessions by default; SESSION_STATUS_ALL opts out and returns every session regardless of status.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_PROVISIONING|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_READY|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_DETACHED|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_DESTROYING|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_DESTROYED|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_FAILED|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_PAUSED|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_ALL|

## ListSessions enumerates sessions for the caller's tenant.

<a id="opIdharness_list_sessions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/agents/sessions`

Keyset-paginated on an opaque cursor. Results are scoped to the authenticated team. Destroyed and failed sessions are omitted by default (matching the Cloud Console); pass `status=SESSION_STATUS_ALL` to list every session regardless of status, or an explicit status such as `status=SESSION_STATUS_FAILED` or `status=SESSION_STATUS_DESTROYED` to list only those.

<h3 id="listsessions-enumerates-sessions-for-the-callers-tenant-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page_size|query|integer(int32)|false|Page size. Defaults to 50 when omitted or non-positive; values above 200 are clamped to 200 (not rejected).|
|page_token|query|string|false|Opaque keyset cursor returned by the previous page. Empty starts from the beginning.|
|status|query|[session_status](#schemasession_status)|false|Optional filter on session status. Empty / SESSION_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED means no explicit filter, which still hides destroyed and failed sessions by default; SESSION_STATUS_ALL opts out and returns every session regardless of status (no session is ever actually in this status; it only means something as a filter value here); any other explicit status overrides the default.|
|name|query|string|false|Optional exact-name filter (case-insensitive). Returns the single live (non-terminal) session that currently holds this name for the caller's team, or an empty list if none does. Matches the live holder only, so historical terminal rows and reused names never make it ambiguous (per-team live-name uniqueness bounds it to at most one). This is how clients (doctl / Console) resolve a session name to its id; the {session_id} path stays UUID-only.|
|search|query|string|false|Optional case-insensitive substring filter on session name (contains), for callers that don't know the exact name (e.g. a UI search box). Unlike `name`, this may return zero, one, or many sessions, including terminal ones. Independent of `name`; at most 64 characters.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_PROVISIONING|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_READY|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_DETACHED|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_DESTROYING|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_DESTROYED|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_FAILED|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_PAUSED|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_ALL|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_LOCKED|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "sessions": [
    {
      "session_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
      "name": "demo-agent",
      "parent_session_id": "example",
      "fork_id": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
```

## CreateSession provisions a sandbox and starts a Harness Runtime session.

<a id="opIdharness_create_session"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "demo-agent",
    "config_id": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
    "resume_on_topoff": false
  }'
```

`POST /v2/agents/sessions`

Returns once the session row is allocated. Sandbox boot completes asynchronously.

Two mutually exclusive request forms are selected by Content-Type (same contract as
harness-api `harness.swagger.json`):
- YAML (`application/x-yaml`, `application/yaml`, `text/yaml`, `text/x-yaml`): the environment
  spec. Two environment-spec formats are accepted during the dual-format transition: the flat
  format (primary) and the legacy `agents.digitalocean.com/v1alpha1` envelope (deprecated). A
  top-level `apiVersion` key selects the legacy parser; its absence selects flat. Internally
  persists a durable Environment Config, then creates the session.
- JSON (`application/json`): `{name, config_id}` loads the config, resolves its credentials from
  Secrets Manager at the version pinned when the config was created, and creates the session.

The OpenAPI `requestBody` schemas the JSON form for client generation (Autorest cannot emit a
multi–content-type body). The live API still accepts the YAML forms listed above.

Successful responses may include `config_id` on the session. `X-Device-UUID` (if present) is
persisted on the session row. Query parameters `openai_session_id` and `resume_on_topoff` apply to
both forms; when both the JSON body field and `?resume_on_topoff=` are present, the query
parameter wins.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "demo-agent",
  "config_id": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
  "resume_on_topoff": false
}
```

<h3 id="createsession-provisions-a-sandbox-and-starts-a-harness-runtime-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Device-UUID|header|string|false|Optional hardware device id forwarded by doctl. Persisted on the session row for lifecycle attribution. Values over 128 bytes are ignored.|
|openai_session_id|query|string|false|OpenAI Agents API session id (sess_…) for adapter: codex-agentapi. doctl creates the OpenAI session before calling DO and passes the resulting id here; harness-api persists it for correlation. Empty/omitted for every other agent kind.|
|resume_on_topoff|query|boolean|false|Opt the new session in to automatic resumption when the team's prepayment balance is restored. Defaults to false. Exists as a query parameter so the environment spec (YAML body) form can carry it too. On the application/json form the body field is idiomatic, but this parameter wins when both are present. Must be exactly one of true/false/1/0; anything else is a 400.|
|body|body|[create_session_config_request](#schemacreate_session_config_request)|true|CreateSessionConfigRequest with `application/json`. The live API also accepts a raw environment<br>spec under YAML Content-Types (see operation description); those forms are omitted from `content`<br>so generated clients (pydo/autorest) can emit this operation.|
|» name|body|string|true|Session name, independent of the config name. Must satisfy the existing environment-spec metadata.name rules and must not be UUID-shaped.|
|» config_id|body|string(uuid)|true|none|
|» resume_on_topoff|body|boolean|false|Opt the new session in to automatic resumption when the team's prepayment balance is restored. Defaults to false. Session-scoped, not config-scoped: the referenced config never confers this, so one shared config cannot enrol every session created from it. Omit to leave the default (or to let the ?resume_on_topoff= query parameter supply it).|

## ValidatePolicy checks a manifest's tool-permission policy against the agent's capabilities without creating a session.

<a id="opIdharness_validate_session_policy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/policy/validate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-yaml' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{"apiVersion":"agents.digitalocean.com/v1alpha1","kind":"Agent","metadata":{"name":"example","description":"Use when ...","labels":{}},"spec":{"permissions":{"defaultAction":"allow","rules":[{"tool":"example","match":{"property1":"string","property2":"string"},"action":"allow","enforcement":"strict"}],"filesystem":{"mode":"read-only","allowWrite":["example"]},"network":{"default":"allow","allow":["example"]}},"mode":"interactive","runtime":{"adapter":"claude-code","custom":{"image":"example.registry/image@sha256:abc","entrypoint":["example"]},"config":{}},"workspace":{"repos":["example"]},"sandbox":{"template":"example","persistentWorkspace":true,"idleTimeoutSeconds":1,"maxLifetimeSeconds":1,"sizeSlug":"example","mounts":[{"type":"s3fuse","path":"/mnt/data","bucket":"my-bucket","endpoint":"https://nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com","readOnly":true,"accessKeyRef":"my-secret","secretKeyRef":"my-secret"}],"egress":{"allow":[{"host":"api.example.com"}],"allowIps":["example"],"vpcUuid":"example","subnetUuid":"example","unrestricted":true}},"model":{"default":"example","routing":"example","profile":"example"},"tools":{"mcpServers":[{"ref":"do.actions","name":"example","url":"https://example.com","tools":["example"],"preloadTools":["example"],"auth":{"header":"Authorization","secretRef":"my-secret"}}],"bundle":"default"},"skills":[{"name":"example","description":"Use when ...","instructions":"Use when diagnosing errors.","license":"Apache-2.0","metadata":{},"allowedTools":["example"]}],"env":{},"memory":{"backend":"example","scope":"tenant"},"secrets":[{"name":"example","source":"oauth","provider":"openai","ref":"do.actions","value":"sk-example","env":true}],"defaults":{"budget":{"maxCostUSD":1,"maxSteps":1,"maxWallClockSeconds":1,"onBreach":"pause"}},"serving":{"minReplicas":1,"maxReplicas":1,"targetConcurrency":1,"scaleToZero":{"idleSeconds":1}}}}'
```

`POST /v2/agents/sessions/policy/validate`

Stateless preflight: parses the same environment spec as CreateSession and runs the identical resolve + validate pipeline against the capability descriptor stamped on the selected template's image (resolved per-request via the sandbox, not a separate registry). Returns per-rule verdicts. Nothing is provisioned or persisted.

Each rule is validated against the descriptor for the (agent, version) the template resolves to and gets a verdict: `exact`, `degraded`, `unsupported`, or `unverified`. `ok` is false when any strict rule is unsupported or unverified — i.e. CreateSession would reject the policy for that agent. An empty `spec.permissions` returns `ok: true` with no verdicts. Because it shares the create path's descriptor lookup, the verdicts match what CreateSession would compute.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "apiVersion": "agents.digitalocean.com/v1alpha1",
  "kind": "Agent",
  "metadata": {
    "name": "example",
    "description": "Use when ...",
    "labels": {}
  },
  "spec": {
    "permissions": {
      "defaultAction": "allow",
      "rules": [
        {
          "tool": "example",
          "match": {
            "property1": "string",
            "property2": "string"
          },
          "action": "allow",
          "enforcement": "strict"
        }
      ],
      "filesystem": {
        "mode": "read-only",
        "allowWrite": [
          "example"
        ]
      },
      "network": {
        "default": "allow",
        "allow": [
          "example"
        ]
      }
    },
    "mode": "interactive",
    "runtime": {
      "adapter": "claude-code",
      "custom": {
        "image": "example.registry/image@sha256:abc",
        "entrypoint": [
          "example"
        ]
      },
      "config": {}
    },
    "workspace": {
      "repos": [
        "example"
      ]
    },
    "sandbox": {
      "template": "example",
      "persistentWorkspace": true,
      "idleTimeoutSeconds": 1,
      "maxLifetimeSeconds": 1,
      "sizeSlug": "example",
      "mounts": [
        {
          "type": "s3fuse",
          "path": "/mnt/data",
          "bucket": "my-bucket",
          "endpoint": "https://nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com",
          "readOnly": true,
          "accessKeyRef": "my-secret",
          "secretKeyRef": "my-secret"
        }
      ],
      "egress": {
        "allow": [
          {
            "host": "api.example.com"
          }
        ],
        "allowIps": [
          "example"
        ],
        "vpcUuid": "example",
        "subnetUuid": "example",
        "unrestricted": true
      }
    },
    "model": {
      "default": "example",
      "routing": "example",
      "profile": "example"
    },
    "tools": {
      "mcpServers": [
        {
          "ref": "do.actions",
          "name": "example",
          "url": "https://example.com",
          "tools": [
            "example"
          ],
          "preloadTools": [
            "example"
          ],
          "auth": {
            "header": "Authorization",
            "secretRef": "my-secret"
          }
        }
      ],
      "bundle": "default"
    },
    "skills": [
      {
        "name": "example",
        "description": "Use when ...",
        "instructions": "Use when diagnosing errors.",
        "license": "Apache-2.0",
        "metadata": {},
        "allowedTools": [
          "example"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "env": {},
    "memory": {
      "backend": "example",
      "scope": "tenant"
    },
    "secrets": [
      {
        "name": "example",
        "source": "oauth",
        "provider": "openai",
        "ref": "do.actions",
        "value": "sk-example",
        "env": true
      }
    ],
    "defaults": {
      "budget": {
        "maxCostUSD": 1,
        "maxSteps": 1,
        "maxWallClockSeconds": 1,
        "onBreach": "pause"
      }
    },
    "serving": {
      "minReplicas": 1,
      "maxReplicas": 1,
      "targetConcurrency": 1,
      "scaleToZero": {
        "idleSeconds": 1
      }
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="validatepolicy-checks-a-manifests-tool-permission-policy-against-the-agents-capabilities-without-creating-a-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[agent_manifest](#schemaagent_manifest)|true|The same environment spec you would submit to CreateSession (YAML). Only agent/template selection<br>and the permissions block are used. The live API also accepts `application/yaml`, `text/yaml`, and<br>`text/x-yaml`; OpenAPI `content` lists a single media type so generated clients can emit this<br>operation.|
|» apiVersion|body|string|false|Legacy envelope only - must be "agents.digitalocean.com/v1alpha1", and its presence is what routes the document to the deprecated legacy parser. Flat-format manifests carry no version key (the endpoint owns the contract); required, with kind and spec, when authoring the legacy format.|
|» kind|body|string|false|Must be "Agent".|
|» metadata|body|object|false|none|
|» » name|body|string|false|Optional team-unique session name: 1-64 chars of letters, digits, '-', '.', '_', starting and ending alphanumeric; case-insensitive; must not be UUID-shaped. Omit to have the control plane generate one ("session-<agent-type>-<date-time>"). Unique among the team's ACTIVE (non-terminal) sessions; destroying a session frees its name for reuse.|
|» » description|body|string|false|Free-form description (max 1024 chars), stored and echoed back for Console / catalog surfaces.|
|» » labels|body|object|false|none|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» spec|body|object|false|none|
|» » permissions|body|[permissions](#schemapermissions)|false|Customer-declared tool-execution permission policy (spec.permissions). REQUEST only: the policy engine resolves it (∩ tenant ∩ platform) into the canonical policy and validates it against the (agent, version) capability descriptor. Absent or empty means the agent keeps its built-in default gating — no policy is shipped to the sandbox.|
|» » mode|body|string|false|Explicit lifecycle discriminator. Defaults to "interactive" (spec.serving forbidden); "served" requires spec.serving.|
|» » runtime|body|object|true|Canonical adapter ids: claude-code \| opencode \| codex \| cursor \| hermes \| codex-agentapi \| custom. codex-agentapi is the OpenAI sandbox-provider runtime (DO runs codex exec-server; the agent loop lives at OpenAI) and pairs with the opaque spec.runtime.config block. codex-cli and cursor-cli are deprecated aliases (accepted with a create-time warning). The framework adapters (openai-agents, claude-agent-sdk, crewai, langgraph) are declared but not yet supported; CreateSession rejects them. adapter: custom requires the custom block.|
|» » » adapter|body|string|true|none|
|» » » custom|body|object|false|BYO container; requires adapter: custom. image is required and should be digest-pinned.|
|» » » » image|body|string|true|none|
|» » » » entrypoint|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » » config|body|object|false|OPAQUE, provider-specific runtime config. Only for adapter: codex-agentapi today, where it is the OpenAI Agents API create-session body (agent/environment/input) that doctl forwards verbatim to OpenAI's POST /v1/agents/sessions; harness-api stores and echoes it but never parses or validates its contents (so DO stays forward-compatible as OpenAI's schema evolves). The OpenAI session_id is passed on the create call (the openai_session_id query parameter), not in this block.|
|» » workspace|body|object|false|Repositories the session works against.|
|» » » repos|body|[string]|false|GitHub OWNER/REPO entries, unique. The first entry becomes the session's repo_hint; the full list is the forward shape for multi-repo sessions.|
|» » sandbox|body|object|false|none|
|» » » template|body|string|false|Optional sandbox template. Empty (or the legacy placeholder "coding") means "no preference": the template derives from the adapter.|

Absent or empty means no destination ACL (same as unrestricted). Flat authors prefer egress: unrestricted (scalar), a bare host list, or an object with allow_hosts / allow_ips / vpc_uuid / subnet_uuid. Platform host defaults are unioned only when allow names something; allowIps does not trigger that union (IP-only turns the destination ACL on without domain rules). VPC attachment is create-time immutable; ownership is verified at session create. Allowlists are a request only: the server intersects them with tenant + platform policy and can only narrow them.|

|» » » » url|body|string|false|Inline server endpoint; https:// only.|
|» » » » tools|body|[string]|false|Optional selection allowlist; omitted means all tools the server advertises. Each entry is an individual tool name with an optional integer version pin (e.g. web_search, execute_code@3) or a toolbelt reference - a server-defined named tool group written toolbelt:<name>[@<int>] (e.g. toolbelt:read-only@1; catalog refs only). Versions are integer pins (no semver). The server owns belt expansion; a pinned tool or belt attaches exactly that version, an unpinned one resolves at session create and is frozen for the session (no floating latest). Entries non-empty, unique per server. The selection bounds the session and is never preloaded into the session MCP tools/list; see preloadTools.|
|» » » » preloadTools|body|[string]|false|Catalog form only. Each entry must appear in tools when tools is set; toolbelt references are rejected. Every preloaded schema is in the model's context on every turn, so keep this to a handful of tools. Omitted means nothing is preloaded.|

## ListSandboxSizes returns the customer-selectable sandbox (microVM) size catalog.

<a id="opIdharness_list_session_sandbox_sizes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/sandbox/sizes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/agents/sessions/sandbox/sizes`

Read-only catalog the UI (and other clients) render as the size picker, instead of hardcoding the list. The set is the single source of truth shared with create-time validation and the default-size fallback, so every `slug` returned here is accepted by CreateSession as spec.sandbox.sizeSlug. Sizes are returned smallest-to-largest. Static and safe to cache; independent of team/session; no pagination.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "sizes": [
    {
      "slug": "mars-2vcpu-4gb",
      "vcpus": 2,
      "memory_mb": 4096,
      "price_per_hour_usd": 0.00003,
      "price_per_month_usd": 93.744
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json

}
```

## DestroySession tears down the sandbox and marks the session DESTROYED.

<a id="opIdharness_delete_session"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}`

Persistent workspace contents are retained per tenant policy. Returns 204 No Content on success.

## PatchSession updates session-scoped settings on an existing session.

<a id="opIdharness_update_session"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "resume_on_topoff": false
  }'
```

`PATCH /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}`

Partial update of session-scoped settings (not the agent manifest / config). The body must include at least one recognized patchable property; an empty object {} is 400. Only properties listed on PatchSessionRequest are accepted — any other top-level JSON key is rejected with 400. Omitted properties are left unchanged. Today the only patchable field is resume_on_topoff; more session settings may be added over time. Terminal sessions (DESTROYED, FAILED) cannot be patched.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "resume_on_topoff": false
}
```

<h3 id="patchsession-updates-session-scoped-settings-on-an-existing-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session_id|path|string|true|The session UUID.|
|body|body|[patch_session_request](#schemapatch_session_request)|true|PATCH body: allowlisted session-scoped settings. At least one property required.|
|» resume_on_topoff|body|boolean|false|When present, sets whether this session opts in to automatic resumption when the team's prepayment balance is restored after a low-balance pause. Session-scoped consent, not config-scoped. Omitted properties are not modified.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "session": {
    "session_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
    "name": "demo-agent",
    "parent_session_id": "example",
    "fork_id": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
    "fork_from_checkpoint_id": "example",
    "agent_kind": "AGENT_KIND_UNSPECIFIED",
    "status": "SESSION_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED",
    "sandbox_id": "example",
    "created_at": "2026-08-01T12:00:00Z",
    "last_event_at": "2026-08-01T12:00:00Z",
    "keep_warm": false,
    "resume_on_topoff": false,
    "pause_reason": "example",
    "idle_timeout_seconds": 60,
    "repo_hint": "example",
    "warnings": [],
    "config_id": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
    "openai_session_id": "example",
    "openai_environment_id": "example"
  }
}
```

## CreateCheckpoint captures the session's live sandbox state as a durable checkpoint.

<a id="opIdharness_create_session_checkpoint"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/checkpoints \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "label": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/checkpoints`

Synchronous: blocks until the capture reaches READY and returns the terminal Checkpoint — clients never see PENDING on this endpoint and need no poll loop. The checkpoint binds the machine-state capture to the event-log cursor at the cut, so it can later seed forks (POST .../fork) and rollback. Checkpoints are taken between turns; a session with an active turn in flight returns 409.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "label": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="createcheckpoint-captures-the-sessions-live-sandbox-state-as-a-durable-checkpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session_id|path|string|true|The session UUID.|
|body|body|[create_checkpoint_request](#schemacreate_checkpoint_request)|false|Optional; an empty or omitted body creates an unlabeled checkpoint.|
|» label|body|string|false|Optional human-readable label stored on the checkpoint; "" if omitted.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "checkpoint": {
    "checkpoint_id": "cp_9f2c1a4b",
    "session_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
    "status": "READY",
    "kind": "explicit",
    "label": "before-refactor",
    "event_id": "01JABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTVWXYZ",
    "size_bytes": 1048576,
    "created_at": "2026-08-01T12:00:00Z",
    "error_message": "capture timed out"
  }
}
```

## DeleteCheckpoint removes a checkpoint and its underlying machine-state capture.

```bash

  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/checkpoints/{checkpoint_id}`

## RollbackToCheckpoint rewinds a session to a checkpoint.

<a id="opIdharness_revert_session_checkpoint"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/checkpoints/cp_9f2c1a4b/rollback \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/checkpoints/{checkpoint_id}/rollback`

In-place restore: boots a fresh sandbox from the checkpoint and atomically swaps the session's sandbox pointer to it, so the session keeps its same session_id; the old sandbox is then torn down.

<h3 id="rollbacktocheckpoint-rewinds-a-session-to-a-checkpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session_id|path|string|true|The session UUID.|
|checkpoint_id|path|string|true|The checkpoint id.|

> Example responses


## ForkSession creates child sessions from a checkpoint of this session.

<a id="opIdharness_create_session_fork"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/fork \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "from_checkpoint_id": "string",
    "count": 1
  }'
```

`POST /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/fork`

Each child boots a fresh sandbox from the checkpoint's machine-state capture and is drivable exactly like any other session (input, HITL), with parent_session_id and fork_id set for lineage. When from_checkpoint_id is omitted, an implicit checkpoint of the session "now" is captured first and the children fork from that. All-or-nothing: on failure nothing is left running.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "from_checkpoint_id": "string",
  "count": 1
}
```

<h3 id="forksession-creates-child-sessions-from-a-checkpoint-of-this-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session_id|path|string|true|The session UUID.|
|body|body|[fork_session_request](#schemafork_session_request)|false|Optional; an empty or omitted body forks a single child from an implicit checkpoint of "now".|
|» from_checkpoint_id|body|string|false|Checkpoint to fork from; must be READY. Omitted/empty means capture an implicit checkpoint of the session "now" first and fork from that.|
|» count|body|integer(int32)|false|Number of child sessions to create, 1-4. Defaults to 1 when omitted; a value outside 1-4 is rejected with 400.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "sessions": [
    {
      "session_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
      "name": "demo-agent",
      "parent_session_id": "example",
      "fork_id": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
      "fork_from_checkpoint_id": "example",
      "agent_kind": "AGENT_KIND_UNSPECIFIED",
      "status": "SESSION_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED",
      "sandbox_id": "example",
      "created_at": "2026-08-01T12:00:00Z",
      "last_event_at": "2026-08-01T12:00:00Z",

      "resume_on_topoff": false,
      "pause_reason": "example",
      "idle_timeout_seconds": 60,
      "repo_hint": "example",
      "warnings": [],
      "config_id": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
      "openai_session_id": "example",
      "openai_environment_id": "example"
    }
  ]
}
```

## ResolveHITL records the user's decision on a pending HITL request.

<a id="opIdharness_post_session_hitl"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/hitl/hitl_example \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "outcome": "HITL_OUTCOME_UNSPECIFIED",
    "reason": "example",
    "source": "RESOLUTION_SOURCE_UNSPECIFIED"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/hitl/{request_id}`

harness-api forwards the decision into the owning microVM via the inbound runtime.v1.OHR.ResolveHITL RPC (dialed through the guest-fronting proxy), which unblocks the gated agent action. The resolution is also echoed to all attached clients as a HITLResolved event on StreamSession. Returns 204 No Content on success.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "outcome": "HITL_OUTCOME_UNSPECIFIED",
  "reason": "example",
  "source": "RESOLUTION_SOURCE_UNSPECIFIED"
}
```

<h3 id="resolvehitl-records-the-users-decision-on-a-pending-hitl-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session_id|path|string|true|The session UUID.|
|request_id|path|string|true|The HITL request identifier.|
|X-Device-UUID|header|string|false|Optional hardware device id forwarded by doctl. Recorded on the resulting HITL decision.|
|body|body|[resolve_hitl_request](#schemaresolve_hitl_request)|true|none|
|» outcome|body|[hitl_outcome](#schemahitl_outcome)|true|HITLOutcome is the user's decision on a HITL request. DEFER backs off this attempt without treating it as a rejection.|
|» reason|body|string|false|Optional free-text reason. Captured in the audit trail; not interpreted.|
|» source|body|[resolution_source](#schemaresolution_source)|false|How a HITL resolution was triggered. Defaults to RESOLUTION_SOURCE_OUT_OF_BAND when omitted.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» outcome|HITL_OUTCOME_UNSPECIFIED|
|» outcome|HITL_OUTCOME_APPROVE|
|» outcome|HITL_OUTCOME_REJECT|
|» outcome|HITL_OUTCOME_DEFER|
|» source|RESOLUTION_SOURCE_UNSPECIFIED|
|» source|RESOLUTION_SOURCE_INLINE_KEYSTROKE|
|» source|RESOLUTION_SOURCE_OUT_OF_BAND|

## SendInput delivers a user chat message into the session.

<a id="opIdharness_create_session_input"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/input \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "text": "example"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/input`

The agent observes it on its next turn and emits subsequent events via StreamSession. The input is forwarded to the owning microVM's OHR inbound surface, which attributes it to a run and returns the run id.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "text": "example"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|session_id|path|string|true|The session UUID.|
|body|body|[send_input_request](#schemasend_input_request)|true|none|
|» text|body|string|true|The user message to deliver into the session. Required and non-empty.|

```json
{
  "run_id": "example"
}
```

## PauseSession freezes the session's microVM sandbox.

<a id="opIdharness_post_session_pause"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/pause \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/pause`

Supported on microvm-substrate sessions only; dewdrop/docker sessions return 501 Not Implemented. Paused sessions count against quota. Clients learn state via GetSession/ListSessions; no live session.updated event is emitted.

## ResumeSession explicitly thaws a PAUSED session's microVM sandbox.

<a id="opIdharness_post_session_resume"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/resume \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/resume`

Only valid for microvm-substrate sessions; dewdrop/docker sessions return 501 Not Implemented. Implicit resume also occurs when SendInput or ResolveHITL is called on a paused session. Returns synchronously once the sandbox is ready.

<h3 id="resumesession-explicitly-thaws-a-paused-sessions-microvm-sandbox-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session_id|path|string|true|The session UUID.|
|X-Device-UUID|header|string|false|Optional hardware device id forwarded by doctl. Recorded for audit.|

```json
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

## ExecInSandbox runs a one-shot command inside the session's sandbox.

<a id="opIdharness_post_session_sandbox_exec"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/sandbox/exec \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "argv": [
      "uname",
      "-a"
    ],
    "workdir": "/workspace",
    "stdin": "",
    "timeout_seconds": 60
  }'
```

`POST /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/sandbox/exec`

Runs `argv` directly in the guest (no shell). Stdout/stderr are buffered and capped at 1 MiB each;
truncation is indicated via response headers when present. A non-zero exit code is still HTTP 200.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "argv": [
    "uname",
    "-a"
  ],
  "workdir": "/workspace",
  "stdin": "",
  "timeout_seconds": 60
}
```

<h3 id="execinsandbox-runs-a-one-shot-command-inside-the-sessions-sandbox-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session_id|path|string|true|The session UUID.|
|body|body|[exec_in_sandbox_request](#schemaexec_in_sandbox_request)|true|Command to run inside the sandbox.|
|» argv|body|[string]|true|Program and arguments. Required and non-empty; run directly, with no shell interpretation.|
|» workdir|body|string|false|Working directory inside the sandbox. Empty uses the sandbox default (/workspace); not restricted to the workspace root.|
|» stdin|body|string(byte)|false|Optional base64 stdin payload, delivered in full and then closed so the process sees EOF. One-shot only — there is no streaming stdin on this endpoint.|
|» timeout_seconds|body|integer(int64)|false|Optional timeout. Clamped server-side (default 60, maximum 240) regardless of the value sent.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "exit_code": 0,
  "stdout": "Linux",
  "stderr": "",
  "duration_ms": 12
}
```

```json
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you were accessing could not be found.",
```

## Download a file or tar archive from the session's sandbox workspace.

<a id="opIdharness_get_session_workspace_download"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/workspace/download?path=example' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/workspace/download`

Streams the workspace payload back as `application/octet-stream` using chunked transfer encoding, followed by a fixed integrity footer.

Response body layout: `<payload>` + `<footer>`, where the footer is exactly 73 bytes: `DOWSSHA1` (8 bytes) + 64-char lowercase SHA-256 hex + `\n`. The client MUST strip the trailing 73 bytes before saving, verify SHA-256(payload) equals the footer digest, and treat a tail that does not match this shape (magic + 64 hex + newline) as a failed (truncated/corrupt) transfer.

Other metadata:
- `X-Workspace-Is-Archive: true` when the payload is a tar archive.
- `X-Workspace-Size-Bytes` is a progress hint (not Content-Length) and excludes the footer.
- The `X-Content-Sha256` trailer also carries the digest but is best-effort: edge proxies may strip HTTP trailers, so the body footer is authoritative.

Concurrent transfers (upload + download) are capped server-side; over the cap the request blocks and may return 503.

<h3 id="download-a-file-or-tar-archive-from-the-sessions-sandbox-workspace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session_id|path|string|true|The session UUID.|
|path|query|string|true|Source path inside the sandbox workspace. Relative paths resolve under the workspace root; paths that escape the workspace are rejected. Required.|
|as_archive|query|boolean|false|If true, the guest returns a tar stream of `path` (e.g. for a directory). Defaults to false (single file).|

## Start a staged (large-file) workspace transfer.

<a id="opIdharness_create_session_workspace_transfer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/workspace/transfers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "direction": "upload",
    "path": "example",
    "is_archive": true,
    "as_archive": true,
    "size_bytes": "example",
    "sha256": "example"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/workspace/transfers`

Creates an asynchronous, object-storage-backed transfer for payloads larger than the streaming path supports (> ~50 MiB). Bulk bytes never traverse harness-api: the client PUTs/GETs presigned DO Spaces URLs directly.

Set `direction` to `upload` or `download`.
- `upload`: responds 201 with `transfer_id` + `part_size`; the client then requests per-part presigned PUT URLs, uploads them to Spaces, and calls `commit`.
- `download`: responds 202 with `transfer_id`; the client polls GET until `completed` and then fetches `download_url` from Spaces.

Upload and cancel currently return 501 until the sandbox backend RPCs ship; download is live.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "direction": "upload",
  "path": "example",
  "is_archive": true,
  "as_archive": true,
  "size_bytes": "example",
  "sha256": "example"
}
```

<h3 id="start-a-staged-large-file-workspace-transfer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session_id|path|string|true|The session UUID.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» direction|body|string|true|Transfer direction.|
|» path|body|string|true|Workspace-relative path. Destination for upload, source for download. Paths that escape the workspace root are rejected.|
|» is_archive|body|boolean|false|Upload only. When true, the payload is a tar the guest extracts at `path`.|
|» as_archive|body|boolean|false|Download only. When true, `path` is exported as a tar stream.|
|» size_bytes|body|string(int64)|false|Optional total payload size. Validated against the maximum staged object size (50 GiB); a larger value returns 413.|
|» sha256|body|string|false|Optional lowercase hex SHA-256 of the full payload. If set on an upload, it must match on commit.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» direction|upload|
|» direction|download|

```json
  "expires_at": "2026-07-27T12:00:00Z"
}
```

## Get the status of a staged workspace transfer.

<a id="opIdharness_get_session_workspace_transfer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/workspace/transfers/tr_example \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/workspace/transfers/{transfer_id}`

Returns the current transfer state. For a completed download the response also carries a freshly minted presigned GET `download_url` (its TTL starts at poll time) and the payload `sha256` for client-side verification.

<h3 id="get-the-status-of-a-staged-workspace-transfer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session_id|path|string|true|The session UUID.|
|transfer_id|path|string|true|The workspace transfer identifier.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "transfer_id": "example",
  "direction": "upload",
  "status": "pending",
  "bytes_written": 1,
  "sha256": "example",
  "download_url": "example",
  "expires_at": "2026-07-27T12:00:00Z",
  "error_message": "example"
}
```

## Cancel a staged workspace transfer.

<a id="opIdharness_cancel_session_workspace_transfer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/workspace/transfers/tr_example/cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "reason": "example"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/workspace/transfers/{transfer_id}/cancel`

Aborts an in-flight transfer. Idempotent: cancelling an already-terminal transfer returns `aborted: false` with the current status. The request body is optional.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reason": "example"
}
```

<h3 id="cancel-a-staged-workspace-transfer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session_id|path|string|true|The session UUID.|
|transfer_id|path|string|true|The workspace transfer identifier.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» reason|body|string|false|Optional caller-visible audit/debug context.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "transfer_id": "example",
  "aborted": true,
  "status": "pending"
```

## Finalize a staged upload.

<a id="opIdharness_commit_session_workspace_transfer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/workspace/transfers/tr_example/commit \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "sha256": "example"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/workspace/transfers/{transfer_id}/commit`

Upload only. Call once, after all parts have been uploaded. Completes the multipart upload and starts the asynchronous import into the workspace. Responds 202; poll the transfer until `completed` or `failed`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "sha256": "example"
}
```

<h3 id="finalize-a-staged-upload-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session_id|path|string|true|The session UUID.|
|transfer_id|path|string|true|The workspace transfer identifier.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» sha256|body|string|false|Optional lowercase hex SHA-256. Must match the value supplied at create when both are set.|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "transfer_id": "example",
  "status": "pending",
  "size_bytes": 1
}
```

## Mint presigned PUT URLs for one or more multipart upload parts.

<a id="opIdharness_create_session_workspace_part_upload_urls"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/workspace/transfers/tr_example/part-upload-urls \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "part_numbers": [
      1
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/workspace/transfers/{transfer_id}/part-upload-urls`

Upload only. Pass one or more 1-based `part_numbers`; the response returns a presigned `upload_url` per part (all sharing one `expires_at`), so a client can drive parallel part uploads without a round trip per part. PUT each part's bytes directly to its URL (bypassing harness-api). If URLs expire before the PUT, request them again.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "part_numbers": [
    1
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="mint-presigned-put-urls-for-one-or-more-multipart-upload-parts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session_id|path|string|true|The session UUID.|
|transfer_id|path|string|true|The workspace transfer identifier.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» part_numbers|body|[integer(int32)]|true|1-based part indices to presign (single or batched).|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "transfer_id": "example",
  "part_urls": [
    {
      "part_number": 1,
      "upload_url": "example"
    }
  ],
  "expires_at": "2026-07-27T12:00:00Z"
}
```

## Upload a file or tar archive into the session's sandbox workspace.

<a id="opIdharness_create_session_workspace_upload"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/workspace/upload?path=example' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  --data-binary '@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/workspace/upload`

Streams the raw request body to a path inside the sandbox workspace. Concurrent transfers (upload + download) are capped server-side; over the cap the request blocks and may return 503. The optional `X-Content-Sha256` request header carries a hex digest the guest verifies after the full payload is written.

<h3 id="upload-a-file-or-tar-archive-into-the-sessions-sandbox-workspace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session_id|path|string|true|The session UUID.|
|path|query|string|true|Destination path inside the sandbox workspace. Relative paths resolve under the workspace root; paths that escape the workspace are rejected. Required.|
|is_archive|query|boolean|false|If true, the body is a tar stream that the guest extracts under `path`. Defaults to false (single file).|
|X-Content-Sha256|header|string|false|Optional hex SHA-256 of the full payload. The guest verifies it after writing; a mismatch returns 400.|
|body|body|string(binary)|true|Raw file bytes (or tar stream when is_archive=true). Capped at 500 MiB.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "path": "example",
  "bytes_written": 1
}
```

> 400 Response

```json

  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you were accessing could not be found.",
  "request_id": "4d9d8375-3c56-4925-a3e7-eb137fed17e9"
}
```

## StreamSessionEvents opens the session's Server-Sent Events feed.

<a id="opIdharness_get_session_events"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/events`

Opens a `text/event-stream` of the session's canonical events, served by the MARS data plane (OHP).
Each frame is `event: <type>` plus a `data:` line holding a JSON event envelope; comment lines
(`: keepalive`) arrive about every 15s and must be ignored. Decode every `data:` with one envelope
parser and dispatch on the envelope's `type`. Every stream opens with a `stream.state` control frame
(its `data` is a `stream_state`).

Delivery is at-least-once: clients MUST de-duplicate and order by `event_id` (a ULID), never by
`seq`. The same path serves two modes:
  - live attach (default): recent context, then an open stream that stays live until the client
    disconnects. Pass `Last-Event-ID` (or `cursor`) to resume strictly after the last event the
    client already rendered, suppressing the last-N context floor.
  - finite replay (`replay_only=true`): writes a bounded slice of the stored transcript and closes.
    This is what `doctl agents logs` uses; paginate it with `replay_from`.

OHP serves recent history only (bounded by Kafka retention and an event window); it is not an
archive. OHP's own errors (404/429/500/503) use the DO-standard JSON `{id, message, request_id}`
envelope (cthulhu#179797 / MARSOHS-2065); the 401 comes from the edge.

<h3 id="streamsessionevents-opens-the-sessions-server-sent-events-feed-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session_id|path|string|true|The session UUID.|
|replay_only|query|boolean|false|Write the selected history and then close the stream, rather than going live. Does not advance the device's delivery cursor, so it never supersedes a live attach from the same device.|
|replay_from|query|string|false|Event-id pagination cursor for the `replay_only` lane only; return events after this one. There is no last-N floor, so a cursor already at the head yields nothing. Ignored on a live attach.|
|cursor|query|string|false|Query-param equivalent of `Last-Event-ID`, because a browser EventSource cannot set request headers. Takes precedence over the header when both are present. Live-attach lane only.|
|device_id|query|string|false|Query-param equivalent of `X-Device-UUID`. Identifies one client install so its delivery cursor and live slot are its own; a second attach from the same device supersedes the first.|
|Last-Event-ID|header|string|false|The last event this client rendered (not merely received). Its presence marks the request a reconnect, so OHP serves strictly what follows it with no last-N floor. Persist it only after rendering.|
|X-Device-UUID|header|string|false|A stable per-install device id. See `device_id`.|

```json
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
  "request_id": "4d9d8375-3c56-4925-a3e7-eb137fed17e9"
}
```

## PortForwardSession opens a WebSocket tunnel to a guest TCP port.

<a id="opIdharness_get_session_port_forward"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/port-forward/8000 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/port-forward/{port}`

Upgrades the request to a WebSocket and bridges it to one TCP connection on the session sandbox's
guest `port`. Binary frames carry the opaque byte stream in both directions; the server closes with
a descriptive WebSocket close code when the tunnel ends. This is the raw TCP tunnel; browser clients
reaching the in-guest OpenHands Agent Server use the ingress URL
(`GET /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/ingress`), which has replaced this bridge for them.

WebSocket is not expressible in OpenAPI; this documents the GET that initiates the upgrade handshake
(HTTP 101 Switching Protocols). The handler dials the guest before upgrading, so a PAUSED session is
woken and served rather than rejected. `port` must be between 1024 and 65535. A request without the
WebSocket upgrade headers is answered 400 by the handshake layer.

<h3 id="portforwardsession-opens-a-websocket-tunnel-to-a-guest-tcp-port-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session_id|path|string|true|The session UUID.|
|port|path|integer|true|The guest TCP port to connect to. Must be between 1024 and 65535.|

```json

  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

## GetIngressURL returns the public HTTPS URL of the session's OpenHands Agent Server.

<a id="opIdharness_get_session_ingress"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/sessions/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890/ingress \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id}/ingress`

Publishes the URL on first call and returns it. Idempotent while the session runs: the same URL is
returned until the session is paused, locked or rolled back, after which the next call returns a new
hostname (pause and lock revoke the URL; rollback moves the session to a new sandbox, so re-fetch
after resume, unlock or rollback). The URL fronts guest port 8000 (the OpenHands Agent Server,
HTTP + WebSocket) and replaces the port-forward bridge for browser clients. Requests to the URL carry
the caller's DO token as a Bearer header. Poll until `state` is INGRESS_URL_STATE_READY; there is no
failed state. Only OpenHands sessions support ingress, and it is gated per team.

<h3 id="getingressurl-returns-the-public-https-url-of-the-sessions-openhands-agent-server-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session_id|path|string|true|The session UUID.|

> Example responses

```json

  "ingress_url": {
    "ingress_url_id": "3f2a1b0c-9d8e-7f6a-5b4c-3d2e1f0a9b8c",
    "session_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
    "port": 8000,
    "url": "https://abc123.nyc3.sandbox.ondigitalocean.com",
    "state": "INGRESS_URL_STATE_READY",
    "created_at": "2026-07-27T12:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

## CreateTemplate creates a team custom template and kicks a build.

<a id="opIdharness_create_template"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/templates \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "base_template": "string",
    "source_oci_ref": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/agents/templates`

Creates a team-owned template from a customer OCI ref rebased onto a base template. team_id is stamped from the authenticated principal.

```json
  "base_template": "string",
  "source_oci_ref": "string"
```

|» name|body|string|true|none|
|» base_template|body|string|true|Base template key. One of: coding-base, coding-claude-code, coding-codex, coding-hermes, coding-opencode, langgraph.|
|» source_oci_ref|body|string|true|none|
