## Create a New Certificate

<a id="opIdcertificates_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/certificates \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "web-cert-01",
    "type": "lets_encrypt",
    "dns_names": [
      "www.example.com",
      "example.com"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/certificates`

To upload new SSL certificate which you have previously generated, send a POST
request to `/v2/certificates`.

When uploading a user-generated certificate, the `private_key`,
`leaf_certificate`, and optionally the `certificate_chain` attributes should
be provided. The type must be set to `custom`.

When using Let's Encrypt to create a certificate, the `dns_names` attribute
must be provided, and the type must be set to `lets_encrypt`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "web-cert-01",
  "type": "lets_encrypt",
  "dns_names": [
    "www.example.com",
    "example.com"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-certificate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[certificate_request_lets_encrypt](#schemacertificate_request_lets_encrypt) \| [certificate_request_custom](#schemacertificate_request_custom)|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[certificate_request_lets_encrypt](#schemacertificate_request_lets_encrypt)|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[certificate_request_custom](#schemacertificate_request_custom)|false|none|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "certificate": {
    "id": "892071a0-bb95-49bc-8021-3afd67a210bf",
    "name": "web-cert-01",
    "not_after": "2017-02-22T00:23:00Z",
    "sha1_fingerprint": "dfcc9f57d86bf58e321c2c6c31c7a971be244ac7",
    "created_at": "2017-02-08T16:02:37Z",
    "dns_names": [
      ""
    ],
    "state": "verified",
    "type": "custom"
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

The value of this will be an object that contains the standard attributes associated with a certificate.<br>When using Let's Encrypt, the initial value of the certificate's `state` attribute will be `pending`. When the certificate has been successfully issued by Let's Encrypt, this will transition to `verified` and be ready for use.|Inline|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-container-registry">Container Registry</h1>

DigitalOcean offers the ability for you to create a
[private container registry](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/container-registry/)
to store your Docker images for use with your Kubernetes clusters. This
container registry runs inside the same datacenters as your cluster,
ensuring reliable and performant rollout of image deployments.

You can only create one registry per DigitalOcean account, but you can use
that registry to create as many repositories as you wish.

## Create Container Registry

<a id="opIdregistry_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/registry \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "example",
    "subscription_tier_slug": "basic",
    "region": "fra1"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/registry`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Note: This endpoint is deprecated. Please use the `/v2/registries` endpoint instead.**

To create your container registry, send a POST request to `/v2/registry`.

The `name` becomes part of the URL for images stored in the registry. For
example, if your registry is called `example`, an image in it will have the
URL `registry.digitalocean.com/example/image:tag`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "example",
  "subscription_tier_slug": "basic",
  "region": "fra1"
}
```

<h3 id="create-container-registry-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[registry_create](#schemaregistry_create)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|A globally unique name for the container registry. Must be lowercase and be composed only of numbers, letters and `-`, up to a limit of 63 characters.|
|» subscription_tier_slug|body|string|true|The slug of the subscription tier to sign up for. Valid values can be retrieved using the options endpoint.|
|» region|body|string|false|Slug of the region where registry data is stored. When not provided, a region will be selected.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» subscription_tier_slug|starter|
|» subscription_tier_slug|basic|
|» subscription_tier_slug|professional|
|» region|nyc3|
|» region|sfo3|
|» region|ams3|
|» region|sgp1|
|» region|fra1|

## Get Docker Credentials for Container Registry

<a id="opIdregistry_get_dockerCredentials"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/registry/docker-credentials \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/registry/docker-credentials`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Note: This endpoint is deprecated. Please use the `/v2/registries` endpoint instead.**

In order to access your container registry with the Docker client or from a
Kubernetes cluster, you will need to configure authentication. The necessary
JSON configuration can be retrieved by sending a GET request to
`/v2/registry/docker-credentials`.

The response will be in the format of a Docker `config.json` file. To use the
config in your Kubernetes cluster, create a Secret with:

    kubectl create secret generic docr \
      --from-file=.dockerconfigjson=config.json \
      --type=kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson

By default, the returned credentials have read-only access to your registry
and cannot be used to push images. This is appropriate for most Kubernetes
clusters. To retrieve read/write credentials, suitable for use with the Docker
client or in a CI system, read_write may be provided as query parameter. For
example: `/v2/registry/docker-credentials?read_write=true`

By default, the returned credentials will not expire. To retrieve credentials
with an expiry set, expiry_seconds may be provided as a query parameter. For
example: `/v2/registry/docker-credentials?expiry_seconds=3600` will return
credentials that expire after one hour.


<h3 id="get-docker-credentials-for-container-registry-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expiry_seconds|query|integer|false|The duration in seconds that the returned registry credentials will be valid. If not set or 0, the credentials will not expire.|
|read_write|query|boolean|false|By default, the registry credentials allow for read-only access. Set this query parameter to `true` to obtain read-write credentials.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "auths": {
    "registry.digitalocean.com": {
      "auth": "YjdkMDNhNjk0N2IyMTdlZmI2ZjNlYzNiZDM1MDQ1ODI6YjdkMDNhNjk0N2IyMTdlZmI2ZjNlYzNiZDM1MDQ1ODIK"
    }
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<aside class="warning">

To delete a container repository tag, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/registry/$REGISTRY_NAME/repositories/$REPOSITORY_NAME/tags/$TAG`.

Note that if your repository name contains `/` characters, it must be

`/v2/registry/example/repositories/my%2Frepo/tags/mytag`.

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.
This indicates that the request was processed successfully.

## Start Garbage Collection

<a id="opIdregistry_run_garbageCollection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/registry/example/garbage-collection \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "unreferenced blobs only"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/registry/{registry_name}/garbage-collection`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Note: This endpoint is deprecated. Please use the `/v2/registries` endpoint instead.**

Garbage collection enables users to clear out unreferenced blobs (layer &
manifest data) after deleting one or more manifests from a repository. If
there are no unreferenced blobs resulting from the deletion of one or more
manifests, garbage collection is effectively a noop.
[See here for more information](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/container-registry/how-to/clean-up-container-registry/)
about how and why you should clean up your container registry periodically.

To request a garbage collection run on your registry, send a POST request to
`/v2/registry/$REGISTRY_NAME/garbage-collection`. This will initiate the
following sequence of events on your registry.

* Set the registry to read-only mode, meaning no further write-scoped
  JWTs will be issued to registry clients. Existing write-scoped JWTs will
  continue to work until they expire which can take up to 15 minutes.
* Wait until all existing write-scoped JWTs have expired.
* Scan all registry manifests to determine which blobs are unreferenced.
* Delete all unreferenced blobs from the registry.
* Record the number of blobs deleted and bytes freed, mark the garbage
  collection status as `success`.
* Remove the read-only mode restriction from the registry, meaning write-scoped
  JWTs will once again be issued to registry clients.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "unreferenced blobs only"
}
```

<h3 id="start-garbage-collection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|registry_name|path|string|true|The name of a container registry.|
|body|body|[registry_run_gc](#schemaregistry_run_gc)|false|none|
|» type|body|string|false|Type of the garbage collection to run against this registry|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|untagged manifests only|
|» type|unreferenced blobs only|
|» type|untagged manifests and unreferenced blobs|

## List Registry Options (Subscription Tiers and Available Regions)

<a id="opIdregistry_get_options"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/registry/options \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/registry/options`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Note: This endpoint is deprecated and may be removed in a future version. There is no alternative.****Note: This endpoint is deprecated. Please use the `/v2/registries` endpoint instead.**

This endpoint serves to provide additional information as to which option values
are available when creating a container registry.

There are multiple subscription tiers available for container registry. Each
tier allows a different number of image repositories to be created in your
registry, and has a different amount of storage and transfer included.

There are multiple regions available for container registry and controls
where your data is stored.

To list the available options, send a GET request to
`/v2/registry/options`.


> Example responses

```json
    "available_regions": [
      "nyc3",
      "sfo3",
      "ams3",
      "sgp1",
      "fra1"
    ],

        "name": "Starter",
        "slug": "starter",
        "included_repositories": 1,
        "included_storage_bytes": 524288000,
        "allow_storage_overage": false,
        "included_bandwidth_bytes": 524288000,
        "monthly_price_in_cents": 0,
        "eligible": false,

        "eligible": true
      },
      {
        "name": "Professional",

        "included_storage_bytes": 107374182400,
        "allow_storage_overage": true,
        "included_bandwidth_bytes": 107374182400,
        "monthly_price_in_cents": 2000,
        "eligible": true
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-container-registries">Container Registries</h1>

DigitalOcean now supports up to nine additional registries (for a total maximum of 10) per team
if your container registry uses the Professional subscription plan. The storage is shared among
the registries. This set of new APIs is backward compatible with `/v2/registry`. However, if you
create more than one registry under a Professional plan, some of the `/v2/registry` APIs would not work.
Hence, it is recommended to use `/v2/registries` for multiple registries.

## Create Container Registry

<a id="opIdregistries_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/registries \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "example",
    "subscription_tier_slug": "basic",
    "region": "fra1"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/registries`

To create your container registry, send a POST request to `/v2/registries`.

The `name` becomes part of the URL for images stored in the registry. For
example, if your registry is called `example`, an image in it will have the
URL `registry.digitalocean.com/example/image:tag`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "example",
  "subscription_tier_slug": "basic",
  "region": "fra1"
}
```

<h3 id="create-container-registry-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[multiregistry_create](#schemamultiregistry_create)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|A globally unique name for the container registry. Must be lowercase and be composed only of numbers, letters and `-`, up to a limit of 63 characters.|
|» subscription_tier_slug|body|string|false|The slug of the subscription tier to sign up for. Valid values can be retrieved using the options endpoint.|
|» region|body|string|false|Slug of the region where registry data is stored. When not provided, a region will be selected.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» subscription_tier_slug|starter|
|» subscription_tier_slug|basic|
|» subscription_tier_slug|professional|
|» region|nyc3|
|» region|sfo3|
|» region|sfo2|
|» region|ams3|
|» region|sgp1|
|» region|fra1|
|» region|blr1|
|» region|syd1|

## Get Docker Credentials By Registry Name

<a id="opIdregistries_get_dockerCredentials"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/registries/example/docker-credentials \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/registries/{registry_name}/docker-credentials`

In order to access your container registry with the Docker client or from a
Kubernetes cluster, you will need to configure authentication. The necessary
JSON configuration can be retrieved by sending a GET request to
`/v2/registries/{registry_name}/docker-credentials`.

The response will be in the format of a Docker `config.json` file. To use the
config in your Kubernetes cluster, create a Secret with:

    kubectl create secret generic docr \
      --from-file=.dockerconfigjson=config.json \
      --type=kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson

By default, the returned credentials have read-only access to your registry
and cannot be used to push images. This is appropriate for most Kubernetes
clusters. To retrieve read/write credentials, suitable for use with the Docker
client or in a CI system, read_write may be provided as query parameter. For
example: `/v2/registries/{registry_name}/docker-credentials?read_write=true`

By default, the returned credentials will not expire. To retrieve credentials
with an expiry set, expiry_seconds may be provided as a query parameter. For
example: `/v2/registries/{registry_name}/docker-credentials?expiry_seconds=3600` will return
credentials that expire after one hour.


<h3 id="get-docker-credentials-by-registry-name-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|registry_name|path|string|true|The name of a container registry.|

```json
    "registry.digitalocean.com": {
      "auth": "YjdkMDNhNjk0N2IyMTdlZmI2ZjNlYzNiZDM1MDQ1ODI6YjdkMDNhNjk0N2IyMTdlZmI2ZjNlYzNiZDM1MDQ1ODIK"
    }
  }
}
```

## Update Subscription Tier

<a id="opIdregistries_update_subscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/registries/subscription \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "tier_slug": "basic"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/registries/subscription`

After creating your registry, you can switch to a different subscription tier to better suit your needs. To do this, send a POST request to `/v2/registries/subscription`. It is similar to POST `/v2/registry/subscription`.

```json
  "tier_slug": "basic"
}
```

## List Registry Options (Subscription Tiers and Available Regions)

<a id="opIdregistries_get_options"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/registries/options \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/registries/options`

This endpoint serves to provide additional information as to which option values are available when creating a container registry.
There are multiple subscription tiers available for container registry. Each tier allows a different number of image repositories to be created in your registry, and has a different amount of storage and transfer included.
There are multiple regions available for container registry and controls where your data is stored.
To list the available options, send a GET request to `/v2/registries/options`. This is similar to GET `/v2/registry/options`.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "options": {
    "available_regions": [
      "nyc3",
      "sfo3",
      "ams3",
      "sgp1",
      "fra1"
    ],
    "subscription_tiers": [
      {
        "name": "Starter",
        "slug": "starter",
        "included_repositories": 1,
        "included_storage_bytes": 524288000,
        "allow_storage_overage": false,
        "included_bandwidth_bytes": 524288000,
        "monthly_price_in_cents": 0,
        "eligible": false,
        "eligibility_reasons": [
          "OverRepositoryLimit"
        ]
      },
      {
        "name": "Basic",
        "slug": "basic",
        "included_repositories": 5,
        "included_storage_bytes": 5368709120,
        "allow_storage_overage": true,
        "included_bandwidth_bytes": 5368709120,
        "monthly_price_in_cents": 500,
        "eligible": true
      },
      {
        "name": "Professional",
        "slug": "professional",
        "included_repositories": 0,
        "included_storage_bytes": 107374182400,
        "allow_storage_overage": true,
        "included_bandwidth_bytes": 107374182400,
        "monthly_price_in_cents": 2000,
        "eligible": true
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

```json
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

## Start Garbage Collection

<a id="opIdregistries_run_garbageCollection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/registries/example/garbage-collection \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/registries/{registry_name}/garbage-collection`

Garbage collection enables users to clear out unreferenced blobs (layer &
manifest data) after deleting one or more manifests from a repository. If
there are no unreferenced blobs resulting from the deletion of one or more
manifests, garbage collection is effectively a noop.
[See here for more information](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/container-registry/how-to/clean-up-container-registry/)
about how and why you should clean up your container registry periodically.

To request a garbage collection run on your registry, send a POST request to
`/v2/registries/$REGISTRY_NAME/garbage-collection`. This will initiate the
following sequence of events on your registry.

* Set the registry to read-only mode, meaning no further write-scoped
  JWTs will be issued to registry clients. Existing write-scoped JWTs will
  continue to work until they expire which can take up to 15 minutes.
* Wait until all existing write-scoped JWTs have expired.
* Scan all registry manifests to determine which blobs are unreferenced.
* Delete all unreferenced blobs from the registry.
* Record the number of blobs deleted and bytes freed, mark the garbage
  collection status as `success`.
* Remove the read-only mode restriction from the registry, meaning write-scoped
  JWTs will once again be issued to registry clients.


<h3 id="start-garbage-collection-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|registry_name|path|string|true|The name of a container registry.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "garbage_collection": {
    "uuid": "eff0feee-49c7-4e8f-ba5c-a320c109c8a8",
    "registry_name": "example",
    "status": "requested",
    "created_at": "2020-10-30T21:03:24Z",
    "updated_at": "2020-10-30T21:03:44Z",
    "blobs_deleted": 42,
    "freed_bytes": 667
  }
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

## Update Garbage Collection

```json
}
```

## Delete Container Registry Repository

<a id="opIdregistries_delete_repository"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/registries/example/repositories/repo-1 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/registries/{registry_name}/repositories/{repository_name}`

To delete a container repository including all of its tags, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/registries/$REGISTRY_NAME/repositories/$REPOSITORY_NAME`.

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.
This indicates that the request was processed successfully.


<h3 id="delete-container-registry-repository-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|registry_name|path|string|true|The name of a container registry.|
|repository_name|path|string|true|The name of a container registry repository. If the name contains `/` characters, they must be URL-encoded, e.g. `%2F`.|

## List All Container Registry Repository Tags

<a id="opIdregistries_list_repositoryTags"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/registries/example/repositories/repo-1/tags \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/registries/{registry_name}/repositories/{repository_name}/tags`

To list all tags in one of your container registry's repository, send a GET
request to `/v2/registries/$REGISTRY_NAME/repositories/$REPOSITORY_NAME/tags`.

Note that if your repository name contains `/` characters, it must be
URL-encoded in the request URL. For example, to list tags for
`registry.digitalocean.com/example/my/repo`, the path would be
`/v2/registry/example/repositories/my%2Frepo/tags`. 

It is similar to GET `/v2/registry/$REGISTRY_NAME/repositories/$REPOSITORY_NAME/tags`.


<h3 id="list-all-container-registry-repository-tags-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|
|registry_name|path|string|true|The name of a container registry.|
|repository_name|path|string|true|The name of a container registry repository. If the name contains `/` characters, they must be URL-encoded, e.g. `%2F`.|

## Delete Container Registry Repository Tag

<a id="opIdregistries_delete_repositoryTag"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/registries/example/repositories/repo-1/tags/06a447a \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/registries/{registry_name}/repositories/{repository_name}/tags/{repository_tag}`

To delete a container repository tag in on of our container registries, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/registries/$REGISTRY_NAME/repositories/$REPOSITORY_NAME/tags/$TAG`.

Note that if your repository name contains `/` characters, it must be
URL-encoded in the request URL. For example, to delete
`registry.digitalocean.com/example/my/repo:mytag`, the path would be
`/v2/registry/example/repositories/my%2Frepo/tags/mytag`.

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.
This indicates that the request was processed successfully. It is similar to DELETE `/v2/registry/$REGISTRY_NAME/repositories/$REPOSITORY_NAME/tags/$TAG`.

|repository_name|path|string|true|The name of a container registry repository. If the name contains `/` characters, they must be URL-encoded, e.g. `%2F`.|

## List All Container Registry Repository Manifests

<a id="opIdregistries_list_repositoryManifests"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/registries/example/repositories/repo-1/digests \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/registries/{registry_name}/repositories/{repository_name}/digests`

To list all manifests in your container registry repository, send a GET
request to `/v2/registries/$REGISTRY_NAME/repositories/$REPOSITORY_NAME/digests`.

Note that if your repository name contains `/` characters, it must be
URL-encoded in the request URL. For example, to list manifests for
`registry.digitalocean.com/example/my/repo`, the path would be
`/v2/registry/example/repositories/my%2Frepo/digests`.

It is similar to `/v2/registry/$REGISTRY_NAME/repositories/$REPOSITORY_NAME/digests`.

|repository_name|path|string|true|The name of a container registry repository. If the name contains `/` characters, they must be URL-encoded, e.g. `%2F`.|

## Delete Container Registry Repository Manifest

<a id="opIdregistries_delete_repositoryManifest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/registries/example/repositories/repo-1/digests/sha256%3Acb8a924afdf0229ef7515d9e5b3024e23b3eb03ddbba287f4a19c6ac90b8d221 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/registries/{registry_name}/repositories/{repository_name}/digests/{manifest_digest}`

To delete a container repository manifest by digest in one of your registries, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/registries/$REGISTRY_NAME/repositories/$REPOSITORY_NAME/digests/$MANIFEST_DIGEST`.

Note that if your repository name contains `/` characters, it must be
URL-encoded in the request URL. For example, to delete
`registry.digitalocean.com/example/my/repo@sha256:abcd`, the path would be
`/v2/registry/example/repositories/my%2Frepo/digests/sha256:abcd`.

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.
This indicates that the request was processed successfully.

It is similar to DELETE `/v2/registry/$REGISTRY_NAME/repositories/$REPOSITORY_NAME/digests/$MANIFEST_DIGEST`.


<h3 id="delete-container-registry-repository-manifest-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|registry_name|path|string|true|The name of a container registry.|
|repository_name|path|string|true|The name of a container registry repository. If the name contains `/` characters, they must be URL-encoded, e.g. `%2F`.|
|manifest_digest|path|string|true|The manifest digest of a container registry repository tag.|

## Validate a Container Registry Name

<a id="opIdregistries_validate_name"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/registries/validate-name \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "example"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/registries/validate-name`

To validate that a container registry name is available for use, send a POST
request to `/v2/registries/validate-name`.

If the name is both formatted correctly and available, the response code will
be 204 and contain no body. If the name is already in use, the response will
be a 409 Conflict. 

It is similar to `/v2/registry/validate-name`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "example"
}
```

|» name|body|string|true|A globally unique name for the container registry. Must be lowercase and be composed only of numbers, letters and `-`, up to a limit of 63 characters.|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-databases">Databases</h1>

DigitalOcean's [managed database service](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/databases)
simplifies the creation and management of highly available database clusters. Currently, it
offers support for [PostgreSQL](http://docs.digitalocean.com/products/databases/postgresql/),
[Caching](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/databases/redis/),
[Valkey](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/databases/valkey/),
[MySQL](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/databases/mysql/),
[MongoDB](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/databases/mongodb/), and
[OpenSearch](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/databases/opensearch/).

By sending requests to the `/v2/databases` endpoint, you can list, create, or delete
database clusters as well as scale the size of a cluster, add or remove read-only replicas,
and manage other configuration details.

Database clusters may be deployed in a multi-node, high-availability configuration.
If your machine type is above the basic nodes, your node plan is above the smallest option,
or you are running MongoDB, you may additionally include up to two standby nodes in your cluster.

The size of individual nodes in a database cluster is represented by a human-readable slug,
which is used in some of the following requests. Each slug denotes the node's identifier,
CPU count, and amount of RAM, in that order.

For a list of currently available database slugs and options, use the `/v2/databases/options` endpoint or use the
`doctl databases options` [command](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl/reference/databases/options).

## List All Database Clusters

<a id="opIddatabases_list_clusters"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/databases`

To list all of the database clusters available on your account, send a GET request to `/v2/databases`. To limit the results to database clusters with a specific tag, include the `tag_name` query parameter set to the name of the tag. For example, `/v2/databases?tag_name=$TAG_NAME`.

The result will be a JSON object with a `databases` key. This will be set to an array of database objects, each of which will contain the standard database attributes.

The embedded `connection` and `private_connection` objects will contain the information needed to access the database cluster. For multi-node clusters, the `standby_connection` and `standby_private_connection` objects will contain the information needed to connect to the cluster's standby node(s).

The embedded `maintenance_window` object will contain information about any scheduled maintenance for the database cluster.

<h3 id="list-all-database-clusters-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tag_name|query|string|false|Limits the results to database clusters with a specific tag.<br><br>Requires `tag:read` scope.|

## Create a New Database Cluster

<a id="opIddatabases_create_cluster"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "backend",
    "engine": "pg",
    "version": "14",
    "region": "nyc3",
    "size": "db-s-2vcpu-4gb",
    "storage_size_mib": 61440,
    "num_nodes": 2,
    "tags": [
      "production"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/databases`

To create a database cluster, send a POST request to `/v2/databases`. To see a list  of options for each engine, such as available regions, size slugs, and versions, send a GET request to the `/v2/databases/options` endpoint. The available sizes for  the `storage_size_mib` field depends on the cluster's size. To see a list of available sizes, see [Managed Database Pricing](https://www.digitalocean.com/pricing/managed-databases).

The create response returns a JSON object with a key called `database`. The value of this is an object that contains the standard attributes associated with a database cluster. The initial value of the database cluster's `status` attribute is `creating`. When the cluster is ready to receive traffic, this changes to `online`.

The embedded `connection` and `private_connection` objects contains the information needed to access the database cluster. For multi-node clusters, the `standby_connection` and `standby_private_connection` objects contain the information needed to connect to the cluster's standby node(s).

DigitalOcean managed PostgreSQL and MySQL database clusters take automated daily backups. To create a new database cluster based on a backup of an existing cluster, send a POST request to `/v2/databases`. In addition to the standard database cluster attributes, the JSON body must include a key named `backup_restore` with the name of the original database cluster and the timestamp of the backup to be restored. Creating a database from a backup is the same as forking a database in the control panel.

PostgreSQL and MySQL Advanced Edition clusters can be provisioned by setting `engine` to `advanced_pg` or `advanced_mysql`. Advanced Edition clusters are currently in public preview and target highly available workloads. `advanced_pg` supports 1-, 2-, and 3-node deployments; `advanced_mysql` only supports 1- and 3-node deployments. See the [PostgreSQL Advanced Edition](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/databases/postgresql/how-to/use-advanced-edition-clusters/) and [MySQL Advanced Edition](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/databases/mysql/how-to/use-advanced-edition-clusters/) documentation for the feature differences vs. Standard Edition and current preview limitations.

Note: Caching cluster creates are no longer supported as of 2025-04-30T00:00:00Z. Backups are also not supported for Caching or Valkey clusters.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "backend",
  "engine": "pg",
  "version": "14",
  "region": "nyc3",
  "size": "db-s-2vcpu-4gb",
  "storage_size_mib": 61440,
  "num_nodes": 2,
  "tags": [
    "production"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-database-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|A unique, human-readable name referring to a database cluster.|
|» engine|body|string|true|A slug representing the database engine used for the cluster. The possible values are: "pg" for PostgreSQL, "mysql" for MySQL, "redis" for Caching, "mongodb" for MongoDB, "kafka" for Kafka, "opensearch" for OpenSearch, "valkey" for Valkey, "advanced_pg" for PostgreSQL Advanced Edition, and "advanced_mysql" for MySQL Advanced Edition. Advanced Edition engines are currently in public preview.|
|» version|body|string|false|A string representing the version of the database engine in use for the cluster.|
|» num_nodes|body|integer|true|The number of nodes in the database cluster.|
|» size|body|string|true|The slug identifier representing the size of the nodes in the database cluster.|
|» region|body|string|true|The slug identifier for the region where the database cluster is located.|
|» private_network_uuid|body|string|false|A string specifying the UUID of the VPC to which the database cluster will be assigned. If excluded, the cluster when creating a new database cluster, it will be assigned to your account's default VPC for the region. <br><br>Requires `vpc:read` scope.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|An array of tags (as strings) to apply to the database cluster. <br><br>Requires `tag:create` scope.|
|» ui_connection|body|object|false|The connection details for OpenSearch dashboard. |
|» schema_registry_connection|body|object|false|The connection details for Schema Registry.|
|» connection|body|object|false|none|
|» private_connection|body|object|false|none|
|» standby_connection|body|object|false|none|
|» standby_private_connection|body|object|false|none|
|» maintenance_window|body|object|false|none|
|» » day|body|string|true|The day of the week on which to apply maintenance updates.|
|» » hour|body|string|true|The hour in UTC at which maintenance updates will be applied in 24 hour format.|
|» project_id|body|string(uuid)|false|The ID of the project that the database cluster is assigned to. If excluded when creating a new database cluster, it will be assigned to your default project.<br><br>Requires `project:assign_resource` scope.|
|» rules|body|[[firewall_rule](#schemafirewall_rule)]|false|none|
|» storage_size_mib|body|integer|false|Additional storage added to the cluster, in MiB. If null, no additional storage is added to the cluster, beyond what is provided as a base amount from the 'size' and any previously added additional storage.|
|» autoscale|body|object|false|Autoscaling configuration for the database cluster. Currently only supports storage autoscaling. If null, autoscaling is not configured for the cluster.|
|» » storage|body|object|false|none|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|true|Whether storage autoscaling is enabled for the cluster|
|» » » threshold_percent|body|integer|false|The storage usage threshold percentage that triggers autoscaling. When storage usage exceeds this percentage, additional storage will be added automatically.|
|» » » increment_gib|body|integer|false|The amount of additional storage to add (in GiB) when autoscaling is triggered|
|» do_settings|body|object|false|none|
|» » service_cnames|body|[string]|false|An array of custom CNAMEs for the database cluster. Each CNAME must be a valid RFC 1123 hostname (e.g., "db.example.com"). Maximum of 16 CNAMEs allowed, each up to 253 characters.|
|» backup_restore|body|[database_backup](#schemadatabase_backup)|false|none|

|» engine|kafka|

|» engine|advanced_pg|
|» engine|advanced_mysql|

## Retrieve an Existing Database Cluster

<a id="opIddatabases_get_cluster"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}`

To show information about an existing database cluster, send a GET request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID`.

The response will be a JSON object with a database key. This will be set to an object containing the standard database cluster attributes.

The embedded `connection` and `private_connection` objects will contain the information needed to access the database cluster. For multi-node clusters, the `standby_connection` and `standby_private_connection` objects contain the information needed to connect to the cluster's standby node(s).

The embedded maintenance_window object will contain information about any scheduled maintenance for the database cluster.

<h3 id="retrieve-an-existing-database-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|

`DELETE /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}`

`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/ca`

To retrieve the public certificate used to secure the connection to the database cluster send a GET request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/ca`.

containing the base64 encoding of the public key certificate.

## Start an Online Migration

<a id="opIddatabases_update_onlineMigration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/online-migration \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "source": {
      "host": "source-db.example.com",
      "dbname": "defaultdb",
      "port": 25060,
      "username": "doadmin",
      "password": "example_password"
    },
    "disable_ssl": false,
    "ignore_dbs": [
      "db0",
      "db1"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/online-migration`

To start an online migration, send a PUT request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/online-migration` endpoint. Migrating a cluster establishes a connection with an existing cluster and replicates its contents to the target cluster. Online migration is only available for MySQL, PostgreSQL, Caching, and Valkey clusters.
If the existing database is continuously being written to,  the migration process will continue for up to two weeks unless it is manually stopped. Online migration is only available for [MySQL](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/databases/mysql/how-to/migrate/#:~:text=To%20migrate%20a%20MySQL%20database,then%20select%20Set%20Up%20Migration),  [PostgreSQL](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/databases/postgresql/how-to/migrate/),  [Caching](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/databases/redis/how-to/migrate/), and [Valkey](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/databases/valkey/how-to/migrate/) clusters. 

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "source": {
    "host": "source-db.example.com",
    "dbname": "defaultdb",
    "port": 25060,
    "username": "doadmin",
    "password": "example_password"
  },
  "disable_ssl": false,
  "ignore_dbs": [
    "db0",
    "db1"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="start-an-online-migration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|body|body|[source_database](#schemasource_database)|true|none|
|» source|body|object|true|none|
|» » host|body|string|false|The FQDN pointing to the database cluster's current primary node.|
|» » port|body|integer|false|The port on which the database cluster is listening.|
|» » dbname|body|string|false|The name of the default database.|
|» » username|body|string|false|The default user for the database.|
|» » password|body|string|false|The randomly generated password for the default user.|
|» disable_ssl|body|boolean|false|Enables SSL encryption when connecting to the source database.|
|» ignore_dbs|body|[string]|false|List of databases that should be ignored during migration.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "77b28fc8-19ff-11eb-8c9c-c68e24557488",
  "status": "running",
  "created_at": "2020-10-29T15:57:38Z"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Migrate a Database Cluster to a New Region

<a id="opIddatabases_update_region"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/migrate \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "region": "lon1"
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/migrate`

To migrate a database cluster to a new region, send a `PUT` request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/migrate`. The body of the request must specify a
`region` attribute.

A successful request will receive a 202 Accepted status code with no body in
response. Querying the database cluster will show that its `status` attribute
will now be set to `migrating`. This will transition back to `online` when the
migration has completed.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "region": "lon1"
}
```

<h3 id="migrate-a-database-cluster-to-a-new-region-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» region|body|string|true|A slug identifier for the region to which the database cluster will be migrated.|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
  "id": "not_found",
```

```json
}
```

> default Response

```json
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Resize a Database Cluster

<a id="opIddatabases_update_clusterSize"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/resize \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "size": "db-s-4vcpu-8gb",
    "num_nodes": 3,
    "storage_size_mib": 163840
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/resize`

To resize a database cluster, send a PUT request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/resize`. The body of the request must specify both the size and num_nodes attributes.
A successful request will receive a 202 Accepted status code with no body in response. Querying the database cluster will show that its status attribute will now be set to resizing. This will transition back to online when the resize operation has completed.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "size": "db-s-4vcpu-8gb",
  "num_nodes": 3,
  "storage_size_mib": 163840
}
```

<h3 id="resize-a-database-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|body|body|[database_cluster_resize](#schemadatabase_cluster_resize)|true|none|
|» size|body|string|true|A slug identifier representing desired the size of the nodes in the database cluster.|
|» num_nodes|body|integer(int32)|true|The number of nodes in the database cluster. Valid values are are 1-3. In addition to the primary node, up to two standby nodes may be added for highly available configurations.|
|» storage_size_mib|body|integer|false|Additional storage added to the cluster, in MiB. If null, no additional storage is added to the cluster, beyond what is provided as a base amount from the 'size' and any previously added additional storage.|

> Example responses

```json
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

```json
{

}
```

```json
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Update Firewall Rules (Trusted Sources) for a Database

<a id="opIddatabases_update_firewall_rules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/firewall \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "rules": [
      {
        "type": "ip_addr",
        "value": "192.168.1.1"
      },
      {
        "type": "k8s",
        "value": "ff2a6c52-5a44-4b63-b99c-0e98e7a63d61"
      },
      {
        "type": "droplet",
        "value": "163973392"
      },
      {
        "type": "tag",
        "value": "backend",
        "description": "a backend tag"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/firewall`

To update a database cluster's firewall rules (known as "trusted sources" in the control panel), send a PUT request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/firewall` specifying which resources should be able to open connections to the database. You may limit connections to specific Droplets, Kubernetes clusters, or IP addresses. When a tag is provided, any Droplet or Kubernetes node with that tag applied to it will have access. The firewall is limited to 100 rules (or trusted sources). You cannot add IPv6 addresses as trusted sources. For additional limits, see your database engine's limits page. When possible, we recommend [placing your databases into a VPC network](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/networking/vpc/) to limit access to them instead of using a firewall.
A successful request returns a 204 status code with no content.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "rules": [
    {
      "type": "ip_addr",
      "value": "192.168.1.1"
    },
    {
      "type": "k8s",
      "value": "ff2a6c52-5a44-4b63-b99c-0e98e7a63d61"
    },
    {
      "type": "droplet",
      "value": "163973392"
    },
    {
      "type": "tag",
      "value": "backend",
      "description": "a backend tag"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Update DO Settings for a Database Cluster

<a id="opIddatabases_update_do_settings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/do_settings \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "do_settings": {
      "service_cnames": [
        "db.example.com",
        "db-replica.example.com"
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/do_settings`

To update the DigitalOcean-specific settings for a database cluster, send a PUT request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/do_settings`.
Currently, the only supported setting is `service_cnames`, which allows you to specify custom DNS names (CNAMEs) to be included in the TLS certificate Subject Alternative Names (SANs) for the database cluster nodes. This enables TLS verification when connecting via a custom hostname.
After updating, the database nodes will be replaced to apply the new certificate. This process is performed as a rolling replacement and does not cause downtime.
To clear all custom CNAMEs, send an empty array or omit the field.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "do_settings": {
    "service_cnames": [
      "db.example.com",
      "db-replica.example.com"
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-do-settings-for-a-database-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» do_settings|body|[do_settings](#schemado_settings)|true|DigitalOcean-specific settings for the database cluster.|

`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/backups`

## Create a Read-only Replica

<a id="opIddatabases_create_replica"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/replicas \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "read-nyc3-01",
    "region": "nyc3",
    "size": "db-s-2vcpu-4gb",
    "storage_size_mib": 61440
  }'
```

`POST /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/replicas`

To create a read-only replica for a PostgreSQL or MySQL database cluster, send a POST request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/replicas` specifying the name it should be given, the size of the node to be used, and the region where it will be located.

**Note**: Read-only replicas are not supported for Caching or Valkey clusters.

The response will be a JSON object with a key called `replica`. The value of this will be an object that contains the standard attributes associated with a database replica. The initial value of the read-only replica's `status` attribute will be `forking`. When the replica is ready to receive traffic, this will transition to `active`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "read-nyc3-01",
  "region": "nyc3",
  "size": "db-s-2vcpu-4gb",
  "storage_size_mib": 61440
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-read-only-replica-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name to give the read-only replicating|
|» region|body|string|false|A slug identifier for the region where the read-only replica will be located. If excluded, the replica will be placed in the same region as the cluster.|
|» size|body|string|true|A slug identifier representing the size of the node for the read-only replica. The size of the replica must be at least as large as the node size for the database cluster from which it is replicating.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|A flat array of tag names as strings to apply to the read-only replica after it is created. Tag names can either be existing or new tags. <br><br>Requires `tag:create` scope.|
|» private_network_uuid|body|string|false|A string specifying the UUID of the VPC to which the read-only replica will be assigned. If excluded, the replica will be assigned to your account's default VPC for the region. <br><br>Requires `vpc:read` scope.|
|» connection|body|object|false|none|
|» private_connection|body|object|false|none|
|» storage_size_mib|body|integer|false|Additional storage added to the cluster, in MiB. If null, no additional storage is added to the cluster, beyond what is provided as a base amount from the 'size' and any previously added additional storage.|
|» do_settings|body|object|false|none|
|» » service_cnames|body|[string]|false|An array of custom CNAMEs for the database cluster. Each CNAME must be a valid RFC 1123 hostname (e.g., "db.example.com"). Maximum of 16 CNAMEs allowed, each up to 253 characters.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "replica": {
    "name": "read-nyc3-01",
    "connection": {
      "uri": "",
      "database": "defaultdb",
      "host": "read-db.example.com",
      "port": 25060,
      "user": "doadmin",
      "password": "example_password",
      "ssl": true
    },
    "private_connection": {
      "uri": "postgres://doadmin:example_password@private-read-db.example.com:25060/defaultdb?sslmode=require",
      "database": "",
      "host": "private-read-db.example.com",
      "port": 25060,
      "user": "doadmin",
      "password": "example_password",
      "ssl": true
    },
    "region": "nyc3",
    "status": "online",
```

`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/replicas/{replica_name}`

## List all Database Users

<a id="opIddatabases_list_users"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/users \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/users`

To list all of the users for your database cluster, send a GET request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/users`.

Note: User management is not supported for Caching or Valkey clusters.

The result will be a JSON object with a `users` key. This will be set to an array
of database user objects, each of which will contain the standard database user attributes.
User passwords will not show without the `database:view_credentials` scope.

For MySQL clusters, additional options will be contained in the mysql_settings object.

For PostgreSQL clusters, additional options will be contained in the `settings`
object (for example, `pg_allow_replication`).

For Kafka clusters, additional options will be contained in the `settings` object.

For MongoDB clusters, additional information will be contained in the mongo_user_settings object


<h3 id="list-all-database-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|

```json
      "role": "primary",
```

## Add a Database User

<a id="opIddatabases_add_user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/users \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "app-01"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/users`

To add a new database user, send a POST request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/users`
with the desired username.

Note: User management is not supported for Caching or Valkey clusters.

When adding a user to a MySQL cluster, additional options can be configured in the
`mysql_settings` object.

When adding a user to a PostgreSQL cluster, additional options can be configured in
the `settings` object (for example, `pg_allow_replication`). When
`pg_allow_replication` is omitted, it defaults to `false`.

When adding a user to a Kafka cluster, additional options can be configured in
the `settings` object.

When adding a user to a MongoDB cluster, additional options can be configured in
the `settings.mongo_user_settings` object.

The response will be a JSON object with a key called `user`. The value of this will be an
object that contains the standard attributes associated with a database user including
its randomly generated password.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "app-01"
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-database-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of a database user.|
|» mysql_settings|body|[mysql_settings](#schemamysql_settings)|false|none|
|» settings|body|[user_settings](#schemauser_settings)|false|none|
|» readonly|body|boolean|false|(To be deprecated: use settings.mongo_user_settings.role instead for access controls to MongoDB databases). <br>For MongoDB clusters, set to `true` to create a read-only user.<br>This option is not currently supported for other database engines.<br>           <br>|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "user": {
    "name": "app-01",
    "role": "normal",
    "password": "example_password"
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Update a Database User

<a id="opIddatabases_update_user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/users/app-01 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "settings": {
      "pg_allow_replication": true
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/users/{username}`

To update an existing database user, send a PUT request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/users/$USERNAME`
with the desired settings.

**Note**: only `settings` can be updated via this type of request. If you wish to change the name of a user,
you must recreate a new user.

For PostgreSQL clusters, you can update `settings.pg_allow_replication` to enable or
disable replication privileges for the user. When omitted, the value defaults to `false`.

For Kafka and OpenSearch clusters, additional options can be configured in the
`settings` object (for example, topic or index ACLs).

Updating users is supported for PostgreSQL, Kafka, and OpenSearch clusters. For
other engines, the request returns a 422. MongoDB roles and database access are
set with `settings.mongo_user_settings` when creating a user and cannot be
changed afterward; recreate the user to apply different roles or databases.

The response will be a JSON object with a key called `user`. The value of this will be an
object that contains the name of the updated database user, along with the `settings` object that
has been updated.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "settings": {
    "pg_allow_replication": true
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-database-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|username|path|string|true|The name of the database user.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» settings|body|[user_settings_update](#schemauser_settings_update)|true|User settings that can be updated via the Update a Database User endpoint.<br>Supported for PostgreSQL, Kafka, and OpenSearch clusters. For other engines,<br>the request returns a 422. MongoDB user roles and database access<br>(`mongo_user_settings`) cannot be updated after creation; recreate the user<br>to change them.<br>|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

## Remove a Database User

<a id="opIddatabases_delete_user"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/users/app-01 \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/users/{username}`

To remove a specific database user, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/users/$USERNAME`.

A status of 204 will be given. This indicates that the request was processed
successfully, but that no response body is needed.

Note: User management is not supported for Caching or Valkey clusters.

## Reset a Database User's Password or Authentication Method

<a id="opIddatabases_reset_auth"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/users/app-01/reset_auth \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "mysql_settings": {
      "auth_plugin": "caching_sha2_password"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/users/{username}/reset_auth`

To reset the password for a database user, send a POST request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/users/$USERNAME/reset_auth`.

For `mysql` databases, the authentication method can be specifying by
including a key in the JSON body called `mysql_settings` with the `auth_plugin`
value specified.

The response will be a JSON object with a `user` key. This will be set to an
object containing the standard database user attributes.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "mysql_settings": {
    "auth_plugin": "caching_sha2_password"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="reset-a-database-users-password-or-authentication-method-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|username|path|string|true|The name of the database user.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» mysql_settings|body|[mysql_settings](#schemamysql_settings)|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "user": {
    "name": "app-01",
    "role": "normal",
    "password": "example_password"
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
}
```

`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/dbs`

## Add a New Connection Pool (PostgreSQL)

<a id="opIddatabases_add_connectionPool"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/pools \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "backend-pool",
    "mode": "transaction",
    "size": 10,
    "db": "defaultdb",
    "user": "doadmin"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/pools`

For PostgreSQL database clusters, connection pools can be used to allow a
database to share its idle connections. The popular PostgreSQL connection
pooling utility PgBouncer is used to provide this service. [See here for more information](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/databases/postgresql/how-to/manage-connection-pools/)
about how and why to use PgBouncer connection pooling including
details about the available transaction modes.

To add a new connection pool to a PostgreSQL database cluster, send a POST
request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/pools` specifying a name for the pool,
the user to connect with, the database to connect to, as well as its desired
size and transaction mode.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "backend-pool",
  "mode": "transaction",
  "size": 10,
  "db": "defaultdb",
  "user": "doadmin"
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-new-connection-pool-postgresql-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|body|body|[connection_pool](#schemaconnection_pool)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|A unique name for the connection pool. Must be between 3 and 60 characters.|
|» mode|body|string|true|The PGBouncer transaction mode for the connection pool. The allowed values are session, transaction, and statement.|
|» size|body|integer(int32)|true|The desired size of the PGBouncer connection pool. The maximum allowed size is determined by the size of the cluster's primary node. 25 backend server connections are allowed for every 1GB of RAM. Three are reserved for maintenance. For example, a primary node with 1 GB of RAM allows for a maximum of 22 backend server connections while one with 4 GB would allow for 97. Note that these are shared across all connection pools in a cluster.|
|» db|body|string|true|The database for use with the connection pool.|
|» user|body|string|false|The name of the user for use with the connection pool. When excluded, all sessions connect to the database as the inbound user.|
|» connection|body|object|false|none|
|» private_connection|body|object|false|none|
|» standby_connection|body|object|false|none|
|» standby_private_connection|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "pool": {
    "user": "doadmin",
    "name": "backend-pool",
    "size": 10,
    "db": "defaultdb",
    "mode": "transaction",
    "connection": {
      "uri": "postgres://doadmin:example_password@db.example.com:25061/backend-pool?sslmode=require",
      "database": "backend-pool",
      "host": "db.example.com",
      "port": 25061,
      "user": "doadmin",
      "password": "example_password",
      "ssl": true
    }
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Update Connection Pools (PostgreSQL)

<a id="opIddatabases_update_connectionPool"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/pools/backend-pool \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "mode": "transaction",
    "size": 10,
    "db": "defaultdb",
    "user": "doadmin"
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/pools/{pool_name}`

To update a connection pool for a PostgreSQL database cluster, send a PUT request to  `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/pools/$POOL_NAME`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "mode": "transaction",
  "size": 10,
  "db": "defaultdb",
  "user": "doadmin"
}
```

<h3 id="update-connection-pools-postgresql-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|pool_name|path|string|true|The name used to identify the connection pool.|
|body|body|[connection_pool_update](#schemaconnection_pool_update)|true|none|
|» mode|body|string|true|The PGBouncer transaction mode for the connection pool. The allowed values are session, transaction, and statement.|
|» size|body|integer(int32)|true|The desired size of the PGBouncer connection pool. The maximum allowed size is determined by the size of the cluster's primary node. 25 backend server connections are allowed for every 1GB of RAM. Three are reserved for maintenance. For example, a primary node with 1 GB of RAM allows for a maximum of 22 backend server connections while one with 4 GB would allow for 97. Note that these are shared across all connection pools in a cluster.|
|» db|body|string|true|The database for use with the connection pool.|
|» user|body|string|false|The name of the user for use with the connection pool. When excluded, all sessions connect to the database as the inbound user.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/eviction_policy`

|401|Unauthorized|Authentication failed due to invalid credentials.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|404|Not Found|The resource was not found.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|The API rate limit has been exceeded.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|There was a server error.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|There was an unexpected error.|[error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="retrieve-the-eviction-policy-for-a-caching-or-valkey-cluster-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|eviction_policy|[eviction_policy_model](#schemaeviction_policy_model)|true|none|A string specifying the desired eviction policy for a Caching or Valkey cluster.<br><br>- `noeviction`: Don't evict any data, returns error when memory limit is reached.<br>- `allkeys_lru:` Evict any key, least recently used (LRU) first.<br>- `allkeys_random`: Evict keys in a random order.<br>- `volatile_lru`: Evict keys with expiration only, least recently used (LRU) first.<br>- `volatile_random`: Evict keys with expiration only in a random order.<br>- `volatile_ttl`: Evict keys with expiration only, shortest time-to-live (TTL) first.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|eviction_policy|noeviction|
|eviction_policy|allkeys_lru|
|eviction_policy|allkeys_random|
|eviction_policy|volatile_lru|
|eviction_policy|volatile_random|

## Configure the Eviction Policy for a Caching or Valkey Cluster

<a id="opIddatabases_update_evictionPolicy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/eviction_policy \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "eviction_policy": "allkeys_lru"
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/eviction_policy`

To configure an eviction policy for an existing Caching or Valkey cluster, send a PUT request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/eviction_policy` specifying the desired policy.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "eviction_policy": "allkeys_lru"
}
```

<h3 id="configure-the-eviction-policy-for-a-caching-or-valkey-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» eviction_policy|body|[eviction_policy_model](#schemaeviction_policy_model)|true|A string specifying the desired eviction policy for a Caching or Valkey cluster.<br><br>- `noeviction`: Don't evict any data, returns error when memory limit is reached.<br>- `allkeys_lru:` Evict any key, least recently used (LRU) first.<br>- `allkeys_random`: Evict keys in a random order.<br>- `volatile_lru`: Evict keys with expiration only, least recently used (LRU) first.<br>- `volatile_random`: Evict keys with expiration only in a random order.<br>- `volatile_ttl`: Evict keys with expiration only, shortest time-to-live (TTL) first.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» eviction_policy|noeviction|
|» eviction_policy|allkeys_lru|
|» eviction_policy|allkeys_random|
|» eviction_policy|volatile_lru|
|» eviction_policy|volatile_random|
|» eviction_policy|volatile_ttl|

## Configure Autoscale Settings for a Database Cluster

<a id="opIddatabases_update_autoscale"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/autoscale \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "storage": {
      "enabled": true,
      "threshold_percent": 80,
      "increment_gib": 10
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/autoscale`

To configure autoscale settings for an existing database cluster, send a PUT request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/autoscale`, specifying the autoscale configuration.
A successful request will receive a 204 No Content status code with no body in response.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "storage": {
    "enabled": true,
    "threshold_percent": 80,
    "increment_gib": 10
  }
}
```

<h3 id="configure-autoscale-settings-for-a-database-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|body|body|[database_autoscale_params](#schemadatabase_autoscale_params)|true|none|
|» storage|body|object|false|none|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|true|Whether storage autoscaling is enabled for the cluster|
|» » threshold_percent|body|integer|false|The storage usage threshold percentage that triggers autoscaling. When storage usage exceeds this percentage, additional storage will be added automatically.|
|» » increment_gib|body|integer|false|The amount of additional storage to add (in GiB) when autoscaling is triggered|

`POST /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/topics`

To create a topic attached to a Kafka cluster, send a POST request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/topics`.

## Get Topic for a Kafka Cluster

<a id="opIddatabases_get_kafka_topic"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/topics/customer-events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/topics/{topic_name}`

To retrieve a given topic by name from the set of a Kafka cluster's topics,
send a GET request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/topics/$TOPIC_NAME`.

The result will be a JSON object with a `topic` key.

|topic_name|path|string|true|The name used to identify the Kafka topic.|

## Update Topic for a Kafka Cluster

<a id="opIddatabases_update_kafka_topic"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/topics/customer-events \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "partitions": 3,
    "replication": 2,
    "config": {
      "retention_bytes": -1,
      "retention_ms": 100000
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/topics/{topic_name}`

To update a topic attached to a Kafka cluster, send a PUT request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/topics/$TOPIC_NAME`.

The result will be a JSON object with a `topic` key.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "partitions": 3,
  "replication": 2,
  "config": {
    "retention_bytes": -1,
    "retention_ms": 100000
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-topic-for-a-kafka-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|topic_name|path|string|true|The name used to identify the Kafka topic.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» replication_factor|body|integer|false|The number of nodes to replicate data across the cluster.|
|» partition_count|body|integer|false|The number of partitions available for the topic. On update, this value can only be increased.|
|» config|body|[kafka_topic_config](#schemakafka_topic_config)|false|none|

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/logsink \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "sink_name": "logs-sink",

    "config": {
      "url": "https://user:passwd@192.168.0.1:25060",
      "index_prefix": "opensearch-logs",
      "index_days_max": 5
    }
  }'
```

`DELETE /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/indexes/{index_name}`

To delete a single index within OpenSearch cluster, send a DELETE request
to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/indexes/$INDEX_NAME`.

processed successfully, but that no response body is needed.

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-dedicated-inference">Dedicated Inference</h1>

[Dedicated Inference](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/agent-platform/dedicated-inference/)
delivers scalable production-grade LLM hosting on DigitalOcean. Create, list, get, update,
and delete Dedicated Inference instances; manage accelerators, CA certificate, sizes,
GPU model config, and access tokens.

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/dedicated-inferences/{dedicated_inference_id}`
