## Update a Dedicated Inference

<a id="opIddedicatedInferences_patch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/dedicated-inferences/6b5c619c-359c-44ca-87e2-47e98170c01d \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "spec": {
      "version": 1,
      "name": "new-dedicated-inference",
      "region": "atl1",
      "vpc": {
        "uuid": "997615ce-132d-4bae-9270-9ee21b395e5d"
      },
      "enable_public_endpoint": true,
      "model_deployments": [
        {
          "model_id": "",
          "model_slug": "mistral/mistral-7b-instruct-v3",
          "model_provider": "hugging_face",
          "workload_config": {},
          "accelerators": [
            {
              "scale": 1,
              "type": "prefill_decode",
              "accelerator_slug": "gpu-mi300x1-192gb"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    "access_tokens": {
      "hugging_face_token": "$HF_TOKEN"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /v2/dedicated-inferences/{dedicated_inference_id}`

Update an existing Dedicated Inference. Send a PATCH request to
`/v2/dedicated-inferences/{dedicated_inference_id}` with updated `spec` and/or
`access_tokens`. Status will move to updating and return to active when done.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "spec": {
    "version": 1,
    "name": "new-dedicated-inference",
    "region": "atl1",
    "vpc": {
      "uuid": "997615ce-132d-4bae-9270-9ee21b395e5d"
    },
    "enable_public_endpoint": true,
    "model_deployments": [
      {
        "model_id": "",
        "model_slug": "mistral/mistral-7b-instruct-v3",
        "model_provider": "hugging_face",
        "workload_config": {},
        "accelerators": [
          {
            "scale": 1,
            "type": "prefill_decode",
            "accelerator_slug": "gpu-mi300x1-192gb"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  },
  "access_tokens": {
    "hugging_face_token": "$HF_TOKEN"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-dedicated-inference-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dedicated_inference_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a Dedicated Inference instance.|
|body|body|[dedicated_inference_update_request](#schemadedicated_inference_update_request)|true|none|
|» spec|body|[dedicated_inference_spec](#schemadedicated_inference_spec)|false|Structured configuration for a Dedicated Inference deployment.|
|» access_tokens|body|object|false|Provider tokens for model access (e.g. gated Hugging Face models).|
|» » hugging_face_token|body|string|false|Hugging Face token required for gated models.|

## List Dedicated Inferences

<a id="opIddedicatedInferences_list"></a>

`GET /v2/dedicated-inferences`

List all Dedicated Inference instances for your team. Send a GET request to
`/v2/dedicated-inferences`. You may filter by region and use page and per_page
for pagination.


<h3 id="list-dedicated-inferences-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|
|region|query|string|false|Filter by region. Dedicated Inference is only available in nyc2, tor1, and atl1.|

|---|---|
|region|nyc2|
|region|tor1|
|region|atl1|

## Create a Dedicated Inference

<a id="opIddedicatedInferences_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/dedicated-inferences \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "spec": {
      "version": 1,
      "name": "new-dedicated-inference",
      "region": "atl1",
      "vpc": {
        "uuid": "997615ce-132d-4bae-9270-9ee21b395e5d"
      },
      "enable_public_endpoint": true,
      "model_deployments": [
        {
          "model_id": "",
          "model_slug": "mistral/mistral-7b-instruct-v3",
          "model_provider": "hugging_face",
          "workload_config": {},
          "accelerators": [
            {
              "scale": 1,
              "type": "prefill_decode",
              "accelerator_slug": "gpu-mi300x1-192gb"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    "access_tokens": {
      "hugging_face_token": "$HF_TOKEN"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v2/dedicated-inferences`

Create a new Dedicated Inference for your team. Send a POST request to
`/v2/dedicated-inferences` with a `spec` object (version, name, region, vpc,
enable_public_endpoint, model_deployments) and optional `access_tokens` (e.g.
hugging_face_token for gated models). The response code 202 Accepted indicates
the request was accepted for processing; it does not indicate success or failure.
The token value is returned only on create; store it securely.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "spec": {
    "version": 1,
    "name": "new-dedicated-inference",
    "region": "atl1",
    "vpc": {
      "uuid": "997615ce-132d-4bae-9270-9ee21b395e5d"
    },
    "enable_public_endpoint": true,
    "model_deployments": [
      {
        "model_id": "",
        "model_slug": "mistral/mistral-7b-instruct-v3",
        "model_provider": "hugging_face",
        "workload_config": {},
        "accelerators": [
          {
            "scale": 1,
            "type": "prefill_decode",
            "accelerator_slug": "gpu-mi300x1-192gb"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  },
  "access_tokens": {
    "hugging_face_token": "$HF_TOKEN"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-dedicated-inference-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[dedicated_inference_create_request](#schemadedicated_inference_create_request)|true|none|
|» spec|body|[dedicated_inference_spec](#schemadedicated_inference_spec)|true|Structured configuration for a Dedicated Inference deployment.|
|» access_tokens|body|object|false|Key-value pairs for provider tokens (e.g. Hugging Face).|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

## List Dedicated Inference Accelerators

<a id="opIddedicatedInferences_list_accelerators"></a>

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/dedicated-inferences/{dedicated_inference_id}/accelerators`

List all accelerators (GPUs) in use by a Dedicated Inference instance. Send a
GET request to `/v2/dedicated-inferences/{dedicated_inference_id}/accelerators`.
Optionally filter by slug and use page/per_page for pagination.

|dedicated_inference_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a Dedicated Inference instance.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|
|slug|query|string|false|Filter accelerators by GPU slug.|

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/dedicated-inferences/6b5c619c-359c-44ca-87e2-47e98170c01d/tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

    "name": "new-inference-token"
```

```json
    "name": "first-token",
    "value": "di_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
    "created_at": "2024-01-09T20:44:32Z",
    "is_managed": false
  }
}
```

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-domain-records">Domain Records</h1>

Domain record resources are used to set or retrieve information about the
individual DNS records configured for a domain. This allows you to build
and manage DNS zone files by adding and modifying individual records for a
domain.

The [DigitalOcean DNS management interface](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/networking/dns/)
allows you to configure the following DNS records:

Name  | Description                                                                                                                                        |
------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
A     | This record type is used to map an IPv4 address to a hostname.                                                                                     |
AAAA  | This record type is used to map an IPv6 address to a hostname.                                                                                     |
CAA   | As specified in RFC-6844, this record type can be used to restrict which certificate authorities are permitted to issue certificates for a domain. |
CNAME | This record type defines an alias for your canonical hostname (the one defined by an A or AAAA record).                                            |
MX    | This record type is used to define the mail exchanges used for the domain.                                                                         |
NS    | This record type defines the name servers that are used for this zone.                                                                             |
TXT   | This record type is used to associate a string of text with a hostname, primarily used for verification.                                           |
SRV   | This record type specifies the location (hostname and port number) of servers for specific services.                                               |
SOA   | This record type defines administrative information about the zone. Can only have ttl changed, cannot be deleted                                   |

## List All Domain Records

<a id="opIddomains_list_records"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/domains/example.com/records \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/domains/{domain_name}/records`

To get a listing of all records configured for a domain, send a GET request to `/v2/domains/$DOMAIN_NAME/records`.
The list of records returned can be filtered by using the `name` and `type` query parameters. For example, to only include A records for a domain, send a GET request to `/v2/domains/$DOMAIN_NAME/records?type=A`. `name` must be a fully qualified record name. For example, to only include records matching `sub.example.com`, send a GET request to `/v2/domains/$DOMAIN_NAME/records?name=sub.example.com`. Both name and type may be used together.



<h3 id="list-all-domain-records-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|domain_name|path|string|true|The name of the domain itself.|
|name|query|string|false|A fully qualified record name. For example, to only include records matching sub.example.com, send a GET request to `/v2/domains/$DOMAIN_NAME/records?name=sub.example.com`.|
|type|query|string|false|The type of the DNS record. For example: A, CNAME, TXT, ...|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|A|
|type|AAAA|
|type|CAA|
|type|CNAME|
|type|MX|
|type|NS|
|type|SOA|
|type|SRV|
|type|TXT|

```bash
    "tag": null
  }'
```

## Update a Domain Record

<a id="opIddomains_update_record"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/domains/example.com/records/3352896 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "blog",
    "type": "CNAME"
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/domains/{domain_name}/records/{domain_record_id}`

To update an existing record, send a PUT request to
`/v2/domains/$DOMAIN_NAME/records/$DOMAIN_RECORD_ID`. Any attribute valid for
the record type can be set to a new value for the record.

See the [attribute table](#tag/Domain-Records) for details regarding record
types and their respective attributes.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "blog",
  "type": "CNAME"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-domain-record-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|domain_name|path|string|true|The name of the domain itself.|
|domain_record_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the domain record.|
|body|body|[domain_record](#schemadomain_record)|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of the DNS record. For example: A, CNAME, TXT, ...|
|» name|body|string|false|The host name, alias, or service being defined by the record.|
|» data|body|string|false|Variable data depending on record type. For example, the "data" value for an A record would be the IPv4 address to which the domain will be mapped. For a CAA record, it would contain the domain name of the CA being granted permission to issue certificates.|
|» priority|body|integer \| null|false|The priority for SRV and MX records.|
|» port|body|integer \| null|false|The port for SRV records.|
|» ttl|body|integer|false|This value is the time to live for the record, in seconds. This defines the time frame that clients can cache queried information before a refresh should be requested.|
|» weight|body|integer \| null|false|The weight for SRV records.|
|» flags|body|integer \| null|false|An unsigned integer between 0-255 used for CAA records.|
|» tag|body|string \| null|false|The parameter tag for CAA records. Valid values are "issue", "issuewild", or "iodef"|

```json

    "weight": null,
    "flags": null,

  }
}
```

```json
}
```

## Delete a Domain Record

```bash
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/domains/{domain_name}/records/{domain_record_id}`

To delete a record for a domain, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/domains/$DOMAIN_NAME/records/$DOMAIN_RECORD_ID`.

indicates a successful request with no body returned.

## Update a Domain Record

<a id="opIddomains_patch_record"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/domains/example.com/records/3352896 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "blog",
    "type": "A"
  }'
```

`PATCH /v2/domains/{domain_name}/records/{domain_record_id}`

To update an existing record, send a PATCH request to
`/v2/domains/$DOMAIN_NAME/records/$DOMAIN_RECORD_ID`. Any attribute valid for
the record type can be set to a new value for the record.

See the [attribute table](#tag/Domain-Records) for details regarding record
types and their respective attributes.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "blog",
  "type": "A"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-domain-record-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|domain_name|path|string|true|The name of the domain itself.|
|domain_record_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the domain record.|
|body|body|[domain_record](#schemadomain_record)|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of the DNS record. For example: A, CNAME, TXT, ...|
|» name|body|string|false|The host name, alias, or service being defined by the record.|
|» data|body|string|false|Variable data depending on record type. For example, the "data" value for an A record would be the IPv4 address to which the domain will be mapped. For a CAA record, it would contain the domain name of the CA being granted permission to issue certificates.|
|» priority|body|integer \| null|false|The priority for SRV and MX records.|
|» port|body|integer \| null|false|The port for SRV records.|
|» ttl|body|integer|false|This value is the time to live for the record, in seconds. This defines the time frame that clients can cache queried information before a refresh should be requested.|
|» weight|body|integer \| null|false|The weight for SRV records.|
|» flags|body|integer \| null|false|An unsigned integer between 0-255 used for CAA records.|
|» tag|body|string \| null|false|The parameter tag for CAA records. Valid values are "issue", "issuewild", or "iodef"|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "domain_record": {
    "id": 3352896,
    "type": "A",
    "name": "blog",
    "data": "162.10.66.0",
    "priority": null,
    "port": null,
    "ttl": 1800,
    "weight": null,
    "flags": null,
    "tag": null
  }
}
```

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-domains">Domains</h1>

Domain resources are domain names that you have purchased from a domain
name registrar that you are managing through the
[DigitalOcean DNS interface](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/networking/dns/).

This resource establishes top-level control over each domain. Actions that
affect individual domain records should be taken on the
[Domain Records](#tag/Domain-Records) resource.

## Create a New Domain

<a id="opIddomains_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/domains \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/domains`

To create a new domain, send a POST request to `/v2/domains`. Set the "name"
attribute to the domain name you are adding. Optionally, you may set the
"ip_address" attribute, and an A record will be automatically created pointing
to the apex domain.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-domain-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[domain](#schemadomain)|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the domain itself. This should follow the standard domain format of domain.TLD. For instance, `example.com` is a valid domain name.|
|» ip_address|body|string|false|This optional attribute may contain an IP address. When provided, an A record will be automatically created pointing to the apex domain.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "domain": {
    "name": "example.com",
    "ttl": 1800,
    "zone_file": null
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-droplet-actions">Droplet Actions</h1>

Droplet actions are tasks that can be executed on a Droplet. These can be
things like rebooting, resizing, snapshotting, etc.

Droplet action requests are generally targeted at one of the "actions"
endpoints for a specific Droplet. The specific actions are usually
initiated by sending a POST request with the action and arguments as
parameters.

Droplet action requests create a Droplet actions object, which can be used
to get information about the status of an action. Creating a Droplet
action is asynchronous: the HTTP call will return the action object before
the action has finished processing on the Droplet. The current status of
an action can be retrieved from either the Droplet actions endpoint or the
global actions endpoint. If a Droplet action is uncompleted it may block
the creation of a subsequent action for that Droplet, the locked attribute
of the Droplet will be true and attempts to create a Droplet action will
fail with a status of 422.

## List Actions for a Droplet

`GET /v2/droplets/{droplet_id}/actions`

To retrieve a list of all actions that have been executed for a Droplet, send
a GET request to `/v2/droplets/$DROPLET_ID/actions`.

The results will be returned as a JSON object with an `actions` key. This will
be set to an array filled with `action` objects containing the standard
`action` attributes.

## Initiate a Droplet Action

<a id="opIddropletActions_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/droplets/3164444/actions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "reboot"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/droplets/{droplet_id}/actions`

To initiate an action on a Droplet send a POST request to
`/v2/droplets/$DROPLET_ID/actions`. In the JSON body to the request,
set the `type` attribute to one of the supported action types:

| Action                                   | Details | Required Permissions |
| ---------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------- |
| <nobr>`enable_backups`</nobr>            | Enables backups for a Droplet | <nobr>`droplet:update`</nobr> |
| <nobr>`disable_backups`</nobr>           | Disables backups for a Droplet | <nobr>`droplet:update`</nobr> |
| <nobr>`change_backup_policy`</nobr>      | Update the backup policy for a Droplet | <nobr>`droplet:update`</nobr> |
| <nobr>`reboot`</nobr>                    | Reboots a Droplet. A `reboot` action is an attempt to reboot the Droplet in a graceful way, similar to using the `reboot` command from the console. | <nobr>`droplet:update`</nobr> |
| <nobr>`power_cycle`</nobr>               | Power cycles a Droplet. A `powercycle` action is similar to pushing the reset button on a physical machine, it's similar to booting from scratch. | <nobr>`droplet:update`</nobr> |
| <nobr>`shutdown`</nobr>                  | Shuts down a Droplet. A shutdown action is an attempt to shutdown the Droplet in a graceful way, similar to using the `shutdown` command from the console. Since a `shutdown` command can fail, this action guarantees that the command is issued, not that it succeeds. The preferred way to turn off a Droplet is to attempt a shutdown, with a reasonable timeout, followed by a `power_off` action to ensure the Droplet is off. | <nobr>`droplet:update`</nobr> |
| <nobr>`power_off`</nobr>                 | Powers off a Droplet. A `power_off` event is a hard shutdown and should only be used if the `shutdown` action is not successful. It is similar to cutting the power on a server and could lead to complications. | <nobr>`droplet:update`</nobr> |
| <nobr>`power_on`</nobr>                  | Powers on a Droplet. | <nobr>`droplet:update`</nobr> |
| <nobr>`restore`</nobr>                   | Restore a Droplet using a backup image. The image ID that is passed in must be a backup of the current Droplet instance. The operation will leave any embedded SSH keys intact. | <nobr>`droplet:update`</nobr><br><nobr>`droplet:admin`</nobr> |
| <nobr>`password_reset`</nobr>            | Resets the root password for a Droplet. A new password will be provided via email. It must be changed after first use. | <nobr>`droplet:update`</nobr><br><nobr>`droplet:admin`</nobr> |
| <nobr>`resize`</nobr>                    | Resizes a Droplet. Set the `size` attribute to a size slug. If a permanent resize with disk changes included is desired, set the `disk` attribute to `true`. | <nobr>`droplet:update`</nobr><br><nobr>`droplet:create`</nobr> |
| <nobr>`rebuild`</nobr>                   | Rebuilds a Droplet from a new base image. Set the `image` attribute to an image ID or slug. | <nobr>`droplet:update`</nobr><br><nobr>`droplet:admin`</nobr> |
| <nobr>`rename`</nobr>                    | Renames a Droplet. | <nobr>`droplet:update`</nobr> |
| <nobr>`change_kernel`</nobr>             | Changes a Droplet's kernel. Only applies to Droplets with externally managed kernels. All Droplets created after March 2017 use internal kernels by default. | <nobr>`droplet:update`</nobr> |
| <nobr>`enable_ipv6`</nobr>               | Enables IPv6 for a Droplet. Once enabled for a Droplet, IPv6 can not be disabled. **Warning:** The Droplet must be powered off before enabling IPv6 on an existing Droplet. When enabling IPv6 on an existing Droplet, [additional OS-level configuration](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/networking/ipv6/how-to/enable/#on-existing-droplets) is required. | <nobr>`droplet:update`</nobr> |
| <nobr>`snapshot`</nobr>                  | Takes a snapshot of a Droplet. | <nobr>`droplet:update`</nobr><br><nobr>`image:create`</nobr> |


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "reboot"
}
```

<h3 id="initiate-a-droplet-action-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|droplet_id|path|integer|true|A unique identifier for a Droplet instance.|
|body|body|[droplet_action](#schemadroplet_action) \| [droplet_action_enable_backups](#schemadroplet_action_enable_backups) \| [droplet_action_change_backup_policy](#schemadroplet_action_change_backup_policy) \| [droplet_action_restore](#schemadroplet_action_restore) \| [droplet_action_resize](#schemadroplet_action_resize) \| [droplet_action_rebuild](#schemadroplet_action_rebuild) \| [droplet_action_rename](#schemadroplet_action_rename) \| [droplet_action_change_kernel](#schemadroplet_action_change_kernel) \| [droplet_action_snapshot](#schemadroplet_action_snapshot)|false|The `type` attribute set in the request body will specify the  action that<br>will be taken on the Droplet. Some actions will require additional<br>attributes to be set as well.<br>|
|» *anyOf*|body|[droplet_action](#schemadroplet_action)|false|Specifies the action that will be taken on the Droplet.|
|» *anyOf*|body|[droplet_action_enable_backups](#schemadroplet_action_enable_backups)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[droplet_action_change_backup_policy](#schemadroplet_action_change_backup_policy)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[droplet_action_restore](#schemadroplet_action_restore)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[droplet_action_resize](#schemadroplet_action_resize)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[droplet_action_rebuild](#schemadroplet_action_rebuild)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[droplet_action_rename](#schemadroplet_action_rename)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[droplet_action_change_kernel](#schemadroplet_action_change_kernel)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[droplet_action_snapshot](#schemadroplet_action_snapshot)|false|none|

## Acting on Tagged Droplets

<a id="opIddropletActions_post_byTag"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/droplets/actions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "reboot"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/droplets/actions`

Some actions can be performed in bulk on tagged Droplets. The actions can be
initiated by sending a POST to `/v2/droplets/actions?tag_name=$TAG_NAME` with
the action arguments.

Only a sub-set of action types are supported:

- `power_cycle`
- `power_on`
- `power_off`
- `shutdown`
- `enable_ipv6` (**Warning:** The Droplet must be powered off before enabling IPv6 on an existing Droplet.)
- `enable_backups`
- `disable_backups`
- `snapshot` (also requires `image:create` permission)


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "reboot"
}
```

<h3 id="acting-on-tagged-droplets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tag_name|query|string|false|Used to filter Droplets by a specific tag. Can not be combined with `name` or `type`.<br>Requires `tag:read` scope.|
|body|body|[droplet_action](#schemadroplet_action) \| [droplet_action_snapshot](#schemadroplet_action_snapshot)|false|The `type` attribute set in the request body will specify the action that<br>will be taken on the Droplet. Some actions will require additional<br>attributes to be set as well.<br>|
|» *oneOf*|body|[droplet_action](#schemadroplet_action)|false|Specifies the action that will be taken on the Droplet.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[droplet_action_snapshot](#schemadroplet_action_snapshot)|false|none|

> Example responses

## Retrieve a Droplet Action

<a id="opIddropletActions_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/droplets/3164444/actions/36804636 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/droplets/{droplet_id}/actions/{action_id}`

To retrieve a Droplet action, send a GET request to
`/v2/droplets/$DROPLET_ID/actions/$ACTION_ID`.

The response will be a JSON object with a key called `action`. The value will
be a Droplet action object.

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-droplets">Droplets</h1>

A [Droplet](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/droplets/) is a DigitalOcean
virtual machine. By sending requests to the Droplet endpoint, you can
list, create, or delete Droplets.

Some of the attributes will have an object value. The `region` and `image`
objects will all contain the standard attributes of their associated
types. Find more information about each of these objects in their
respective sections.

## List All Droplets

<a id="opIddroplets_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/droplets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/droplets`

To list all Droplets in your account, send a GET request to `/v2/droplets`.

The response body will be a JSON object with a key of `droplets`. This will be
set to an array containing objects each representing a Droplet. These will
contain the standard Droplet attributes.

### Filtering Results by Tag

It's possible to request filtered results by including certain query parameters.
To only list Droplets assigned to a specific tag, include the `tag_name` query
parameter set to the name of the tag in your GET request. For example,
`/v2/droplets?tag_name=$TAG_NAME`.

### GPU Droplets

By default, only non-GPU Droplets are returned. To list only GPU Droplets, set
the `type` query parameter to `gpus`. For example, `/v2/droplets?type=gpus`.


<h3 id="list-all-droplets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|
|tag_name|query|string|false|Used to filter Droplets by a specific tag. Can not be combined with `name` or `type`.<br>Requires `tag:read` scope.|
|name|query|string|false|Used to filter list response by Droplet name returning only exact matches. It is case-insensitive and can not be combined with `tag_name`.|
|type|query|string|false|When `type` is set to `gpus`, only GPU Droplets will be returned. By default, only non-GPU Droplets are returned. Can not be combined with `tag_name`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|droplets|
|type|gpus|

## Create a New Droplet

<a id="opIddroplets_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/droplets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "example.com",
    "region": "nyc3",
    "size": "s-1vcpu-1gb",
    "image": "ubuntu-20-04-x64",
    "ssh_keys": [
      289794,
      "3b:16:e4:bf:8b:00:8b:b8:59:8c:a9:d3:f0:19:fa:45"
    ],
    "backups": true,
    "ipv6": true,
    "monitoring": true,
    "tags": [
      "env:prod",
      "web"
    ],
    "user_data": "#cloud-config\nruncmd:\n  - touch /test.txt\n",
    "vpc_uuid": "760e09ef-dc84-11e8-981e-3cfdfeaae000",
    "subnet_uuid": "9c7a0d63-3c4e-4d3d-9f56-3b0fb0e5e4a1"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/droplets`

To create a new Droplet, send a POST request to `/v2/droplets` setting the
required attributes.

A Droplet will be created using the provided information. The response body
will contain a JSON object with a key called `droplet`. The value will be an
object containing the standard attributes for your new Droplet. The response
code, 202 Accepted, does not indicate the success or failure of the operation,
just that the request has been accepted for processing. The `actions` returned
as part of the response's `links` object can be used to check the status
of the Droplet create event.

### Create Multiple Droplets

Creating multiple Droplets is very similar to creating a single Droplet.
Instead of sending `name` as a string, send `names` as an array of strings. A
Droplet will be created for each name you send using the associated
information. Up to ten Droplets may be created this way at a time.

Rather than returning a single Droplet, the response body will contain a JSON
array with a key called `droplets`. This will be set to an array of JSON
objects, each of which will contain the standard Droplet attributes. The
response code, 202 Accepted, does not indicate the success or failure of any
operation, just that the request has been accepted for processing. The array
of `actions` returned as part of the response's `links` object can be used to
check the status of each individual Droplet create event.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "example.com",
  "region": "nyc3",
  "size": "s-1vcpu-1gb",
  "image": "ubuntu-20-04-x64",
  "ssh_keys": [
    289794,
    "3b:16:e4:bf:8b:00:8b:b8:59:8c:a9:d3:f0:19:fa:45"
  ],
  "backups": true,
  "ipv6": true,
  "monitoring": true,
  "tags": [
    "env:prod",
    "web"
  ],
  "user_data": "#cloud-config\nruncmd:\n  - touch /test.txt\n",
  "vpc_uuid": "760e09ef-dc84-11e8-981e-3cfdfeaae000",
  "subnet_uuid": "9c7a0d63-3c4e-4d3d-9f56-3b0fb0e5e4a1"
}
```

## Deleting Droplets by Tag

<a id="opIddroplets_destroy_byTag"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/droplets?tag_name=env%3Atest' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/droplets`

To delete **all** Droplets assigned to a specific tag, include the `tag_name`
query parameter set to the name of the tag in your DELETE request. For
example, `/v2/droplets?tag_name=$TAG_NAME`.

This endpoint requires `tag:read` scope.

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.
This indicates that the request was processed successfully.


<h3 id="deleting-droplets-by-tag-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tag_name|query|string|true|Specifies Droplets to be deleted by tag.|

## List Backups for a Droplet

<a id="opIddroplets_list_backups"></a>

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

```

`GET /v2/droplets/{droplet_id}/backups`

## List Neighbors for a Droplet

<a id="opIddroplets_list_neighbors"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/droplets/3164444/neighbors \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/droplets/{droplet_id}/neighbors`

To retrieve a list of any "neighbors" (i.e. Droplets that are co-located on
the same physical hardware) for a specific Droplet, send a GET request to
`/v2/droplets/$DROPLET_ID/neighbors`.

The results will be returned as a JSON object with a key of `droplets`. This
will be set to an array containing objects representing any other Droplets
that share the same physical hardware. An empty array indicates that the
Droplet is not co-located any other Droplets associated with your account.


<h3 id="list-neighbors-for-a-droplet-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|droplet_id|path|integer|true|A unique identifier for a Droplet instance.|

`GET /v2/droplets/{droplet_id}/destroy_with_associated_resources`

To list the associated billable resources that can be destroyed along with a
Droplet, send a GET request to the
`/v2/droplets/$DROPLET_ID/destroy_with_associated_resources` endpoint.

This endpoint will only return resources that you are authorized to see. For
example, to see associated Reserved IPs, include the `reserved_ip:read` scope.

The response will be a JSON object containing `snapshots`, `volumes`, and
`volume_snapshots` keys. Each will be set to an array of objects containing
information about the associated resources.

|droplet_id|path|integer|true|A unique identifier for a Droplet instance.|

## Selectively Destroy a Droplet and its Associated Resources

<a id="opIddroplets_destroy_withAssociatedResourcesSelective"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/droplets/3164444/destroy_with_associated_resources/selective \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "floating_ips": [
      "6186916"
    ],
    "reserved_ips": [
      "6186916"
    ],
    "snapshots": [
      "61486916"
    ],
    "volumes": [
      "ba49449a-7435-11ea-b89e-0a58ac14480f"
    ],
    "volume_snapshots": [
      "edb0478d-7436-11ea-86e6-0a58ac144b91"
    ]
  }'
```

`DELETE /v2/droplets/{droplet_id}/destroy_with_associated_resources/selective`

To destroy a Droplet along with a sub-set of its associated resources, send a
DELETE request to the `/v2/droplets/$DROPLET_ID/destroy_with_associated_resources/selective`
endpoint. The JSON body of the request should include `reserved_ips`, `snapshots`, `volumes`,
or `volume_snapshots` keys each set to an array of IDs for the associated
resources to be destroyed. The IDs can be found by querying the Droplet's
associated resources. Any associated resource not included in the request
will remain and continue to accrue changes on your account.

A successful response will include a 202 response code and no content. Use
the status endpoint to check on the success or failure of the destruction of
the individual resources.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "floating_ips": [
    "6186916"
  ],
  "reserved_ips": [
    "6186916"
  ],
  "snapshots": [
    "61486916"
  ],
  "volumes": [
    "ba49449a-7435-11ea-b89e-0a58ac14480f"
  ],
  "volume_snapshots": [
    "edb0478d-7436-11ea-86e6-0a58ac144b91"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="selectively-destroy-a-droplet-and-its-associated-resources-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|droplet_id|path|integer|true|A unique identifier for a Droplet instance.|
|body|body|[selective_destroy_associated_resource](#schemaselective_destroy_associated_resource)|false|none|
|» floating_ips|body|[string]|false|**Deprecated.** An array of unique identifiers for the floating IPs to be scheduled for deletion.|
|» reserved_ips|body|[string]|false|An array of unique identifiers for the reserved IPs to be scheduled for deletion.|
|» snapshots|body|[string]|false|An array of unique identifiers for the snapshots to be scheduled for deletion.|
|» volumes|body|[string]|false|An array of unique identifiers for the volumes to be scheduled for deletion.|
|» volume_snapshots|body|[string]|false|An array of unique identifiers for the volume snapshots to be scheduled for deletion.|

## Destroy a Droplet and All of its Associated Resources (Dangerous)

<a id="opIddroplets_destroy_withAssociatedResourcesDangerous"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/droplets/3164444/destroy_with_associated_resources/dangerous \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'X-Dangerous: true'
```

`DELETE /v2/droplets/{droplet_id}/destroy_with_associated_resources/dangerous`

To destroy a Droplet along with all of its associated resources, send a DELETE
request to the `/v2/droplets/$DROPLET_ID/destroy_with_associated_resources/dangerous`
endpoint. The headers of this request must include an `X-Dangerous` key set to
`true`. To preview which resources will be destroyed, first query the
Droplet's associated resources. This operation _can not_ be reverse and should
be used with caution.

A successful response will include a 202 response code and no content. Use the
status endpoint to check on the success or failure of the destruction of the
individual resources.


<h3 id="destroy-a-droplet-and-all-of-its-associated-resources-dangerous-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|droplet_id|path|integer|true|A unique identifier for a Droplet instance.|
|X-Dangerous|header|boolean|true|Acknowledge this action will destroy the Droplet and all associated resources and _can not_ be reversed.|

## Retry a Droplet Destroy with Associated Resources Request

<a id="opIddroplets_destroy_retryWithAssociatedResources"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/droplets/3164444/destroy_with_associated_resources/retry \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/droplets/{droplet_id}/destroy_with_associated_resources/retry`

If the status of a request to destroy a Droplet with its associated resources
reported any errors, it can be retried by sending a POST request to the
`/v2/droplets/$DROPLET_ID/destroy_with_associated_resources/retry` endpoint.

Only one destroy can be active at a time per Droplet. If a retry is issued
while another destroy is in progress for the Droplet a 409 status code will
be returned. A successful response will include a 202 response code and no
content.


<h3 id="retry-a-droplet-destroy-with-associated-resources-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|droplet_id|path|integer|true|A unique identifier for a Droplet instance.|

## List All Droplet Neighbors

<a id="opIddroplets_list_neighborsIds"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/reports/droplet_neighbors_ids \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/reports/droplet_neighbors_ids`

To retrieve a list of all Droplets that are co-located on the same physical
hardware, send a GET request to `/v2/reports/droplet_neighbors_ids`.

The results will be returned as a JSON object with a key of `neighbor_ids`.
This will be set to an array of arrays. Each array will contain a set of
Droplet IDs for Droplets that share a physical server. An empty array
indicates that all Droplets associated with your account are located on
separate physical hardware.

```json
}
```

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-droplet-autoscale-pools">Droplet Autoscale Pools</h1>

Droplet autoscale pools manage automatic horizontal scaling for your applications based on resource usage (CPU, memory, or both) or a static configuration.

## List All Autoscale Pools

<a id="opIdautoscalepools_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/droplets/autoscale \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/droplets/autoscale`

To list all autoscale pools in your team, send a GET request to `/v2/droplets/autoscale`.
The response body will be a JSON object with a key of `autoscale_pools` containing an array of autoscale pool objects.
These each contain the standard autoscale pool attributes.


<h3 id="list-all-autoscale-pools-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|
|name|query|string|false|The name of the autoscale pool|

## Create a New Autoscale Pool

<a id="opIdautoscalepools_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/droplets/autoscale \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "my-autoscale-pool",
    "config": {
      "min_instances": 1,
      "max_instances": 5,
      "target_cpu_utilization": 0.5,
      "cooldown_minutes": 10
    },
    "droplet_template": {
      "name": "example.com",
      "region": "nyc3",
      "size": "c-2",
      "image": "ubuntu-20-04-x64",
      "ssh_keys": [
        "3b:16:e4:bf:8b:00:8b:b8:59:8c:a9:d3:f0:19:fa:45"
      ],
      "backups": true,
      "ipv6": true,
      "monitoring": true,
      "tags": [
        "env:prod",
        "web"
      ],
      "user_data": "#cloud-config\nruncmd:\n  - touch /test.txt\n",
      "vpc_uuid": "760e09ef-dc84-11e8-981e-3cfdfeaae000"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v2/droplets/autoscale`

To create a new autoscale pool, send a POST request to `/v2/droplets/autoscale` setting the required attributes.

The response body will contain a JSON object with a key called `autoscale_pool` containing the standard attributes for the new autoscale pool.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "my-autoscale-pool",
  "config": {
    "min_instances": 1,
    "max_instances": 5,
    "target_cpu_utilization": 0.5,
    "cooldown_minutes": 10
  },
  "droplet_template": {
    "name": "example.com",
    "region": "nyc3",
    "size": "c-2",
    "image": "ubuntu-20-04-x64",
    "ssh_keys": [
      "3b:16:e4:bf:8b:00:8b:b8:59:8c:a9:d3:f0:19:fa:45"
    ],
    "backups": true,
    "ipv6": true,
    "monitoring": true,
    "tags": [
      "env:prod",
      "web"
    ],
    "user_data": "#cloud-config\nruncmd:\n  - touch /test.txt\n",
    "vpc_uuid": "760e09ef-dc84-11e8-981e-3cfdfeaae000"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-autoscale-pool-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[autoscale_pool_create](#schemaautoscale_pool_create)|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The human-readable name of the autoscale pool. This field cannot be updated|
|» config|body|object|true|The scaling configuration for an autoscale pool, which is how the pool scales up and down (either by resource utilization or static configuration).|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[autoscale_pool_static_config](#schemaautoscale_pool_static_config)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[autoscale_pool_dynamic_config](#schemaautoscale_pool_dynamic_config)|false|none|
|» droplet_template|body|[autoscale_pool_droplet_template](#schemaautoscale_pool_droplet_template)|true|none|

```bash
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/droplets/autoscale/{autoscale_pool_id}`

To update the configuration of an existing autoscale pool, send a PUT request to
`/v2/droplets/autoscale/$AUTOSCALE_POOL_ID`. The request must contain a full representation
of the autoscale pool including existing attributes. 


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "my-autoscale-pool",
  "config": {
    "target_number_instances": 2
  },
  "droplet_template": {
    "name": "example.com",
    "region": "nyc3",
    "size": "c-2",
    "image": "ubuntu-20-04-x64",
    "ssh_keys": [

  }
}
```

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-firewalls">Firewalls</h1>

[DigitalOcean Cloud Firewalls](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/networking/firewalls/)
provide the ability to restrict network access to and from a Droplet
allowing you to define which ports will accept inbound or outbound
connections. By sending requests to the `/v2/firewalls` endpoint, you can
list, create, or delete firewalls as well as modify access rules.

## List All Firewalls

<a id="opIdfirewalls_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/firewalls \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/firewalls`

To list all of the firewalls available on your account, send a GET request to `/v2/firewalls`.

## Create a New Firewall

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/firewalls \
  -X POST \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "firewall",
    "inbound_rules": [
      {
        "protocol": "tcp",
        "ports": "80",
        "action": "allow",
        "sources": {

          ]
        }
      },
      {
        "protocol": "tcp",
        "ports": "22",
        "action": "allow",
        "sources": {

        "protocol": "tcp",
        "ports": "80",
        "action": "allow",
        "destinations": {
          "addresses": [
            "0.0.0.0/0",
            "::/0"
          ]
        }
      }
    ],
    "droplet_ids": [
      8043964
```
```bash
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/firewalls/{firewall_id}`

To update the configuration of an existing firewall, send a PUT request to
`/v2/firewalls/$FIREWALL_ID`. The request should contain a full representation
of the firewall including existing attributes. **Note that any attributes that
are not provided will be reset to their default values.**
<br><br>You must have read access (e.g. `droplet:read`) to all resources attached
to the firewall to successfully update the firewall.

```json
  "inbound_rules": [
    {
      "protocol": "tcp",
      "ports": "8080",

      "ports": "8080",
      "action": "allow",
      "destinations": {
        "addresses": [
          "0.0.0.0/0",
          "::/0"
```

|» » » kubernetes_ids|body|[string]|false|An array containing the IDs of the Kubernetes clusters to which the firewall will allow traffic.|

## Add Rules to a Firewall

<a id="opIdfirewalls_add_rules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/firewalls/bb4b2611-3d72-467b-8602-280330ecd65c/rules \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "inbound_rules": [
      {
        "protocol": "tcp",
        "ports": "3306",
        "action": "allow",
        "sources": {
          "droplet_ids": [
            49696269
          ]
        }
      }
    ],
    "outbound_rules": [
      {
        "protocol": "tcp",
        "ports": "3306",
        "action": "allow",
        "destinations": {
          "droplet_ids": [
            49696269
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/firewalls/{firewall_id}/rules`

To add additional access rules to a firewall, send a POST request to
`/v2/firewalls/$FIREWALL_ID/rules`. The body of the request may include an
inbound_rules and/or outbound_rules attribute containing an array of rules to
be added.

No response body will be sent back, but the response code will indicate
success. Specifically, the response code will be a 204, which means that the
action was successful with no returned body data.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "inbound_rules": [
    {
      "protocol": "tcp",
      "ports": "3306",
      "action": "allow",
      "sources": {
        "droplet_ids": [
          49696269
        ]
      }
    }
  ],
  "outbound_rules": [
    {
      "protocol": "tcp",
      "ports": "3306",
      "action": "allow",
      "destinations": {
        "droplet_ids": [
          49696269
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-rules-to-a-firewall-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|firewall_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique ID that can be used to identify and reference a firewall.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» inbound_rules|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » protocol|body|string|true|The type of traffic to be allowed. This may be one of `tcp`, `udp`, or `icmp`.|
|» » ports|body|string|true|The ports on which traffic will be allowed specified as a string containing a single port, a range (e.g. "8000-9000"), or "0" when all ports are open for a protocol. For ICMP rules this parameter will always return "0".|
|» » action|body|string|false|The action to be taken when traffic matches the rule. This may be one of `allow` or `deny`. For backward compatibility, this field is optional. When not set, it defaults to `allow`.|
|» » sources|body|object|true|none|
|» » » addresses|body|[string]|false|An array of strings containing the IPv4 addresses, IPv6 addresses, IPv4 CIDRs, and/or IPv6 CIDRs to which the firewall will allow traffic.|
|» » » droplet_ids|body|[integer]|false|An array containing the IDs of the Droplets to which the firewall will allow traffic.|
|» » » load_balancer_uids|body|[string]|false|An array containing the IDs of the load balancers to which the firewall will allow traffic.|
|» » » kubernetes_ids|body|[string]|false|An array containing the IDs of the Kubernetes clusters to which the firewall will allow traffic.|
|» » » tags|body|object|false|none|
|» outbound_rules|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » protocol|body|string|true|The type of traffic to be allowed. This may be one of `tcp`, `udp`, or `icmp`.|

|» » action|body|string|false|The action to be taken when traffic matches the rule. This may be one of `allow` or `deny`. For backward compatibility, this field is optional. When not set, it defaults to `allow`.|
|» » destinations|body|object|true|none|
|» » » addresses|body|[string]|false|An array of strings containing the IPv4 addresses, IPv6 addresses, IPv4 CIDRs, and/or IPv6 CIDRs to which the firewall will allow traffic.|
|» » » droplet_ids|body|[integer]|false|An array containing the IDs of the Droplets to which the firewall will allow traffic.|

|» » » kubernetes_ids|body|[string]|false|An array containing the IDs of the Kubernetes clusters to which the firewall will allow traffic.|

<a id="opIdfirewalls_delete_rules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/firewalls/bb4b2611-3d72-467b-8602-280330ecd65c/rules \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "inbound_rules": [
      {
        "protocol": "tcp",
        "ports": "3306",
        "action": "allow",
        "sources": {
          "droplet_ids": [
            49696269
          ]
        }
      }
    ],
    "outbound_rules": [
      {
        "protocol": "tcp",
        "ports": "3306",
        "action": "allow",
        "destinations": {
          "droplet_ids": [
            49696269
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`DELETE /v2/firewalls/{firewall_id}/rules`

To remove access rules from a firewall, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/firewalls/$FIREWALL_ID/rules`. The body of the request may include an
`inbound_rules` and/or `outbound_rules` attribute containing an array of rules
to be removed.

No response body will be sent back, but the response code will indicate
success. Specifically, the response code will be a 204, which means that the
action was successful with no returned body data.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "inbound_rules": [
    {
      "protocol": "tcp",
      "ports": "3306",
      "action": "allow",
      "sources": {
        "droplet_ids": [
          49696269
        ]
      }
    }
  ],
  "outbound_rules": [
    {
      "protocol": "tcp",
      "ports": "3306",
      "action": "allow",
      "destinations": {
        "droplet_ids": [
          49696269
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

|» » ports|body|string|true|The ports on which traffic will be allowed specified as a string containing a single port, a range (e.g. "8000-9000"), or "0" when all ports are open for a protocol. For ICMP rules this parameter will always return "0".|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-floating-ip-actions">Floating IP Actions</h1>

As of 16 June 2022, we have renamed the Floating IP product to [Reserved IPs](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/api-reference/#tag/Reserved-IPs).
The Reserved IP product's endpoints function the exact same way as Floating IPs.
The only difference is the name change throughout the URLs and fields.
For example, the `floating_ips` field is now the `reserved_ips` field.
The Floating IP endpoints will remain active until fall 2023 before being
permanently deprecated.

With the exception of the [Projects API](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/api-reference/#tag/Projects),
we will reflect this change as an additional field in the responses across the API
where the `floating_ip` field is used. For example, the Droplet metadata response
will contain the field `reserved_ips` in addition to the `floating_ips` field.
Floating IPs retrieved using the Projects API will retain the original name.

Floating IP actions are commands that can be given to a DigitalOcean
floating IP. These requests are made on the actions endpoint of a specific
floating IP.

An action object is returned. These objects hold the current status of the
requested action.

## Initiate a Floating IP Action

<a id="opIdfloatingIPsAction_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/floating_ips/45.55.96.47/actions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "assign"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/floating_ips/{floating_ip}/actions`

To initiate an action on a floating IP send a POST request to
`/v2/floating_ips/$FLOATING_IP/actions`. In the JSON body to the request,
set the `type` attribute to on of the supported action types:

| Action     | Details
|------------|--------
| `assign`   | Assigns a floating IP to a Droplet
| `unassign` | Unassign a floating IP from a Droplet


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "assign"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|floating_ip|path|string(ipv4)|true|A floating IP address.|
|body|body|[floating_ip_action_unassign](#schemafloating_ip_action_unassign) \| [floating_ip_action_assign](#schemafloating_ip_action_assign)|false|The `type` attribute set in the request body will specify the action that<br>will be taken on the floating IP.<br>|
|» *anyOf*|body|[floating_ip_action_unassign](#schemafloating_ip_action_unassign)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[floating_ip_action_assign](#schemafloating_ip_action_assign)|false|none|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-floating-ips">Floating IPs</h1>

As of 16 June 2022, we have renamed the Floating IP product to [Reserved IPs](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/api-reference/#tag/Reserved-IPs).
The Reserved IP product's endpoints function the exact same way as Floating IPs.
The only difference is the name change throughout the URLs and fields.
For example, the `floating_ips` field is now the `reserved_ips` field.
The Floating IP endpoints will remain active until fall 2023 before being
permanently deprecated.

With the exception of the [Projects API](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/api-reference/#tag/Projects),
we will reflect this change as an additional field in the responses across the API
where the `floating_ip` field is used. For example, the Droplet metadata response
will contain the field `reserved_ips` in addition to the `floating_ips` field.
Floating IPs retrieved using the Projects API will retain the original name.

[DigitalOcean Floating IPs](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/networking/reserved-ips/)
are publicly-accessible static IP addresses that can be mapped to one of
your Droplets. They can be used to create highly available setups or other
configurations requiring movable addresses.

Floating IPs are bound to a specific region.

## Create a New Floating IP

<a id="opIdfloatingIPs_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/floating_ips \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "droplet_id": 2457247
  }'
```

`POST /v2/floating_ips`

On creation, a floating IP must be either assigned to a Droplet or reserved to a region.
* To create a new floating IP assigned to a Droplet, send a POST
  request to `/v2/floating_ips` with the `droplet_id` attribute.

* To create a new floating IP reserved to a region, send a POST request to
  `/v2/floating_ips` with the `region` attribute.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "droplet_id": 2457247
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-floating-ip-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[floating_ip_create](#schemafloating_ip_create)|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» droplet_id|body|integer|true|The ID of the Droplet that the floating IP will be assigned to.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» region|body|string|true|The slug identifier for the region the floating IP will be reserved to.|
|» project_id|body|string(uuid)|false|The UUID of the project to which the floating IP will be assigned.|

## Delete a Floating IP

<a id="opIdfloatingIPs_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/floating_ips/45.55.96.47 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/floating_ips/{floating_ip}`

To delete a floating IP and remove it from your account, send a DELETE request
to `/v2/floating_ips/$FLOATING_IP_ADDR`.

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.
This indicates that the request was processed successfully.

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-functions">Functions</h1>

[Serverless functions](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/functions) are blocks of code that run on demand without the need to manage any infrastructure.
You can develop functions on your local machine and then deploy them to a namespace using `doctl`, the [official DigitalOcean CLI tool](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl).

The Serverless Functions API currently only supports creating and managing namespaces.

## Create Namespace

<a id="opIdfunctions_create_namespace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/functions/namespaces \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "region": "nyc1",
    "label": "my namespace"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/functions/namespaces`

Creates a new serverless functions namespace in the desired region and associates it with the provided label. A namespace is a collection of functions and their associated packages, triggers, and project specifications. To create a namespace, send a POST request to `/v2/functions/namespaces` with the `region` and `label` properties.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "region": "nyc1",
  "label": "my namespace"
}
```

<h3 id="create-namespace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[create_namespace](#schemacreate_namespace)|true|none|
|» region|body|string|true|The [datacenter region](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/platform/availability-matrix/#available-datacenters) in which to create the namespace.|
|» label|body|string|true|The namespace's unique name.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "namespace": {
    "api_host": "https://api_host.io",
    "namespace": "fn-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx",
    "created_at": "2022-09-14T04:16:45Z",
    "updated_at": "2022-09-14T04:16:45Z",

    "region": "nyc1",

}
```

## Delete Namespace

<a id="opIdfunctions_delete_namespace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/functions/namespaces/fn-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/functions/namespaces/{namespace_id}`

Deletes the given namespace.  When a namespace is deleted all assets, in the namespace are deleted, this includes packages, functions and triggers. Deleting a namespace is a destructive operation and assets in the namespace are not recoverable after deletion. Some metadata is retained, such as activations, or soft deleted for reporting purposes.
To delete namespace, send a DELETE request to `/v2/functions/namespaces/$NAMESPACE_ID`.
A successful deletion returns a 204 response.

<h3 id="delete-namespace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace_id|path|string|true|The ID of the namespace to be managed.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "namespace not found",
  "request_id": "88d17b7a-630b-4083-99ce-5b91045efdb4"
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

## Create Trigger

<a id="opIdfunctions_create_trigger"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/functions/namespaces/fn-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx/triggers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "my trigger",
    "function": "hello",
    "type": "SCHEDULED",
    "is_enabled": true,
    "scheduled_details": {
      "cron": "* * * * *",
      "body": {
        "name": "Welcome to DO!"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v2/functions/namespaces/{namespace_id}/triggers`

Creates a new trigger for a given function in a namespace. To create a trigger, send a POST request to `/v2/functions/namespaces/$NAMESPACE_ID/triggers` with the `name`, `function`, `type`, `is_enabled` and `scheduled_details` properties.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "my trigger",
  "function": "hello",
  "type": "SCHEDULED",
  "is_enabled": true,
  "scheduled_details": {
    "cron": "* * * * *",
    "body": {
      "name": "Welcome to DO!"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-trigger-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace_id|path|string|true|The ID of the namespace to be managed.|
|body|body|[create_trigger](#schemacreate_trigger)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The trigger's unique name within the namespace.|
|» function|body|string|true|Name of function(action) that exists in the given namespace.|
|» type|body|string|true|One of different type of triggers. Currently only SCHEDULED is supported.|
|» is_enabled|body|boolean|true|Indicates weather the trigger is paused or unpaused.|
|» scheduled_details|body|[scheduled_details](#schemascheduled_details)|true|Trigger details for SCHEDULED type, where body is optional.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "trigger": {
    "namespace": "fn-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx",
    "name": "my trigger",
    "function": "hello",
    "type": "SCHEDULED",
    "is_enabled": true,
    "created_at": "2022-11-11T04:16:45Z",
    "updated_at": "2022-11-11T04:16:45Z",
    "scheduled_details": {
      "cron": "* * * * *",
      "body": {
        "name": "Welcome to DO!"
      }
    },
    "scheduled_runs": {
      "last_run_at": "2022-11-11T04:16:45Z",
      "next_run_at": "2022-11-11T04:16:45Z"
    }
  }
}
```

```json
  "id": "bad_request",
  "message": "validating create trigger: validation error: missing trigger name, missing function name, missing source details",
  "request_id": "4851a473-1621-42ea-b2f9-5071c0ea8414"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "namespace not found",
  "request_id": "88d17b7a-630b-4083-99ce-5b91045efdb4"

```

> 422 Response

`GET /v2/functions/namespaces/{namespace_id}/triggers/{trigger_name}`

Gets the trigger details. To get the trigger details, send a GET request to `/v2/functions/namespaces/$NAMESPACE_ID/triggers/$TRIGGER_NAME`.

## Update Trigger

<a id="opIdfunctions_update_trigger"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/functions/namespaces/fn-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx/triggers/my%20trigger \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "is_enabled": true,
    "scheduled_details": {
      "cron": "* * * * *",
      "body": {
        "name": "Welcome to DO!"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/functions/namespaces/{namespace_id}/triggers/{trigger_name}`

Updates the details of the given trigger. To update a trigger, send a PUT request to `/v2/functions/namespaces/$NAMESPACE_ID/triggers/$TRIGGER_NAME` with new values for the `is_enabled ` or `scheduled_details` properties.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "is_enabled": true,
  "scheduled_details": {
    "cron": "* * * * *",
    "body": {
      "name": "Welcome to DO!"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-trigger-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace_id|path|string|true|The ID of the namespace to be managed.|
|trigger_name|path|string|true|The name of the trigger to be managed.|
|body|body|[update_trigger](#schemaupdate_trigger)|true|none|
|» is_enabled|body|boolean|false|Indicates weather the trigger is paused or unpaused.|
|» scheduled_details|body|[scheduled_details](#schemascheduled_details)|false|Trigger details for SCHEDULED type, where body is optional.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "trigger": {
    "namespace": "fn-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx",
    "name": "my trigger",
    "function": "hello",
    "type": "SCHEDULED",
    "is_enabled": true,
    "created_at": "2022-11-11T04:16:45Z",
    "updated_at": "2022-11-11T04:16:45Z",
    "scheduled_details": {
      "cron": "* * * * *",
      "body": {
        "name": "Welcome to DO!"
      }
    },
    "scheduled_runs": {
      "last_run_at": "2022-11-11T04:16:45Z",
      "next_run_at": "2022-11-11T04:16:45Z"
    }
  }
}
```

`DELETE /v2/functions/namespaces/{namespace_id}/triggers/{trigger_name}`

## Create a Namespace Access Key

<a id="opIdfunctionsAccessKey_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/functions/namespaces/fn-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx/keys \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "my-function-access-key"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/functions/namespaces/{namespace_id}/keys`

Creates a new access key for a serverless functions namespace. 
The access key can be used to authenticate requests to the namespace's functions.
The secret key is only returned once upon creation.

To create an access key, send a POST request to `/v2/functions/namespaces/{namespace_id}/keys`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "my-function-access-key"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-namespace-access-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace_id|path|string|true|The ID of the namespace to be managed.|
|body|body|[access_key_create_request](#schemaaccess_key_create_request)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The access key's name.|
|» expires_in|body|string|false|The duration after which the access key expires, specified as a human-readable duration string in the format `<int>h` (hours) or `<int>d` (days). Minimum value is `1h`. If omitted, the key will never expire.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "access_key": {
    "id": "dof_v1-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx",
    "name": "my-function-access-key",
    "secret": "DOSECRETKEYEXAMPLE",
    "expires_at": "2026-12-19T10:30:00Z",
    "created_at": "2025-12-19T10:30:00Z",
    "updated_at": "2025-12-19T10:30:00Z"
  }
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "namespace not found",
  "request_id": "88d17b7a-630b-4083-99ce-5b91045efdb4"
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "id": "conflict",
  "message": "The request could not be completed due to a conflict."
}
```

```json
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

```json
  "id": "server_error",

}
```

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-image-actions">Image Actions</h1>

Image actions are commands that can be given to a DigitalOcean image. In
general, these requests are made on the actions endpoint of a specific
image.

An image action object is returned. These objects hold the current status
of the requested action.

## List All Actions for an Image

<a id="opIdimageActions_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/images/62137902/actions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/images/{image_id}/actions`

To retrieve all actions that have been executed on an image, send a GET request to `/v2/images/$IMAGE_ID/actions`.

## Initiate an Image Action

<a id="opIdimageActions_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/images/62137902/actions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "convert"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/images/{image_id}/actions`

The following actions are available on an Image.

## Convert an Image to a Snapshot

To convert an image, for example, a backup to a snapshot, send a POST request
to `/v2/images/$IMAGE_ID/actions`. Set the `type` attribute to `convert`.

## Transfer an Image

To transfer an image to another region, send a POST request to
`/v2/images/$IMAGE_ID/actions`. Set the `type` attribute to `transfer` and set
`region` attribute to the slug identifier of the region you wish to transfer
to.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "convert"
}
```

<h3 id="initiate-an-image-action-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|image_id|path|integer|true|A unique number that can be used to identify and reference a specific image.|
|body|body|[image_action_base](#schemaimage_action_base) \| [image_action_transfer](#schemaimage_action_transfer)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[image_action_base](#schemaimage_action_base)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[image_action_transfer](#schemaimage_action_transfer)|false|none|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-images">Images</h1>

A DigitalOcean [image](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/images/) can be
used to create a Droplet and may come in a number of flavors. Currently,
there are five types of images: snapshots, backups, applications,
distributions, and custom images.

* [Snapshots](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/snapshots/) provide
a full copy of an existing Droplet instance taken on demand.

* [Backups](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/backups/) are similar
to snapshots but are created automatically at regular intervals when
enabled for a Droplet.

* [Custom images](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/custom-images/)
are Linux-based virtual machine images (raw, qcow2, vhdx, vdi, and vmdk
formats are supported) that you may upload for use on DigitalOcean.

* Distributions are the public Linux distributions that are available to
be used as a base to create Droplets.

* Applications, or [1-Click Apps](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/marketplace/),
are distributions pre-configured with additional software.

To interact with images, you will generally send requests to the images
endpoint at /v2/images.

## List All Images

<a id="opIdimages_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/images \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/images`

To list all of the images available on your account, send a GET request to /v2/images.

## Filtering Results
-----

It's possible to request filtered results by including certain query parameters.

**Image Type**

Either 1-Click Application or OS Distribution images can be filtered by using the `type` query parameter.

> Important: The `type` query parameter does not directly relate to the `type` attribute.

To retrieve only ***distribution*** images, include the `type` query parameter set to distribution, `/v2/images?type=distribution`.

To retrieve only ***application*** images, include the `type` query parameter set to application, `/v2/images?type=application`.

**User Images**

To retrieve only the private images of a user, include the `private` query parameter set to true, `/v2/images?private=true`.

**Tags**

To list all images assigned to a specific tag, include the `tag_name` query parameter set to the name of the tag in your GET request. For example, `/v2/images?tag_name=$TAG_NAME`.


<h3 id="list-all-images-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|query|string|false|Filters results based on image type which can be either `application` or `distribution`.|
|private|query|boolean|false|Used to filter only user images.|
|tag_name|query|string|false|Used to filter images by a specific tag.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|application|
|type|distribution|

## Create a Custom Image

<a id="opIdimages_create_custom"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/images \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "ubuntu-18.04-minimal",
    "url": "http://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/minimal/releases/bionic/release/ubuntu-18.04-minimal-cloudimg-amd64.img",
    "distribution": "Ubuntu",
    "region": "nyc3",
    "description": "Cloud-optimized image w/ small footprint",
    "tags": [
      "base-image",
      "prod"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/images`

To create a new custom image, send a POST request to /v2/images.
The body must contain a url attribute pointing to a Linux virtual machine
image to be imported into DigitalOcean.
The image must be in the raw, qcow2, vhdx, vdi, or vmdk format.
It may be compressed using gzip or bzip2 and must be smaller than 100 GB after
 being decompressed.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "ubuntu-18.04-minimal",
  "url": "http://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/minimal/releases/bionic/release/ubuntu-18.04-minimal-cloudimg-amd64.img",
  "distribution": "Ubuntu",
  "region": "nyc3",
  "description": "Cloud-optimized image w/ small footprint",
  "tags": [
    "base-image",
    "prod"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-custom-image-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[image_new_custom](#schemaimage_new_custom)|true|none|
|» name|body|[image_name](#schemaimage_name)|true|The display name that has been given to an image.  This is what is shown in the control panel and is generally a descriptive title for the image in question.|
|» distribution|body|[distribution](#schemadistribution)|false|The name of a custom image's distribution. Currently, the valid values are  `Arch Linux`, `CentOS`, `CoreOS`, `Debian`, `Fedora`, `Fedora Atomic`,  `FreeBSD`, `Gentoo`, `openSUSE`, `RancherOS`, `Rocky Linux`, `Ubuntu`, and `Unknown`.  Any other value will be accepted but ignored, and `Unknown` will be used in its place.|
|» description|body|[image_description](#schemaimage_description)|false|An optional free-form text field to describe an image.|
|» url|body|string|true|A URL from which the custom Linux virtual machine image may be retrieved.  The image it points to must be in the raw, qcow2, vhdx, vdi, or vmdk format.  It may be compressed using gzip or bzip2 and must be smaller than 100 GB after being decompressed.|
|» region|body|[region_slug](#schemaregion_slug)|true|The slug identifier for the region where the resource will initially be  available.|
|» tags|body|[tags_array](#schematags_array)|false|A flat array of tag names as strings to be applied to the resource. Tag names may be for either existing or new tags. <br><br>Requires `tag:create` scope.|

## Update an Image

<a id="opIdimages_update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/images/62137902 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Nifty New Snapshot",
    "distribution": "Ubuntu",
    "description": " "
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/images/{image_id}`

To update an image, send a `PUT` request to `/v2/images/$IMAGE_ID`.
Set the `name` attribute to the new value you would like to use.
For custom images, the `description` and `distribution` attributes may also be updated.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Nifty New Snapshot",
  "distribution": "Ubuntu",
  "description": " "
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-image-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|image_id|path|integer|true|A unique number that can be used to identify and reference a specific image.|
|body|body|[image_update](#schemaimage_update)|true|none|
|» name|body|[image_name](#schemaimage_name)|false|The display name that has been given to an image.  This is what is shown in the control panel and is generally a descriptive title for the image in question.|
|» distribution|body|[distribution](#schemadistribution)|false|The name of a custom image's distribution.
