`PUT /v2/load_balancers/{lb_id}`

To update a load balancer's settings, send a PUT request to
`/v2/load_balancers/$LOAD_BALANCER_ID`. The request should contain a full
representation of the load balancer including existing attributes. It may
contain _one of_ the `droplets_ids` or `tag` attributes as they are mutually
exclusive. **Note that any attribute that is not provided will be reset to its
default value.**


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "updated-example-lb-01",
  "region": "nyc3",
  "droplet_ids": [
    3164444,
    3164445
  ],
  "algorithm": "round_robin",
  "forwarding_rules": [
    {
      "entry_protocol": "http",
      "entry_port": 80,
      "target_protocol": "http",
      "target_port": 80,
      "certificate_id": "",
      "tls_passthrough": false
    },
    {
      "entry_protocol": "https",
      "entry_port": 443,
      "target_protocol": "https",
      "target_port": 443,
      "certificate_id": "",
      "tls_passthrough": true
    }
  ],
  "health_check": {
    "protocol": "http",
    "port": 80,
    "path": "/",
    "check_interval_seconds": 10,
    "response_timeout_seconds": 5,
    "healthy_threshold": 5,
    "unhealthy_threshold": 3
  },
  "sticky_sessions": {
    "type": "none"
  },
  "redirect_http_to_https": false,
  "enable_proxy_protocol": true,
  "enable_backend_keepalive": true,
  "vpc_uuid": "c33931f2-a26a-4e61-b85c-4e95a2ec431b",
  "subnet_uuid": "cbd79771-23eb-49be-b5ea-59cc56222622",
  "project_id": "9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30",
  "http_idle_timeout_seconds": 60,
  "firewall": {
    "deny": [
      "cidr:1.2.0.0/16",
      "ip:2.3.4.5"
    ],
    "allow": [
      "ip:1.2.3.4",
      "cidr:2.3.4.0/24"
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-load-balancer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lb_id|path|string|true|A unique identifier for a load balancer.|
|body|body|[load_balancer_update](#schemaload_balancer_update)|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» droplet_ids|body|[integer]|true|An array containing the IDs of the Droplets assigned to the load balancer.|
|» region|body|[region_slug](#schemaregion_slug)|true|The slug identifier for the region where the resource will initially be  available.|
|» name|body|string|false|A human-readable name for a load balancer instance.|
|» project_id|body|string|false|The ID of the project that the load balancer is associated with. If no ID is provided at creation, the load balancer associates with the user's default project. If an invalid project ID is provided, the load balancer will not be created.|
|» size_unit|body|integer|false|How many nodes the load balancer contains. Each additional node increases the load balancer's ability to manage more connections. Load balancers can be scaled up or down, and you can change the number of nodes after creation up to once per hour. This field is currently not available in the AMS2, NYC2, or SFO1 regions. Use the `size` field to scale load balancers that reside in these regions.|
|» size|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** This field has been replaced by the `size_unit` field for all regions except in AMS2, NYC2, and SFO1. Each available load balancer size now equates to the load balancer having a set number of nodes.<br>* `lb-small` = 1 node<br>* `lb-medium` = 3 nodes<br>* `lb-large` = 6 nodes<br><br>You can resize load balancers after creation up to once per hour. You cannot resize a load balancer within the first hour of its creation.|
|» algorithm|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** This field has been deprecated. You can no longer specify an algorithm for load balancers.|
|» forwarding_rules|body|[[forwarding_rule](#schemaforwarding_rule)]|true|An array of objects specifying the forwarding rules for a load balancer.|
|» health_check|body|[health_check](#schemahealth_check)|false|An object specifying health check settings for the load balancer.|
|» sticky_sessions|body|[sticky_sessions](#schemasticky_sessions)|false|An object specifying sticky sessions settings for the load balancer.|
|» redirect_http_to_https|body|boolean|false|A boolean value indicating whether HTTP requests to the load balancer on port 80 will be redirected to HTTPS on port 443.|
|» enable_proxy_protocol|body|boolean|false|A boolean value indicating whether PROXY Protocol is in use.|
|» enable_backend_keepalive|body|boolean|false|A boolean value indicating whether HTTP keepalive connections are maintained to target Droplets.|
|» http_idle_timeout_seconds|body|integer|false|An integer value which configures the idle timeout for HTTP requests to the target droplets.|
|» vpc_uuid|body|string(uuid)|false|A string specifying the UUID of the VPC to which the load balancer is assigned.|
|» subnet_uuid|body|string(uuid)|false|A string specifying the UUID of the VPC subnet to which the load balancer is assigned.|
|» disable_lets_encrypt_dns_records|body|boolean|false|A boolean value indicating whether to disable automatic DNS record creation for Let's Encrypt certificates that are added to the load balancer.|
|» firewall|body|[lb_firewall](#schemalb_firewall)|false|An object specifying allow and deny rules to control traffic to the load balancer.|
|» network|body|string|false|A string indicating whether the load balancer should be external or internal. Internal load balancers have no public IPs and are only accessible to resources on the same VPC network. This property cannot be updated after creating the load balancer.|
|» network_stack|body|string|false|A string indicating whether the load balancer will support IPv4 or both IPv4 and IPv6 networking. This property cannot be updated after creating the load balancer.|
|» type|body|string|false|A string indicating whether the load balancer should be a standard regional HTTP load balancer, a regional network load balancer that routes traffic at the TCP/UDP transport layer, or a global load balancer.|
|» domains|body|[[domains](#schemadomains)]|false|An array of objects specifying the domain configurations for a Global load balancer.|

`DELETE /v2/load_balancers/{lb_id}`

To delete a load balancer instance, disassociating any Droplets assigned to it

This indicates that the request was processed successfully.

## Add Droplets to a Load Balancer

<a id="opIdloadBalancers_add_droplets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/load_balancers/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6/droplets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "droplet_ids": [
      3164444,
      3164445
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/load_balancers/{lb_id}/droplets`

To assign a Droplet to a load balancer instance, send a POST request to
`/v2/load_balancers/$LOAD_BALANCER_ID/droplets`. In the body of the request,
there should be a `droplet_ids` attribute containing a list of Droplet IDs.
Individual Droplets can not be added to a load balancer configured with a
Droplet tag. Attempting to do so will result in a "422 Unprocessable Entity"
response from the API.

No response body will be sent back, but the response code will indicate
success. Specifically, the response code will be a 204, which means that the
action was successful with no returned body data.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "droplet_ids": [
    3164444,
    3164445
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-droplets-to-a-load-balancer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lb_id|path|string|true|A unique identifier for a load balancer.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» droplet_ids|body|[integer]|true|An array containing the IDs of the Droplets assigned to the load balancer.|

## Add Forwarding Rules to a Load Balancer

<a id="opIdloadBalancers_add_forwardingRules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/load_balancers/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6/forwarding_rules \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
```

`POST /v2/load_balancers/{lb_id}/forwarding_rules`

array of rules to be added.

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-microvms-public-preview">MicroVMs [Public Preview]</h1>

[DigitalOcean MicroVMs](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/microvms/)
are lightweight virtual machines that run a `linux/amd64` container image
in an isolated kernel. A MicroVM pauses automatically when it is idle and
resumes on the next HTTP request, command, or console session, with its
memory, files, and processes intact. By sending requests to the
`/v2/microvms` endpoints, you can create, list, pause, resume, and delete
MicroVMs, run commands and open a console in them, and create checkpoints
to start new MicroVMs from a saved state.

Each MicroVM serves its HTTP port at
`https://{microvm_id}.{region}.microvm.ondigitalocean.com`. Requests to
that endpoint require a token with the `microvm:access` scope.

## List all MicroVMs

<a id="opIdmicrovms_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/microvms \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/microvms`

To list all of the MicroVMs on your team, send a GET request to `/v2/microvms`.

The `region`, `name`, and `tag_name` filters combine with AND.


<h3 id="list-all-microvms-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page.|
|region|query|string|false|Only return MicroVMs in this region.|
|name|query|string|false|Only return the MicroVM with this exact name.|
|tag_name|query|string|false|Only return MicroVMs with this tag. A tag that matches no MicroVMs returns an empty list.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "microvms": [
    {
      "id": "01a0ef1a-d873-793d-ae6a-5dd6239be62a",

      "size": {
        "cpu": 1,

      },
```

## Create a MicroVM

<a id="opIdmicrovms_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/microvms \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "example-microvm",
    "region": "mkc1",
    "size": {
      "cpu": 1,
      "memory": 2048
    },
    "source": {
      "oci_ref": "docker.io/library/nginx:latest"
    },
    "http_port": 80,
    "http_protocol": "http",
    "auto_pause": {
      "idle_timeout": "5m"
    },
    "tags": [
      "example"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/microvms`

To create a MicroVM, send a POST request to `/v2/microvms`.

`name` and `source` are required. Set `source.oci_ref` to create the MicroVM from a
`linux/amd64` container image, or `source.checkpoint_id` to create it from a checkpoint.
With `oci_ref`, `region` and `size` are also required.

A MicroVM created from an image is returned with `state` set to `creating`. Poll
`GET /v2/microvms/{microvm_id}` until `state` is `running`. A MicroVM created from a
checkpoint is usually returned already `running`.

All settings are fixed at creation. There is no update endpoint.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "example-microvm",
  "region": "mkc1",
  "size": {
    "cpu": 1,
    "memory": 2048
  },
  "source": {
    "oci_ref": "docker.io/library/nginx:latest"
  },
  "http_port": 80,
  "http_protocol": "http",
  "auto_pause": {
    "idle_timeout": "5m"
  },
  "tags": [
    "example"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-microvm-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[microvm_create](#schemamicrovm_create)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the MicroVM. Must be unique in the region and contain 1 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens.|
|» source|body|[microvm_source](#schemamicrovm_source)|true|What the MicroVM runs. Set exactly one of `oci_ref` or `checkpoint_id`.|
|» region|body|string|false|The slug of the region to create the MicroVM in. Required with `source.oci_ref`.|
|» size|body|[microvm_size](#schemamicrovm_size)|false|The MicroVM's size. `cpu` and `memory` must be one of the pairs `1`/`2048`, `2`/`4096`, `8`/`16384`, or `16`/`32768`. The size sets the disk, which is returned in responses.|
|» networking|body|string|false|`public` sends outbound traffic through a shared NAT gateway. `vpc` places the MicroVM in the VPC network set by `vpc_uuid`.|
|» vpc_uuid|body|string(uuid)|false|The ID of a VPC network in the same region that belongs to your team. Required when `networking` is `vpc`.|
|» auto_pause|body|[microvm_auto_pause](#schemamicrovm_auto_pause)|false|Automatic pause settings. A MicroVM always pauses after it is idle for `idle_timeout`. Sending `enabled` set to `false` is rejected.|
|» auto_resume|body|boolean|false|Whether an HTTP request, command, or console session resumes the MicroVM when it is paused. Set to `false` to require a manual resume.|
|» http_port|body|integer|false|The guest port the workload serves HTTP on. Defaults to `8080`. Not returned in responses. When creating from a checkpoint without `ports`, must be one of the checkpoint's ports.|
|» http_protocol|body|string|false|The protocol the HTTP port serves.|
|» ports|body|[integer]|false|The guest ports to declare, up to five. Must include `http_port`. Defaults to only the HTTP port. During the public preview, only the HTTP port is reachable through the MicroVM's endpoint.|
|» environment|body|object|false|Environment variables passed into the MicroVM at boot, as key and value pairs. Not returned in responses.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|Tags to apply to the MicroVM.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» networking|public|
|» networking|vpc|
|» http_protocol|http|
|» http_protocol|http2|

## List checkpoints

`GET /v2/microvms/checkpoints`

To list your team's checkpoints, newest first, send a GET request to
`/v2/microvms/checkpoints`. To list one MicroVM's checkpoints, add the `microvm_id` query
parameter.

|microvm_id|query|string(uuid)|false|Only return checkpoints taken from this MicroVM.|

`DELETE /v2/microvms/checkpoints/{checkpoint_id}`

To delete a checkpoint, send a DELETE request to `/v2/microvms/checkpoints/{checkpoint_id}`.
You can no longer create MicroVMs from a deleted checkpoint.

The request returns HTTP 400 while the checkpoint is still being captured. A successful
request returns a `204 No Content` status code.

## Retrieve a MicroVM


`GET /v2/microvms/{microvm_id}`

To show information about a MicroVM, send a GET request to `/v2/microvms/{microvm_id}`.

The endpoint is in the `urls` entry with `default` set to `true`. Its `hostname` is empty
and its `status` is `PENDING` until provisioning finishes.


<h3 id="retrieve-a-microvm-parameters">Parameters</h3>

```json
    "size": {
      "cpu": 1,
      "memory": 2048,
      "disk": 50
    },
    "source": {
      "oci_ref": "docker.io/library/nginx:latest"

    "state": "running",
    "networking": "public",

    ],

}
```

## Pause a MicroVM

<a id="opIdmicrovms_post_pause"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/microvms/01a0ef1a-d873-793d-ae6a-5dd6239be62a/pause \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/microvms/{microvm_id}/pause`

To pause a MicroVM, send a POST request to `/v2/microvms/{microvm_id}/pause`.

Pausing suspends the MicroVM's processes and preserves its memory, files, and processes.
A paused MicroVM incurs storage charges only. The request returns when the change
completes. Pausing a MicroVM that is already paused succeeds. The request returns HTTP 400
when the MicroVM is `creating`, `terminated`, or `failed`.


<h3 id="pause-a-microvm-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|microvm_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The unique ID of the MicroVM.|

```json
}
```

## Resume a MicroVM

<a id="opIdmicrovms_post_resume"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/microvms/01a0ef1a-d873-793d-ae6a-5dd6239be62a/resume \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/microvms/{microvm_id}/resume`

To resume a paused MicroVM, send a POST request to `/v2/microvms/{microvm_id}/resume`.

The request returns when the change completes. Resuming a MicroVM that is already running
succeeds. The request returns HTTP 400 when the MicroVM is `creating`, `terminated`, or
`failed`.


<h3 id="resume-a-microvm-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|microvm_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The unique ID of the MicroVM.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "microvm": {
    "id": "01a0ef1a-d873-793d-ae6a-5dd6239be62a",
    "name": "example-microvm",
    "region": "mkc1",
    "size": {
      "cpu": 1,
      "memory": 2048,
      "disk": 50
    },
    "source": {
      "oci_ref": "docker.io/library/nginx:latest"
    },
    "state": "running",
    "networking": "public",
    "auto_pause": {
      "enabled": true,
      "idle_timeout": "5m0s"
    },
    "auto_resume": true,
    "http_protocol": "http",
    "ports": [
      80
    ],
    "tags": [
      "example"
    ],
    "urls": [
      {
        "hostname": "01a0ef1a-d873-793d-ae6a-5dd6239be62a.mkc1.microvm.ondigitalocean.com",
        "port": 80,
        "default": true,
        "status": "ACTIVE"
      }
    ],
    "created_at": "2026-09-29T21:38:29Z"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "INVALID_SIZE",
  "message": "no supported size matches the requested resources: 3 vCPU with 2048 MiB of memory (supported: 1vCPU/2048MiB, 2vCPU/4096MiB, 8vCPU/16384MiB, 16vCPU/32768MiB)"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json

  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

```json

  "code": "NOT_FOUND",
  "message": "MicroVM not found"
}
```

```json
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

```json
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

```json
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Run a command in a MicroVM

<a id="opIdmicrovms_run_command"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/microvms/01a0ef1a-d873-793d-ae6a-5dd6239be62a/exec \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "argv": [
      "nginx",
      "-v"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/microvms/{microvm_id}/exec`

To run a command in a MicroVM's workload container, send a POST request to
`/v2/microvms/{microvm_id}/exec`.

`argv` runs directly, not through a shell, with standard input closed. If the MicroVM is
paused and auto-resume is on, the request resumes it and waits until it is running.

A command has 60 seconds to finish. Your team can run 32 commands at once and 60 commands
per minute. Rejected requests count toward the per-minute limit.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "argv": [
    "nginx",
    "-v"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="run-a-command-in-a-microvm-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|microvm_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The unique ID of the MicroVM.|
|body|body|[exec_request](#schemaexec_request)|true|none|
|» argv|body|[string]|true|The command and its arguments.|
|» cwd|body|string|false|The working directory to run the command in.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "stdout": "",
  "stderr": "nginx version: nginx/1.29.1\n",
  "exit_code": 0
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "INVALID_SIZE",
  "message": "no supported size matches the requested resources: 3 vCPU with 2048 MiB of memory (supported: 1vCPU/2048MiB, 2vCPU/4096MiB, 8vCPU/16384MiB, 16vCPU/32768MiB)"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "code": "PERMISSION_DENIED",
  "message": "permission denied"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": "NOT_FOUND",
  "message": "MicroVM not found"
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> 502 Response

```json
{
  "code": "UNAVAILABLE",
  "message": "workload unavailable"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<h3 id="run-a-command-in-a-microvm-responses">Responses</h3>

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The command ran. HTTP 200 is returned even when the command itself fails. Check `exit_code` for the command's result.|[exec_response](#schemaexec_response)|
|400|Bad Request|The request was malformed, failed validation, or is not allowed in the resource's current state.|[microvm_error](#schemamicrovm_error)|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication failed due to invalid credentials.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|The token does not have the required scope, or your team has reached a limit.|[microvm_error](#schemamicrovm_error)|
|404|Not Found|The MicroVM or checkpoint does not exist, or it belongs to another team.|[microvm_error](#schemamicrovm_error)|
|429|Too Many Requests|The API rate limit has been exceeded.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|There was a server error.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|502|Bad Gateway|The command did not reach the workload, for example because the container is not running.|[microvm_error](#schemamicrovm_error)|
|default|Default|There was an unexpected error.|[error](#schemaerror)|

## Open a console in a MicroVM

<a id="opIdmicrovms_get_console"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/microvms/01a0ef1a-d873-793d-ae6a-5dd6239be62a/console \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/microvms/{microvm_id}/console`

To open an interactive `/bin/sh` console in a MicroVM's workload container, open a
WebSocket connection to `wss://api.digitalocean.com/v2/microvms/{microvm_id}/console`.

Send the API token in the `Authorization` header of the handshake. Browsers cannot set this
header, so you cannot open the console from browser JavaScript. The image must include
`/bin/sh`. A MicroVM can have four consoles open at a time. If the MicroVM is paused and
auto-resume is on, opening a console resumes it.


<h3 id="open-a-console-in-a-microvm-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|microvm_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The unique ID of the MicroVM.|
|rows|query|integer|false|The initial number of terminal rows.|
|cols|query|integer|false|The initial number of terminal columns.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "code": "PERMISSION_DENIED",
  "message": "permission denied"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": "NOT_FOUND",
  "message": "MicroVM not found"
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<h3 id="open-a-console-in-a-microvm-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|101|Switching Protocols|The connection is upgraded to a WebSocket. Binary frames from the client are terminal input, and text frames are resize messages such as `{"resize":{"rows":40,"cols":120}}`. Binary frames from the server are terminal output with `stdout` and `stderr` combined. Text frames from the server are control messages: `{"status":{"state":"resuming"}}` while a paused MicroVM resumes, `{"error":{"code":"...","message":"..."}}` when the console fails to connect or start (with `code` set to `dial_failed`, `start_failed`, or `agent_error`), and `{"exit":{"code":0}}` when the shell exits. The server sends a ping every 30 seconds. A console closes after 4 hours, or after 30 minutes with no input and no output. A message larger than 1 MiB closes the console with WebSocket code 1009.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Authentication failed due to invalid credentials.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|The token does not have the required scope, or your team has reached a limit.|[microvm_error](#schemamicrovm_error)|
|404|Not Found|The MicroVM or checkpoint does not exist, or it belongs to another team.|[microvm_error](#schemamicrovm_error)|
|429|Too Many Requests|The API rate limit has been exceeded.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|There was a server error.|[error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|There was an unexpected error.|[error](#schemaerror)|

## Create a checkpoint of a MicroVM

<a id="opIdmicrovmCheckpoints_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/microvms/01a0ef1a-d873-793d-ae6a-5dd6239be62a/checkpoints \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "example-checkpoint"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/microvms/{microvm_id}/checkpoints`

To create a checkpoint of a running or paused MicroVM, send a POST request to
`/v2/microvms/{microvm_id}/checkpoints`.

The capture runs in the background and does not change the MicroVM's state. Poll
`GET /v2/microvms/checkpoints/{checkpoint_id}` until `status` is `CHECKPOINT_AVAILABLE`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "example-checkpoint"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-checkpoint-of-a-microvm-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|microvm_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The unique ID of the MicroVM.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|A name for the checkpoint. If you omit it, a name such as `checkpoint-20260929-143559` is generated.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "checkpoint": {
    "id": "01a0ed98-0a74-75dd-a625-e4856adbc298",
    "name": "example-checkpoint",
    "microvm_id": "01a0ef1a-d873-793d-ae6a-5dd6239be62a",
    "microvm_name": "example-microvm",
    "region": "mkc1",
    "size": {
      "cpu": 1,
      "memory": 2048,
      "disk": 50
    },
    "status": "CHECKPOINT_AVAILABLE",
    "memory_bytes": 2147483648,
    "disk_bytes": 1073741824,
    "created_at": "2026-09-29T14:35:59Z"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "INVALID_SIZE",
  "message": "no supported size matches the requested resources: 3 vCPU with 2048 MiB of memory (supported: 1vCPU/2048MiB, 2vCPU/4096MiB, 8vCPU/16384MiB, 16vCPU/32768MiB)"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json

  "code": "NOT_FOUND",
  "message": "MicroVM not found"
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

```json
  "id": "server_error",

}
```

```json
  "id": "example_error",

}
```

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-monitoring">Monitoring</h1>

The DigitalOcean Monitoring API makes it possible to programmatically retrieve metrics as well as configure alert
policies based on these metrics. The Monitoring API can help you gain insight into how your apps are performing
and consuming resources.

## List Alert Policies

<a id="opIdmonitoring_list_alertPolicy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/monitoring/alerts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/monitoring/alerts`

Returns all alert policies that are configured for the given account. To List all alert policies, send a GET request to `/v2/monitoring/alerts`.

<h3 id="list-alert-policies-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

## Create Alert Policy

<a id="opIdmonitoring_create_alertPolicy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/monitoring/alerts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "alerts": {
      "email": [
        "bob@exmaple.com"
      ],
      "slack": [
        {
          "channel": "Production Alerts",
          "url": "https://hooks.slack.com/services/T1234567/AAAAAAAA/ZZZZZZ"
        }
      ]
    },
    "compare": "GreaterThan",
    "description": "CPU Alert",
    "enabled": true,
    "entities": [
      "192018292"
    ],
    "tags": [
      "droplet_tag"
    ],
    "type": "v1/insights/droplet/cpu",
    "value": 80,
    "window": "5m"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/monitoring/alerts`

To create a new alert, send a POST request to `/v2/monitoring/alerts`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "alerts": {
    "email": [
      "bob@exmaple.com"
    ],
    "slack": [
      {
        "channel": "Production Alerts",
        "url": "https://hooks.slack.com/services/T1234567/AAAAAAAA/ZZZZZZ"
      }
    ]
  },
  "compare": "GreaterThan",
  "description": "CPU Alert",
  "enabled": true,
  "entities": [
    "192018292"
  ],
  "tags": [
    "droplet_tag"
  ],
  "type": "v1/insights/droplet/cpu",
  "value": 80,
  "window": "5m"
}
```

```json
    "alerts": {
      "email": [
```

```bash
      "192018292"
    ],
    "tags": [
      "droplet_tag"
    ],
    "type": "v1/insights/droplet/cpu",
    "value": 80,
    "window": "5m"
  }'
```

## Get Droplet Bandwidth Metrics

<a id="opIdmonitoring_get_dropletBandwidthMetrics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/monitoring/metrics/droplet/bandwidth?host_id=17209102&interface=private&direction=inbound&start=1620683817&end=1620705417' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/monitoring/metrics/droplet/bandwidth`

To retrieve bandwidth metrics for a given Droplet, send a GET request to `/v2/monitoring/metrics/droplet/bandwidth`. Use the `interface` query parameter to specify if the results should be for the `private` or `public` interface. Use the `direction` query parameter to specify if the results should be for `inbound` or `outbound` traffic.
The metrics in the response body are in megabits per second (Mbps).

<h3 id="get-droplet-bandwidth-metrics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|host_id|query|string|true|The droplet ID.|
|interface|query|string|true|The network interface.|
|direction|query|string|true|The traffic direction.|
|start|query|string|true|UNIX timestamp to start metric window.|
|end|query|string|true|UNIX timestamp to end metric window.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|interface|private|
|interface|public|
|direction|inbound|
|direction|outbound|

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/monitoring/sinks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

      }
    ]
  }'
```

```json
}
```

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-nfs">NFS</h1>

NFS lets you create fully managed, POSIX-compliant network file storage that delivers secure,
high-performance shared storage right inside your VPC. This enables seamless data sharing across Droplets in a VPC.

## List NFS shares per region

<a id="opIdnfs_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/nfs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/nfs`

To list NFS shares, send a GET request to `/v2/nfs?region=${region}`.

A successful request will return all NFS shares belonging to the authenticated user.


<h3 id="list-nfs-shares-per-region-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|region|query|string|false|The DigitalOcean region slug (e.g., nyc2, atl1) where the NFS share resides.|

## Create a new NFS share

<a id="opIdnfs_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/nfs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "sammy-share-drive",
    "size_gib": 1024,
    "region": "atl1",
    "vpc_ids": [
      "796c6fe3-2a1d-4da2-9f3e-38239827dc91"
    ],
    "performance_tier": "standard"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/nfs`

To create a new NFS share, send a POST request to `/v2/nfs`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "sammy-share-drive",
  "size_gib": 1024,
  "region": "atl1",
  "vpc_ids": [
    "796c6fe3-2a1d-4da2-9f3e-38239827dc91"
  ],
  "performance_tier": "standard"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-nfs-share-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[nfs_request](#schemanfs_request)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The human-readable name of the share.|
|» size_gib|body|integer|true|The desired/provisioned size of the share in GiB (Gibibytes). Must be >= 50.|
|» region|body|string|true|The DigitalOcean region slug (e.g., nyc2, atl1) where the NFS share resides.|
|» vpc_ids|body|[string]|true|List of VPC IDs that should be able to access the share.|
|» performance_tier|body|string|false|The performance tier of the share.|

> Example responses

```json
    ],

      {
        "id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4a5b-9c8d-1e2f3a4b5c6d",
        "name": "other-vpc",
        "share_id": "0a1b2c3d-4e5f-6a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d",
        "path": "/other-vpc",
        "status": "ACCESS_POINT_ACTIVE",
        "access_policy": {
          "anonuid": 65534,
```

## List NFS snapshots per region

<a id="opIdnfs_list_snapshot"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/nfs/snapshots \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/nfs/snapshots`

To list all NFS snapshots, send a GET request to `/v2/nfs/snapshots?region=${region}&share_id={share_id}`.

A successful request will return all NFS snapshots belonging to the authenticated user in the specified region.

Optionally, you can filter snapshots by a specific NFS share by including the `share_id` query parameter.


<h3 id="list-nfs-snapshots-per-region-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|region|query|string|false|The DigitalOcean region slug (e.g., nyc2, atl1) where the NFS share resides.|
|share_id|query|string|false|The unique ID of an NFS share. If provided, only snapshots of this specific share will be returned.|

## List NFS access points for a share

<a id="opIdnfs_list_access_points"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/nfs/shares/baf4827c-6fa9-456f-9dbd-9ddfcacd0720/access_points \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/nfs/shares/{share_id}/access_points`

To list access points for an NFS share, send a GET request to
`/v2/nfs/shares/{share_id}/access_points`. You may use query parameters to filter
by status.

A successful request will return a list of NFS access points ordered with the default
access point first, then by `created_at` ascending.


<h3 id="list-nfs-access-points-for-a-share-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|share_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The unique identifier of the NFS share.|
|status|query|string|false|Filter access points by status.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|ACCESS_POINT_CREATING|
|status|ACCESS_POINT_ACTIVE|
|status|ACCESS_POINT_FAILED|
|status|ACCESS_POINT_DELETED|

## Create an NFS access point

<a id="opIdnfs_create_access_point"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/nfs/shares/baf4827c-6fa9-456f-9dbd-9ddfcacd0720/access_points \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "other-vpc",
    "path": "/other-vpc",
    "vpc_id": "3f34cdb2-1e4f-4100-b5c7-f55f2762085f",
    "access_policy": {
      "anonuid": 65534,
      "anongid": 65534,
      "protocols": [
        "NFS4",
        "NFS"
      ],
      "squash_config": "ROOT_SQUASH",
      "identity_enforcement_enabled": false
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v2/nfs/shares/{share_id}/access_points`

To create a new access point on an NFS share, send a POST request to
`/v2/nfs/shares/{share_id}/access_points`.

A successful request will return the newly created access point and an action object.

The parent share must be in `ACTIVE` or `INACTIVE` status. Validation failures and
precondition errors (such as an ineligible share state) return `400 Bad Request`.
Duplicate name or path conflicts return `409 Conflict`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "other-vpc",
  "path": "/other-vpc",
  "vpc_id": "3f34cdb2-1e4f-4100-b5c7-f55f2762085f",
  "access_policy": {
    "anonuid": 65534,
    "anongid": 65534,
    "protocols": [
      "NFS4",
      "NFS"
    ],
    "squash_config": "ROOT_SQUASH",
    "identity_enforcement_enabled": false
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-nfs-access-point-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|share_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The unique identifier of the NFS share.|
|body|body|[access_point_request](#schemaaccess_point_request)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name for the access point. Must be unique per share. Must be 2–63<br>characters and match `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-]{1,61}[a-zA-Z0-9]$`.<br>The name `default` is reserved (case-insensitive) for the implicit default<br>access point created with each share.<br>|
|» path|body|string|true|The export sub-path. Must start with `/`, must not be exactly `/` (reserved<br>for the default access point), must be at most 1024 characters, may contain<br>only alphanumerics, `-`, `_`, `.`, and `/`, and must not contain `..` path<br>segments.<br>|
|» access_policy|body|[access_policy](#schemaaccess_policy)|true|Provider-agnostic NFS access policy for an access point. Network CIDRs are<br>managed by attach, detach, and managed-access workflows and are not part of<br>this policy.<br>|
|» vpc_id|body|string|true|Required. The VPC this access point will be pinned to. A storage gateway is<br>provisioned (or reused) in this VPC, and the access point becomes mountable from<br>this VPC regardless of whether the parent share is currently attached to it.<br>|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "access_point": {
    "id": "7659ce91-354d-4f61-9cda-ae2c7feb61d9",
    "name": "other-vpc",
    "share_id": "baf4827c-6fa9-456f-9dbd-9ddfcacd0720",
    "path": "/other-vpc",
    "vpc_id": "3f34cdb2-1e4f-4100-b5c7-f55f2762085f",
    "status": "ACCESS_POINT_CREATING",
    "is_default": false,
    "created_at": "2026-06-25T08:11:12Z",
    "updated_at": "",
    "access_policy": {
      "anonuid": 65534,
      "anongid": 65534,
      "protocols": [
        "NFS4",
        "NFS"
      ],
      "squash_config": "ROOT_SQUASH",
      "identity_enforcement_enabled": false
    }
  },
  "action": {
    "id": "084c3b9c-2382-441b-92d4-10b095bb5d7c",
    "region_slug": "s2r1",
    "resource_id": "7659ce91-354d-4f61-9cda-ae2c7feb61d9",
    "resource_type": "SHARE",
    "type": "CREATE_ACCESS_POINT",
    "status": "IN_PROGRESS",
    "started_at": "2026-06-25T08:11:12Z"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "MISSING_NAME",
  "message": "name is required"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

```json
  "code": "AlreadyExists",

}
```

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

## Delete an NFS access point

<a id="opIdnfs_delete_access_point"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/nfs/access_points/becd9f04-8afa-4ccd-b03e-9676447df603 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/nfs/access_points/{access_point_id}`

To delete an NFS access point, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/nfs/access_points/{access_point_id}`.

A successful request will soft-delete the access point and return the deleted access point
with status `ACCESS_POINT_DELETED` and an action object indicating the delete operation.

The default access point (`is_default: true`) cannot be deleted. Access points already
in `ACCESS_POINT_DELETED` or `ACCESS_POINT_FAILED` status return `400 Bad Request`.


<h3 id="delete-an-nfs-access-point-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|access_point_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The unique identifier of the NFS access point.|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-nfs-actions">NFS Actions</h1>

NFS actions are tasks that can be executed on an NFS share. These can be
things like resizing, snapshotting, etc.

## Initiate an NFS action

<a id="opIdnfs_create_action"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/nfs/0a1b2c3d-4e5f-6a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d/actions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "resize",
    "region": "atl1",
    "params": {
      "size_gib": 2048
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v2/nfs/{nfs_id}/actions`

To execute an action (such as resize) on a specified NFS share, 
send a POST request to `/v2/nfs/{nfs_id}/actions`. In the JSON body 
to the request, set the `type` attribute to on of the supported action types:

| Action                           | Details |
| -------------------------------- | ----------- |
| <nobr>`resize`</nobr>            | Resizes an NFS share. Set the size_gib attribute to a desired value in GiB |
| <nobr>`snapshot`</nobr>          | Takes a snapshot of an NFS share |
| <nobr>`attach`</nobr>            | Attaches an NFS share to a VPC. Set the vpc_id attribute to the desired VPC ID |
| <nobr>`detach`</nobr>            | Detaches an NFS share from a VPC. Set the vpc_id attribute to the desired VPC ID |
| <nobr>`reassign`</nobr>          | Reassigns an NFS share from one VPC to another. Set the old_vpc_id and new_vpc_id attributes to the desired VPC IDs |
| <nobr>`switch_performance_tier`</nobr> | Switches the performance tier of an NFS share. Set the performance_tier attribute to the desired tier (e.g., standard, high) |


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "resize",
  "region": "atl1",
  "params": {
    "size_gib": 2048
  }
}
```

<h3 id="initiate-an-nfs-action-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|nfs_id|path|string|true|The unique ID of the NFS share|
|body|body|[nfs_action_resize](#schemanfs_action_resize) \| [nfs_action_snapshot](#schemanfs_action_snapshot) \| [nfs_action_attach](#schemanfs_action_attach) \| [nfs_action_detach](#schemanfs_action_detach) \| [nfs_action_reassign](#schemanfs_action_reassign) \| [nfs_action_switch_performance_tier](#schemanfs_action_switch_performance_tier)|true|The `type` attribute set in the request body will specify the  action that<br>will be taken on the NFS share. Some actions will require additional<br>attributes to be set as well.<br>|
|» *anyOf*|body|[nfs_action_resize](#schemanfs_action_resize)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[nfs_action_snapshot](#schemanfs_action_snapshot)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[nfs_action_attach](#schemanfs_action_attach)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[nfs_action_detach](#schemanfs_action_detach)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[nfs_action_reassign](#schemanfs_action_reassign)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[nfs_action_switch_performance_tier](#schemanfs_action_switch_performance_tier)|false|none|

```json
    "id": "084c3b9c-2382-441b-92d4-10b095bb5d7c",

  }

}
```

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-organizations">Organizations</h1>

Organizations group multiple teams under a shared administrative boundary.
The Organizations API lets you create teams within an organization and
list the teams that belong to it.

These endpoints must be called in an organization context.

## Create a Team in an Organization

<a id="opIdorganizations_create_team"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/organizations/team \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "production"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/organizations/team`

To create a new team within an organization, send a POST request to
`/v2/organizations/team`.

This endpoint must be called in an organization context. Optionally include
`invitations` to invite users to the new team. The `owner` role cannot be
assigned via invitation.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "production"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-team-in-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[create_team_request](#schemacreate_team_request)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The human-readable name for the team to create.|
|» invitations|body|[[team_invitation](#schemateam_invitation)]|false|Optional invitations to send when creating the team. Each invitation includes an email address and a role. The `owner` role cannot be assigned via invitation.<br>|

```json
    "uuid": "4e1bfbc3-dc3e-41f2-a18f-1b4d7ba71679",

    },

    }

}
```

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-partner-network-connect">Partner Network Connect</h1>

Partner Network Connect lets you establish high-bandwidth, low-latency
network connections directly between DigitalOcean VPC networks and other
public cloud providers or on-premises datacenters.

## List all partner attachments

<a id="opIdpartnerAttachments_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/partner_network_connect/attachments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/partner_network_connect/attachments`

## Create a new partner attachment

<a id="opIdpartnerAttachments_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/partner_network_connect/attachments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "env.prod-partner-network-connect",
    "connection_bandwidth_in_mbps": 1000,
    "region": "nyc",
    "naas_provider": "megaport",
    "vpc_ids": [
      "c140286f-e6ce-4131-8b7b-df4590ce8d6a",
      "994a2735-dc84-11e8-80bc-3cfdfea9fba1"
    ],
    "parent_uuid": "d594cf8d-8c79-4bc5-aec1-6f9b211506b3",
    "bgp": {
      "local_router_ip": "169.254.0.1/29",
      "peer_router_ip": "169.254.0.6/29",
      "peer_router_asn": 64532,
      "auth_key": "0xsNnb1pwQlowdoMySEfWwk4I"
    },
    "redundancy_zone": "MEGAPORT_BLUE"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/partner_network_connect/attachments`

To create a new partner attachment, send a `POST` request to
`/v2/partner_network_connect/attachments` with a JSON object containing the
required configuration details.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "env.prod-partner-network-connect",
  "connection_bandwidth_in_mbps": 1000,
  "region": "nyc",
  "naas_provider": "megaport",
  "vpc_ids": [
    "c140286f-e6ce-4131-8b7b-df4590ce8d6a",
    "994a2735-dc84-11e8-80bc-3cfdfea9fba1"
  ],
  "parent_uuid": "d594cf8d-8c79-4bc5-aec1-6f9b211506b3",
  "bgp": {
    "local_router_ip": "169.254.0.1/29",
    "peer_router_ip": "169.254.0.6/29",
    "peer_router_asn": 64532,
    "auth_key": "0xsNnb1pwQlowdoMySEfWwk4I"
  },
  "redundancy_zone": "MEGAPORT_BLUE"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-partner-attachment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[partner_attachment_writable](#schemapartner_attachment_writable)|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the partner attachment. Must be unique and may only contain alphanumeric characters, dashes, and periods.|
|» connection_bandwidth_in_mbps|body|integer|true|Bandwidth (in Mbps) of the connection.|
|» region|body|string|true|The region to create the partner attachment.|
|» naas_provider|body|string|true|none|
|» vpc_ids|body|[string(string)]|true|An array of VPCs IDs.|
|» parent_uuid|body|string|false|Optional associated partner attachment UUID|
|» bgp|body|object|false|Optional BGP configurations|
|» » local_router_ip|body|string|true|IP of the DO router|
|» » peer_router_ip|body|string|true|IP of the Naas Provider router|
|» » peer_router_asn|body|integer|true|ASN of the peer router|
|» » auth_key|body|string|true|BGP Auth Key|
|» redundancy_zone|body|string|false|Optional redundancy zone for the partner attachment.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» connection_bandwidth_in_mbps|1000|
|» connection_bandwidth_in_mbps|2000|
|» connection_bandwidth_in_mbps|5000|
|» connection_bandwidth_in_mbps|10000|
|» region|nyc|
|» region|sfo|
|» region|fra|
|» region|ams|
|» region|sgp|
|» redundancy_zone|MEGAPORT_BLUE|
|» redundancy_zone|MEGAPORT_RED|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-project-resources">Project Resources</h1>

Project Resources are resources that can be grouped into your projects.
You can group resources (like Droplets, Spaces, load balancers, domains,
and floating IPs) in ways that align with the applications you host on
DigitalOcean.

### Supported Resource Types Examples

Projects resources are identified by uniform resource names or URNs. A
valid URN has the following format: `do:resource_type:resource_id`. The
following resource types are supported:

Resource Type      | Example URN
-------------------|------------
App Platform App   | `do:app:be5aab85-851b-4cab-b2ed-98d5a63ba4e8`
Database           | `do:dbaas:83c7a55f-0d84-4760-9245-aba076ec2fb2`
Domain             | `do:domain:example.com`
Droplet            | `do:droplet:4126873`
Floating IP        | `do:floatingip:192.168.99.100`
Kubernetes Cluster | `do:kubernetes:bd5f5959-5e1e-4205-a714-a914373942af`
Load Balancer      | `do:loadbalancer:39052d89-8dd4-4d49-8d5a-3c3b6b365b5b`
Space              | `do:space:my-website-assets`
Volume             | `do:volume:6fc4c277-ea5c-448a-93cd-dd496cfef71f`

### Resource Status Codes

When assigning and retrieving resources in projects, a `status` attribute
is returned that indicates if a resource was successfully retrieved or
assigned. The status codes can be one of the following:

Status Code        | Explanation
-------------------|------------
`ok`               | There was no problem retrieving or assigning a resource.
`not_found`        | The resource was not found.
`assigned`         | The resource was successfully assigned.
`already_assigned` | The resource was already assigned.
`service_down`     | There was a problem retrieving or assigning a resource. Please try again.

## List Project Resources

<a id="opIdprojects_list_resources"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/projects/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6/resources \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/projects/{project_id}/resources`

To list all your resources in a project, send a GET request to `/v2/projects/$PROJECT_ID/resources`.

This endpoint will only return resources that you are authorized to see. For example, to see Droplets in a project, include the `droplet:read` scope.


<h3 id="list-project-resources-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|project_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a project.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

```json
  "resources": [
```

## Assign Resources to a Project

<a id="opIdprojects_assign_resources"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/projects/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6/resources \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "resources": [
      "do:droplet:13457723",
      "do:domain:example.com"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/projects/{project_id}/resources`

To assign resources to a project, send a POST request to `/v2/projects/$PROJECT_ID/resources`.

You must have both `project:assign_resource` and `<resource>:read` scopes to assign new resources. For example, to assign a Droplet to a project, include both the `project:assign_resource` and `droplet:read` scopes. The `project:update` scope also grants `project:assign_resource`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "resources": [
    "do:droplet:13457723",
    "do:domain:example.com"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="assign-resources-to-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a project.|
|body|body|[project_assignment](#schemaproject_assignment)|true|none|
|» resources|body|[[urn](#schemaurn)]|false|A list of uniform resource names (URNs) to be added to a project. Only resources that you are authorized to see will be returned.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "resources": [
    {
      "urn": "do:droplet:13457723",
      "assigned_at": "2018-09-28T19:26:37Z",

      "status": "ok"
    },
    {

      "assigned_at": "2019-03-31T16:24:14Z",
      "links": {

      },
      "status": "ok"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

> default Response

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-projects">Projects</h1>

Projects allow you to organize your resources into groups that fit the way
you work. You can group resources (like Droplets, Spaces, load balancers,
domains, and floating IPs) in ways that align with the applications
you host on DigitalOcean.

## List All Projects

<a id="opIdprojects_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/projects \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/projects`

To list all your projects, send a GET request to `/v2/projects`.

<h3 id="list-all-projects-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

  "projects": [
    {
```

## Create a Project

<a id="opIdprojects_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/projects \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "my-web-api",
    "description": "My website API",
    "purpose": "Service or API",
    "environment": "Production"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/projects`

To create a project, send a POST request to `/v2/projects`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "my-web-api",
  "description": "My website API",
  "purpose": "Service or API",
  "environment": "Production"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The human-readable name for the project. The maximum length is 175 characters and the name must be unique.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the project. The maximum length is 255 characters.|
|» purpose|body|string|true|The purpose of the project. The maximum length is 255 characters. It can<br>have one of the following values:<br><br>- Just trying out DigitalOcean<br>- Class project / Educational purposes<br>- Website or blog<br>- Web Application<br>- Service or API<br>- Mobile Application<br>- Machine learning / AI / Data processing<br>- IoT<br>- Operational / Developer tooling<br><br>If another value for purpose is specified, for example, "your custom purpose",<br>your purpose will be stored as `Other: your custom purpose`.<br>|
|» environment|body|string|false|The environment of the project's resources.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» environment|Development|
|» environment|Staging|
|» environment|Production|

## Update a Project

<a id="opIdprojects_update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/projects/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "my-web-api",
    "description": "My website API",
    "purpose": "Service or API",
    "environment": "Production",
    "is_default": false
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/projects/{project_id}`

To update a project, send a PUT request to `/v2/projects/$PROJECT_ID`. All of the following attributes must be sent.

> Body parameter

```json

  "name": "my-web-api",
  "description": "My website API",
  "purpose": "Service or API",
  "environment": "Production",
  "is_default": false
}
```

## Delete an Existing Project

<a id="opIdprojects_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/projects/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/projects/{project_id}`

To delete a project, send a DELETE request to `/v2/projects/$PROJECT_ID`. To
be deleted, a project must not have any resources assigned to it. Any existing
resources must first be reassigned or destroyed, or you will receive a 412 error.

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.
This indicates that the request was processed successfully.


<h3 id="delete-an-existing-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a project.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 412 Response

```json
{
  "id": "precondition_failed",
  "message": "cannot delete a project with resources. move or remove the resources first"
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{

  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Patch a Project

<a id="opIdprojects_patch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/projects/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "my-web-api"
  }'
```

`PATCH /v2/projects/{project_id}`

To update only specific attributes of a project, send a PATCH request to `/v2/projects/$PROJECT_ID`. At least one of the following attributes needs to be sent.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "my-web-api"
}
```

<h3 id="patch-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a project.|
|body|body|[project](#schemaproject)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The human-readable name for the project. The maximum length is 175 characters and the name must be unique.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the project. The maximum length is 255 characters.|
|» purpose|body|string|false|The purpose of the project. The maximum length is 255 characters. It can<br>have one of the following values:<br><br>- Just trying out DigitalOcean<br>- Class project / Educational purposes<br>- Website or blog<br>- Web Application<br>- Service or API<br>- Mobile Application<br>- Machine learning / AI / Data processing<br>- IoT<br>- Operational / Developer tooling<br><br>If another value for purpose is specified, for example, "your custom purpose",<br>your purpose will be stored as `Other: your custom purpose`.<br>|
|» environment|body|string|false|The environment of the project's resources.|
|» is_default|body|boolean|false|If true, all resources will be added to this project if no project is specified.|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-reserved-ip-actions">Reserved IP Actions</h1>

As of 16 June 2022, we have renamed the [Floating IP](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/api-reference/#tag/Floating-IPs)
product to Reserved IPs. The Reserved IP product's endpoints function the exact
same way as Floating IPs. The only difference is the name change throughout the
URLs and fields. For example, the `floating_ips` field is now the `reserved_ips` field.
The Floating IP endpoints will remain active until fall 2023 before being
permanently deprecated.

With the exception of the [Projects API](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/api-reference/#tag/Projects),
we will reflect this change as an additional field in the responses across the API
where the `floating_ip` field is used. For example, the Droplet metadata response
will contain the field `reserved_ips` in addition to the `floating_ips` field.
Floating IPs retrieved using the Projects API will retain the original name.

Reserved IP actions are commands that can be given to a DigitalOcean
reserved IP. These requests are made on the actions endpoint of a specific
reserved IP.

An action object is returned. These objects hold the current status of the
requested action.

## List All Actions for a Reserved IP

<a id="opIdreservedIPsActions_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/reserved_ips/45.55.96.47/actions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/reserved_ips/{reserved_ip}/actions`

## Initiate a Reserved IP Action

<a id="opIdreservedIPsActions_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/reserved_ips/45.55.96.47/actions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "assign"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/reserved_ips/{reserved_ip}/actions`

To initiate an action on a reserved IP send a POST request to
`/v2/reserved_ips/$RESERVED_IP/actions`. In the JSON body to the request,
set the `type` attribute to on of the supported action types:

| Action     | Details
|------------|--------
| `assign`   | Assigns a reserved IP to a Droplet
| `unassign` | Unassign a reserved IP from a Droplet


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "assign"
}
```

<h3 id="initiate-a-reserved-ip-action-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|reserved_ip|path|string(ipv4)|true|A reserved IP address.|
|body|body|[reserved_ip_action_unassign](#schemareserved_ip_action_unassign) \| [reserved_ip_action_assign](#schemareserved_ip_action_assign)|false|The `type` attribute set in the request body will specify the action that<br>will be taken on the reserved IP.<br>|
|» *anyOf*|body|[reserved_ip_action_unassign](#schemareserved_ip_action_unassign)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[reserved_ip_action_assign](#schemareserved_ip_action_assign)|false|none|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-reserved-ips">Reserved IPs</h1>

As of 16 June 2022, we have renamed the [Floating IP](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/api-reference/#tag/Floating-IPs)
product to Reserved IPs. The Reserved IP product's endpoints function the exact
same way as Floating IPs. The only difference is the name change throughout the
URLs and fields. For example, the `floating_ips` field is now the `reserved_ips` field.
The Floating IP endpoints will remain active until fall 2023 before being
permanently deprecated.

With the exception of the [Projects API](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/api-reference/#tag/Projects),
we will reflect this change as an additional field in the responses across the API
where the `floating_ip` field is used. For example, the Droplet metadata response
will contain the field `reserved_ips` in addition to the `floating_ips` field.
Floating IPs retrieved using the Projects API will retain the original name.

DigitalOcean Reserved IPs are publicly-accessible static IP addresses that can be
mapped to one of your Droplets. They can be used to create highly available
setups or other configurations requiring movable addresses.

Reserved IPs are bound to a specific region.

## Create a New Reserved IP

<a id="opIdreservedIPs_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/reserved_ips \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "droplet_id": 2457247
  }'
```

`POST /v2/reserved_ips`

On creation, a reserved IP must be either assigned to a Droplet or reserved to a region.
* To create a new reserved IP assigned to a Droplet, send a POST
  request to `/v2/reserved_ips` with the `droplet_id` attribute.

* To create a new reserved IP reserved to a region, send a POST request to
  `/v2/reserved_ips` with the `region` attribute.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "droplet_id": 2457247
}
```

|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|

|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» region|body|string|true|The slug identifier for the region the reserved IP will be reserved to.|
|» project_id|body|string(uuid)|false|The UUID of the project to which the reserved IP will be assigned.|

## Delete a Reserved IP

<a id="opIdreservedIPs_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/reserved_ips/45.55.96.47 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/reserved_ips/{reserved_ip}`

To delete a reserved IP and remove it from your account, send a DELETE request
to `/v2/reserved_ips/$RESERVED_IP_ADDR`.

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.
This indicates that the request was processed successfully.

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-reserved-ipv6">Reserved IPv6</h1>

DigitalOcean Reserved IPv6s are publicly-accessible static IP addresses that can be
mapped to one of your Droplets. They can be used to create highly available
setups or other configurations requiring movable addresses.

Reserved IPv6s are bound to a specific region.

## List All Reserved IPv6s

<a id="opIdreservedIPv6_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/reserved_ipv6 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/reserved_ipv6`

To list all of the reserved IPv6s available on your account, send a GET request to `/v2/reserved_ipv6`.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

## Create a New Reserved IPv6

<a id="opIdreservedIPv6_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/reserved_ipv6 \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "region_slug": "nyc3"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/reserved_ipv6`

On creation, a reserved IPv6 must be reserved to a region.
* To create a new reserved IPv6 reserved to a region, send a POST request to
  `/v2/reserved_ipv6` with the `region_slug` attribute.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "region_slug": "nyc3"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[reserved_ipv6_create](#schemareserved_ipv6_create)|true|none|
|» region_slug|body|string|true|The slug identifier for the region the reserved IPv6 will be reserved to.|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-reserved-ipv6-actions">Reserved IPv6 Actions</h1>

Reserved IPv6 actions requests are made on the actions endpoint of a specific
reserved IPv6.

An action object is returned. These objects hold the current status of the
requested action.

## Initiate a Reserved IPv6 Action

<a id="opIdreservedIPv6Actions_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/reserved_ipv6/2409%3A40d0%3Af7%3A1017%3A74b4%3A3a96%3A105e%3A4c6e/actions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "assign"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/reserved_ipv6/{reserved_ipv6}/actions`

To initiate an action on a reserved IPv6 send a POST request to
`/v2/reserved_ipv6/$RESERVED_IPV6/actions`. In the JSON body to the request,
set the `type` attribute to on of the supported action types:

| Action     | Details
|------------|--------
| `assign`   | Assigns a reserved IPv6 to a Droplet
| `unassign` | Unassign a reserved IPv6 from a Droplet


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "assign"
}
```

<h3 id="initiate-a-reserved-ipv6-action-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|reserved_ipv6|path|string(ipv6)|true|A reserved IPv6 address.|
|body|body|[reserved_ipv6_action_unassign](#schemareserved_ipv6_action_unassign) \| [reserved_ipv6_action_assign](#schemareserved_ipv6_action_assign)|false|The `type` attribute set in the request body will specify the action that<br>will be taken on the reserved IPv6.<br>|
|» *anyOf*|body|[reserved_ipv6_action_unassign](#schemareserved_ipv6_action_unassign)|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|[reserved_ipv6_action_assign](#schemareserved_ipv6_action_assign)|false|none|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-signals">Signals</h1>

The DigitalOcean Signals API provides observability for environment
conversations, such as Harness Runtime conversations and Serverless
Inference chat completions, detecting behavioral signals such as
user disengagement, execution failures, and satisfaction indicators.

Use the consent endpoints to manage whether signals collection is
enabled — per environment for Harness Runtime (`source=agent`) and per team
for Serverless Inference chat completions (`source=inference`) — the
session endpoints to browse conversations and their detected signals,
the export endpoints to create downloadable archives of signals data
for offline analysis, and the deletion endpoints to permanently delete
Signals conversations for an environment or Serverless Inference
conversations for a whole team (aggregated Insights or metrics
summaries may still remain).

## List All Consent Records

<a id="opIdsignals_list_consents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v1/consent \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/consent`

To list all signals consent records for your team, send a GET request to
`/v1/consent`. Each record indicates whether signals collection is enabled
for a source: per-environment records (`source: agent`) for Harness Runtime, and
the team-level record (`source: inference`) for Serverless Inference chat
completions.

Pass `?source=agent` or `?source=inference` to return only that source's

## Update Team-Level Consent

<a id="opIdsignals_update_team_consent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.digitalocean.com/v1/consent?source=inference' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "enabled": true
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/consent`

To enable or disable signals collection for a source that is consented at
the team level, send a PUT request to `/v1/consent?source=inference` with
an `enabled` boolean in the request body. Currently the only team-level
source is `inference`, which covers Serverless Inference chat completions
made by your team.

To revoke consent, send the same request with `enabled` set to `false`.
The `source` query parameter is required. Per-environment consent for Harness
Runtime environments is managed with `PUT /v1/consent/{environment_id}` instead.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enabled": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-team-level-consent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|source|query|string|true|The consent source to update. Only team-level sources are accepted on this endpoint; currently `inference` (Serverless Inference chat completions). Per-environment consent (`agent`) is managed with `PUT /v1/consent/{environment_id}` instead.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» enabled|body|boolean|true|Whether to enable signals collection for this source.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|source|inference|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "consent": {
    "id": 21,
    "team_id": 39449946,
    "source": "inference",
    "agent_id": "",
    "enabled": true,
    "updated_at": "2026-10-09T11:41:27.104822Z"
  }
}
```

## Retrieve Consent for an Environment

<a id="opIdsignals_get_consent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/consent/{environment_id}`

To retrieve the consent record for a specific environment, send a GET
request to `/v1/consent/{environment_id}`. The response includes an `enabled`
field indicating whether signals collection is on for this environment.

This endpoint only serves per-environment (`source: agent`) records. Team-level
inference consent is read from `GET /v1/consent?source=inference`.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|environment_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for an environment. For Harness Runtime, this is the Environment Config ID. Formerly named agent_id.|

```json
{
```

## Create an Export Job

<a id="opIdsignals_create_export"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v1/signals/exports \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "environment_id": "01a0f3d5-b58d-7c99-a743-7ca0397b7f5d",
    "signal_type": [
      "ExecutionFailureToolNotFound"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v1/signals/exports`

To create a new signals data export, send a POST request to
`/v1/signals/exports`. To export one Harness Runtime environment, include its
`environment_id` (`type` defaults to `agent`). Deprecated `agent_id` is still
accepted. To export the team's Serverless Inference Signals conversations, set
`type` to `inference` and omit `environment_id` and `agent_id`. You may
optionally filter the export by `signal_type`,
`session_ids`, `start_time`, and `end_time`. Use the export options endpoint
to discover available signal types.

The export job runs asynchronously. Poll the get export endpoint to check
its status. When complete, use the download endpoint to retrieve a
pre-signed URL.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "environment_id": "01a0f3d5-b58d-7c99-a743-7ca0397b7f5d",
  "signal_type": [
    "ExecutionFailureToolNotFound"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-export-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[create_export_request](#schemacreate_export_request)|true|none|
|» type|body|string|false|The scope of the export. `agent` exports Signals conversations for one Harness Runtime environment and requires `environment_id` (or deprecated `agent_id`). `inference` exports Serverless Inference Signals conversations for the whole team (team-wide; omit `environment_id` and `agent_id`). Defaults to `agent` when `environment_id` or `agent_id` is provided and to `inference` when both are omitted.|
|» environment_id|body|string(uuid)|false|The environment whose data should be exported. For Harness Runtime, this is the Environment Config ID. Required when `type` is `agent` if `agent_id` is omitted; must be omitted when `type` is `inference`. Prefer this over `agent_id`.|
|» agent_id|body|string(uuid)|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated alias for `environment_id`. Accepted for backward compatibility; must equal `environment_id` when both are set. Both set and different returns 400. Required when `type` is `agent` if `environment_id` is omitted; must be omitted when `type` is `inference`.|
|» signal_type|body|[string]|false|Filter the export to only include the specified signal types. Use the export options endpoint to list available values.|
|» session_ids|body|[string(uuid)]|false|Optional list of specific session IDs to include in the export.|
|» start_time|body|string(date-time)|false|Include only sessions that started at or after this timestamp.|
|» end_time|body|string(date-time)|false|Include only sessions that started at or before this timestamp.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|agent|
|» type|inference|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "export_id": "9f13c09c-c877-436b-9863-dcc39c9dd737",
  "type": "agent",
  "agent_id": "01a0f3d5-b58d-7c99-a743-7ca0397b7f5d",
```
