## Send Prompt to a Model Using the Responses API

<a id="opIdinference_create_response"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v1/responses \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "model": "openai-gpt-oss-20b",
    "input": "What is the capital of France?",
    "max_output_tokens": 50,
    "temperature": 0.7,
    "stream": false,
    "instructions": "You are a helpful assistant.",
    "top_p": 1,
    "stream_options": null,
    "tools": [
      {
        "type": "function",
        "name": "get_weather",
        "description": "Get the current weather in a given location.",
        "parameters": {}
      }
    ],
    "tool_choice": "auto",
    "stop": null,
    "metadata": {
      "session_id": "abc123"
    },
    "user": "user-1234"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/responses`

Generate text responses from text prompts. This endpoint supports both streaming and non-streaming responses for supported text models.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "model": "openai-gpt-oss-20b",
  "input": "What is the capital of France?",
  "max_output_tokens": 50,
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "stream": false,
  "instructions": "You are a helpful assistant.",
  "top_p": 1,
  "stream_options": null,
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "name": "get_weather",
      "description": "Get the current weather in a given location.",
      "parameters": {}
    }
  ],
  "tool_choice": "auto",
  "stop": null,
  "metadata": {
    "session_id": "abc123"
  },
  "user": "user-1234"
}
```

<h3 id="send-prompt-to-a-model-using-the-responses-api-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[create_response_request](#schemacreate_response_request)|true|none|
|» model|body|string|true|The model ID of the model you want to use. Get the model ID using `/v1/models` or on the available models page.<br>|
|» input|body|string \| [object]|true|The prompt or input content you want the model to respond to. Can be a simple text string or an array of message objects for conversation context.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|Simple text input prompt.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[object]|false|Array of message objects for conversation context.|
|» role|body|string|false|The role of the message author.|
|» content|body|string|true|The content of the message.|
|» max_output_tokens|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.<br>|
|» temperature|body|number \| null|false|A value between 0.0 and 2.0 to control randomness and creativity. Lower values like 0.2 make the output more focused and deterministic, while higher values like 0.8 make it more random.<br>|
|» stream|body|boolean \| null|false|Set to true to stream partial responses as Server-Sent Events.<br>|
|» instructions|body|string \| null|false|System-level instructions for the model. This sets the behavior and context for the response generation.<br>|
|» top_p|body|number \| null|false|An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass.<br>|
|» stream_options|body|object \| null|false|Options for streaming response. Only set this when you set stream to true.|
|» » include_usage|body|boolean|false|If set, an additional chunk will be streamed before the data: [DONE] message with token usage statistics for the entire request.<br>|
|» tools|body|[object]|false|A list of tools the model may call.<br>|
|» » type|body|string|true|The type of the tool.|
|» » name|body|string|false|The name of the function to be called.|
|» » description|body|string|false|A description of what the function does.|
|» » parameters|body|object|false|The parameters the function accepts, described as a JSON Schema object.|
|» tool_choice|body|string \| object|false|Controls which (if any) tool is called by the model.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » type|body|string|true|none|
|» » function|body|object|true|none|
|» » » name|body|string|true|The name of the function to call.|
|» stop|body|string \| [string] \| null|false|Up to 4 sequences where the API will stop generating further tokens.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» metadata|body|object \| null|false|Set of key-value pairs that can be attached to the request.<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» user|body|string \| null|false|A unique identifier representing your end-user.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» role|user|
|» role|assistant|
|» role|system|
|» role|tool|
|» role|developer|
|» » type|function|
|» » *oneOf*|none|
|» » *oneOf*|auto|
|» » *oneOf*|required|
|» » type|function|

## Generate Image, Audio, or Text-to-Speech Using fal Models

<a id="opIdinference_create_async_invoke"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v1/async-invoke \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "model_id": "fal-ai/flux/schnell",
    "input": {
      "prompt": "A futuristic city at sunset"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v1/async-invoke`

Generate Image, Audio, or Text-to-Speech Using fal Models. This endpoint starts an asynchronous job and returns a request_id. The job status is QUEUED initially. Use the request_id to poll for the result.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "model_id": "fal-ai/flux/schnell",
  "input": {
    "prompt": "A futuristic city at sunset"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="generate-image-audio-or-text-to-speech-using-fal-models-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[async_invoke_request](#schemaasync_invoke_request)|true|none|
|» model_id|body|string|true|The ID of the model to invoke asynchronously.<br>|
|» input|body|object|true|The input parameters for the model invocation. Fields vary by model type.<br><br>For **image generation** models (e.g., `fal-ai/flux/schnell`, `fal-ai/fast-sdxl`), use `prompt` along with optional image parameters like `output_format`, `num_inference_steps`, `guidance_scale`, `num_images`, and `enable_safety_checker`.<br><br>For **audio generation** models (e.g., `fal-ai/stable-audio-25/text-to-audio`), use `prompt` along with `seconds_total` to control the duration.<br><br>For **text-to-speech** models (e.g., `fal-ai/elevenlabs/tts/multilingual-v2`), use `text` with the content you want converted to speech.<br>|
|» » prompt|body|string|false|The text prompt describing the desired output. Used for image generation and audio generation models.<br>|
|» » text|body|string|false|The text content to convert to speech. Used for text-to-speech models.<br>|
|» » output_format|body|string \| null|false|The desired output format or aspect ratio for image generation.<br>|
|» » num_inference_steps|body|integer \| null|false|The number of inference steps to use during image generation. More steps generally produce higher quality output but take longer.<br>|
|» » guidance_scale|body|number \| null|false|Controls how closely the image generation model follows the prompt. Higher values produce output more closely matching the prompt.<br>|
|» » num_images|body|integer \| null|false|The number of images to generate.|
|» » enable_safety_checker|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether to enable the safety checker for generated content.|
|» » seconds_total|body|integer \| null|false|The total duration in seconds for generated audio. Used for audio generation models.<br>|
|» tags|body|[object]|false|An optional list of key-value tags to attach to the invocation request for tracking or categorization.<br>|
|» » key|body|string|true|The tag key.|
|» » value|body|string|true|The tag value.|

## Generate speech from text

<a id="opIdinference_create_speech"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v1/audio/speech \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "model": "qwen3-tts-voicedesign",
    "input": "Hello, world!",
    "voice": "alloy",
    "response_format": "mp3",
    "instructions": "Speak naturally."
  }'
```

`POST /v1/audio/speech`

Convert text input to speech audio. The response may be raw audio bytes (`audio/mpeg`, `audio/wav`, and similar) or a JSON envelope with base64-encoded audio in `data[].b64_json`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "model": "qwen3-tts-voicedesign",
  "input": "Hello, world!",
  "voice": "alloy",
  "response_format": "mp3",
  "instructions": "Speak naturally."
}
```

<h3 id="generate-speech-from-text-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[create_speech_request](#schemacreate_speech_request)|true|none|
|» model|body|string|true|The text-to-speech model to use.|
|» input|body|string|true|The text to convert to speech.|
|» voice|body|string|false|The voice to use for synthesis.|
|» response_format|body|string|false|The audio format to return. Supported values include `mp3` and `wav`. The API may return raw audio bytes or a JSON envelope with base64-encoded audio.<br>|
|» instructions|body|string|false|Optional style or delivery instructions for the synthesizer.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "created": 1710700000,
  "data": [
    {
      "b64_json": "//uQxAAAA..."
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Start a video generation job

<a id="opIdinference_create_video"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v1/videos \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "model": "wan2-2-t2v-a14b",
    "prompt": "Two anthropomorphic cats in boxing gear fight intensely on a spotlighted stage",
    "size": "1280x720",
    "fps": 16
  }'
```

`POST /v1/videos`

Start an asynchronous video generation job from a text prompt. Poll `GET /v1/videos/{video_id}` until the job reaches a terminal status, then download the MP4 with `GET /v1/videos/{video_id}/content` or from `output.url` when present.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "model": "wan2-2-t2v-a14b",
  "prompt": "Two anthropomorphic cats in boxing gear fight intensely on a spotlighted stage",
  "size": "1280x720",
  "fps": 16
}
```

<h3 id="start-a-video-generation-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[create_video_request](#schemacreate_video_request)|true|none|
|» model|body|string|true|The video generation model to use.|
|» prompt|body|string|true|A text description of the desired video.|
|» size|body|string|false|The output resolution, for example `1280x720`.|
|» fps|body|integer|false|Frames per second for the generated video.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "video_bGl0ZWxsbTpjdXN0b21fbGxtX3Byb3ZpZGVyOm9wZW5haTttb2RlbF9pZDo7dmlkZW9faWQ6ZGExYjFmYzMtYTM3NC00MmM0LTgxMWMtOWE5NmE3ZWY0OTIz",
  "object": "video",
  "created_at": 1777003604,
  "model": "wan2.2-t2v-a14b",
  "status": "processing",
  "output": {
    "url": "https://example.com/output.mp4"
  },
  "error": {},
  "x_request_id": "string"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-agent-inference">Agent Inference</h1>

DigitalOcean Agent Platform allows you to create multi-agent workflows
to power your AI applications. This allows developers to integrate agents into your
AI applications.

**Note:** The Agent Inference API uses a customer-specific base URL (the agent endpoint)
and is independent of the main DigitalOcean control-plane API (`https://api.digitalocean.com`).

## Create a model response for the given chat conversation

<a id="opIdagentInference_create_chat_completion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.digitalocean.com/api/v1/chat/completions?agent=true' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "user",
        "content": "Hello, how are you?",
        "refusal": null,
        "tool_calls": [
          {
            "id": "call_abc123",
            "type": "function",
            "function": {
              "name": "get_weather",
              "arguments": "{\"location\": \"Boston\"}"
            }
          }
        ],
        "tool_call_id": "call_abc123",
        "reasoning_content": null
      }
    ],
    "model": "llama3-8b-instruct",
    "max_tokens": 0,
    "max_completion_tokens": 256,
    "frequency_penalty": 0,
    "presence_penalty": 0,
    "top_logprobs": 0,
    "tools": [
      {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
          "name": "get_weather",
          "description": "Get the current weather for a location.",
          "parameters": {}
        }
      }
    ],
    "tool_choice": "none",
    "stream": false,
    "stop": null,
    "logit_bias": null,
    "logprobs": false,
    "n": 1,
    "stream_options": null,
    "reasoning_effort": "none",
    "seed": 0,
    "metadata": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "temperature": 1,
    "top_p": 1,
    "user": "user-1234"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/chat/completions`

<h3 id="create-a-model-response-for-the-given-chat-conversation-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|agent|query|boolean|true|Must be set to true for agent-based completion behavior.|
|body|body|[chat_completion_request](#schemachat_completion_request)|true|none|
|» messages|body|[[chat_message](#schemachat_message)]|true|A list of messages comprising the conversation so far.|
|» model|body|string|true|Model ID used to generate the response.|
|» max_tokens|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of tokens that can be generated in the completion. The token count of your prompt plus max_tokens cannot exceed the model's context length.<br>|
|» max_completion_tokens|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum number of completion tokens that may be used over the course of the run. The run will make a best effort to use only the number of completion tokens specified, across multiple turns of the run.<br>|
|» frequency_penalty|body|number \| null|false|Number between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values penalize new tokens based on their existing frequency in the text so far, decreasing the model's likelihood to repeat the same line verbatim.<br>|
|» presence_penalty|body|number \| null|false|Number between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values penalize new tokens based on whether they appear in the text so far, increasing the model's likelihood to talk about new topics.<br>|
|» top_logprobs|body|integer \| null|false|An integer between 0 and 20 specifying the number of most likely tokens to return at each token position, each with an associated log probability. logprobs must be set to true if this parameter is used.<br>|
|» tools|body|[[chat_completion_tool](#schemachat_completion_tool)]|false|A list of tools the model may call. Currently, only functions are supported as a tool.|
|» tool_choice|body|string \| object|false|Controls which (if any) tool is called by the model. none means the model will not call any tool and instead generates a message. auto means the model can pick between generating a message or calling one or more tools. required means the model must call one or more tools. Specifying a particular tool via {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "my_function"}} forces the model to call that tool. none is the default when no tools are present. auto is the default if tools are present.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|Force a specific tool to be called.|
|» » type|body|string|true|none|
|» » function|body|object|true|none|
|» » » name|body|string|true|The name of the function to call.|
|» stream|body|boolean \| null|false|If set to true, the model response data will be streamed to the client as it is generated using server-sent events.<br>|
|» stop|body|string \| [string]|false|Up to 4 sequences where the API will stop generating further tokens. The returned text will not contain the stop sequence.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» logit_bias|body|object \| null|false|Modify the likelihood of specified tokens appearing in the completion. Accepts a JSON object that maps tokens (specified by their token ID in the tokenizer) to an associated bias value from -100 to 100. Mathematically, the bias is added to the logits generated by the model prior to sampling. The exact effect will vary per model, but values between -1 and 1 should decrease or increase likelihood of selection; values like -100 or 100 should result in a ban or exclusive selection of the relevant token.<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|integer|false|none|
|» logprobs|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether to return log probabilities of the output tokens or not. If true, returns the log probabilities of each output token returned in the content of message.<br>|
|» n|body|integer \| null|false|How many chat completion choices to generate for each input message. Note that you will be charged based on the number of generated tokens across all of the choices. Keep n as 1 to minimize costs.|
|» stream_options|body|object \| null|false|Options for streaming response. Only set this when you set stream to true.|
|» » include_usage|body|boolean|false|If set, an additional chunk will be streamed before the data [DONE] message. The usage field on this chunk shows the token usage statistics for the entire request, and the choices field will always be an empty array.|
|» reasoning_effort|body|string \| null|false|Constrains effort on reasoning for reasoning models. Reducing reasoning effort can result in faster responses and fewer tokens used on reasoning in a response.<br>|
|» seed|body|integer \| null|false|If specified, the system will make a best effort to sample deterministically, such that repeated requests with the same seed and parameters should return the same result. Determinism is not guaranteed.<br>|
|» metadata|body|object \| null|false|Set of 16 key-value pairs that can be attached to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Keys are strings with a maximum length of 64 characters. Values are strings with a maximum length of 512 characters.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» temperature|body|number \| null|false|What sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic. We generally recommend altering this or top_p but not both.<br>|
|» top_p|body|number \| null|false|An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered. We generally recommend altering this or temperature but not both.<br>|
|» user|body|string|false|A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help DigitalOcean to monitor and detect abuse.|

#### Enumerated Values

|» » *oneOf*|none|
|» » *oneOf*|auto|
|» » *oneOf*|required|
|» » type|function|
|» reasoning_effort|none|
|» reasoning_effort|minimal|
|» reasoning_effort|low|
|» reasoning_effort|medium|
|» reasoning_effort|high|
|» reasoning_effort|xhigh|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-batch-inference">Batch Inference</h1>

Batch Inference is an asynchronous processing capability designed to help
you scale high-volume AI projects more efficiently. Ideal for heavy-duty
workloads like large-scale data classification, evaluations, and content
enrichment, you can submit thousands or even millions of requests in a
single job with a guaranteed results window of 24 hours. By utilizing
off-peak GPU capacity, Batch Inference provides high-performance LLM
access at a significantly reduced price point compared to standard
synchronous APIs, making it a cost-effective choice for non-interactive
workloads.

## Create a Batch Inference Input File

<a id="opIdinference_create_batch_file"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v1/batches/files \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "file_name": "batch_requests.jsonl"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/batches/files`

Creates a file record and returns a `file_id` plus a short-lived presigned `PUT` URL (typically valid for ~15 minutes). Upload the raw JSONL bytes to `upload_url` (see `PUT /{upload_path}`) before calling `POST /v1/batches`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "file_name": "batch_requests.jsonl"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-batch-inference-input-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[batch_file_create_request](#schemabatch_file_create_request)|true|none|
|» file_name|body|string|true|The file you plan to upload. Must end with `.jsonl` (case-insensitive) and contain one request per line in the schema expected by the target `provider`.<br>|

## Upload a Batch Inference Input File

<a id="opIdinference_upload_batch_file"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.digitalocean.com/<upload_url>' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  --data-binary '@/path/to/file'
```

`PUT /<upload_url>`

Uploads the raw JSONL bytes to the presigned `upload_url` returned by `POST /v1/batches/files`.

**The URL is dynamic — do not construct it.** Use the `upload_url` value from the previous step verbatim. Its host, path, and query parameters are part of the short-lived (~15 minute) signature and change per request; the server and path shown here are illustrative. If the URL expires before the upload completes, create a new file intent and retry.

`POST /v1/batches` performs a `HEAD` check on the uploaded object and will reject the batch if this upload has not completed.

Send the raw JSONL bytes verbatim. Presigned PUT URLs are signature-sensitive to request headers — prefer `application/octet-stream` or omit `Content-Type` entirely. A custom value (for example `application/jsonl`) can cause signature mismatches unless the URL was signed for that exact header.


<h3 id="upload-a-batch-inference-input-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|string(binary)|true|Raw JSONL bytes — one request per line.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json

  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

`GET /v1/batches`

Returns a cursor-paginated list of batch jobs, ordered newest first. Use `limit` to control page size and `after` to page forward using the `last_id` from the previous response.

|status|query|string|false|Optional filter restricting results to batches in the given lifecycle state.<br>|

## Create a Batch Inference Job

<a id="opIdinference_create_batch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v1/batches \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "file_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4789-90ab-cdef12345678",
    "provider": "openai",
    "endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions",
    "completion_window": "24h",
    "request_id": "c7e3ad1e-20c3-4e47-9bf2-6f2a4d6a2f11"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/batches`

Submits a batch job against a previously uploaded JSONL input file. The upload must have completed before this call; otherwise the request is rejected.

Supply a unique `request_id` to make the submission idempotent — retries with the same value return the existing job. When `provider` is `openai`, the `url` on each JSONL line must match `endpoint`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "file_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4789-90ab-cdef12345678",
  "provider": "openai",
  "endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions",
  "completion_window": "24h",
  "request_id": "c7e3ad1e-20c3-4e47-9bf2-6f2a4d6a2f11"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-batch-inference-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[batch_create_request](#schemabatch_create_request)|true|none|
|» file_id|body|string(uuid)|true|The `file_id` returned by `POST /v1/batches/files`.|
|» provider|body|string|true|The inference provider whose JSONL schema the input file conforms to. `openai` follows the OpenAI Batch API input schema (`custom_id`, `method`, `url`, `body`); `anthropic` follows the Anthropic Message Batches JSONL conventions.<br>|
|» endpoint|body|string|false|Inference endpoint each request is dispatched to. **Required when `provider` is `openai` and must match the `url` on every JSONL line. Must be omitted when `provider` is `anthropic`.**<br>|
|» completion_window|body|string|true|Time window in which the job must complete. Jobs that do not finish in time transition to `expired`.<br>|
|» request_id|body|string|true|Client-supplied idempotency key. Retries with the same value return the existing job instead of creating a duplicate.<br>|
|» metadata|body|object \| null|false|Optional string-valued metadata to attach to the job.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» provider|openai|
|» provider|anthropic|
|» endpoint|/v1/responses|
|» endpoint|/v1/chat/completions|
|» completion_window|24h|

## Retrieve a Batch Inference Job

<a id="opIdinference_get_batch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v1/batches/0e9d1d35-3d1e-4d66-9a2f-8c7e0f6b3e21 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/batches/{batch_id}`

Returns the current state of a batch job. Poll until `status` reaches a terminal value (`completed`, `failed`, `expired`, or `cancelled`).

## Get Batch Inference Results Download Links

<a id="opIdinference_get_batch_results"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v1/batches/0e9d1d35-3d1e-4d66-9a2f-8c7e0f6b3e21/results \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/batches/{batch_id}/results`

Returns short-lived presigned download URLs for the output (and optional error sidecar) of a completed batch job. If results are not yet ready, the response sets `result_available: false` or returns `412 Precondition Failed`; in both cases, keep polling batch status and retry.

Download the artifacts soon after fetching — the URLs are short-lived. Result files themselves are retained for up to 30 days after the job completes, after which they are deleted.


<h3 id="get-batch-inference-results-download-links-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|batch_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The batch job identifier.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "batch_id": "0e9d1d35-3d1e-4d66-9a2f-8c7e0f6b3e21",
  "result_available": true,
  "output_file_url": "https://batch-inference.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/outputs/0e9d1d35-3d1e-4d66-9a2f-8c7e0f6b3e21.jsonl?X-Amz-Signature=...",
  "error_file_url": null,
  "expires_at": "2026-04-24T20:19:19Z"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json

  "id": "forbidden",
  "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 412 Response

```json

  "id": "precondition_failed",
  "message": "Batch results are not yet available. Retry once the job has completed."
}
```

```json

  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API rate limit exceeded."
}
```

```json
}
```

> default Response

```json
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Cancel a Batch Inference Job

<a id="opIdinference_cancel_batch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.digitalocean.com/v1/batches/0e9d1d35-3d1e-4d66-9a2f-8c7e0f6b3e21/cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v1/batches/{batch_id}/cancel`

Requests cancellation of a batch job. The job transitions to `cancelling` and, once in-flight requests drain, to `cancelled`. Jobs already in a terminal state (`completed`, `failed`, `expired`, `cancelled`) cannot be cancelled and return `409 Conflict`. Cancellation is also rejected with `409 Conflict` while the job has not yet been submitted to the upstream provider — there is nothing to cancel until the provider batch id is assigned.

Partial results produced before cancellation remain available via `GET /v1/batches/{batch_id}/results`.


<h3 id="cancel-a-batch-inference-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|batch_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The batch job identifier.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|request_id|string|false|none|Optionally, some endpoints may include a request ID that should be  provided when reporting bugs or opening support tickets to help  identify the issue.|

<h2 id="tocS_connection">connection</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaconnection"></a>
<a id="schema_connection"></a>
<a id="tocSconnection"></a>
<a id="tocsconnection"></a>

```json
{
  "id": "39f9f768-a7f9-4c91-9557-3328c53dd054",
  "provider": "jira",
  "provider_display_name": "Jira",
  "user_id": "alice",
  "status": "active",
  "created_at": "2026-07-14T00:50:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-07-14T00:52:10Z",
  "revoked_at": null,
  "connection_parameters": {
    "site_url": "https://example.atlassian.net"
  },
  "credential_kind": "digitalocean_oauth",
  "credential_id": "",
  "network": {
    "vpc": {
      "vpc_uuid": "5a4981aa-9653-4bd1-bef5-d6bff52042e4",
      "region": "nyc3",
      "destinations": [
        {
          "host": "jira.internal.example.com",
          "port": 443,
          "allowed_ip_cidrs": [
            "10.116.0.0/20"
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "oauth": {
    "scopes": [
      "write:jira-work"
    ],
    "granted_at": "2026-07-14T00:52:10Z"
  },
  "api_key": {},
  "scopes": [
    "write:jira-work"
  ],
  "granted_at": "2026-07-14T00:52:10Z",
  "owning_user_id": "2f8e1c3a-6b4d-4f7e-9a1c-5d3b7e9f1a2c"
}
```

One connection of any kind. Everything every kind has stays on the envelope, so a reader takes an ID, a status or a provider without first asking what kind it is; only the members a kind alone has move into details.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string(uuid)|false|none|Opaque connection ID.|
|provider|string|false|none|Provider slug, for example `jira`.|
|provider_display_name|string|false|none|Human-readable provider name, for example `Jira`.|
|user_id|string|false|none|Your identifier for the user the connection acts for.|
|status|string|false|none|pending, active, revoked, or expired.|
|created_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the connection was created.|
|updated_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the connection was last modified.|
|revoked_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the connection was revoked.|
|connection_parameters|object \| null|false|none|Non-sensitive provider configuration.|
|credential_kind|string|false|none|`digitalocean_oauth`, `private_oauth`, or `team_api_key`.|
|credential_id|string|false|none|Empty for `digitalocean_oauth`; otherwise the ID of the team provider credential the connection uses.|
|network|object|false|none|Private network the connection's calls use, when configured.|
|oauth|object|false|none|Set for `digitalocean_oauth` and `private_oauth` connections.|
|api_key|object|false|none|Set for `team_api_key` connections.|
|scopes|[string]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: read `oauth.scopes`. Duplicated here so a reader of the pre-union shape keeps working; empty for a kind with no OAuth grant.|
|granted_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: read `oauth.granted_at`.|
|owning_user_id|string|false|none|DigitalOcean user ID of the user who created the connection, when recorded.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|pending|
|status|active|
|status|revoked|
|status|expired|
|credential_kind|digitalocean_oauth|
|credential_kind|private_oauth|
|credential_kind|team_api_key|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|provider|string|true|none|Required provider slug, from the provider list.|

|connection_parameters|object|false|none|Values for the provider's `connection_parameters`, validated against their specifications.|
|credential|object|false|none|Optional credential to connect through. Omitted uses DigitalOcean's shared OAuth application.|
|network|object|false|none|Optional private network for the connection's calls. Requires VPC networking to be enabled for your account (403 otherwise).|

|expires_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the authorization expires. The link can stop working earlier; if the connection becomes expired, create it again for a new link.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|requires_authorization|

|credentialRefSource|string|false|none|How requests to the server authenticate: none, secret (a key or token sent in the Authorization header), or connection (each user's own OAuth authorization).|
|credentialRef|string|false|none|The secret reference supplied at registration when source=secret, or the team's OAuth credential ID when source=connection. Empty when the server was registered with an `api_key`, whose storage DigitalOcean manages.|
|syncStatus|string|false|none|Outcome of the latest discovery: pending (no discovery has finished yet), ok, failed, or `unsupported_protocol`. It is not reset while a resync runs.|
|syncError|string|false|none|Why the latest discovery failed; empty after a successful one.|
|lastSyncedAt|string|false|none|When discovery last succeeded, in RFC 3339 format; empty until the first success.|
|protocolVersion|string|false|none|MCP protocol revision negotiated with the server.|
|toolCount|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of tools discovered on the server, whether enabled or not.|
|createdAt|string|false|none|When the server was registered, in RFC 3339 format.|
|updatedAt|string|false|none|When the server was last modified, in RFC 3339 format.|
|description|string|false|none|Team-authored description, shown on the server's catalog card. A resync does not replace it.|
|oauth_authorize_url|string|false|none|OAuth authorization endpoint. Set only when `credentialRefSource` is connection; the client secret is never returned.|
|oauth_scopes|[string]|false|none|OAuth scopes requested from each user. Set only when `credentialRefSource` is connection.|
|oauth_authorization_ttl_seconds|string(uint64)|false|none|How long a user's authorization is reused before re-consent. Echoed so a team can read the window without re-registering to discover it.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|transport|streamable_http|
|credentialRefSource|none|
|credentialRefSource|secret|
|credentialRefSource|connection|
|syncStatus|pending|
|syncStatus|ok|
|syncStatus|failed|
|syncStatus|unsupported_protocol|

<h2 id="tocS_mcp_server_create">mcp_server_create</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamcp_server_create"></a>
<a id="schema_mcp_server_create"></a>
<a id="tocSmcp_server_create"></a>
<a id="tocsmcp_server_create"></a>

```json
{
  "serverRef": "docs",
  "endpoint": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
  "transport": "streamable_http",
  "credentialRefSource": "secret",
  "description": "Internal documentation search.",
  "credentialRef": "",
  "api_key": "sk_live_example",
  "oauth_client_id": "",
  "oauth_client_secret": "",
  "oauth_authorize_url": "",
  "oauth_token_url": "",
  "oauth_scopes": [],
  "oauth_authorization_ttl_seconds": "86400"
}
```

Describes an MCP server to register.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|serverRef|string|true|none|Identifier for the server, unique within your team. Must match `^`[a-z]``[a-z0-9-]`{0,63}$`.|
|endpoint|string|true|none|HTTPS URL of the server's MCP endpoint. Its host must resolve only to public IP addresses. Required.|
|transport|string|false|none|Optional. `streamable_http`, the default and only accepted value.|
|credentialRefSource|string|false|none|How requests to the server authenticate: none (the default), secret, or connection. With secret, the value from `credentialRef` or `api_key` is sent in the Authorization header, prefixed with "Bearer " unless it already contains a space.|
|description|string|false|none|Optional description shown on the server's catalog card. At most 1024 characters.|
|credentialRef|string|false|none|For `credentialRefSource` secret: a reference to a secret your team stores with DigitalOcean. Must match `^`[A-Za-z0-9]``[A-Za-z0-9:/_.-]`{0,254}$`. Set exactly one of `credentialRef` and `api_key`.|
|api_key|string|false|write-only|For `credentialRefSource` secret: the key or token itself. DigitalOcean stores it; it is write-only and no response returns it. Set exactly one of `credentialRef` and `api_key`.|
|oauth_client_id|string|false|none|Required for `credentialRefSource` connection: the client ID of your team's OAuth client for the server. Each user of the server then authorizes individually.|
|oauth_client_secret|string|false|write-only|Required for `credentialRefSource` connection. Write-only; no response returns it.|
|oauth_authorize_url|string|false|none|Required for `credentialRefSource` connection: the OAuth authorization endpoint. It must use the endpoint's scheme and port, on the endpoint's host or another host under the same registrable domain.|
|oauth_token_url|string|false|none|Required for `credentialRefSource` connection: the OAuth token endpoint, under the same rules as `oauth_authorize_url`.|
|oauth_scopes|[string]|false|none|Required for `credentialRefSource` connection: the scopes to request from each user, 1 to 64 of them.|
|oauth_authorization_ttl_seconds|string(uint64)|false|none|How long, in seconds, a user's authorization may be reused before they must consent again. Optional;<br>0 means 30 days, and the maximum is 100 years.<br><br>Authorizations are not refreshed automatically, so this window, not the provider's token lifetime,<br>decides how often a user is sent back through consent. Set it no longer than the provider's own<br>token lifetime, so the prompt arrives before a tool call fails against an expired token.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|transport|streamable_http|
|credentialRefSource|none|
|credentialRefSource|secret|
|credentialRefSource|connection|

```json
  ]
```

Describes a projection of one tool version's output.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tool|string|false|none|Exactly one of tool or `tool_id` selects the tool version. tool is a provider-qualified slug, optionally pinned as `<tool>@<version>`. You can bind only the released version your catalog exposes: an unpinned slug resolves it and the response echoes it as version; a pin must equal it, and a `tool_id` (the opaque identity from tool search) must be that version. Any other version returns 404.|
|tool_id|string|false|none|Opaque ID of the tool version; see tool.|
|name|string|true|none|View name. Must match `^`[a-z]``[a-z0-9_-]`{0,63}$` and be unique per tool version within your team.|
|description|string|false|none|Optional description. At most 512 bytes.|
|fields|[string]|true|none|Output paths to keep, 1 to 64 of them. Each is a dotted path of up to 8 segments made of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, and must be declared by the tool's output schema; arrays are traversed element-wise. Paths may not repeat or be a prefix of one another. The tool version must declare an object output schema.|

```json
{
```

```json
    "defaultAction": "ask",

      {
        "tool": "exa_web_search",

      }
    ]
```
```json
  },
```

```json
    "toolbelt:search-toolbelt@1",

  ],

      "exa_web_search"
    ],
    "outputViews": {
      "exa_web_search": "titles-and-urls"
    },

    "vpcUuid": "5a4981aa-9653-4bd1-bef5-d6bff52042e4"

    "traces": false
  }

```

Describes a session to create.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|Required human-readable session name.|
|actorId|string|false|none|Optional actor binding: the user whose connections the session's tool calls use, matched against connection `user_id`. When set it must use the same alphabet as a connection's `user_id`, `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, at most 64 characters; anything else is rejected with 400.|
|policy|object|false|none|Optional tool-permission policy. Omitted asks before every call.|
|tools|[string]|false|none|Omitted enables every tool. An explicit empty array enables no tools. Direct tools may be `<tool>` or `<tool>@<version>`, using provider-qualified tool slugs, and a pinned version must be the released one; toolbelt references must be version-pinned as `toolbelt:<belt-name>@<version>`.|
|config|object|false|none|Optional session options. config.preloadTools may contain concrete tool names (optionally version-pinned) and version-pinned toolbelt references. config.customInstructions is a string of at most 1000 characters. config.outputViews maps up to 100 tool slugs to the name of an output view to apply to that tool's results.|
|network|object|false|none|Product-level session network binding. When set, `vpc_uuid` must identify a VPC owned by the session's team.|
|insights|object|false|none|Omitted when the request omitted insights or explicitly sent null.|

|description|string|false|none|Optional description. At most 255 bytes.|
|tools|[string]|false|none|Optional initial members, as catalog tool slugs (`<provider>_<name>`). Each may be pinned as `<tool_slug>@<version>`; a pin must equal the tool's current released version, and an unpinned tool is pinned to that version. Every tool must be an active catalog tool. Duplicates are merged; at most 500 tools. Empty creates a toolbelt with no tools.|

Catalog metadata for one toolbelt member, so a client can render a toolbelt without also fetching the tool catalog. Input and output schemas are omitted; the tool catalog (`GET /v2/action-gateway/tools`) carries them.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tool_slug|string|false|none|The provider-qualified, stable tool identifier (`<provider>_<name>`). Treat it as opaque and pass it back verbatim.|
|name|string|false|none|The unqualified tool name, without the provider prefix.|
|title|string|false|none|Human-readable tool title.|
|description|string|false|none|What the tool does.|
|provider|string|false|none|The ID of the provider that offers the tool, broken out so a client never has to split `tool_slug`.|
|category|string|false|none|Best-effort catalog metadata and is empty for a large share of the catalog. Do not rely on it being present.|
|version|integer(int32)|false|none|The version this toolbelt version pins for the member, matching the `@<version>` suffix in the corresponding toolbelt.tools entry.|

It is a page, so it is not the membership of the toolbelt: read toolbelt.tools for that, and toolbelt.tool_count for the total. Ordering matches toolbelt.tools.|

<h2 id="tocS_toolbelt_provider_summary">toolbelt_provider_summary</h2>

```json
{
  "provider": "exa",
  "tool_count": 2,
  "id": "exa",
  "name": "Exa",
  "description": "Web search tools backed by Exa.",
  "categories": [
    "web-search"
  ],
  "created_at": "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

One provider represented in a toolbelt's membership. Its provider fields (ID, name, description, `created_at`) match the toolkit entries of `GET /v2/action-gateway/tools/toolkits`, so a client can render the same provider card without a second request.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|provider|string|false|none|The provider ID. Members recorded without a provider are grouped under `_legacy`, which is also accepted in the provider path.|
|tool_count|integer(int32)|false|none|How many toolbelt members belong to this provider.|
|id|string|false|none|Equals provider; present so the entry has the same shape as a toolkit.|
|name|string|false|none|The provider's display name. Empty for `_legacy`.|
|description|string|false|none|Provider description. Empty for `_legacy`.|
|categories|[string]|false|none|The distinct tool categories among this toolbelt's members for the provider (sorted). Empty for `_legacy` or when no member has a category.|
|created_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the provider was added to the catalog. Unset for `_legacy`.|

Summarizes a released tool.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|Tool name, without the provider prefix.|
|toolkitId|string|false|none|ID of the provider that offers the tool. For a tool from one of your team's MCP servers it is that server's `serverRef`.|
|toolSlug|string|false|none|The provider-qualified, stable tool identifier `<toolkit_id>_<name>`. Pass this value back verbatim to the toolbelt add/remove endpoints; clients should treat it as opaque rather than reconstructing it from `toolkitId` and name.|
|title|string|false|none|Human-readable tool title.|
|description|string|false|none|What the tool does.|
|version|string|false|none|Released version, for example `v3`.|
|inputSchema|object \| null|false|none|JSON Schema the tool's arguments must satisfy.|
|outputSchema|object \| null|false|none|JSON Schema of the tool's result, when declared.|
|annotations|object|false|none|Advisory behavior hints for the tool.|
|parallelizable|boolean|false|none|Catalog hint that calls to the tool may run in parallel.|
|streamingSafe|boolean|false|none|Catalog hint that the tool's result can be streamed.|

<h2 id="tocS_health_metrics">health_metrics</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemahealth_metrics"></a>

<a id="tocShealth_metrics"></a>
<a id="tocshealth_metrics"></a>

```json
{
  "data_status": "HEALTH_DATA_STATUS_AVAILABLE",
  "uptime_percentage": 99.82,
  "latency_p50_ms": 412.5,
  "latency_p95_ms": 1180
}
```

Availability and latency of a tool or provider over a window, aggregated across all customers. Request volumes are not reported.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data_status|string|false|none|`HEALTH_DATA_STATUS_AVAILABLE` when the window has calls to measure; `HEALTH_DATA_STATUS_NO_DATA` when it has none, in which case the metrics are null. Do not treat no data as healthy.|
|uptime_percentage|number(double) \| null|false|none|Percentage of calls that did not fail because of the provider (an upstream error, timeout, rate limit, or unavailability). Calls that failed for other reasons are not counted.|
|latency_p50_ms|number(double) \| null|false|none|Median duration of successful calls, in milliseconds. Durations above 40960 ms are reported as 40960.|
|latency_p95_ms|number(double) \| null|false|none|95th-percentile duration of successful calls, in milliseconds. Durations above 40960 ms are reported as 40960.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|data_status|HEALTH_DATA_STATUS_AVAILABLE|
|data_status|HEALTH_DATA_STATUS_NO_DATA|

```json
{
  "key": "site_url",
  "label": "Jira site URL",
  "description": "The HTTPS origin of the Jira Cloud site to use.",
  "input_kind": "https_origin",
  "required": true,
  "normalization": "https_origin",
  "allowed_values": [],

    "atlassian.net"
  ],
  "max_length": 255,
  "pattern": ""
}
```

Describes one non-sensitive value collected while configuring a provider connection. Clients can render these specifications generically.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|key|string|false|none|Key of the value in `connection_parameters` or `credential_parameters`.|
|label|string|false|none|Display label.|
|description|string|false|none|Help text.|
|input_kind|string|false|none|How the value is entered: string, `https_origin`, or enum.|
|required|boolean|false|none|Whether the value must be supplied.|
|normalization|string|false|none|How the value is normalized before it is validated and stored: trim, lowercase, uppercase, or `https_origin`.|
|allowed_values|[string]|false|none|For enum inputs, the accepted values.|
|allowed_host_suffixes|[string]|false|none|For `https_origin` inputs, the host suffixes the origin's host must match.|
|max_length|integer(int32)|false|none|Maximum length of the value. 0 means the default maximum of 4096.|
|pattern|string|false|none|Optional RE2 expression matched against the whole normalized value.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|input_kind|string|
|input_kind|https_origin|
|input_kind|enum|

```json
    }
  ],

```

Describes a catalog provider and how to authenticate to it.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|Provider slug, used as provider when creating a connection or a provider credential.|
|display_name|string|false|none|Human-readable provider name.|
|description|string|false|none|Provider description.|
|auth_types|[string]|false|none|Credential kinds the provider accepts, sorted:<br>none\|oauth\|`shared_api_key`\|unknown\|`user_oauth_app`\|`user_token`.<br><br>`none` means the provider needs no credential. `oauth` means users can connect through<br>DigitalOcean's shared OAuth application. `user_oauth_app` means users can connect through an OAuth<br>client your team registers as a provider credential; without `oauth` alongside it, that is the only<br>way to connect. `shared_api_key` means DigitalOcean supplies the key. `user_token` means your team<br>or its users supply a key or token.<br><br>`unknown` means the provider declares no kind this API recognizes, including an OAuth provider whose<br>shared application is not available. It is never paired with another kind.|
|auth_type|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: read `auth_types`, since a provider may accept more than one credential kind. This is the first entry of `auth_types` other than `none`, or `none` when that is the only entry.|
|scopes|[string]|false|none|The OAuth scopes a connection may request; a connection that requests none gets all of them. Set only when `auth_types` contains `oauth` or `user_oauth_app`.|
|connection_parameters|[[connection_parameter_spec](#schemaconnection_parameter_spec)]|false|none|Non-sensitive values collected when creating a connection. Set only when `auth_types` contains `oauth` or `user_oauth_app`.|
|credential_parameters|[[connection_parameter_spec](#schemaconnection_parameter_spec)]|false|none|Non-secret values collected when registering an API key provider credential. They are validated against the provider's declaration and used to derive the credential's `base_url`; callers cannot supply header names or arbitrary destinations.|
|oauth_redirect_url|string|false|none|Callback URL a team must register with the provider when it creates its own OAuth client. It is the same for every provider and cannot be changed per credential. Empty unless `auth_types` contains `user_oauth_app`.|
|oauth_client_setup_url|string|false|none|HTTPS page at the provider where a team creates that OAuth client, such as its developer console or setup guide. Empty unless `auth_types` contains `user_oauth_app` and the provider declares one.|

Summarizes one matching tool. Input and output schemas are omitted; the tool catalog (`GET /v2/action-gateway/tools`) carries them.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tool_slug|string|false|none|The provider-qualified, stable tool identifier (`<provider>_<name>`). Treat it as opaque and pass it back verbatim.|

|title|string|false|none|Human-readable tool title.|
|description|string|false|none|What the tool does.|
|provider|string|false|none|The owning toolkit ID, broken out so a client never has to split `tool_slug`. It is what a client groups results by.|
|category|string|false|none|Best-effort catalog metadata and is empty for a large share of the catalog. Do not rely on it being present.|
|version|integer(int32)|false|none|The released version number of the tool, for example 3.|

<h2 id="tocS_tool_result">tool_result</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematool_result"></a>
<a id="schema_tool_result"></a>
<a id="tocStool_result"></a>
<a id="tocstool_result"></a>

```json
{
  "status": "succeeded",
  "output": {
    "provider": "exa",
    "results": [
      {
        "title": "DigitalOcean",
        "url": "https://www.digitalocean.com/"
      }
    ]
  },
  "error": {
    "class": "invalid_argument",
    "message": "Request is invalid. Fix request arguments and retry.",
    "retriable": false,
    "recovery_hint": "fix_args"
  },
  "call_id": "call_8b7c6d5e-4f3a-4b2c-9d1e-0f9a8b7c6d5e",
  "_meta": {
    "status": "requires_approval",
    "approval_id": "7d3c2b1a-9e8f-4a6b-8c5d-4e3f2a1b0c9d",
    "tool_name": "exa_web_search",
    "expires_at": "2026-10-09T18:30:00Z",
    "decide": {
      "method": "POST",
      "path": "/approvals/session/2b3c9f0e-1a4d-4e5f-8a7b-6c5d4e3f2a1b/7d3c2b1a-9e8f-4a6b-8c5d-4e3f2a1b0c9d",
      "body": "{\"decision\": \"approve\"}"
    }
  }
}
```

The result of one tool call. Check `status` before reading `output`. A call that needs approval, authorization, or connection setup fails with a `_meta.status` that names the step to complete.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|status|string|true|none|none|
|output|object|false|none|The tool's JSON output. Present when `status` is `succeeded`. Its shape is the tool's output schema, or the output view bound to the tool in the session.|
|error|[error_envelope](#schemaerror_envelope)|false|none|Describes why a request or tool call failed and whether retrying can help.|
|call_id|string|true|none|A unique identifier for this call. Include it when contacting support.|
|_meta|object|false|none|Additional result metadata. Keys include:<br><br>- `status`: `requires_approval`, `requires_authorization`, or<br>  `requires_connection_configuration` when the call stopped before<br>  running.<br><br>- `approval_id`, `tool_name`, `expires_at`, and `decide`: present with<br>  `requires_approval`. `decide` gives the `method`, `path`, and `body`<br>  of the approval request to send. Approve the call, then repeat it<br>  with the same arguments before `expires_at`.<br><br>- `retry`: `{"attempt_count": N, "exhausted": bool}` when the gateway<br>  retried the call.<br><br>- `output_view`: the output view applied to the result.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|succeeded|
|status|failed|

Per-signal DigitalOcean Insights telemetry opt-in, mirroring the Insights-owned schema insights.telemetry.opt_in. Each signal is independently optional and tri-state: omitted or null records that the customer expressed no choice and falls back to the product default, which is NOT equivalent to false.

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|logs|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the agent's logs are sent to Insights.|
|traces|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether the agent's traces are sent to Insights.|

```json
      "tool": "example",

      },
```

```json
    }
  ],

    ]
  },
  "network": {
    "default": "allow",
    "allow": [
      "example"
    ]
  }
}
```

Customer-declared tool-execution permission policy (spec.permissions). REQUEST only: the policy engine resolves it (∩ tenant ∩ platform) into the canonical policy and validates it against the (agent, version) capability descriptor. Absent or empty means the agent keeps its built-in default gating — no policy is shipped to the sandbox.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|defaultAction|string|false|none|Disposition for tool calls that match no rule. Defaults to "ask" when omitted.|
|rules|[[permission_rule](#schemapermission_rule)]|false|none|Ordered match→action rules. Declared order is authoritative: the LAST matching rule wins (author-order last-match).|
|filesystem|[permission_filesystem](#schemapermission_filesystem)|false|none|Filesystem boundary, enforced by the microVM (read-only root + bind-mounted writable roots) for every agent.|
|network|[permission_network](#schemapermission_network)|false|none|Network boundary. Narrows (subtract-only) spec.sandbox.egress; link-local/internal addresses stay blocked by the broader egress policy.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|defaultAction|allow|
|defaultAction|ask|
|defaultAction|deny|

Customer-authored agents.yaml Agent manifest, sent as the CreateSession request body with a YAML Content-Type. Two formats are accepted during the dual-format transition: the FLAT format (primary - no envelope, snake_case, duration strings; authoritative published schema contracts/agent.flat.schema.json, field reference docs/agent-manifest.md) and the legacy v1alpha1 envelope documented by the properties below (DEPRECATED; schema contracts/agent.v1alpha1.schema.json; parses append a deprecation notice to session.warnings). A top-level apiVersion key selects the legacy parser; its absence selects flat. Untrusted input: every value is a request that is validated and clamped server-side. Decoding is strict in both formats: unknown or misspelled fields are rejected with HTTP 400 (with did-you-mean and legacy-spelling hints on the flat path).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|apiVersion|string|false|none|Legacy envelope only - must be "agents.digitalocean.com/v1alpha1", and its presence is what routes the document to the deprecated legacy parser. Flat-format manifests carry no version key (the endpoint owns the contract); required, with kind and spec, when authoring the legacy format.|
|kind|string|false|none|Must be "Agent".|
|metadata|object|false|none|none|
|spec|object|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|apiVersion|agents.digitalocean.com/v1alpha1|
|kind|Agent|

|manifest|object|true|none|Canonical runnable environment spec JSON, immutable after create. Validated non-secret spec.env and spec.permissions remain; spec.secrets retains name/source/provider but omits ref and the write-only value; metadata.name is cleared while safe metadata such as labels remains.|
|content_hash|string|true|none|Lowercase SHA-256 hex digest of the canonical sanitized manifest JSON.|
|insights|object|false|none|none|
|created_by|string|true|none|Authenticated user identity that created the config.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|credentials|[[agent_config_credential_slot](#schemaagent_config_credential_slot)]|false|none|Redacted credential slot metadata (name/source/provider). Secret values are never included.|

<h2 id="tocS_agent_kind">agent_kind</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaagent_kind"></a>
<a id="schema_agent_kind"></a>
<a id="tocSagent_kind"></a>
<a id="tocsagent_kind"></a>

```json
"AGENT_KIND_UNSPECIFIED"
```

AgentKind identifies what runs inside the session sandbox. CreateSession accepts CLAUDE_CODE, OPENCODE, CODEX_CLI, CURSOR_CLI, OPENAI_CODEX, LANGGRAPH, and CREWAI (the supported set is overridable via HARNESS_SUPPORTED_AGENT_KINDS); other values are rejected with 400. AGENT_KIND_OPENAI_CODEX is the OpenAI sandbox-provider kind (DO runs codex exec-server; the agent loop lives at OpenAI). AGENT_KIND_LANGGRAPH is the LangGraph framework adapter. AGENT_KIND_CREWAI is the CrewAI Crew framework adapter: like LANGGRAPH the template bakes no agent code, so spec.env must supply FRAMEWORK_REPO and FRAMEWORK_REPO_SHA; a Crew kickoff is one-shot and exposes no HITL surface. CREWAI is additionally gated per team and returns 400 for teams it is not enabled for.

<h2 id="tocS_session_status">session_status</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasession_status"></a>
<a id="schema_session_status"></a>
<a id="tocSsession_status"></a>
<a id="tocssession_status"></a>

```json
"SESSION_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED"
```

SessionStatus is the lifecycle state of the sandbox + agent pair. SESSION_STATUS_ALL is a ListSessions status-filter value only -- no session is ever actually in this status. SESSION_STATUS_LOCKED is reserved for internal use and never appears in an end-user-facing response.

Session is the user-facing record of a environment session + sandbox pair.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session_id|string|false|none|none|
|name|string|false|none|User-assignable display name, unique per team among non-terminal sessions. Usable in place of session_id by clients (doctl / Console resolve it to the id via the ListSessions ?name= filter; the {session_id} path stays UUID-only). Supplied via the environment-spec metadata.name, or auto-generated ("session-<agent-type>-<date-time>") when omitted.|
|parent_session_id|string|false|none|Lineage: id of the session this one was forked from. Omitted/empty for root (non-fork) sessions.|
|fork_id|string(uuid)|false|none|Lineage: branch label assigned when this session was created by ForkSession (or rollback's internal fork). Omitted/empty for root sessions.|
|fork_from_checkpoint_id|string|false|none|Lineage: harness-api checkpoint id (cp_<hex>) the child booted from at fork time. Drives OHP inherited-history replay on attach. Omitted/empty for root sessions and legacy forks created before this field was persisted.|
|agent_kind|[agent_kind](#schemaagent_kind)|false|none|AgentKind identifies what runs inside the session sandbox. CreateSession accepts CLAUDE_CODE, OPENCODE, CODEX_CLI, CURSOR_CLI, OPENAI_CODEX, LANGGRAPH, and CREWAI (the supported set is overridable via HARNESS_SUPPORTED_AGENT_KINDS); other values are rejected with 400. AGENT_KIND_OPENAI_CODEX is the OpenAI sandbox-provider kind (DO runs codex exec-server; the agent loop lives at OpenAI). AGENT_KIND_LANGGRAPH is the LangGraph framework adapter. AGENT_KIND_CREWAI is the CrewAI Crew framework adapter: like LANGGRAPH the template bakes no agent code, so spec.env must supply FRAMEWORK_REPO and FRAMEWORK_REPO_SHA; a Crew kickoff is one-shot and exposes no HITL surface. CREWAI is additionally gated per team and returns 400 for teams it is not enabled for.|
|status|[session_status](#schemasession_status)|false|none|SessionStatus is the lifecycle state of the sandbox + agent pair. SESSION_STATUS_ALL is a ListSessions status-filter value only -- no session is ever actually in this status. SESSION_STATUS_LOCKED is reserved for internal use and never appears in an end-user-facing response.|
|sandbox_id|string|false|none|Sandbox identity for support / debugging. Informational; omitted until a sandbox is allocated.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|last_event_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp of the most recent event in this session's canonical stream. Drives the inactivity policy that destroys idle sessions.|
|keep_warm|boolean|false|none|Session is exempt from idle auto-pause (manifest keep_warm, or the agent-kind default: hermes sessions keep warm). Pause requests against such a session are rejected with 409. Omitted when false.|
|resume_on_topoff|boolean|false|none|Session consents to being resumed automatically when the team's prepayment balance is restored after a low-balance pause. Defaults to false at create time; may be toggled later via PATCH /v2/agents/sessions/{session_id} (resume_on_topoff only). Only a session paused with reason low_balance whose latest run did not complete is ever resumed automatically - a session the customer paused themselves, or one that idled out, stays paused regardless. Not an environment-spec field, and forks do not inherit it. Omitted when false.|
|pause_reason|string|false|none|Why this session is paused. Present only when status is SESSION_STATUS_PAUSED; omitted otherwise. Known values: manual (PauseSession RPC), idle (inactivity auto-pause), low_balance (prepay gate). Clients should treat an unrecognized value as an opaque reason string.|
|idle_timeout_seconds|integer(int64)|false|none|This session's own idle-pause timeout (manifest idle_timeout). Omitted when the session uses the deployment-wide default.|
|repo_hint|string|false|none|Optional repository hint supplied at session creation (first spec.workspace.repos entry of the manifest). Not authoritative; the agent may change repos in-session.|
|warnings|[string]|false|none|Non-fatal advisories computed from the manifest at create time: one entry per populated accepted-but-not-yet-enforced section (flat names: secrets, model, tools, memory, budget, max_lifetime, mounts; legacy manifests get the corresponding spec.* paths), a deprecation entry when a legacy-envelope manifest or an adapter alias (codex-cli, cursor-cli) is used, and a heuristic entry per credential-looking spec.env value. Populated on the CreateSession response only.|
|config_id|string(uuid)|false|none|Durable Environment Config UUID the session was created from (inline manifests persist a config too, named after the session). Persisted and returned on create/get/list; absent only for sessions created before config references were stored.|
|openai_session_id|string|false|none|OpenAI Agents API session id (sess_…) this DO sandbox hosts. Populated only for AGENT_KIND_OPENAI_CODEX sessions (empty otherwise). Non-secret correlation metadata; a client (doctl agents attach) reads it to bridge to the OpenAI session. See docs/design/openai-sandbox-provider.md.|
|openai_environment_id|string|false|none|OpenAI Agents API environment id (env_…), captured from the resolved CODEX_ENVIRONMENT_ID guest env value. Populated only for AGENT_KIND_OPENAI_CODEX sessions. Non-secret correlation metadata.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_UNSPECIFIED|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_CLAUDE_CODE|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_OPENCODE|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_CODEX_CLI|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_CURSOR_CLI|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_NONE|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_CUSTOM|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_HERMES|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_OPENAI_CODEX|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_LANGGRAPH|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_CREWAI|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_PROVISIONING|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_READY|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_DETACHED|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_DESTROYING|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_DESTROYED|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_FAILED|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_PAUSED|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_ALL|
|status|SESSION_STATUS_LOCKED|

Session-scoped, not config-scoped: the referenced config never confers this, so one shared config cannot enrol every session created from it. Omit to leave the default (or to let the ?resume_on_topoff= query parameter supply it).|

|reason|string|false|none|Human-readable explanation of the verdict.|

Response of POST /v2/agents/sessions/policy/validate: per-rule verdicts for the (agent, version). The same shape is persisted per session in session_policies.verdicts.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|agent|string|false|none|none|
|version|string|false|none|none|
|ok|boolean|false|none|False when any strict rule is unsupported or unverified — i.e. CreateSession would reject this policy for this (agent, version).|
|defaultAction|string|false|none|Catch-all disposition AS SHIPPED (after unverified allow→ask downgrade). When defaultActionVerdict is degraded, this remains the shipped value; see defaultActionRendered for what the agent will actually enforce.|
|defaultActionVerdict|string|false|none|exact — agent can enforce the catch-all as written; degraded — agent cannot enforce the requested defaultAction (warn-only; shipped value unchanged); omitted when no descriptor was available to classify against.|
|defaultActionRendered|string|false|none|Disposition the agent will actually enforce as the catch-all: equals defaultAction when exact; the more-restrictive degrade target (usually ask) when degraded.|
|defaultActionReason|string|false|none|Human-readable explanation when defaultActionVerdict is degraded.|
|verdicts|[[rule_verdict](#schemarule_verdict)]|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|defaultAction|allow|
|defaultAction|ask|
|defaultAction|deny|
|defaultActionVerdict|exact|

```json
"READY"
```

Capture lifecycle: PENDING -> READY | FAILED. Only READY checkpoints are forkable/restorable. CreateCheckpoint blocks until terminal, so PENDING is only ever observable via list/get while a capture is in flight.

```json
"explicit"
```

How the checkpoint came to exist: explicit - requested via CreateCheckpoint; implicit - minted automatically by the platform (on run completion, or when ForkSession is called without from_checkpoint_id).

<h2 id="tocS_checkpoint">checkpoint</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacheckpoint"></a>
<a id="schema_checkpoint"></a>
<a id="tocScheckpoint"></a>
<a id="tocscheckpoint"></a>

```json
{
  "checkpoint_id": "cp_9f2c1a4b",
  "session_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
  "status": "READY",
  "kind": "explicit",
  "label": "before-refactor",
  "event_id": "01JABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTVWXYZ",
  "size_bytes": 1048576,
  "created_at": "2026-08-01T12:00:00Z",
  "error_message": "capture timed out"
}
```

Checkpoint is a durable capture of a session's live sandbox machine state bound to the event-log cursor at the cut. READY checkpoints seed forks (ForkSession) and rollback. Internal fields (team_id, the substrate checkpoint id, event_seq) are never serialized.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|checkpoint_id|string|false|none|Public checkpoint id, stable for the checkpoint's lifetime (e.g. cp_9f2c1a4b).|
|session_id|string|false|none|Owning session.|
|status|[checkpoint_status](#schemacheckpoint_status)|false|none|Capture lifecycle: PENDING -> READY \| FAILED. Only READY checkpoints are forkable/restorable. CreateCheckpoint blocks until terminal, so PENDING is only ever observable via list/get while a capture is in flight.|
|kind|[checkpoint_kind](#schemacheckpoint_kind)|false|none|How the checkpoint came to exist: explicit - requested via CreateCheckpoint; implicit - minted automatically by the platform (on run completion, or when ForkSession is called without from_checkpoint_id).|
|label|string|false|none|Optional user-supplied label from CreateCheckpoint; empty when omitted.|
|event_id|string|false|none|Event-log cursor (ULID) of the last event included in the cut; forks resume event replay from here.|
|size_bytes|integer(int64)|false|none|Size of the captured machine state. 0 until the checkpoint reaches READY.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|error_message|string|false|none|Client-safe failure detail; set only when status is FAILED.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|PENDING|
|status|READY|
|status|FAILED|
|kind|explicit|
|kind|implicit|

<h2 id="tocS_stream_event">stream_event</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemastream_event"></a>
<a id="schema_stream_event"></a>
<a id="tocSstream_event"></a>
<a id="tocsstream_event"></a>

```json
{
  "event_id": "example",
  "run_id": "example",
  "tenant_id": "example",
  "session_id": "example",
  "trace_parent": "example",
  "timestamp": "2026-07-27T12:00:00Z",
  "seq": 1,
  "source_event_id": "example",
  "source_event_type": "example",
  "source_tenant_id": "example",
  "producer": "agent",
  "definition_id": "example",
  "revision_id": "example",
  "credential_binding_set_id": "example",
  "type": "run.started",
  "data": {}
}
```

The JSON payload carried in each SSE event's `data:` field (canonical SPI event envelope). The SSE `event:` field repeats `type`, and the `id:` field repeats `event_id`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|event_id|string|false|none|none|
|run_id|string|false|none|none|
|tenant_id|string|false|none|DO Team ID rendered as a decimal string.|
|session_id|string|false|none|none|
|trace_parent|string|false|none|none|
|timestamp|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|seq|integer(int64)|false|none|Producer-supplied sequence number; nonzero values increase monotonically within an ingress stream.|
|source_event_id|string|false|none|none|
|source_event_type|string|false|none|none|
|source_tenant_id|string|false|none|Optional runtime-native tenant identifier; distinct from authoritative tenant_id.|
|producer|string|false|none|Server-assigned component that submitted the event.|
|definition_id|string|false|none|none|
|revision_id|string|false|none|none|
|credential_binding_set_id|string|false|none|none|
|type|string|false|none|Canonical SPI event type. The SSE `event:` field carries the same value.|
|data|object|false|none|Type-specific payload, discriminated by `type` (canonical SPI shapes; numeric fields are JSON numbers):<br>- run.started: {agent}<br>- run.token_delta: {text}<br>- run.tool_call_started: {tool_call_id, name, input}<br>- run.tool_call_completed: {tool_call_id, ok, duration_ms, summary}<br>- run.human_input_requested: {hitl_id, payload}<br>- run.human_input_received: {hitl_id, outcome, actor, reason}<br>- run.completed: {total_tokens_in, total_tokens_out, run_cost_micros}<br>- run.failed: {code, message}<br>- run.paused: {reason}<br>- run.resumed: {}<br>- session.updated: {}<br>- run.state_checkpointed: {checkpoint_id, digest}<br>- run.handoff: {from, to, description}<br>- run.usage_recorded: {step_id, model_id, usage: {input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_input_tokens, reasoning_tokens, tool_seconds}}<br>- run.sandbox_allocated: {sandbox_id, kind, template}<br>- run.sandbox_released: {sandbox_id, exit_code, duration_ms}<br>- run.cost_accrued: {running_total_micros, delta_micros}<br>- run.log: {level, message, fields}|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|producer|agent|
|producer|ohr|
|producer|ohp|
|producer|ohs|
|type|run.started|
|type|run.token_delta|
|type|run.tool_call_started|
|type|run.tool_call_completed|
|type|run.human_input_requested|
|type|run.human_input_received|
|type|run.completed|
|type|run.failed|
|type|run.paused|
|type|run.resumed|

<h2 id="tocS_ingress_url_state">ingress_url_state</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaingress_url_state"></a>
<a id="schema_ingress_url_state"></a>
<a id="tocSingress_url_state"></a>
<a id="tocsingress_url_state"></a>

```json
"INGRESS_URL_STATE_READY"
```

PENDING: route not yet published, URL not servable. READY: servable. There is no failed state; the substrate retries until READY.

<h2 id="tocS_session_ingress_url">session_ingress_url</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasession_ingress_url"></a>
<a id="schema_session_ingress_url"></a>
<a id="tocSsession_ingress_url"></a>
<a id="tocssession_ingress_url"></a>

```json
{
  "ingress_url_id": "3f2a1b0c-9d8e-7f6a-5b4c-3d2e1f0a9b8c",
  "session_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
  "port": 8000,
  "url": "https://abc123.nyc3.sandbox.ondigitalocean.com",
  "state": "INGRESS_URL_STATE_READY",
  "created_at": "2026-07-27T12:00:00Z"
}
```

A publicly routable HTTPS URL to one guest port of the session's sandbox. The hostname is stable while the session runs; it is revoked on pause and lock, and rollback moves the session to a new sandbox, so re-fetch after resume, unlock or rollback. Requests must carry the caller's DO token as a Bearer header.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ingress_url_id|string|false|none|none|
|session_id|string|false|none|none|
|port|integer(int64)|false|none|Guest port the URL fronts; 8000 (OpenHands Agent Server) today.|
|url|string|false|none|Immutable HTTPS origin, e.g. https://<id>.nyc3.sandbox.ondigitalocean.com.|
|state|[ingress_url_state](#schemaingress_url_state)|false|none|PENDING: route not yet published, URL not servable. READY: servable. There is no failed state; the substrate retries until READY.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|INGRESS_URL_STATE_PENDING|
|state|INGRESS_URL_STATE_READY|
