<h2 id="tocS_trigger">trigger</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematrigger"></a>
<a id="schema_trigger"></a>
<a id="tocStrigger"></a>
<a id="tocstrigger"></a>

```json
{
  "trigger_id": "b1a0c6de-1f2e-4a3b-9c8d-0e1f2a3b4c5d",
  "kind": "webhook",
  "name": "nightly-deploy-check",
  "status": "active",
  "session_mode": "fresh",
  "agent_kind": "AGENT_KIND_UNSPECIFIED",
  "prompt_template": "Review the latest push and summarize risks.",
  "output": {
    "mode": "email",
    "email_configured": true,
    "slack_configured": false
  },
  "session_template": "",
  "bound_session_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
  "webhook": {
    "provider": "github",
    "webhook_url": "https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/agents/triggers/b1a0.../webhook"
  },
  "cron": {
    "cron_expr": "0 9 * * 1-5",
    "timezone": "America/New_York",
    "next_run_at": "2026-07-27T13:00:00Z"
  },
  "created_at": "2026-07-27T12:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-07-27T12:00:00Z"
}
```

A single automation bound to exactly one agent/session (agent == session in v1). The nested block present depends on `kind` (webhook xor cron) and `session_mode` (fresh => session_template; reuse => bound_session_id). `agent_kind` is read-only and derived; the webhook secret, the output email address / Slack webhook URL, and any env values inside session_template are write-only and never returned.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|trigger_id|string|false|none|Server-allocated UUID; opaque to clients.|
|kind|[trigger_kind](#schematrigger_kind)|false|none|How the trigger fires - on an event (webhook) or on a schedule (cron). Immutable after create.|
|name|string|false|none|Unique per team among non-deleted triggers. Same rules as session names; not UUID-form.|
|status|[trigger_status](#schematrigger_status)|false|none|Trigger lifecycle state. Soft-deleted triggers are never returned (404).|
|session_mode|[trigger_session_mode](#schematrigger_session_mode)|false|none|fresh = a new session is created from the trigger's spec on every firing and destroyed after. reuse = the trigger binds an existing PAUSED session, resumed on each firing and paused after; multiple triggers may bind one session.|
|agent_kind|[agent_kind](#schemaagent_kind)|false|none|AgentKind identifies what runs inside the session sandbox. CreateSession accepts CLAUDE_CODE, OPENCODE, CODEX_CLI, CURSOR_CLI, OPENAI_CODEX, LANGGRAPH, and CREWAI (the supported set is overridable via HARNESS_SUPPORTED_AGENT_KINDS); other values are rejected with 400. AGENT_KIND_OPENAI_CODEX is the OpenAI sandbox-provider kind (DO runs codex exec-server; the agent loop lives at OpenAI). AGENT_KIND_LANGGRAPH is the LangGraph framework adapter. AGENT_KIND_CREWAI is the CrewAI Crew framework adapter: like LANGGRAPH the template bakes no agent code, so spec.env must supply FRAMEWORK_REPO and FRAMEWORK_REPO_SHA; a Crew kickoff is one-shot and exposes no HITL surface. CREWAI is additionally gated per team and returns 400 for teams it is not enabled for.|
|prompt_template|string|false|none|The prompt sent on each fire. Opaque to clients; payload-interpolation syntax is server-defined. For cron triggers it must not reference payload placeholders.|
|output|[trigger_output_read](#schematrigger_output_read)|false|none|Output-delivery configuration as seen on reads. The email address and Slack webhook URL are write-only and never returned.|
|session_template|string|false|none|Present iff session_mode=fresh. The agents.yaml Agent manifest used to CREATE a session on each fire, returned with its env values REDACTED.|
|bound_session_id|string(uuid)|false|none|Present iff session_mode=reuse. UUID of the existing PAUSED session this trigger resumes; may be shared by multiple triggers.|
|webhook|[webhook_config](#schemawebhook_config)|false|none|Present iff kind=webhook. The secret is never in this object (see create_trigger_response / rotate_secret_response).|
|cron|[cron_config](#schemacron_config)|false|none|Present iff kind=cron.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|kind|webhook|
|kind|cron|
|status|active|
|status|paused|
|session_mode|fresh|
|session_mode|reuse|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_UNSPECIFIED|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_CLAUDE_CODE|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_OPENCODE|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_CODEX_CLI|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_CURSOR_CLI|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_NONE|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_CUSTOM|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_HERMES|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_OPENAI_CODEX|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_LANGGRAPH|
|agent_kind|AGENT_KIND_CREWAI|

<h2 id="tocS_update_trigger_request">update_trigger_request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaupdate_trigger_request"></a>
<a id="schema_update_trigger_request"></a>
<a id="tocSupdate_trigger_request"></a>
<a id="tocsupdate_trigger_request"></a>

```json
{
  "name": "nightly-deploy-check",
  "status": "active",
  "prompt_template": "Review the latest push and summarize risks.",
  "output": {
    "mode": "email",
    "email": "oncall@example.com",
    "slack": {
      "webhook_url": "https://hooks.slack.com/services/T0000/B0000/XXXX"
    }
  },
  "session_template": "",
  "bound_session_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
  "cron": {
    "cron_expr": "0 9 * * 1-5",
    "timezone": "America/New_York"
  }
}
```

Partial update. Only the supplied fields change. kind and webhook.provider are immutable. Sending status alone is how pause/re-enable work.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|New team-unique trigger name. Same charset/length rules as create.|
|status|[trigger_status](#schematrigger_status)|false|none|Trigger lifecycle state. Soft-deleted triggers are never returned (404).|
|prompt_template|string|false|none|none|
|output|[trigger_output_write](#schematrigger_output_write)|false|none|Output-delivery configuration on create/update. Exactly one of email / slack is required for the matching mode and forbidden otherwise; destinations are stored encrypted and never returned.|
|session_template|string|false|none|fresh triggers only. A session_template PATCH is a full replacement of the stored template; you must resupply every spec.secrets slot value the new manifest declares, or the request is a 400.|
|bound_session_id|string(uuid)|false|none|reuse triggers only. UUID of an existing session owned by the team.|
|cron|[create_cron_config](#schemacreate_cron_config)|false|none|cron block on create.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|active|
|status|paused|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|execution_id|string|false|none|none|
|trigger_id|string|false|none|none|
|status|[trigger_execution_status](#schematrigger_execution_status)|false|none|Per-firing outcome.|
|session_id|string|false|none|The run's session. Populated once the session is created (fresh) or is known (reuse); empty before then.|

|created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|payload|string|false|none|The raw webhook body or cron tick metadata. Returned by GetTriggerExecution only; omitted from list items. Cleared for terminal executions after the payload retention window (default 7 days from creation).|
|output_text|string|false|none|The doctl-parity transcript rendered from the run's SPI events. Returned by GetTriggerExecution only; omitted from list items.|
|output_truncated|boolean|false|none|True when output_text is incomplete. Returned by GetTriggerExecution only; omitted from list items.|

|Property|Value|

|status|running|
|status|succeeded|
|status|failed|

<h2 id="tocS_app_component_base">app_component_base</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

<a id="schema_app_component_base"></a>

<a id="tocsapp_component_base"></a>

```json
{
  "name": "api",
  "git": {
    "branch": "main",
    "repo_clone_url": "https://github.com/digitalocean/sample-golang.git"
  },
  "github": {
    "branch": "main",
    "deploy_on_push": true,
    "repo": "digitalocean/sample-golang"
  },
  "gitlab": {
    "branch": "main",
    "deploy_on_push": true,
    "repo": "digitalocean/sample-golang"
  },
  "bitbucket": {
    "branch": "main",
    "deploy_on_push": true,
    "repo": "digitalocean/sample-golang"
  },
  "image": {
    "registry": "registry.hub.docker.com",
    "registry_type": "DOCR",
    "registry_credentials": "my-dockerhub-username:dckr_pat_the_access_token",
    "repository": "origin/master",
    "tag": "latest",
    "digest": "sha256:795e91610e9cccb7bb80893fbabf9c808df7d52ae1f39cd1158618b4a33041ac",
    "deploy_on_push": {
      "enabled": true
    }
  },
  "dockerfile_path": "path/to/Dockerfile",
  "build_command": "npm run build",
  "run_command": "bin/api",
  "source_dir": "path/to/dir",
  "envs": [
    {
      "key": "BASE_URL",
      "scope": "BUILD_TIME",
      "type": "GENERAL",
      "value": "http://example.com"
    }
  ],
  "environment_slug": "node-js",
  "log_destinations": [
    {
      "name": "my_log_destination",
      "papertrail": {
        "endpoint": "https://mypapertrailendpoint.com"
      },
      "datadog": {
        "endpoint": "https://mydatadogendpoint.com",
        "api_key": "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"
      },
      "logtail": {
        "token": "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"
      },
      "open_search": {
        "endpoint": "https://example.com:9300",
        "basic_auth": {
          "user": "apps_user",
          "password": "password1"
        },
        "index_name": "logs",
        "cluster_name": "my-opensearch-cluster"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|The name. Must be unique across all components within the same app.|
|git|[apps_git_source_spec](#schemaapps_git_source_spec)|false|none|none|
|github|[apps_github_source_spec](#schemaapps_github_source_spec)|false|none|none|
|gitlab|[apps_gitlab_source_spec](#schemaapps_gitlab_source_spec)|false|none|none|
|bitbucket|[apps_bitbucket_source_spec](#schemaapps_bitbucket_source_spec)|false|none|none|
|image|[apps_image_source_spec](#schemaapps_image_source_spec)|false|none|none|
|dockerfile_path|string|false|none|The path to the Dockerfile relative to the root of the repo. If set, it will be used to build this component. Otherwise, App Platform will attempt to build it using buildpacks.|
|build_command|string|false|none|An optional build command to run while building this component from source.|
|run_command|string|false|none|An optional run command to override the component's default.|
|source_dir|string|false|none|An optional path to the working directory to use for the build. For Dockerfile builds, this will be used as the build context. Must be relative to the root of the repo.|
|envs|[[app_variable_definition](#schemaapp_variable_definition)]|false|none|A list of environment variables made available to the component.|
|environment_slug|string|false|none|An environment slug describing the type of this app. For a full list, please refer to [the product documentation](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/app-platform/).|
|log_destinations|[[app_log_destination_definition](#schemaapp_log_destination_definition)]|false|none|A list of configured log forwarding destinations.|

```json
{
  "allow_origins": [
    {
      "exact": "https://www.example.com"
    },
    {
      "regex": "^.*example.com"
    }
  ],
  "allow_methods": [
    "GET",
    "OPTIONS",
    "POST",
    "PUT",
    "PATCH",
    "DELETE"
  ],
  "allow_headers": [
    "Content-Type",
    "X-Custom-Header"
  ],
  "expose_headers": [
    "Content-Encoding",
    "X-Custom-Header"
  ],
  "max_age": "5h30m",
  "allow_credentials": false
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_origins|[[apps_string_match](#schemaapps_string_match)]|false|none|The set of allowed CORS origins.|
|allow_methods|[string]|false|none|The set of allowed HTTP methods. This configures the `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` header.|
|allow_headers|[string]|false|none|The set of allowed HTTP request headers. This configures the `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` header.|
|expose_headers|[string]|false|none|The set of HTTP response headers that browsers are allowed to access. This configures the `Access-Control-Expose-Headers` header.|
|max_age|string|false|none|An optional duration specifying how long browsers can cache the results of a preflight request. This configures the `Access-Control-Max-Age` header.|
|allow_credentials|boolean|false|none|Whether browsers should expose the response to the client-side JavaScript code when the request’s credentials mode is include. This configures the `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` header.|

```json
{
  "name": "api",
  "git": {
    "branch": "main",
    "repo_clone_url": "https://github.com/digitalocean/sample-golang.git"
  },
  "github": {
    "branch": "main",
    "deploy_on_push": true,
    "repo": "digitalocean/sample-golang"
  },
  "gitlab": {
    "branch": "main",
    "deploy_on_push": true,
    "repo": "digitalocean/sample-golang"
  },
  "bitbucket": {
    "branch": "main",
    "deploy_on_push": true,
    "repo": "digitalocean/sample-golang"
  },
  "image": {
    "registry": "registry.hub.docker.com",
    "registry_type": "DOCR",
    "registry_credentials": "my-dockerhub-username:dckr_pat_the_access_token",
    "repository": "origin/master",
    "tag": "latest",
    "digest": "sha256:795e91610e9cccb7bb80893fbabf9c808df7d52ae1f39cd1158618b4a33041ac",
    "deploy_on_push": {
      "enabled": true
    }
  },
  "dockerfile_path": "path/to/Dockerfile",
  "build_command": "npm run build",
  "run_command": "bin/api",
  "source_dir": "path/to/dir",
  "envs": [
    {
      "key": "BASE_URL",
      "scope": "BUILD_TIME",
      "type": "GENERAL",
      "value": "http://example.com"
    }
  ],
  "environment_slug": "node-js",
  "log_destinations": [
    {
      "name": "my_log_destination",
      "papertrail": {
        "endpoint": "https://mypapertrailendpoint.com"
      },
      "datadog": {
        "endpoint": "https://mydatadogendpoint.com",
        "api_key": "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"
      },
      "logtail": {
        "token": "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"
      },
      "open_search": {
        "endpoint": "https://example.com:9300",
        "basic_auth": {
          "user": "apps_user",
          "password": "password1"
        },
        "index_name": "logs",
        "cluster_name": "my-opensearch-cluster"
      }
    }
  ],
  "instance_count": 2,
  "instance_size_slug": "apps-s-1vcpu-0.5gb",
  "autoscaling": {
    "min_instance_count": 2,
    "max_instance_count": 3,
    "metrics": {
      "requests_per_second": {
        "per_instance": 100
      },
      "request_duration": {
        "p95_milliseconds": 500
      }
    }
  },
  "cors": {
    "allow_origins": [
      {
        "exact": "https://www.example.com"
      },
      {
        "regex": "^.*example.com"
      }
    ],
    "allow_methods": [
      "GET",
      "OPTIONS",
      "POST",
      "PUT",
      "PATCH",
      "DELETE"
    ],
    "allow_headers": [
      "Content-Type",
      "X-Custom-Header"
    ],
    "expose_headers": [
      "Content-Encoding",
      "X-Custom-Header"
    ],
    "max_age": "5h30m",
    "allow_credentials": false
  },
  "health_check": {
    "failure_threshold": 2,
    "port": 80,
    "http_path": "/health",
    "initial_delay_seconds": 30,
    "period_seconds": 60,
    "success_threshold": 3,
    "timeout_seconds": 45
  },
  "liveness_health_check": {
    "failure_threshold": 18,
    "port": 80,
    "http_path": "/health",
    "initial_delay_seconds": 30,
    "period_seconds": 10,
    "success_threshold": 1,
    "timeout_seconds": 1
  },
  "protocol": "HTTP",
  "http_port": 3000,
  "internal_ports": [
    80,
    443
  ],
  "routes": [
    {
      "path": "/api",
      "preserve_path_prefix": true
    }
  ],
  "termination": {
    "drain_seconds": 15,
    "grace_period_seconds": 120
  }
}
```

<h2 id="tocS_app_ingress_spec_rule_routing_component">app_ingress_spec_rule_routing_component</h2>

<a id="schema_app_ingress_spec_rule_routing_component"></a>

<a id="tocsapp_ingress_spec_rule_routing_component"></a>

```json
{
  "name": "web",
  "preserve_path_prefix": "true",
  "rewrite": "/api/v1/"
}
```

The component to route to. Only one of `component` or `redirect` may be set.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the component to route to.|
|preserve_path_prefix|string|false|none|An optional flag to preserve the path that is forwarded to the backend service. By default, the HTTP request path will be trimmed from the left when forwarded to the component. For example, a component with `path=/api` will have requests to `/api/list` trimmed to `/list`. If this value is `true`, the path will remain `/api/list`. Note: this is not applicable for Functions Components and is mutually exclusive with `rewrite`.|
|rewrite|string|false|none|An optional field that will rewrite the path of the component to be what is specified here. By default, the HTTP request path will be trimmed from the left when forwarded to the component. For example, a component with `path=/api` will have requests to `/api/list` trimmed to `/list`. If you specified the rewrite to be `/v1/`, requests to `/api/list` would be rewritten to `/v1/list`. Note: this is mutually exclusive with `preserve_path_prefix`.|

```json
  "uri": "/about",
  "authority": "example.com",
  "port": 443,
  "scheme": "https",
  "redirect_code": 302
}
```

The redirect configuration for the rule. Only one of `component` or `redirect` may be set.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|uri|string|false|none|An optional URI path to redirect to. Note: if this is specified the whole URI of the original request will be overwritten to this value, irrespective of the original request URI being matched.|
|authority|string|false|none|The authority/host to redirect to. This can be a hostname or IP address. Note: use `port` to set the port.|
|port|integer(int64)|false|none|The port to redirect to.|
|scheme|string|false|none|The scheme to redirect to. Supported values are `http` or `https`. Default: `https`.|
|redirect_code|integer(int64)|false|none|The redirect code to use. Defaults to `302`. Supported values are 300, 301, 302, 303, 304, 307, 308.|

The desired configuration of an application.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the app. Must be unique across all apps in the same account.|
|region|string|false|none|The slug form of the geographical origin of the app. Default: `nearest available`|
|disable_edge_cache|boolean|false|none|If set to `true`, the app will **not** be cached at the edge (CDN). Enable this option if you want to manage CDN configuration yourself—whether by using an external CDN provider or by handling static content and caching within your app. This setting is also recommended for apps that require real-time data or serve dynamic content, such as those using Server-Sent Events (SSE) over GET, or hosting an MCP (Model Context Protocol) Server that utilizes SSE.  <br>**Note:** This feature is not available for static site components.  <br>For more information, see [Disable CDN Cache](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/app-platform/how-to/cache-content/#disable-cdn-cache).|
|disable_email_obfuscation|boolean|false|none|If set to `true`, email addresses in the app will not be obfuscated. This is<br>useful for apps that require email addresses to be visible (in the HTML markup).|
|enhanced_threat_control_enabled|boolean|false|none|If set to `true`, suspicious requests will go through additional security checks to help mitigate layer 7 DDoS attacks.|
|domains|[[app_domain_spec](#schemaapp_domain_spec)]|false|none|A set of hostnames where the application will be available.|
|services|[[app_service_spec](#schemaapp_service_spec)]|false|none|Workloads which expose publicly-accessible HTTP services.|
|static_sites|[[app_static_site_spec](#schemaapp_static_site_spec)]|false|none|Content which can be rendered to static web assets.|
|jobs|[[app_job_spec](#schemaapp_job_spec)]|false|none|Pre and post deployment workloads which do not expose publicly-accessible HTTP routes.|
|workers|[[app_worker_spec](#schemaapp_worker_spec)]|false|none|Workloads which do not expose publicly-accessible HTTP services.|
|functions|[[app_functions_spec](#schemaapp_functions_spec)]|false|none|Workloads which expose publicly-accessible HTTP services via Functions Components.|
|databases|[[app_database_spec](#schemaapp_database_spec)]|false|none|Database instances which can provide persistence to workloads within the<br>application.|
|ingress|[app_ingress_spec](#schemaapp_ingress_spec)|false|none|Specification for app ingress configurations.|
|egress|[app_egress_spec](#schemaapp_egress_spec)|false|none|Specification for app egress configurations.|
|maintenance|[app_maintenance_spec](#schemaapp_maintenance_spec)|false|none|Specification to configure maintenance settings for the app, such as maintenance mode and archiving the app.|
|vpc|[apps_vpc](#schemaapps_vpc)|false|read-only|none|

|Property|Value|

|region|atl|
|region|nyc|
|region|sfo|
|region|tor|
|region|ams|
|region|fra|
|region|lon|
|region|blr|
|region|sgp|
|region|syd|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|existing_static_apps|string|false|none|The maximum number of free static apps the account can have. We will charge you for any additional static apps.|
|spec|[app_spec](#schemaapp_spec)|false|none|The desired configuration of an application.|
|app_cost|integer(int32)|false|none|The monthly cost of the proposed app in USD.|
|app_tier_downgrade_cost|integer(int32)|false|none|**Deprecated.** The monthly cost of the proposed app in USD using the previous pricing plan tier. For example, if you propose an app that uses the Professional tier, the `app_tier_downgrade_cost` field displays the monthly cost of the app if it were to use the Basic tier. If the proposed app already uses the lest expensive tier, the field is empty.|

```json
  "deployment_id": "3aa4d20e-5527-4c00-b496-601fbd22520a",
  "skip_pin": false
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|deployment_id|string|false|none|The ID of the deployment to rollback to.|
|skip_pin|boolean|false|none|Whether to skip pinning the rollback deployment. If false, the rollback deployment will be pinned and any new deployments including Auto Deploy on Push hooks will be disabled until the rollback is either manually committed or reverted via the CommitAppRollback or RevertAppRollback endpoints respectively. If true, the rollback will be immediately committed and the app will remain unpinned.|

<h2 id="tocS_app_rollback_validation_condition">app_rollback_validation_condition</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaapp_rollback_validation_condition"></a>
<a id="schema_app_rollback_validation_condition"></a>
<a id="tocSapp_rollback_validation_condition"></a>
<a id="tocsapp_rollback_validation_condition"></a>

```json
{
  "code": "exceeded_revision_limit",
  "message": "the deployment is past the maximum historical revision limit of 0 for the \"starter\" app tier",
  "components": [
    "www"
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code|string|false|none|A code identifier that represents the failing condition.<br><br>Failing conditions:<br>  - `incompatible_phase` - indicates that the deployment's phase is not suitable for rollback.<br>  - `incompatible_result` - indicates that the deployment's result is not suitable for rollback.<br>  - `exceeded_revision_limit` - indicates that the app has exceeded the rollback revision limits for its tier.<br>  - `app_pinned` - indicates that there is already a rollback in progress and the app is pinned.<br>  - `database_config_conflict` - indicates that the deployment's database config is different than the current config.<br>  - `region_conflict` - indicates that the deployment's region differs from the current app region.<br>  <br>Warning conditions:<br>  - `static_site_requires_rebuild` - indicates that the deployment contains at least one static site that will require a rebuild.<br>  - `image_source_missing_digest` - indicates that the deployment contains at least one component with an image source that is missing a digest.<br>|
|message|string|false|none|A human-readable message describing the failing condition.|
|components|[string]|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|code|incompatible_phase|
|code|incompatible_result|
|code|exceeded_revision_limit|
|code|app_pinned|
|code|database_config_conflict|
|code|region_conflict|
|code|static_site_requires_rebuild|
|code|image_source_missing_digest|

```json
{
```

### Properties

|ttl|integer|false|none|The amount of time the content is cached by the CDN's edge servers in seconds. TTL must be one of 60, 600, 3600, 86400, or 604800. Defaults to 3600 (one hour) when excluded.|
|certificate_id|string(uuid)|false|none|The ID of a DigitalOcean managed TLS certificate used for SSL when a custom subdomain is provided.|
|custom_domain|string(hostname)|false|none|The fully qualified domain name (FQDN) of the custom subdomain used with the CDN endpoint.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|read-only|A time value given in ISO8601 combined date and time format that represents when the CDN endpoint was created.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|ttl|600|
|ttl|3600|
|ttl|86400|
|ttl|604800|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|A unique human-readable name referring to a certificate.|
|type|string|false|none|A string representing the type of the certificate. The value will be `custom` for a user-uploaded certificate or `lets_encrypt` for one automatically generated with Let's Encrypt.|
|private_key|string|true|none|The contents of a PEM-formatted private-key corresponding to the SSL certificate.|
|leaf_certificate|string|true|none|The contents of a PEM-formatted public SSL certificate.|
|certificate_chain|string|false|none|The full PEM-formatted trust chain between the certificate authority's certificate and your domain's SSL certificate.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|custom|
|type|lets_encrypt|

<h2 id="tocS_balance">balance</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabalance"></a>
<a id="schema_balance"></a>
<a id="tocSbalance"></a>
<a id="tocsbalance"></a>

```json
{
  "month_to_date_balance": "23.44",
  "account_balance": "12.23",
  "month_to_date_usage": "11.21",
  "generated_at": "2019-07-09T15:01:12Z"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|month_to_date_balance|string|false|none|Balance as of the `generated_at` time.  This value includes the `account_balance` and `month_to_date_usage`.|
|account_balance|string|false|none|Current balance of the customer's most recent billing activity.  Does not reflect `month_to_date_usage`.|
|month_to_date_usage|string|false|none|Amount used in the current billing period as of the `generated_at` time.|
|generated_at|string(date-time)|false|none|The time at which balances were most recently generated.|

<h2 id="tocS_prepayment_config">prepayment_config</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaprepayment_config"></a>
<a id="schema_prepayment_config"></a>
<a id="tocSprepayment_config"></a>
<a id="tocsprepayment_config"></a>

```json
{
  "spend_limit": "100.00",
  "is_auto_prepay_enabled": true,
  "prepay_amount": "50.00",
  "prepay_threshold": "10.00",
  "created_at": "2026-06-22T19:31:51Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-06-25T18:40:07Z"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|spend_limit|string|false|none|Maximum spend allowed before the prepayment gate blocks usage. Decimal dollars, e.g. `"100.00"`.|
|is_auto_prepay_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether automatic prepayment top-up is enabled.|
|prepay_amount|string|false|none|Amount to charge when auto top-up triggers. Decimal dollars, e.g. `"50.00"`.|
|prepay_threshold|string|false|none|Balance threshold that triggers auto top-up. Decimal dollars, e.g. `"10.00"`.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Time at which the prepayment configuration was created.|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Time at which the prepayment configuration was last updated.|

<h2 id="tocS_prepayment_status">prepayment_status</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaprepayment_status"></a>
<a id="schema_prepayment_status"></a>
<a id="tocSprepayment_status"></a>
<a id="tocsprepayment_status"></a>

```json
{
  "balance": "25.00",
  "is_auto_prepay_enabled": true,
  "blocked": true,
  "eligible": true,
  "month_to_date_balance": "75.00"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|balance|string|false|none|Current prepayment balance. Decimal dollars, e.g. `"25.00"`.|
|is_auto_prepay_enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether automatic prepayment top-up is enabled.|
|blocked|boolean|false|none|Whether the prepayment gate is currently blocking usage.|
|eligible|boolean|false|none|Whether the account is eligible for the prepayment gate experience.|
|month_to_date_balance|string|false|none|Current account balance including month-to-date usage. Decimal dollars, e.g. `"75.00"`.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|invoice_uuid|string|false|none|UUID of the invoice associated with the billing history entry, if  applicable.|
|date|string(date-time)|false|none|Time the billing history entry occurred.|
|type|string|false|none|Type of billing history entry.|

<h2 id="tocS_invoice_preview">invoice_preview</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainvoice_preview"></a>
<a id="schema_invoice_preview"></a>
<a id="tocSinvoice_preview"></a>
<a id="tocsinvoice_preview"></a>

```json
{
  "invoice_uuid": "fdabb512-6faf-443c-ba2e-665452332a9e",
  "invoice_id": "123456789",
  "amount": "23.45",
  "invoice_period": "2020-01",
  "updated_at": "2020-01-23T06:31:50Z"
}
```

The invoice preview.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|invoice_uuid|string|false|none|The UUID of the invoice. The canonical reference for the invoice.|
|invoice_id|string|false|none|ID of the invoice. Listed on the face of the invoice PDF as the "Invoice number".|
|amount|string|false|none|Total amount of the invoice, in USD.  This will reflect month-to-date usage in the invoice preview.|
|invoice_period|string|false|none|Billing period of usage for which the invoice is issued, in `YYYY-MM`  format.|

```json
  "opensearch_acl": [
    {
      "index": "index-abc.*",
      "permission": "read"
    }
  ],
  "acl": [
    {
      "id": "aaa",
      "topic": "topic-abc.*",
      "permission": "consume"
    }
  ],
  "mongo_user_settings": {
    "databases": [
      "my-db",
      "my-db-2"
    ],
    "role": "readOnly"
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pg_allow_replication|boolean|false|none|For PostgreSQL clusters, set to `true` to grant the user replication<br>privileges. When omitted on create or update, the value defaults to<br>`false` and replication privileges are not granted. This option is not<br>currently supported for other database engines.<br>|
|opensearch_acl|[object]|false|none|ACLs (Access Control Lists) specifying permissions on index within a OpenSearch cluster.|
|acl|[object]|false|none|ACLs (Access Control Lists) specifying permissions on topics within a Kafka cluster.|
|mongo_user_settings|object|false|none|MongoDB-specific settings for the user. Configure these when creating a user. Updating MongoDB roles or database access after creation is not supported; recreate the user to change them. This option is not currently supported for other database engines.|

|version|string|false|none|A string representing the version of the database engine in use for the cluster.|
|semantic_version|string|false|read-only|A string representing the semantic version of the database engine in use for the cluster.|
|num_nodes|integer|true|none|The number of nodes in the database cluster.|
|size|string|true|none|The slug identifier representing the size of the nodes in the database cluster.|
|region|string|true|none|The slug identifier for the region where the database cluster is located.|
|status|string|false|read-only|A string representing the current status of the database cluster.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|read-only|A time value given in ISO8601 combined date and time format that represents when the database cluster was created.|
|private_network_uuid|string|false|none|A string specifying the UUID of the VPC to which the database cluster will be assigned. If excluded, the cluster when creating a new database cluster, it will be assigned to your account's default VPC for the region. <br><br>Requires `vpc:read` scope.|
|tags|[string]|false|none|An array of tags that have been applied to the database cluster. <br><br>Requires `tag:read` scope.|
|db_names|[string]|false|read-only|An array of strings containing the names of databases created in the database cluster.|
|ui_connection|object|false|none|The connection details for OpenSearch dashboard. |
|schema_registry_connection|object|false|none|The connection details for Schema Registry.|

|private_connection|object|false|none|none|
|standby_connection|object|false|none|none|
|standby_private_connection|object|false|none|none|
|users|[[database_user](#schemadatabase_user)]|false|read-only|none|
|maintenance_window|object|false|none|none|
|project_id|string(uuid)|false|none|The ID of the project that the database cluster is assigned to. If excluded when creating a new database cluster, it will be assigned to your default project.<br><br>Requires `project:read` scope.|
|rules|[[firewall_rule](#schemafirewall_rule)]|false|none|none|
|version_end_of_life|string|false|read-only|A timestamp referring to the date when the particular version will no longer be supported. If null, the version does not have an end of life timeline.|
|version_end_of_availability|string|false|read-only|A timestamp referring to the date when the particular version will no longer be available for creating new clusters. If null, the version does not have an end of availability timeline.|
|storage_size_mib|integer|false|none|Additional storage added to the cluster, in MiB. If null, no additional storage is added to the cluster, beyond what is provided as a base amount from the 'size' and any previously added additional storage.|
|metrics_endpoints|[[database_service_endpoint](#schemadatabase_service_endpoint)]|false|read-only|Public hostname and port of the cluster's metrics endpoint(s). Includes one record for the cluster's primary node and a second entry for the cluster's standby node(s).|

|users|[[database_user](#schemadatabase_user)]|false|read-only|none|
|maintenance_window|object|false|none|none|
|project_id|string(uuid)|false|none|The ID of the project that the database cluster is assigned to. If excluded when creating a new database cluster, it will be assigned to your default project.<br><br>Requires `project:assign_resource` scope.|
|rules|[[firewall_rule](#schemafirewall_rule)]|false|none|none|
|version_end_of_life|string|false|read-only|A timestamp referring to the date when the particular version will no longer be supported. If null, the version does not have an end of life timeline.|
|version_end_of_availability|string|false|read-only|A timestamp referring to the date when the particular version will no longer be available for creating new clusters. If null, the version does not have an end of availability timeline.|
|storage_size_mib|integer|false|none|Additional storage added to the cluster, in MiB. If null, no additional storage is added to the cluster, beyond what is provided as a base amount from the 'size' and any previously added additional storage.|
|metrics_endpoints|[[database_service_endpoint](#schemadatabase_service_endpoint)]|false|read-only|Public hostname and port of the cluster's metrics endpoint(s). Includes one record for the cluster's primary node and a second entry for the cluster's standby node(s).|
|autoscale|object|false|none|Autoscaling configuration for the database cluster. Currently only supports storage autoscaling. If null, autoscaling is not configured for the cluster.|
|do_settings|object|false|none|none|

```json
  "enabled": true,
  "full_backup_week_schedule": "mon,thu"
}
```

MySQL Incremental Backup configuration settings

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Enable periodic incremental backups. When enabled, full_backup_week_schedule must be set. Incremental backups only store changes since the last backup, making them faster and more storage-efficient than full backups. This is particularly useful for large databases where daily full backups would be too time-consuming or expensive.|
|full_backup_week_schedule|string|false|none|Comma-separated list of days of the week when full backups should be created. Valid values: mon, tue, wed, thu, fri, sat, sun. Default is null. Example : "mon,fri,sun". |

```json
  "innodb_print_all_deadlocks": true,
  "innodb_rollback_on_timeout": true,
  "interactive_timeout": 3600,
  "internal_tmp_mem_storage_engine": "TempTable",

  "net_write_timeout": 30,

  "max_seeks_for_key": 1000,
  "optimizer_prune_level": 1,
  "optimizer_search_depth": 62,
  "optimizer_switch": "batched_key_access=on,hash_join=off",
  "sort_buffer_size": 262144,
  "tmp_table_size": 16777216,

  "long_query_time": 10,
  "binlog_retention_period": 600,
  "innodb_change_buffer_max_size": 25,
  "innodb_flush_neighbors": 0,
  "innodb_read_io_threads": 16,
  "innodb_write_io_threads": 16,

    "enabled": true,
    "full_backup_week_schedule": "mon,thu"
  }
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|backup_hour|integer|false|none|The hour of day (in UTC) when backup for the service starts. New backup only starts if previous backup has already completed.|
|backup_minute|integer|false|none|The minute of the backup hour when backup for the service starts. New backup  only starts if previous backup has already completed.|
|automatic_sp_privileges|boolean|false|none|When enabled, grants `EXECUTE` and `ALTER ROUTINE` privileges to the creator of a stored routine. When disabled, these privileges are not granted automatically.|
|sql_mode|string|false|none|Global SQL mode. If empty, uses MySQL server defaults. Must only include uppercase alphabetic characters, underscores, and commas.|
|connect_timeout|integer|false|none|The number of seconds that the mysqld server waits for a connect packet before responding with bad handshake.|
|default_time_zone|string|false|none|Default server time zone, in the form of an offset from UTC (from -12:00 to +12:00), a time zone name (EST), or 'SYSTEM' to use the MySQL server default.|
|div_precision_increment|integer|false|none|The number of digits by which to increase the scale of the result of division operations performed with the `/` operator.|
|end_markers_in_json|boolean|false|none|When enabled, the JSON output of `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON` includes end markers for nested structures.|
|eq_range_index_dive_limit|integer|false|none|The number of equality ranges in an equality comparison condition when the optimizer should switch from using index dives to index statistics.|
|group_concat_max_len|integer|false|none|The maximum permitted result length, in bytes, for the GROUP_CONCAT() function.|
|information_schema_stats_expiry|integer|false|none|The time, in seconds, before cached statistics expire.|
|innodb_adaptive_hash_index|boolean|false|none|When enabled, InnoDB uses an adaptive hash index to speed up equality lookups. The optimal setting is workload-dependent: it can improve performance for some workloads, but under high concurrency the associated latch can become a contention point, in which case disabling it may improve throughput. Default is true.|
|innodb_ft_enable_stopword|boolean|false|none|When enabled, the InnoDB FULLTEXT index stopword list is used. Disabled by default when a custom stopword table is configured.|
|innodb_ft_max_token_size|integer|false|none|The maximum length of words that an InnoDB FULLTEXT index stores. Changing this parameter will lead to a restart of the MySQL service.|
|innodb_ft_min_token_size|integer|false|none|The minimum length of words that an InnoDB FULLTEXT index stores.|
|innodb_ft_num_word_optimize|integer|false|none|The number of words to process during each OPTIMIZE TABLE operation on an InnoDB FULLTEXT index.|
|innodb_ft_result_cache_limit|integer|false|none|The InnoDB FULLTEXT index query result cache size limit, in bytes.|
|innodb_ft_server_stopword_table|string|false|none|The InnoDB FULLTEXT index stopword list for all InnoDB tables.|
|innodb_ft_user_stopword_table|string \| null|false|none|The InnoDB FULLTEXT index stopword list for user-created FULLTEXT indexes. Must be in the form `db_name/table_name`. Set to `null` to clear a previously configured value.|
|innodb_lock_wait_timeout|integer|false|none|The time, in seconds, that an InnoDB transaction waits for a row lock. before giving up.|
|innodb_log_buffer_size|integer|false|none|The size of the buffer, in bytes, that InnoDB uses to write to the log files. on disk.|
|innodb_online_alter_log_max_size|integer|false|none|The upper limit, in bytes, of the size of the temporary log files used during online DDL operations for InnoDB tables.|
|innodb_optimize_fulltext_only|boolean|false|none|When enabled, OPTIMIZE TABLE rebuilds only the InnoDB FULLTEXT index, not the table itself.|
|innodb_print_all_deadlocks|boolean|false|none|When enabled, records information about all deadlocks in InnoDB user transactions  in the error log. Disabled by default.|
|innodb_rollback_on_timeout|boolean|false|none|When enabled, transaction timeouts cause InnoDB to abort and roll back the entire transaction.|
|interactive_timeout|integer|false|none|The time, in seconds, the server waits for activity on an interactive. connection before closing it.|
|internal_tmp_mem_storage_engine|string|false|none|The storage engine for in-memory internal temporary tables.|
|net_read_timeout|integer|false|none|The time, in seconds, to wait for more data from an existing connection. aborting the read.|
|net_write_timeout|integer|false|none|The number of seconds to wait for a block to be written to a connection before aborting the write.|
|sql_require_primary_key|boolean|false|none|Require primary key to be defined for new tables or old tables modified with ALTER TABLE and fail if missing. It is recommended to always have primary keys because various functionality may break if any large table is missing them.|
|wait_timeout|integer|false|none|The number of seconds the server waits for activity on a noninteractive connection before closing it.|
|windowing_use_high_precision|boolean|false|none|When enabled, window functions use a higher precision for internal calculations, which can be more accurate but slower.|
|max_allowed_packet|integer|false|none|The size of the largest message, in bytes, that can be received by the server. Default is 67108864 (64M).|
|max_execution_time|integer|false|none|The execution timeout for `SELECT` statements, in milliseconds. A value of `0` disables the timeout (no limit).|
|max_heap_table_size|integer|false|none|The maximum size, in bytes, of internal in-memory tables. Also set tmp_table_size. Default is 16777216 (16M)|
|max_seeks_for_key|integer|false|none|Limits the assumed maximum number of seeks when looking up rows based on a key. Lower values cause the query optimizer to prefer indexes over table scans for non-covering indexes.|
|optimizer_prune_level|integer|false|none|Controls the heuristics applied during query optimization to prune less promising partial plans from the optimizer search space. `0` disables pruning and `1` enables it.|
|optimizer_search_depth|integer|false|none|The maximum depth of search performed by the query optimizer. Smaller values can reduce compilation time for large joins; a value of `0` lets the server automatically pick a reasonable value.|
|optimizer_switch|string|false|none|Controls query optimizer behavior as a comma-separated list of `option=value` pairs, or `default` to restore server defaults. Each value must be `on`, `off`, or `default`.|
|sort_buffer_size|integer|false|none|The sort buffer size, in bytes, for ORDER BY optimization. Default is 262144. (256K).|
|tmp_table_size|integer|false|none|The maximum size, in bytes, of internal in-memory tables. Also set max_heap_table_size. Default is 16777216 (16M).|
|slow_query_log|boolean|false|none|When enabled, captures slow queries. When disabled, also truncates the mysql.slow_log table. Default is false.|
|long_query_time|number|false|none|The time, in seconds, for a query to take to execute before  being captured by slow_query_logs. Default is 10 seconds.|
|binlog_retention_period|number|false|none|The minimum amount of time, in seconds, to keep binlog entries before deletion.  This may be extended for services that require binlog entries for longer than the default, for example if using the MySQL Debezium Kafka connector.|
|innodb_change_buffer_max_size|integer|false|none|Specifies the maximum size of the InnoDB change buffer as a percentage of the buffer pool.|
|innodb_flush_neighbors|integer|false|none|Specifies whether flushing a page from the InnoDB buffer pool also flushes other dirty pages in the same extent.<br>  - 0 &mdash; disables this functionality, dirty pages in the same extent are not flushed.<br>  - 1 &mdash; flushes contiguous dirty pages in the same extent.<br>  - 2 &mdash; flushes dirty pages in the same extent.|
|innodb_read_io_threads|integer|false|none|The number of I/O threads for read operations in InnoDB. Changing this parameter will lead to a restart of the MySQL service.|
|innodb_write_io_threads|integer|false|none|The number of I/O threads for write operations in InnoDB. Changing this parameter will lead to a restart of the MySQL service.|
|innodb_thread_concurrency|integer|false|none|Defines the maximum number of threads permitted inside of InnoDB. A value of 0 (the default) is interpreted as infinite concurrency (no limit). This variable is intended for performance  tuning on high concurrency systems.|
|net_buffer_length|integer|false|none|Start sizes of connection buffer and result buffer, must be multiple of 1024. Changing this parameter will lead to a restart of the MySQL service.|
|log_output|string|false|none|Defines the destination for logs. Can be `INSIGHTS`, `TABLE`, or both (`INSIGHTS,TABLE`), or `NONE` to disable logs. To specify both destinations, use `INSIGHTS,TABLE` (order matters). Default is NONE.|
|mysql_incremental_backup|[mysql_incremental_backup](#schemamysql_incremental_backup)|false|none|MySQL Incremental Backup configuration settings|

PGBouncer connection pooling settings

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|server_reset_query_always|boolean|false|none|Run server_reset_query (DISCARD ALL) in all pooling modes.|
|ignore_startup_parameters|[string]|false|none|List of parameters to ignore when given in startup packet.|
|min_pool_size|integer|false|none|If current server connections are below this number, adds more. Improves behavior when usual load comes suddenly back after period of total inactivity. The value is effectively capped at the pool size.|
|server_lifetime|integer|false|none|The pooler closes any unused server connection that has been connected longer than this amount of seconds.|
|server_idle_timeout|integer|false|none|Drops server connections if they have been idle more than this many seconds.  If 0, timeout is disabled. |
|autodb_pool_size|integer|false|none|If non-zero, automatically creates a pool of that size per user when a pool doesn't exist.|
|autodb_pool_mode|string|false|none|PGBouncer pool mode|
|autodb_max_db_connections|integer|false|none|Only allows a maximum this many server connections per database (regardless of user). If 0, allows unlimited connections.|
|autodb_idle_timeout|integer|false|none|If the automatically-created database pools have been unused this many seconds, they are freed. If 0, timeout is disabled.|

|ignore_startup_parameters|search_path|
|autodb_pool_mode|session|
|autodb_pool_mode|transaction|
|autodb_pool_mode|statement|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|autovacuum_freeze_max_age|integer|false|none|Specifies the maximum age (in transactions) that a table's pg_class.relfrozenxid field can attain before a VACUUM operation is forced to prevent transaction ID wraparound within the table. Note that the system will launch autovacuum processes to prevent wraparound even when autovacuum is otherwise disabled. This parameter will cause the server to be restarted.|
|autovacuum_max_workers|integer|false|none|Specifies the maximum number of autovacuum processes (other than the autovacuum launcher) that may be running at any one time. The default is three. This parameter can only be set at server start.|
|autovacuum_naptime|integer|false|none|Specifies the minimum delay, in seconds, between autovacuum runs on any given database. The default is one minute.|
|autovacuum_vacuum_threshold|integer|false|none|Specifies the minimum number of updated or deleted tuples needed to trigger a VACUUM in any one table. The default is 50 tuples.|
|autovacuum_analyze_threshold|integer|false|none|Specifies the minimum number of inserted, updated, or deleted tuples needed to trigger an ANALYZE in any one table. The default is 50 tuples.|
|autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor|number|false|none|Specifies a fraction, in a decimal value, of the table size to add to autovacuum_vacuum_threshold when deciding whether to trigger a VACUUM. The default is 0.2 (20% of table size).|
|autovacuum_analyze_scale_factor|number|false|none|Specifies a fraction, in a decimal value, of the table size to add to autovacuum_analyze_threshold when deciding whether to trigger an ANALYZE. The default is 0.2 (20% of table size).|
|autovacuum_vacuum_cost_delay|integer|false|none|Specifies the cost delay value, in milliseconds, that will be used in automatic VACUUM operations. If -1, uses the regular vacuum_cost_delay value, which is 20 milliseconds.|
|autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit|integer|false|none|Specifies the cost limit value that will be used in automatic VACUUM operations. If -1 is specified (which is the default), the regular vacuum_cost_limit value will be used.|
|backup_hour|integer|false|none|The hour of day (in UTC) when backup for the service starts. New backup only starts if previous backup has already completed.|
|backup_minute|integer|false|none|The minute of the backup hour when backup for the service starts. New backup is only started if previous backup has already completed.|
|bgwriter_delay|integer|false|none|Specifies the delay, in milliseconds, between activity rounds for the background writer. Default is 200 ms.|
|bgwriter_flush_after|integer|false|none|The amount of kilobytes that need to be written by the background writer before attempting to force the OS to issue these writes to underlying storage. Specified in kilobytes, default is 512.  Setting of 0 disables forced writeback.|
|bgwriter_lru_maxpages|integer|false|none|The maximum number of buffers that the background writer can write. Setting this to zero disables background writing. Default is 100.|
|bgwriter_lru_multiplier|number|false|none|The average recent need for new buffers is multiplied by bgwriter_lru_multiplier to arrive at an estimate of the number that will be needed during the next round, (up to bgwriter_lru_maxpages). 1.0 represents a “just in time” policy of writing exactly the number of buffers predicted to be needed. Larger values provide some cushion against spikes in demand, while smaller values intentionally leave writes to be done by server processes. The default is 2.0.|
|deadlock_timeout|integer|false|none|The amount of time, in milliseconds, to wait on a lock before checking to see if there is a deadlock condition.|
|default_toast_compression|string|false|none|Specifies the default TOAST compression method for values of compressible columns (the default is lz4).|
|idle_in_transaction_session_timeout|integer|false|none|Time out sessions with open transactions after this number of milliseconds|
|jit|boolean|false|none|Activates, in a boolean, the system-wide use of Just-in-Time Compilation (JIT).|
|log_autovacuum_min_duration|integer|false|none|Causes each action executed by autovacuum to be logged if it ran for at least the specified number of milliseconds. Setting this to zero logs all autovacuum actions. Minus-one (the default) disables logging autovacuum actions.|
|log_error_verbosity|string|false|none|Controls the amount of detail written in the server log for each message that is logged.|
|log_line_prefix|string|false|none|Selects one of the available log-formats. These can support popular log analyzers like pgbadger, pganalyze, etc.|
|log_min_duration_statement|integer|false|none|Log statements that take more than this number of milliseconds to run. If -1, disables.|
|max_files_per_process|integer|false|none|PostgreSQL maximum number of files that can be open per process.|
|max_prepared_transactions|integer|false|none|PostgreSQL maximum prepared transactions. Once increased, this parameter cannot be lowered from its set value.|
|max_pred_locks_per_transaction|integer|false|none|PostgreSQL maximum predicate locks per transaction.|

|max_standby_streaming_delay|integer|false|none|Max standby streaming delay in milliseconds.|
|max_replication_slots|integer|false|none|PostgreSQL maximum replication slots.|
|max_logical_replication_workers|integer|false|none|PostgreSQL maximum logical replication workers (taken from the pool of max_parallel_workers).|
|max_parallel_workers|integer|false|none|Sets the maximum number of workers that the system can support for parallel queries.|
|max_parallel_workers_per_gather|integer|false|none|Sets the maximum number of workers that can be started by a single Gather or Gather Merge node.|
|max_worker_processes|integer|false|none|Sets the maximum number of background processes that the system can support. Once increased, this parameter cannot be lowered from its set value.|
|pg_partman_bgw.role|string|false|none|Controls which role to use for pg_partman's scheduled background tasks. Must consist of alpha-numeric characters, dots, underscores, or dashes. May not start with dash or dot. Maximum of 64 characters.|
|pg_partman_bgw.interval|integer|false|none|Sets the time interval to run pg_partman's scheduled tasks.|
|pg_stat_statements.track|string|false|none|Controls which statements are counted. Specify 'top' to track top-level statements (those issued directly by clients), 'all' to also track nested statements (such as statements invoked within functions), or 'none' to disable statement statistics collection. The default value is top.|
|temp_file_limit|integer|false|none|PostgreSQL temporary file limit in KiB. If -1, sets to unlimited.|
|timezone|string|false|none|PostgreSQL service timezone|
|track_activity_query_size|integer|false|none|Specifies the number of bytes reserved to track the currently executing command for each active session.|
|track_commit_timestamp|string|false|none|Record commit time of transactions.|
|track_functions|string|false|none|Enables tracking of function call counts and time used.|
|track_io_timing|string|false|none|Enables timing of database I/O calls. This parameter is off by default, because it will repeatedly query the operating system for the current time, which may cause significant overhead on some platforms.|
|max_wal_senders|integer|false|none|PostgreSQL maximum WAL senders. Once increased, this parameter cannot be lowered from its set value.|
|wal_sender_timeout|integer|false|none|Terminate replication connections that are inactive for longer than this amount of time, in milliseconds. Setting this value to zero disables the timeout. Must be either 0 or between 5000 and 10800000.|
|wal_writer_delay|integer|false|none|WAL flush interval in milliseconds. Note that setting this value to lower than the default 200ms may negatively impact performance|
|shared_buffers_percentage|number|false|none|Percentage of total RAM that the database server uses for shared memory buffers.  Valid range is 20-60 (float), which corresponds to 20% - 60%.  This setting adjusts the shared_buffers configuration value.|
|pgbouncer|[pgbouncer_advanced_config](#schemapgbouncer_advanced_config)|false|none|PGBouncer connection pooling settings|
|work_mem|integer|false|none|The maximum amount of memory, in MB, used by a query operation (such as a sort or hash table) before writing to temporary disk files. Default is 1MB + 0.075% of total RAM (up to 32MB).|
|timescaledb|[timescaledb_advanced_config](#schematimescaledb_advanced_config)|false|none|TimescaleDB extension configuration values|
|synchronous_replication|string|false|none|Synchronous replication type. Note that the service plan also needs to support synchronous replication.|

|max_failover_replication_time_lag|integer|false|none|Number of seconds of master unavailability before triggering database failover to standby. The default value is 60.|
|max_connections|integer|false|none|Sets the PostgreSQL maximum number of concurrent connections to the database server. This is a limited-release parameter. Contact your account team to confirm your eligibility. You cannot decrease this parameter value when set. For services with a read replica, first increase the read replica's value. After the change is applied to the replica, you can increase the primary service's value. Changing this parameter causes a service restart.|
|max_slot_wal_keep_size|integer|false|none|PostgreSQL maximum WAL size (MB) reserved for replication slots. If -1 is specified, replication slots may retain an unlimited amount of WAL files. The default is -1 (upstream default). wal_keep_size minimum WAL size setting takes precedence over this.|
|pgaudit|object|false|none|System-wide settings for the pgaudit extension. When `feature_enabled` is true, the pgaudit extension is automatically installed. When false, the extension is uninstalled but auditing configurations (such as `log`) are preserved.|

<h2 id="tocS_redis_advanced_config">redis_advanced_config</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaredis_advanced_config"></a>
<a id="schema_redis_advanced_config"></a>
<a id="tocSredis_advanced_config"></a>
<a id="tocsredis_advanced_config"></a>

```json
{
  "redis_maxmemory_policy": "allkeys-lru",
  "redis_pubsub_client_output_buffer_limit": 64,
  "redis_number_of_databases": 16,
  "redis_io_threads": 1,
  "redis_lfu_log_factor": 10,
  "redis_lfu_decay_time": 1,
  "redis_ssl": true,
  "redis_timeout": 300,
  "redis_notify_keyspace_events": "K",
  "redis_persistence": "rdb",
  "redis_acl_channels_default": "allchannels"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|redis_maxmemory_policy|string|false|none|A string specifying the desired eviction policy for the Caching cluster.<br><br>- `noeviction`: Don't evict any data, returns error when memory limit is reached.<br>- `allkeys-lru:` Evict any key, least recently used (LRU) first.<br>- `allkeys-random`: Evict keys in a random order.<br>- `volatile-lru`: Evict keys with expiration only, least recently used (LRU) first.<br>- `volatile-random`: Evict keys with expiration only in a random order.<br>- `volatile-ttl`: Evict keys with expiration only, shortest time-to-live (TTL) first.|
|redis_pubsub_client_output_buffer_limit|integer|false|none|Set output buffer limit for pub / sub clients in MB. The value is the hard limit, the soft limit is 1/4 of the hard limit. When setting the limit, be mindful of the available memory in the selected service plan.|
|redis_number_of_databases|integer|false|none|Set number of redis databases. Changing this will cause a restart of redis service.|
|redis_io_threads|integer|false|none|Caching IO thread count|
|redis_lfu_log_factor|integer|false|none|Counter logarithm factor for volatile-lfu and allkeys-lfu maxmemory-policies|
|redis_lfu_decay_time|integer|false|none|LFU maxmemory-policy counter decay time in minutes|
|redis_ssl|boolean|false|none|Require SSL to access Caching.<br>- When enabled, Caching accepts only SSL connections on port `25061`.<br>- When disabled, port `25060` is opened for non-SSL connections, while port `25061` remains available for SSL connections.<br>|
|redis_timeout|integer|false|none|Caching idle connection timeout in seconds|
|redis_notify_keyspace_events|string|false|none|Set notify-keyspace-events option. Requires at least `K` or `E` and accepts any combination of the following options. Setting the parameter to `""` disables notifications.<br>- `K` &mdash; Keyspace events<br>- `E` &mdash; Keyevent events<br>- `g` &mdash; Generic commands (e.g. `DEL`, `EXPIRE`, `RENAME`, ...)<br>- `$` &mdash; String commands<br>- `l` &mdash; List commands<br>- `s` &mdash; Set commands<br>- `h` &mdash; Hash commands<br>- `z` &mdash; Sorted set commands<br>- `t` &mdash; Stream commands<br>- `d` &mdash; Module key type events<br>- `x` &mdash; Expired events<br>- `e` &mdash; Evicted events<br>- `m` &mdash; Key miss events<br>- `n` &mdash; New key events<br>- `A` &mdash; Alias for `"g$lshztxed"`|
|redis_persistence|string|false|none|Creates an RDB dump of the database every 10 minutes that can be used  to recover data after a node crash. The database does not create the  dump if no keys have changed since the last dump. When set to `off`,  the database cannot fork services, and data can be lost if a service  is restarted or powered off. DigitalOcean Managed Caching databases  do not support the Append Only File (AOF) persistence method.|
|redis_acl_channels_default|string|false|none|Determines default pub/sub channels' ACL for new users if ACL is not supplied. When this option is not defined, all_channels is assumed to keep backward compatibility. This option doesn't affect Caching configuration acl-pubsub-default.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|redis_maxmemory_policy|noeviction|
|redis_maxmemory_policy|allkeys-lru|
|redis_maxmemory_policy|allkeys-random|
|redis_maxmemory_policy|volatile-lru|
|redis_maxmemory_policy|volatile-random|
|redis_maxmemory_policy|volatile-ttl|
|redis_persistence|off|
|redis_persistence|rdb|
|redis_acl_channels_default|allchannels|
|redis_acl_channels_default|resetchannels|

<h2 id="tocS_eviction_policy_model">eviction_policy_model</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaeviction_policy_model"></a>
<a id="schema_eviction_policy_model"></a>
<a id="tocSeviction_policy_model"></a>
<a id="tocseviction_policy_model"></a>

```json
"allkeys_lru"
```

A string specifying the desired eviction policy for a Caching or Valkey cluster.

- `noeviction`: Don't evict any data, returns error when memory limit is reached.
- `allkeys_lru:` Evict any key, least recently used (LRU) first.
- `allkeys_random`: Evict keys in a random order.
- `volatile_lru`: Evict keys with expiration only, least recently used (LRU) first.
- `volatile_random`: Evict keys with expiration only in a random order.
- `volatile_ttl`: Evict keys with expiration only, shortest time-to-live (TTL) first.

```json
  "valkey_pubsub_client_output_buffer_limit": 64,

  "valkey_ssl": true,
  "valkey_timeout": 300,
  "valkey_notify_keyspace_events": "K",
  "valkey_persistence": "rdb",
  "valkey_acl_channels_default": "allchannels",
  "frequent_snapshots": true,
  "valkey_active_expire_effort": 1
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|valkey_maxmemory_policy|[eviction_policy_model](#schemaeviction_policy_model)|false|none|A string specifying the desired eviction policy for a Caching or Valkey cluster.<br><br>- `noeviction`: Don't evict any data, returns error when memory limit is reached.<br>- `allkeys_lru:` Evict any key, least recently used (LRU) first.<br>- `allkeys_random`: Evict keys in a random order.<br>- `volatile_lru`: Evict keys with expiration only, least recently used (LRU) first.<br>- `volatile_random`: Evict keys with expiration only in a random order.<br>- `volatile_ttl`: Evict keys with expiration only, shortest time-to-live (TTL) first.|
|valkey_pubsub_client_output_buffer_limit|integer|false|none|Set output buffer limit for pub / sub clients in MB. The value is the hard limit, the soft limit is 1/4 of the hard limit. When setting the limit, be mindful of the available memory in the selected service plan.|
|valkey_number_of_databases|integer|false|none|Set number of valkey databases. Changing this will cause a restart of valkey service.|
|valkey_io_threads|integer|false|none|Valkey IO thread count|
|valkey_lfu_log_factor|integer|false|none|Counter logarithm factor for volatile-lfu and allkeys-lfu maxmemory-policies|
|valkey_lfu_decay_time|integer|false|none|LFU maxmemory-policy counter decay time in minutes|
|valkey_ssl|boolean|false|none|Require SSL to access Valkey|
|valkey_timeout|integer|false|none|Valkey idle connection timeout in seconds|
|valkey_notify_keyspace_events|string|false|none|Set notify-keyspace-events option. Requires at least `K` or `E` and accepts any combination of the following options. Setting the parameter to `""` disables notifications.<br>- `K` &mdash; Keyspace events<br>- `E` &mdash; Keyevent events<br>- `g` &mdash; Generic commands (e.g. `DEL`, `EXPIRE`, `RENAME`, ...)<br>- `$` &mdash; String commands<br>- `l` &mdash; List commands<br>- `s` &mdash; Set commands<br>- `h` &mdash; Hash commands<br>- `z` &mdash; Sorted set commands<br>- `t` &mdash; Stream commands<br>- `d` &mdash; Module key type events<br>- `x` &mdash; Expired events<br>- `e` &mdash; Evicted events<br>- `m` &mdash; Key miss events<br>- `n` &mdash; New key events<br>- `A` &mdash; Alias for `"g$lshztxed"`|
|valkey_persistence|string|false|none|When persistence is 'rdb', Valkey does RDB dumps each 10 minutes if any key is changed. Also RDB dumps are done according to backup schedule for backup purposes. When persistence is 'off', no RDB dumps and backups are done, so data can be lost at any moment if service is restarted for any reason, or if service is powered off. Also service can't be forked.|
|valkey_acl_channels_default|string|false|none|Determines default pub/sub channels' ACL for new users if ACL is not supplied. When this option is not defined, all_channels is assumed to keep backward compatibility. This option doesn't affect Valkey configuration acl-pubsub-default.|
|frequent_snapshots|boolean|false|none|Frequent RDB snapshots<br>When enabled, Valkey will create frequent local RDB snapshots. When disabled, Valkey will only take RDB snapshots when a backup is created, based on the backup schedule. This setting is ignored when valkey_persistence is set to off.<br>|
|valkey_active_expire_effort|integer|false|none|Active expire effort<br>Valkey reclaims expired keys both when accessed and in the background. The background process scans for expired keys to free memory. Increasing the active-expire-effort setting (default 1, max 10) uses more CPU to reclaim expired keys faster, reducing memory usage but potentially increasing latency.<br>|

|valkey_maxmemory_policy|volatile_random|
|valkey_maxmemory_policy|volatile_ttl|

```json
{
  "compression_type": "gzip",
  "group_initial_rebalance_delay_ms": 3000,
  "group_min_session_timeout_ms": 6000,
  "group_max_session_timeout_ms": 1800000,
  "connections_max_idle_ms": 540000,
  "max_incremental_fetch_session_cache_slots": 1000,
  "message_max_bytes": 1048588,
  "offsets_retention_minutes": 10080,
  "log_cleaner_delete_retention_ms": 86400000,
  "log_cleaner_min_cleanable_ratio": 0.5,
  "log_cleaner_max_compaction_lag_ms": 60000,
  "log_cleaner_min_compaction_lag_ms": 100000,
  "log_cleanup_policy": "delete",
  "log_flush_interval_messages": 9223372036854776000,
  "log_flush_interval_ms": 1000000,
  "log_index_interval_bytes": 4096,
  "log_index_size_max_bytes": 10485760,
  "log_message_downconversion_enable": true,
  "log_message_timestamp_type": "CreateTime",
  "log_message_timestamp_difference_max_ms": 1000000,
  "log_preallocate": false,
  "log_retention_bytes": 1000000,
  "log_retention_hours": 1000000,
  "log_retention_ms": 100000000,
  "log_roll_jitter_ms": 10000000,
  "log_roll_ms": 1000000,
  "log_segment_bytes": 100000000,
  "log_segment_delete_delay_ms": 60000,
  "auto_create_topics_enable": true,
  "min_insync_replicas": 1,
  "num_partitions": 10,
  "default_replication_factor": 2,
  "replica_fetch_max_bytes": 2097152,
  "replica_fetch_response_max_bytes": 20971520,
  "max_connections_per_ip": 512,
  "producer_purgatory_purge_interval_requests": 100,
  "socket_request_max_bytes": 20971520,
  "transaction_state_log_segment_bytes": 104857600,
  "transaction_remove_expired_transaction_cleanup_interval_ms": 3600000,
  "schema_registry": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|compression_type|string|false|none|Specify the final compression type for a given topic. This configuration accepts the standard compression codecs ('gzip', 'snappy', 'lz4', 'zstd'). It additionally accepts 'uncompressed' which is equivalent to no compression; and 'producer' which means retain the original compression codec set by the producer.|
|group_initial_rebalance_delay_ms|integer|false|none|The amount of time, in milliseconds, the group coordinator will wait for more consumers to join a new group before performing the first rebalance. A longer delay means potentially fewer rebalances, but increases the time until processing begins. The default value for this is 3 seconds. During development and testing it might be desirable to set this to 0 in order to not delay test execution time.|
|group_min_session_timeout_ms|integer|false|none|The minimum allowed session timeout for registered consumers. Longer timeouts give consumers more time to process messages in between heartbeats at the cost of a longer time to detect failures.|
|group_max_session_timeout_ms|integer|false|none|The maximum allowed session timeout for registered consumers. Longer timeouts give consumers more time to process messages in between heartbeats at the cost of a longer time to detect failures.|
|connections_max_idle_ms|integer|false|none|Idle connections timeout: the server socket processor threads close the connections that idle for longer than this.|
|max_incremental_fetch_session_cache_slots|integer|false|none|The maximum number of incremental fetch sessions that the broker will maintain.|
|message_max_bytes|integer|false|none|The maximum size of message that the server can receive.|
|offsets_retention_minutes|integer|false|none|Log retention window in minutes for offsets topic|
|log_cleaner_delete_retention_ms|integer|false|none|How long are delete records retained?|
|log_cleaner_min_cleanable_ratio|number|false|none|Controls log compactor frequency. Larger value means more frequent compactions but also more space wasted for logs. Consider setting log_cleaner_max_compaction_lag_ms to enforce compactions sooner, instead of setting a very high value for this option.|
|log_cleaner_max_compaction_lag_ms|integer|false|none|The maximum amount of time message will remain uncompacted. Only applicable for logs that are being compacted|
|log_cleaner_min_compaction_lag_ms|integer|false|none|The minimum time a message will remain uncompacted in the log. Only applicable for logs that are being compacted.|
|log_cleanup_policy|string|false|none|The default cleanup policy for segments beyond the retention window|
|log_flush_interval_messages|integer|false|none|The number of messages accumulated on a log partition before messages are flushed to disk|
|log_flush_interval_ms|integer|false|none|The maximum time in ms that a message in any topic is kept in memory before flushed to disk. If not set, the value in log.flush.scheduler.interval.ms is used|
|log_index_interval_bytes|integer|false|none|The interval with which Kafka adds an entry to the offset index|
|log_index_size_max_bytes|integer|false|none|The maximum size in bytes of the offset index|
|log_message_downconversion_enable|boolean|false|none|This configuration controls whether down-conversion of message formats is enabled to satisfy consume requests.|
|log_message_timestamp_type|string|false|none|Define whether the timestamp in the message is message create time or log append time.|
|log_message_timestamp_difference_max_ms|integer|false|none|The maximum difference allowed between the timestamp when a broker receives a message and the timestamp specified in the message|
|log_preallocate|boolean|false|none|Controls whether to preallocate a file when creating a new segment|
|log_retention_bytes|integer|false|none|The maximum size of the log before deleting messages|
|log_retention_hours|integer|false|none|The number of hours to keep a log file before deleting it|
|log_retention_ms|integer|false|none|The number of milliseconds to keep a log file before deleting it (in milliseconds), If not set, the value in log.retention.minutes is used. If set to -1, no time limit is applied.|
|log_roll_jitter_ms|integer|false|none|The maximum jitter to subtract from logRollTimeMillis (in milliseconds). If not set, the value in log.roll.jitter.hours is used|
|log_roll_ms|integer|false|none|The maximum time before a new log segment is rolled out (in milliseconds).|
|log_segment_bytes|integer|false|none|The maximum size of a single log file|
|log_segment_delete_delay_ms|integer|false|none|The amount of time to wait before deleting a file from the filesystem|
|auto_create_topics_enable|boolean|false|none|Enable auto creation of topics|
|min_insync_replicas|integer|false|none|When a producer sets acks to 'all' (or '-1'), min_insync_replicas specifies the minimum number of replicas that must acknowledge a write for the write to be considered successful.|
|num_partitions|integer|false|none|Number of partitions for autocreated topics|
|default_replication_factor|integer|false|none|Replication factor for autocreated topics|
|replica_fetch_max_bytes|integer|false|none|The number of bytes of messages to attempt to fetch for each partition (defaults to 1048576). This is not an absolute maximum, if the first record batch in the first non-empty partition of the fetch is larger than this value, the record batch will still be returned to ensure that progress can be made.|
|replica_fetch_response_max_bytes|integer|false|none|Maximum bytes expected for the entire fetch response (defaults to 10485760). Records are fetched in batches, and if the first record batch in the first non-empty partition of the fetch is larger than this value, the record batch will still be returned to ensure that progress can be made. As such, this is not an absolute maximum.|
|max_connections_per_ip|integer|false|none|The maximum number of connections allowed from each ip address (defaults to 2147483647).|
|producer_purgatory_purge_interval_requests|integer|false|none|The purge interval (in number of requests) of the producer request purgatory (defaults to 1000).|
|socket_request_max_bytes|integer|false|none|The maximum number of bytes in a socket request (defaults to 104857600).|
|transaction_state_log_segment_bytes|integer|false|none|The transaction topic segment bytes should be kept relatively small in order to facilitate faster log compaction and cache loads (defaults to 104857600 (100 mebibytes)).|
|transaction_remove_expired_transaction_cleanup_interval_ms|integer|false|none|The interval at which to remove transactions that have expired due to transactional.id.expiration.ms passing (defaults to 3600000 (1 hour)).|
|schema_registry|boolean|false|none|Enable creation of schema registry for the Kafka cluster. Schema_registry only works with General Purpose - Dedicated CPU plans.|

```json
  "ism_history_max_age_hours": 24,
```
