<a id="tocscreate_response_request"></a>

```json
{
  "model": "openai-gpt-oss-20b",
  "input": "What is the capital of France?",
  "max_output_tokens": 50,
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "stream": false,
  "instructions": "You are a helpful assistant.",
  "top_p": 1,
  "stream_options": null,
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "name": "get_weather",
      "description": "Get the current weather in a given location.",
      "parameters": {}
    }
  ],
  "tool_choice": "auto",
  "stop": null,
  "metadata": {
    "session_id": "abc123"
  },
  "user": "user-1234"
}
```

Request body for sending a prompt to a model using the Responses API.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model|string|true|none|The model ID of the model you want to use. Get the model ID using `/v1/models` or on the available models page.<br>|
|input|string \| [object]|true|none|The prompt or input content you want the model to respond to. Can be a simple text string or an array of message objects for conversation context.<br>|
|max_output_tokens|integer \| null|false|none|The maximum number of tokens to generate in the response.<br>|
|temperature|number \| null|false|none|A value between 0.0 and 2.0 to control randomness and creativity. Lower values like 0.2 make the output more focused and deterministic, while higher values like 0.8 make it more random.<br>|
|stream|boolean \| null|false|none|Set to true to stream partial responses as Server-Sent Events.<br>|
|instructions|string \| null|false|none|System-level instructions for the model. This sets the behavior and context for the response generation.<br>|
|top_p|number \| null|false|none|An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass.<br>|
|stream_options|object \| null|false|none|Options for streaming response. Only set this when you set stream to true.|
|tools|[object]|false|none|A list of tools the model may call.<br>|
|tool_choice|string \| object|false|none|Controls which (if any) tool is called by the model.<br>|
|stop|string \| [string] \| null|false|none|Up to 4 sequences where the API will stop generating further tokens.<br>|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Set of key-value pairs that can be attached to the request.<br>|
|user|string \| null|false|none|A unique identifier representing your end-user.<br>|

Request body for asynchronously invoking a model. Supports image generation, audio generation, and text-to-speech models. The `input` object fields vary depending on the model type.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|model_id|string|true|none|The ID of the model to invoke asynchronously.<br>|
|input|object|true|none|The input parameters for the model invocation. Fields vary by model type.<br><br>For **image generation** models (e.g., `fal-ai/flux/schnell`, `fal-ai/fast-sdxl`), use `prompt` along with optional image parameters like `output_format`, `num_inference_steps`, `guidance_scale`, `num_images`, and `enable_safety_checker`.<br><br>For **audio generation** models (e.g., `fal-ai/stable-audio-25/text-to-audio`), use `prompt` along with `seconds_total` to control the duration.<br><br>For **text-to-speech** models (e.g., `fal-ai/elevenlabs/tts/multilingual-v2`), use `text` with the content you want converted to speech.<br>|
|tags|[object]|false|none|An optional list of key-value tags to attach to the invocation request for tracking or categorization.<br>|

```json
{
  "model": "qwen3-tts-voicedesign",
  "input": "Hello, world!",
  "voice": "alloy",
  "response_format": "mp3",
  "instructions": "Speak naturally."
}
```

Request body for text-to-speech generation.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|model|string|true|none|The text-to-speech model to use.|
|input|string|true|none|The text to convert to speech.|
|voice|string|false|none|The voice to use for synthesis.|
|response_format|string|false|none|The audio format to return. Supported values include `mp3` and `wav`. The API may return raw audio bytes or a JSON envelope with base64-encoded audio.<br>|
|instructions|string|false|none|Optional style or delivery instructions for the synthesizer.|

```json
{
  "batch_id": "0e9d1d35-3d1e-4d66-9a2f-8c7e0f6b3e21",
  "status": "in_progress",
  "provider": "openai",
  "endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions",

  "input_file_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4789-90ab-cdef12345678",
  "output_file_id": null,
  "error_file_id": null,
  "request_counts": {
    "total": 10000,
    "completed": 0,
    "failed": 0
  },
  "request_id": "c7e3ad1e-20c3-4e47-9bf2-6f2a4d6a2f11",
  "metadata": null,
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "invalid_input_file",
      "message": "Line 42: missing required field 'custom_id'.",
      "line": 42
    }
  ],

  "in_progress_at": "2026-04-24T19:20:05Z",
  "finalizing_at": "2026-04-24T20:10:42Z",
  "completed_at": "2026-04-24T20:15:30Z",
  "expires_at": "2026-04-25T19:19:19Z",
  "cancelled_at": "2026-04-24T19:45:11Z",
  "failed_at": "2026-04-24T19:50:00Z"
}
```

A Batch Inference job.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|batch_id|string(uuid)|true|none|Unique identifier for the batch job.|
|status|string|true|none|Lifecycle status. Terminal states: `completed`, `failed`, `expired`, `cancelled`.<br>|
|provider|string|true|none|none|
|endpoint|string|false|none|Inference endpoint each request is dispatched to.|
|completion_window|string|true|none|none|
|input_file_id|string(uuid)|true|none|The uploaded JSONL input file.|
|output_file_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|Output JSONL file. Populated once the job completes.|
|error_file_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|Error sidecar file. Null when no errors were produced.|
|request_counts|object|false|none|Aggregate request counts.|
|request_id|string|false|none|The idempotency key supplied at creation.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Metadata attached at creation.|
|errors|[object]|false|none|Top-level errors that prevented the batch from completing.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|in_progress_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|none|
|finalizing_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|none|
|completed_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|none|
|expires_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|Derived from `created_at` plus `completion_window`.|
|cancelled_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|none|
|failed_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|validating|
|status|in_progress|
|status|finalizing|
|status|completed|
|status|failed|
|status|expired|
|status|cancelling|
|status|cancelled|
|provider|openai|
|provider|anthropic|
|completion_window|24h|

<h2 id="tocS_batch_create_request">batch_create_request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabatch_create_request"></a>
<a id="schema_batch_create_request"></a>
<a id="tocSbatch_create_request"></a>
<a id="tocsbatch_create_request"></a>

```json
{
  "file_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4789-90ab-cdef12345678",
  "provider": "openai",
  "endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions",
  "completion_window": "24h",
  "request_id": "c7e3ad1e-20c3-4e47-9bf2-6f2a4d6a2f11",
  "metadata": {
    "team": "ml-eval",
    "dataset": "prompts_v1"
  }
}
```

Request body for creating a batch inference job.

When `provider` is `openai`, `endpoint` is required and must be one of `/v1/responses` or `/v1/chat/completions`. When `provider` is `anthropic`, `endpoint` must be omitted — the Anthropic Message Batches API does not need a per-job endpoint.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|string(uuid)|true|none|The `file_id` returned by `POST /v1/batches/files`.|
|provider|string|true|none|The inference provider whose JSONL schema the input file conforms to. `openai` follows the OpenAI Batch API input schema (`custom_id`, `method`, `url`, `body`); `anthropic` follows the Anthropic Message Batches JSONL conventions.<br>|
|endpoint|string|false|none|Inference endpoint each request is dispatched to. **Required when `provider` is `openai` and must match the `url` on every JSONL line. Must be omitted when `provider` is `anthropic`.**<br>|
|completion_window|string|true|none|Time window in which the job must complete. Jobs that do not finish in time transition to `expired`.<br>|
|request_id|string|true|none|Client-supplied idempotency key. Retries with the same value return the existing job instead of creating a duplicate.<br>|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Optional string-valued metadata to attach to the job.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|provider|openai|
|provider|anthropic|
|endpoint|/v1/responses|
|endpoint|/v1/chat/completions|
|completion_window|24h|

Presigned download URLs for a batch job. URLs are short-lived — download the artifacts soon after fetching them.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|result_available|boolean|true|none|When `false`, keep polling batch status and retry later.<br>|
|output_file_url|string(uri) \| null|false|none|Presigned URL for the main results JSONL.|
|error_file_url|string(uri) \| null|false|none|Presigned URL for the error sidecar JSONL, if any.|
|expires_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the presigned URLs expire.|
